- **[thir] One spelling rule for integer literals, then the uniform constant fold (second after 0.6).** A variable-free integer binop at a slot sink (a method / function / ctor argument, a return, a field or container element) renders the checked operator chain at the slot width, so `c.bump((2**30 * 4) // 4)` with `k: int` panics with an int32 overflow where CPython prints 1073741824 (`BUGS.md#thir-int-methodarg-shift-not-folded`), and at `--default-int int64` a folded wide literal loses its `static_cast<int64_t>` (`BUGS.md#thir-folded-wide-literal-drops-int64-cast`). Sema already values every both-literal binop (`_try_eval_int_literal_binop`, an `IntLiteralType` with its value), so the fold itself is one line in `_lower_binop` -- once a folded literal is spelled by ONE rule. Today every consumer that picks its C++ from the literal's type spells it its own way, and the 0.6 gate batch E attempt (fold at every sink) broke each of them: the f-string `.to_string()` chosen from the sema type rather than the rendered literal; the operand spelling of `~` / unary `-` over a folded constant (`-2**63` must be one literal, not a negated chain); arithmetic around a folded BigInt operand (`add_check<int32_t>` over a `BigInt` literal); the `pow` / `abs` overload choice on a folded constant; the index / slice bound `to_fixed_check`; list elements that do not retarget a folded scalar to the element type; and the 4300-digit `str()` limit hit when a huge folded value is formatted in a diagnostic. Design: one literal-spelling function keyed on (value, target type), read by every one of those consumers, then the fold. Pin with a condensed case, one section per sink.
- **[sema] `@overload` becomes `@dispatch` variants in an early sema pass (third after 0.6).** Today sema analyzes an `@overload` implementation once, at the union param types, and the per-stub specialization happens late: the codegen driver lowers the body once per stub (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py`, `_thir_lower(..., stub=stub)`) and THIR folds `isinstance`, `is None`, `Literal` `==` / `in` / truthiness, `and` / `or` chains and `match` class patterns against the stub (`_overload_resolve_static`, `_lower_overload_folded_if`, `_lower_overload_folded_match`). About 1,250 lines after sema exist only for this form: the fold, four THIR node types (`THIRFoldedBlock`, `THIRFoldedIfChain`, `THIRMatchFoldBind`, `THIROverloadDefault`), the stub admission gates, a per-stub return check raised in codegen (`_overload_adjusted_return`, which also strips coercions sema built against the union return), and the specialized signature emitters in `codegen_cpp/functions.py` / `records.py`. Sema typing the body at the union while THIR lowers it per stub is what rejects valid code today (`if n > 5: ... elif isinstance(a, Dog):` at `if.overload_true_after_dynamic`, a guarded case at `match.overload_fold_guard`) and what BUGS.md#overload-stub-narrow-type-converts-default comes from. The C++ is already identical to hand-written `@dispatch` variants. **Design:** after type resolution, clone the implementation once per stub (precedent: `sema/method_expansion.py` clones bodies for `@auto_readonly`), prune the statically dead branches on the clone with the same six fold families (skipping params the body reassigns), and hand every later phase plain `@dispatch` variants. Not in the parser: types are unresolved there, and sema has no general dead-branch elimination -- a cloned body with `isinstance(a, Dog)` on `a: Dog` still type-checks its dead branch. Per-stub return checks become ordinary sema checks, and partial-union and non-union stubs (the design doc's future extensions) come free. Estimate: ~1,250 lines deleted, 300-400 added. **Prerequisites** -- `@overload` inherits the `@dispatch` path's open defects: BUGS.md#dispatch-generator-pair-sema-crash (`itertools.repeat` is an `@overload` generator), BUGS.md#literal-dispatch-overload-unmangled-definition, BUGS.md#dispatch-method-params-never-const-inferred. **Open design points:** stub vs implementation type-param names, which decorators come from the stub (the const contract) and which from the implementation (`@error_return`), short stubs and default values (BUGS.md#overload-stub-default-ignored), diagnostics naming the stub being specialized, and sema cost growing from once to once per stub. `docs/OVERLOAD_DESIGN.md` still describes an older design (`overload_param_types`, return validation in codegen) and is rewritten with this unit. Goes through `/tpy-add-feature`; the churn across the 75 `@overload` cases is unmeasured. Dead leftovers the unit deletes: `ctx.overload_missing_param_locals` is written (`codegen_cpp/functions.py`) and never read, and `overload_param_types` / `literal_overload_facts` are read only by old `emit_prims` helpers.
- **[design][MIR] `str` / `bytes` views: MIR precision over the one view rule.** The rule itself is decided and built (branch `str-bytes-view-rule`, 2026-10-01; `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` String Type Semantics): an inferred `str` / `bytes` local is a VIEW only when every source is static storage, a parameter, or a slice / view-returning method / tuple element over a `str`, `bytes` or tuple NAME the function binds (rebind-tracked in every spelling); a field read, a container element, a copy out of a loop variable and an rvalue tuple's element (moved out) are OWNED, for both families alike; `StrView` / `BytesView` is the explicit opt-in to borrow the rest. It is an allow-list a loan analysis can only WIDEN with a proof, never a logic change: MIR's view-local slice relaxes an owned copy back to a view where a loan shows the one-hop source (`y = h.s`, `y = names[i]`, `d["k"]`) is not written while the view lives, through every path the body cannot see today (a `*args` pack, a closure writing the record, a callee writing a global, a second alias of the same element -- `BUGS.md#field-view-escape-needs-place`), and gives an explicit view local the loan it has none of (`BUGS.md#explicit-view-local-source-mutation-unguarded`). Acceptance for that slice: every section of `tests/cases/str/view_rule_sources` keeps CPython's output and the one-hop sections turn back into views. Design record for it: corpus measurement on 02ab5f8c89 -- view locals from a literal 372, a call 232, a tuple element 131 (124 off a call holder), loop variables 104, a container element 73 (49 cases), a name 23, a field 5 (4 cases); stdlib 10 field / 5 element / 15 tuple. Codex (2026-10-01) chose the allow-list over keeping the inference and named the holes the branch closed: a loop variable must never lend to an inferred view (not only `k = n` but `n[:]`, `n.strip()`, `p[0]`), every rebind spelling of a lent name must demote (walrus and a rebound PARAMETER were silent dangles), holders move only when disposable, demotion paths go by ablation. The parity check found the rule unobservable on an immutable value (copy vs view) and asked whether `String` / `bytearray` names may lend; measured 2026-10-01: they do, a subscript store, a writing method, `+=`, a write through a name bound from it, or the name passed to ANY call, anywhere in the function, owning the view at the bind (order-free, from the pre-scan), so a `bytearray` slice stays CPython's copy wherever the name is written. Accepted costs of the order-free rule, for MIR to refine: `s = a; s = b; v = s[0:]` owns although the rebind precedes the bind, and a `String` / `bytearray` passed to any call (`print(st)` included) owns every view over it, the pre-scan knowing no signatures. One asymmetry to widen with the same slice: a bare-name alias of an annotated `str`, `String`, `bytearray` or tuple local copies (`z = s`) while a slice of it views (`w = s[0:]`) -- the lending clause covers a slice, an element and a view-returning call over such a name, but no bare-name alias of it (`_name_lends_view` for a bare name, `name_lends_buffer` for a root, `tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`); one lending predicate for both is the shape. When MIR relaxes a copy to a view, the predictability question returns as a POLICY choice (the user, 2026-09-28: it is hard to judge from the source when a local views and when it owns; options then: an opt-in allocation diagnostic, an error inside `@noalloc`, or keep the relaxation off by default) -- decide it with that slice, not before. `::tpy::Bytes` has no small-buffer storage, so a `bytes` element copied into a local always allocates where a short `std::string` does not; see the `Bytes` small-buffer entry below. The lowering half landed on the same branch: every audited THIR admission site that keyed on the owned-`str` slot alone keys on the view family (`_owned_viewfam_elem`), a `bytes` literal at an operator or record-dunder parameter slot renders the static span, `list[bytes]` element `+=` compiles and `set[bytes]` has its method surface (`tests/cases/bytes/str_bytes_lowering_symmetry`, one section per site).
- **[design][runtime] `Bytes` with small-buffer storage.** `::tpy::Bytes` is a `std::vector<uint8_t>` subclass, so every owned `bytes` value heap-allocates, where a `std::string` keeps up to 15 bytes inline. Under the one view rule a `bytes` local bound from a field or a container element is an owned copy, so short byte strings (protocol tags, delimiters, keys) pay an allocation a `str` twin does not. Candidate: a small-buffer `Bytes` (inline capacity about 16-22 bytes, heap beyond) keeping the `std::vector` surface the runtime and the generated code use (`data()`, `size()`, iterators, `push_back`, the `BytesView` conversion). Measure first: an element-read loop over `list[bytes]` with short vs long elements, against `list[str]`. Raised by the user 2026-10-01 at the view-rule design; not part of that branch.
- **[sema][small] One lending predicate for a bare name and a root.** `_name_lends_view` (a bare-name source, `z = s`) and `name_lends_buffer` (the root of a slice / element / method view, `w = s[0:]`) are two spellings of "a name that lends" in `tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py` and disagree for an annotated `str`, a `String`, a `bytearray` or a tuple local: `z = s` copies while `w = s[0:]` views. Debt of the view-rule branch (2026-10-01), not a MIR question: one predicate with a bare flag, the alias-edge path kept for pending names. Pinned shapes to add when done: the four locals above at both spellings.
- **[sema][small] The declaration block of a name is a pre-scan fact.** `decl_block_depth` is set at the declaration site and moved OUTWARD by `record_branch_decls` when a hoist declares the name in front of an enclosing statement, so a view checked against it before the move read a depth the hoist later changes; `own_hoisted_view` (the `block_new` sets at the hoist) is kept beside `_root_dies_before_view` only for that case, in lockstep, and `declare_local`'s docstring names three writers. A name's C++ declaration block is the innermost block holding all its bindings and uses, which the pre-scan can compute once; with it `_root_dies_before_view` is the only block rule, `own_hoisted_view` goes, and the accepted cost "a root hoisted after the block still owns a view bound to it inside the block" goes with it. Debt of the view-rule branch, 2026-10-01.
- **[sema][small] Pre-scan write views: the leftovers.** DECIDED 2026-10-05: no further sema precision in this area -- every open precision item is a reach fact (what a callee writes through pointers, callbacks and globals; which parameters alias at a call site; whether a builtin can run a closure), and those are MIR's places and effect summaries ("Narrowing proofs over MIR places" below, with the matrix as its acceptance set); the sema rule stays the conservative syntactic one, documented. Of the items below, (b), (f), (g), (h) and (i) RETIRE with MIR narrowing and are not units to build; (c) and (k) move to the MIR entry; (e) is deferred behind the view rule's MIR relaxation; (a), (d), (j) and (l) stay as notes. The one statement walk landed (`prescan.StmtSummary` / `BlockSummary`, table `SemanticContext.write_summaries`; `collect_fact_kills`, `loop_bindings_of` / `block_writes` and `collect_in_place_writes` are views that read the statements' current expressions at ask time) with the kill-set fixes (handler and capture names, the `FactKills.calls` bit, `prescan.closure_exports`). Left open, each a measured change: (a) the may-hold relation still folds a nested def's body into the enclosing namespace (`_in_place_writes` walks the closure unscoped) while the fact kills use the scoped exports; the view rule reads the unscoped one through `InPlaceWrites.writes_through`, so a closure-local alias shadowing an outer name still demotes the outer view -- switch it to the exports and measure the view sections of `tests/cases/str/view_rule_sources`. (b) `FactKills.paths` carries the store statements and `NarrowingTracker.stores_keep` re-derives the non-None verdict from cached expression types at every meet, where recording it at the store in a per-function `IdentityMap` would decide it once; the second representation of the same verdict is `FunctionTrackingState.closure_mutated_paths`, which holds a verdict type per exported path; and the def site feeds the enclosing function THREE records of what a nested def writes (`closure_written_names`, the `nested_mutation_marks` replay that fires at the definition, and `closure_mutated_paths` / `_receivers` that fire at later calls) -- the generic home is one memoized closure-effect record per nested def (its nonlocal names, its paths with their verdict, its receivers), read by the def site, the call-site kill and the meet alike, which also absorbs (i) (decided at the def site by `stores_keep`) beside the meet's store lists -- one store-keyed `IdentityMap` verdict would serve both. (c) The events that may run a closure are explicit and hidden calls (`TpyCall`, `TpyMethodCall`, the `dunder_call` / `property_setter_call` / `dyn_*` fields) on the live path and at the meets alike; an implicit dunder (`with` entry, `for` iteration, an operator) is not counted on either. (d) The call NODE in the loop payload could let a reader consult the callee's signature instead of owning every view of a `bytearray` passed to `print` (deferred: view verdicts are read mid-body, so a signature read must not make them order-dependent). (e) Then ablate the event-site view demotions `root_reseated_in_body` left in place (the `mark_all_view_borrowers_mutated` callers in `tpyc/sema/statements.py`, `calls.py`, `receiver_calls.py`, `context.py`, `expressions.py`), each with a coverage argument (the one view rule or the pre-scan fact), not only a green suite -- its own branch, deferred: "`str` / `bytes` views: MIR precision over the one view rule" subsumes most of these sites. (f) `NarrowingTracker._invalidate_closure_writes` (the call-site kill of closure-exported writes) is a third copy of the fact-kill sweep, and `_strip_call_unstable` a fourth: its `reached_in` re-assembles the receiver / path sweep over a condition's fact snapshot (the `keeps` filter itself goes through `narrowing_kills`, whose `facts` parameter types a snapshot) and its `len_stable` re-implements the len-derived range kill: fold both into "One fact-kill helper". `_strip_call_unstable` also applies the store verdict only to a typed fact dict (a pointer null-fact set passes `keeps=None`): a semantic variant of the rule, not only a copy, so the unification decides it as behaviour. (g) `prescan._closure_scope` / `_names_read` is a fourth free-name analysis beside `liveness._free_names_approx`, `sema/expressions._nested_def_free_names` and `parse/nodes.read_names`: one shared syntactic helper. (h) Each view keeps its own store enumerator and runs-code walker, and they decide "may run a closure" differently: `FactKills.calls` counts `TpyCall` / `TpyMethodCall` nodes, the loop payload's `_CALL_LIKE` adds `TpyBinOp` / `TpyUnaryOp` / `TpyAwait`. (i) `_closure_exports` is rebuilt at the def site and at every meet over a block holding the def: memoize it per def. (j) `BlockSummary.matches` checks only the outer list, so a statement sema appends to a nested def's body (a trailing `return`) after its parent was summarized leaves the closure's summary stale -- harmless today, since the appended statements write nothing. (k) A call whose callee is an unshadowed builtin (`print`, `len`) cannot run a closure, yet it counts as one on the live path and sets `FactKills.calls` at the meets, so a narrowed non-arithmetic Optional read after `print(...)` in a loop is rejected when a closure that rebinds or writes it was defined before the loop (matrix row `meet_closure_before_loop_record`); exempting such calls on BOTH paths needs the callee's effect summary (probe shapes `/tmp/agents/meta-wc/c3.py`, `/tmp/agents/cpar-wc/p3.py`) -- MIR's, not a sema rule. The same fact owns the receiver face: a closure's method receivers are exported syntactically, so a closure calling a method that writes nothing (`@readonly`, or inferred read-only) still kills the facts beneath its receiver at every later call (matrix rows `meet_closure_readonly_receiver_compiles`, `meet_closure_readonly_inferred`, accepted REJECT). `@readonly` is not the answer -- it stops writes through `self` only, and a readonly method may store None into a global a `Ptr` field of the receiver points at -- so the precise answer is the callee's effect over the places reachable from the operand, which only MIR's summaries give (and it must apply to a direct call, which kills beneath its receiver the same way, and to the export alike); routed to "Narrowing proofs over MIR places", whose acceptance set carries the three rows. The acceptance instrument for any of these is `scripts/alias_kill_matrix/` (its README names the three gates). Debt of the view-rule branch, 2026-10-01; collector and fixes landed 2026-10-04. (l) The matrix's third gate is sized by shape only: its meet and closure rows carry `int` facts, which only gain a runtime check, so the two rejections review round 1 found were invisible to it; add a fact-kind axis to those rows (int range, `int | None`, a record-typed Optional, a `Ptr` non-null, a field path vs a bare name) before calling the instrument complete.
- **[sema][small] One fact-kill helper.** RETIRES with MIR narrowing (decided 2026-10-05): not a unit to build; the record below says what the copies are so the MIR cut-over removes them all. `InitTracker._kill_written` (the meet sweep, `tpyc/sema/init_tracker.py`) and `NarrowingTracker._kill_written` (the live path, `tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`) are two copies over the same `InPlaceWrites.affected_facts`; the narrowing part they share is `NarrowingTracker.narrowing_kills`, and the rest (ptr non-null and range kills, and the `is_copy` / `keeps` arguments threaded into both by hand) is duplicated. They disagree in four places: deref-view keys (the live path filters them out, the sweep kills them: `BUGS.md#deref-view-survives-receiver-call`), len-derived ranges (the sweep matches `hi_len_of` against the written key's ROOT, the live `_invalidate_len_ranges` against the full key), name rebinds (the sweep kills only the spelled name, the live path kills across spellings), and a store that keeps the slot non-None (the live `invalidate_for_field_write` weakens a stronger fact at the written key to the non-None type, the sweep drops it). The sound union is a behaviour change -- a readonly method call through a narrowed box would start killing its deref-view fact -- so it is a `/tpy-fix-bug` unit, not a cleanup. The bare-bind over-kill the alias case pins (`none_safety/alias_store_kills_narrowing`, `plain_bind`) is what the live path already does, so a union keeps it; only adopting the sweep's narrower rebind rule would flip it. That bare-bind kill (`t = a` with no store kills `a`'s field facts) is the same question as the name-rebind divergence and is decided inside this unit, not separately. Two more copies joined them with the closure-export kills: `NarrowingTracker._invalidate_closure_writes` and `_strip_call_unstable` (its `reached_in` receiver / path sweep over a condition's fact snapshot and its `len_stable` range kill; "Pre-scan write views: the leftovers" (f)). Found by the review of the may-hold relation, 2026-10-02.
- **[mir][design] Narrowing proofs over MIR places.** Sema's may-hold relation (`InPlaceWrites`, `tpyc/prescan.py`) covers aliases of inline storage only: exact places, a walk related to its start, a pointer hop tracked by its spelling. The MIR analysis must supply an unknown-object or per-type summary for pointer hops, mutating-call reach by type, origins for borrow-producing expressions (call and `@property` results, `with` targets, subscripts, iteration variables), callee effects beyond the operands (globals, captured objects, generator frames) and the implicit calls at a store (a destroyed value's `__del__`, a copy hook, a property setter, a user `__iadd__`), on MIR's place model, which already has deref, container-element and payload projections and seeds external origins as possibly aliasing. Three constraints learned on the may-hold branch (2026-10-02, the matrix at `scripts/alias_kill_matrix/RESULTS.md`) that the design must satisfy: (1) a killed narrowing of a non-arithmetic Optional is a compile error, so any kill rule coarser than type reach rejects valid pointer-walking code (`out.append(node.name)` then `node.name.upper()`); (2) a single pass does not know loop-body types at loop entry, so a rule that needs them is either unsound across the back edge or noisy on everyday loops; (3) classifying a hop by field name collides with stdlib pointer fields named `value`, `state`, `code`. Acceptance set: `BUGS.md#pointer-structure-aliases-unmodelled`, `BUGS.md#may-hold-relation-unmodelled-shapes`, `BUGS.md#borrowed-origin-not-related-to-source`, `BUGS.md#subscript-element-not-keyed`, `BUGS.md#mutating-call-walk-keeps-linked-local-fact`, `BUGS.md#ptr-or-tuple-argument-skips-fact-kill`, `BUGS.md#field-store-destructor-skips-fact-kill`, `BUGS.md#iadd-target-keeps-facts-beneath`, `BUGS.md#property-setter-sibling-write-invisible-to-loop-kill-set`, `BUGS.md#alias-store-rewrites-borrowed-optional-slot`, `BUGS.md#bytearray-param-slice-view-written-through-sibling`, `BUGS.md#field-loan-whole-record-callee-unchecked` (the payload face), `BUGS.md#field-store-keeps-borrower-len-range` (the loan behind the range); and the matrix rows accepted REJECT or UNCHECKED under the sema rule (`scripts/alias_kill_matrix/RESULTS.md`): `meet_closure_before_loop_record` (a builtin callee cannot run a closure), `meet_closure_readonly_receiver_compiles` / `meet_closure_readonly_inferred` (a callee's effect over the places reachable from its receiver), `meet_two_params_distinct_str` with `unm_two_params` (parameter aliasing is a call-site origin), `BUGS.md#lazy-iterator-runs-closure-uncounted` (an implicit `__next__` running a stored callable). Decided 2026-10-05: sema keeps its conservative syntactic kill rule; every precision item of "Pre-scan write views: the leftovers" lands here.
- **[thir] THE CUTOVER ORDER, decided 2026-09-02: flip, delete, fix as we go.** Six steps, each its own change on one branch, in `docs/THIR_CUTOVER_REVIEW.md` Phase 0 "Verdict": (1) fix the two lowering crashes on valid code (DONE: the non-name method-receiver classifier fall-through and the copy() pending-list-type spelling); (2) Gate D4 commit 1 -- flip `thir_codegen` to the default, regenerate, prove `git diff tests/cases` EMPTY (DONE: `e5e9274af`; regeneration left tests/cases and tests/interop byte-identical, and the flip's audit baselines are in `docs/THIR_COMPLETION_LEDGER.md`); (3) `--thir-strict`: a body-boundary reject raises a `CodeGenError` with source line + reject tag, default off, wording pinned now (DONE: raised as `ThirRejectError`, a `CodeGenError` subclass, so a harness comparing both paths' verdicts does not read it as a disagreement; message, location and fold positions pinned in `tpyc/thir/test_thir_strict.py`; the `error_*` case is deferred to the deletion unit, since while the fallback still exists such a case needs the option and its wording changes when the option goes away); (4) one `dualgen.py` run at all three widths (DONE: three populations, ~5,300 programs, run on the flip's parent tree `1be2cf003`; 4 new divergences found, 2 since fixed on the branch, 2 filed in BUGS.md, tables in the ledger); (5) commit 2 -- delete per the ledger's Gate D4 sections D/E, strict becomes the only path (DONE 2026-09-03: the four AST body emitters, both audits, the two committed gates, the conftest oracle pass / ratchet / dial / markers / seven `--thir-*` options, the error-path gate, the interop overlay, the reject tally, `CodeGenOptions.thir_codegen`/`thir_strict` and the migration tooling are gone; `fallback.py` survives as the trimmed `reject.py`, `shape.py` and `faces.py` stay, `review/` stays as the queue -- see the ledger's closing entry); (6) fix rejects as they surface -- **THE LIVE STEP**. **The fix queue for (6) is the BREAKS rows of `scripts/thir_migration/review/bins_*.json` (402 sites, each with a reproducer under `probes/<slice>/`) and the `BREAKS_AT_CUTOVER` entries of `program_verdicts.json` (478 programs)** -- the nine witnesses in the blind-class entry below are a subset of it. The everyday shapes to take first are listed under "What the sites are" in the report; re-measure with `scripts/thir_migration/review/reprobe.py` before each batch (2026-09-03: 388 of 402 still reject; truthiness and the literal-valued `print` kwargs are closed, `**kw` and a computed `sep=` still reject at `print.kwargs`; batch 1 then closed ten shapes, batch 2, 2026-09-04, another 57 rows across every lowering file, and batch 3, same day, switched the unit of work to NAMED PROGRAMS -- `examples/**` plus the `tpy-examples` repo, re-probed front-end-only, the way `reprobe.py` probes the bins -- and made eight of the nine failing programs compile (ant, adatron, async_demo, oliva2 run CPython-identical; sieve after an example fix; curl, path_tracing, tcp_server build; doom compiles with no source workaround and renders the CPython-identical frame since 2026-09-11); named programs that fail rank above tag counts from now on -- the queue markdown tables under the scratchpad recorded each implementer's next row: comprehensions rows 15/16/22 are blocked on other files, resumable row 20, statements row 26, expressions row 33; batch 7, 2026-09-21, re-measured the whole queue at its tip -- 251 of the 402 rows and 385 of the 478 programs still reject -- and added a second committed instrument, `scripts/thir_migration/review/arg_family_sweep.py`, which measures 734 argument rows x 8 callee families and records that only 286 rows are admitted by every family, 213 rows split the families and 235 are admitted by none; 13 of the 17 new `match.*` reject details that batch introduced are pinned by no committed case). Two rows found while fixing step 1 and not in the bins, now tracked in BUGS.md: `copy()` of a str loop variable (the bare binding CLOSED 2026-09-03 -- `_lower_copy_special` resolves pending views like containers; the `out.append(copy(s))` spelling is `copy-str-view-result-into-owned-arg`) or of an int literal (`copy-int-literal-result`), and `copy()` of an Array-resolved literal (`copy-array-literal-into-list-slot`, a sema resolution-sink question). Two more found while lowering the pascal runtime's last bodies: a base-init argument BUILT from the ctor's params (`super().__init__("tag" + str(n))`, reject `ctor.base_init` -- the AST renders base-init args target-less, where its literal-fold rules differ from a threaded slot's, so no bare-render row claims a str concat; the plain concat spelling has since been closed and is pinned by the cases converted from the unit suite, the format-spec spelling `f"tag{n:04d}"` still rejects), and the OPERATOR spelling of a user dunder whose operand is a str (`t == s` with `__eq__(self, other: str)`, reject `binop.shape.==.record`; CLOSED 2026-09-03 for `==`, derived `!=`, `<` and the reflected `s == t`, case `tests/cases/operators/dunder_str_operand`). **Two more found by the post-deletion BUGS/docs pass, both everyday spellings:** a plain `list` local passed to a `list[int32] | None` PARAMETER (reject `call.arg_shape.optional`, reported at whichever position consumes the call -- `stmt.expr_stmt` in the witness; measured 2026-09-03: only the UN-mutated literal-seeded local rejects, because it resolves to `Array` and the AST render failed the C++ build too -- it is the sema sink question under `copy-array-literal-into-list-slot`; annotated or mutated lists route), and a METHOD CALL on an `Own[static protocol]` binding (`expr.method_call:method.protocol.emit`), which rejects although that binding is a `T&&` reached with `.`, not a `unique_ptr`; the `Own[P]` PARAM into a resumable frame was lowered separately and does not reach this. Repros `/tmp/agents/bugs2/p2/i_list_to_optparam.py` and `/tmp/agents/bugs2/p2/l_own_proto_method.py`.
- **[codegen] Emit user dunders as named members; make the C++ operator a forwarder.** Today sema stamps every user dunder with a `cpp_template` (`({self}) + ({0})` for `__add__`) and the record emits the C++ operator itself, so there is no member named `__add__`: the operator form `a + b` and the explicit call `a.__add__(b)` are the same C++ expression, and the explicit call needs its own lowering row (the `record_template` arm and its argument ladder) that admits fewer argument shapes than the operator does -- the two spellings of one method can disagree, which the cutover review found. If the record emitted `__add__` as an ordinary member and `operator+` as a one-line forwarder, an explicit dunder call would be a plain method call with no special ladder and the disagreement could not exist. A design change, not a lowering arm: it touches the record emitter's dunder convention and churns the snapshot of every record that defines a dunder, so it lands as its own change after the cutover. (The operator-spelling queue row it used to be coupled to closed on 2026-09-03 through a THIR operand row, so this item is now purely the convention change.) One batch-1 review follow-up belongs with it: sema should RECORD the resolved dunder and its argument check on the node for every operator spelling (`_validate_comparison` today only confirms the dunder exists, which is why the derived `!=` and reflected `==` had to be re-derived in `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py` and why a mismatched operand was admitted -- `BUGS.md#derived-ne-unchecked-operand`).
- **[thir] Fold `THIRMatchArmEntry.pre_bindings` into a single `bindings` tuple.** The node carries two channels for one concept (the arm's whole-subject binding and the `case x as y` pre-binding); today the seven binding-only emit sites are all on tiers that reject `case x as y` and go through the both-iterating helper `_emit_match_whole_bindings` as an interim, but the guarded multi-entry dedupe in `tpyc/thir/emit.py` still iterates both channels inline, so there is no single choke point. A node-shape change: present before implementing.
- **[thir] View-family mixed-operand cast direction.** `_view_at_runtime` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) answers a REASSIGNED `str`/`bytes` param "view" although the prologue declares an owned local under its name, because the select's mixed-operand cast goes toward the OWNED spelling: an arm that answered "owned" for bytes was tried on 2026-09-03 and made a rebound param against a literal a same-spelling pair whose `std::span` result dangled over the `bytes_literal_owned` temporary (ASan use-after-free, no diagnostic), so it was reverted and that spelling rejects. The cast should choose its direction from the sink's form (view sink: convert the owned side to the view over a live lvalue, reject a prvalue; owned sink: materialize), after which the `valuesel.bytes_mixed` reject (`BUGS.md#bytes-select-mixed-runtime-spelling`) falls away.
- **[thir] Batch-3 review follow-ups, filed rather than done in the round.** (i) CLOSED 2026-09-05 by the method-arg sink union: the gate that excluded `Own`/`readonly` slots (`_comp_container_method_arg`) is gone, and the shared `container_comp` cell now guards on the slot's const-borrow verdict alone, which is what its render was already keyed on (a `readonly` container slot is admitted deliberately, cased as `calls/method_arg_shared_rows`; an `Own` slot is not a container slot to `_container_comp_arg` at all). (ii) `_cont_ptr_local` (`statements.py`) re-inlines the Own-peel + list/dict/set test that `_owned_container_slot` provides, and a third copy in the `container_ok` return arm also admits `bytearray` -- decide once whether `bytearray` is an owned-container slot everywhere. (iii) `_range_step_kind` decides "variable" and the for-range route re-inspects the AST to pick the face -- return the distinguished kind (a node-level fact; present before changing the node). (iv) `_r_record_field_ref` (`checks.py`) does not pass `req.narrowed` while its sibling `_r_record_field_marker` does; measured 2026-09-04: every narrowed `__deref__`-wrapper spelling that reaches the laxer admission rejects downstream in the field lowering (`field.result_type` / `field.receiver_shape`), so no wrong render is witnessable today -- pass it when a case can show a difference. (v) The BigInt variable-step `for` re-evaluates `__step_N > 0` (a BigInt compare) every iteration; hoist to a `bool` before the loop (`tpyc/thir/emit.py` for-range emit).
- **[thir] The container RECEIVER family is still a membership list, not the pure reference axis.** `_builtin_container_type` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) is `_f1_container_ref` plus the value-form `Span`/`varargs` plus the bytes-family leg `_bytes_family_ref`. The pure-axis formula was implemented and reverted: dropping the element/key gates also admits `set[bytes]`, and `sb.discard(b"x")` then turned a loud `method.set.discard` reject into ill-formed C++ (`std::span<const uint8_t>` against `erase(const std::vector<uint8_t>&)`). **That blocker is closed for BOTH spellings since 2026-09-06**, in the RUNTIME rather than in a compiler row: `ordered_set::erase` / `contains` and `set_remove` take the lookup key by view, so the span a `bytes` PARAM and the span a `bytes` LITERAL (`::tpy::bytes_literal`) both render binds and compares without building an element. Measured directly against the runtime headers (a probe over `contains` / `erase` / `set_remove` on `ordered_set<std::vector<uint8_t>>`, empty key included, all of which the branch base rejects) -- the compiler side is untested because the receiver still rejects, which is exactly what this entry is about. The fold still owns re-running its own gates for the other families dropping the element/key gates would admit; do not change the membership here. Measured in the consolidation's stage 4.

- **[thir] The finally-deferred return: move its facts off the parse node and make the scalar the one-part case of the tuple recipe.** `TpyReturn.finally_deferred_capture` / `finally_deferred_leaves` are sema->lowering facts parked on a parse node (CLAUDE.md: a new fact belongs on a THIR node or the lowering context), and the scalar recipe (`_finally_deferred_recipe`) and the tuple one (`_finally_deferred_tuple_recipe`) are two tables for one question -- the scalar is the tuple recipe with one CAPTURE part. `return t`'s eligibility compares `lc.render_type` strings of the local and the return; it should be a type equality. Surfaced by the U1 batch-3 review.
- **[sema] `_is_owned_var`'s top-level branch calls an owning tuple global auto-movable.** `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`'s `_is_owned_var` answers `is_value_type()` at module level, which a tuple always satisfies, so `is_auto_move_use(t)` says an owning tuple global `t` may be moved from at its module-level last use -- but a function body may read it after init, which module-level last-use cannot see. The tuple unpack papers over it with a `not is_top_level` term in `source_consumed` (`_analyze_tuple_unpack`); the honest home is the predicate (a tuple global with reference elements is static storage, never auto-movable), which would let the unpack drop its special case. The rebind refusal that guards the module-level alias (`ctx.tuple_globals_aliased`, filled at the unpack and read at the rebind) is a statement-ORDER property, so a rebind textually before the unpack but reached again through a module-level loop would escape it -- no live shape today (each rejects elsewhere), but recording the alias on the binding, or checking at module end, would hold it by the rule rather than by neighbouring rejects. Related placement: `global_rebind_message` sits in `sema/statements.py` and is imported inside a function from `expressions.py`; it belongs beside `global_binds_by_reference` in `typesys.py`. Surfaced by the U1 readiness gate's second opinion.
- **[thir] The tuple-unpack lowering re-derives the move verdict sema already decided.** Sema tags an `Own` element target owned only when the unpack consumes its source (`is_auto_move_use`), and the sync name arm (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`, the `any(b == "move")` branch) then asks `_is_move_source` again and REJECTS on disagreement (`tuple_unpack.owned_source_not_movable`) rather than consuming `stmt.is_owned`. No disagreeing shape is reachable today (two review probes), but it is the two-phase mirror the U5 elementwise-form fact removes: the arm should read the node's verdict and the reject go. Same family: `_borrow_tuple_arg` compares source and slot through `collapse_tuple_own_elements` where `_own_stripped_tuple_eq` (`predicates.py`) already owns that comparison and does not rebuild a type per call; and `_tuple_global_binding_type` (`sema/statements.py`) spells its own `is_lvalue`-based freshness loop beside the element classifiers `sema/compatibility.py` owns -- both belong on the shared helpers. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the U1 unpack fix.
- **[sema][thir] The tuple-element `Own` copy: one fact at the binding, one lowering helper.** Debt the warn-tier flip (2026-09-23) created, not inherited: (a) the per-element hazard of a tuple NAME comes from construction facts for a literal- or call-bound local (`_derive_copy_into_own_hazards`), and, at a RETURN only, from the declared elements of a parameter or loop variable computed in the consumer (`check_name_borrow_into_own`) -- a module global gets neither (`BUGS.md#global-tuple-name-own-return-unwarned`); at an argument a parameter warns whole-tuple through the coercion path instead, and a name with construction facts can warn TWICE at one argument (a tuple-unpack-bound name; a mixed call-bound local not at its last use warns three times), all pinned in snapshots. Seed `BindingProvenance` at the binding (parameter entry, loop header) so both slots read one fact and warn once, alike. (b) The MIXED verdict (`record_name_copy` -> `own_element_mixed`) is sema's reading of the binding's DECLARED type, while the lowering decides the actual C++ form (`storage_tuple_locals`, `pointers`). Wrongly judging a name mixed is loud (it rejects); wrongly judging it all-borrow would be SILENT -- the whole-tuple copy would take an undeclared by-value element along. No case errs that way today (an `Own` element, a nested tuple holding references and a non-pointer-repr element all read as mixed), but the verdict belongs to the binding's form fact; a nested tuple PARAMETER, which arrives with pointer members, is judged mixed and rejects where a nested lift could serve it. (c) Three lowering sites repeat "is this member a declared copy, of the slot's own type, then render it as `copy(...)`" (`_lower_borrow_tuple_literal`'s consuming path, the Own-element tuple-literal argument arm, the owned-storage tuple return); sema could record the copy's payload (an `IdentityMap`) so the lowering stops re-deriving it with `own_element_copy_type`, and one helper own the render. The name lifts share one admission test (`declared_name_copy`) but still build their `tuple_to_storage` render at four sites. In sema, `_warn_name_element_copy` repeats `_check_own_borrowed_source`'s tail (value-type-param skip, non-copyable error, deferral, warning, declaration) with small drifts, and the literal tail records the copy before the `T: ValueType` skip, so an instantiation whose deferred verdict is "no copy" still renders `copy(...)` (harmless -- a value-type copy -- but the fact is broader than the warning); one tail should serve both. (d) Two hidden costs, correct but slower: a whole `Own[tuple]` argument of all-copied members renders `tuple_to_storage_move<S>(tuple_value_to_borrow<B>(std::tuple<P, P>{P(a), P(b)}))` where the explicit `copy()` twin renders the storage literal directly; and a mixed tuple name cannot lift at all yet (`BUGS.md#mixed-call-local-own-arg-copies-owned`), where `tuple_to_storage<S>(std::move(t))` at its last use would serve.
- **[sema][thir] Tuple parameter element places, owned and mixed together.** A tuple parameter with an owned element -- fully owned (`tuple[Own[Box], Own[Box]]`, `std::tuple<Box, Box>&&`) or mixed (`tuple[Own[Box], Box]`, `std::tuple<Box, Box*>&&`) -- takes the ownership transfer, and writes, `mut(p[0])`, the unpack and frames work for both; the element PLACES do not. One unit for both params: (1) a name bound to the element, `o = p[0]` (`decl.slot_type`); (2) a method call on it or through a field of it, `p[0].inc()` / `p[0].xs.pop()`, and `p[0] += q` (`BUGS.md#owned-tuple-param-element-method-rejects`); (3) the element consume `sink(p[0])` (`BUGS.md#owned-tuple-param-element-consume-rejects`), under a conservative rule: consume the element only where `p` is dead afterwards, as `return p[0]` already moves it -- reading another element after a partial consume is U8 (MIR, `docs/TUPLE_COMPLETION_PLAN.md`); (4) the local `q = p`, a silent whole-tuple copy (`BUGS.md#mixed-tuple-param-local-copy-silent`, `BUGS.md#owned-tuple-param-local-copy-silent`); (5) the fully owned param of a generator or async def, refused at `res.param_type:tuple` (`BUGS.md#res-param-tuple-element-shapes`), while the mixed one routes. Umbrella: `BUGS.md#consume-own-element-of-mixed-tuple`; pins `tests/cases/tuple/error_mixed_own_param_element_*`.

- **[thir] NEXT UNIT, first in line (decided 2026-09-26): fold the target-less base-init arg rows into the ctor-call arg dispatch.** A fresh reference-type base-init argument is rejected; the workarounds are forwarding a parameter of the child's `__init__` by name, or skipping the call (a warned divergence) (BUGS.md#base-init-args-separate-lowering). A `super().__init__(...)` / `Parent.__init__(self, ...)` argument lowers only through `_base_init_arg_ok`'s own target-less rows (`tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`: scalars, str literals / concats / f-strings / conversions, parameter names by family, a scalar-argument record constructor), which re-enumerate without the parameter in view what the ordinary constructor call (`_lower_ctor_call_args`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) decides per parameter. That leaves every fresh reference-type argument rejected and a named value at an `Own[T]` parameter failing the C++ build (BUGS.md#base-init-args-separate-lowering). One table: the base-init cell runs the ctor-call dispatch, with one fact answering whether the parameter keeps the argument (an `arg_lend_ok`-style verdict, not per-table slot guards) and a place for temporaries at the member-init position. The fold replaces the rows rather than choosing between two tables per argument, which needs a parallel slot predicate per table.
- **[sema] Every declared field without a class-level default must be assigned by `__init__` on every path.** Today the constructor split-point check (`_check_init_field_assignments`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) has two outcomes for a field `__init__` leaves unset before the body: a warning ("... it will be default-constructed in C++ (in CPython, the attribute would not exist)") when `T()` can build the type with no arguments (`_is_default_constructible`), and a type-dependent error ("has no default constructor") otherwise. Replace both with one rule: the field must be assigned on every path through `__init__`, else an error. That needs definite assignment over `if`/`elif`/`else` and `match` (a field every branch assigns is assigned), or BUGS.md#split-warning-on-branch-assigned-field turns from a spurious warning into a false error; a lazily-set field (written later by a method) needs a class-level default. Reach at the time of filing: 10 warnings in 9 corpus cases (`grep -r "is not initialized before the constructor body" tests --include=diag.txt`), each needing an assignment or a default.
- **[typesys/codegen] A record gets a C++ default constructor only when Python `T()` is valid.** Codegen emits `X() = default;` for every record whose fields default-construct, including one whose `__init__` requires arguments (`class Handle: id: int32; def __init__(self, id: int32)` -> `Handle() = default;` beside `explicit Handle(int32_t id)`): an internal constructor building a value Python can never produce. Direction: `cpp_default_init` answers the Python question (`T()` callable with no arguments), such a field must be assigned in the init section (it lands in the member-init list; a one-expression ternary still works), and a record holding one has no default constructor either -- which also makes the two default-constructibility readers (codegen's fact and `_is_default_constructible`) one. Measure first, in a scratch worktree: drop the `= default` for records whose `__init__` requires arguments and list what fails in the suite -- candidates are hoisted temporaries declared before assignment, `std::unordered_map::operator[]`, `std::expected<X, E>` in `@error_return`, `Array[X, N]()`, a union field whose first alternative is `X`, container resize, and a field demoted into the constructor body (BUGS.md#demoted-field-init-runs-default-init).

- **[design][sema][codegen] A value record's copy cost is visible and decides its parameter form.** A `ValueType` record is passed by value today (`Coord step(Coord c);`) whatever its fields, so a record holding `str` / `bytes` / `int` (BigInt) allocates at every call, where the primitives it mirrors pass without a copy (`const ::tpy::BigInt& n`, `std::string_view s`). Direction: follow the primitives' precedent -- a value record whose fields are all cheap to copy passes by value, one with an allocating field passes `const P&` like `BigInt`; the existing `TypeDef.is_expensive_copy` fact (`tpyc/type_def_registry.py`, set for BigInt / str / bytes) extends to records through their fields and the parameter-form code reads it (no value-record special case). Open design question, leaning yes: make the property VISIBLE with a marker protocol (name TBD) that the allocating value types carry (`str`, `bytes`, `String`, `int`) and a `ValueType` must declare exactly when a field carries it (checked at the class definition, error with a hint otherwise) -- the source then shows the C ABI (by value vs `const&`) and "unmarked `ValueType`" becomes a trivially-copyable guarantee (Rust's `Copy` vs `Clone` split). Rejected alternative: forbidding allocating fields in a `ValueType` outright (reach at filing: 0 of 7 stdlib value types, 8 of 106 corpus ones hold `int` / `str`) -- it cuts ordinary Python records (`Token(kind: str, text: str)`) for a codegen concern. Check in the design pass: a `const&` parameter observing a rebind of what it aliases during the call (a module global), as `BigInt` already must; `@noalloc` reporting a bind-time copy (`b = a`) of an allocating value record.

One fact, one site: make `SELECT_SLOT` a row the transient sinks carry, have the receiver build it from `arg_lend_ok(fi, -1)` through `_recv_forms` the way `_lower_call_arg` builds `_lend_forms`, leave it off the coercion row, and drop both patches.
