- **[thir][tooling] Fold the field-write admission cells into `ref_sink_sweep`'s in-process harness.** `scripts/thir_migration/review/field_admission_sweep.py` (1544 cells: ctor member-init, method, generator / async method, local-holder `h.f` and a local control x 16 slot types x 19 source shapes) compiles every cell as its own `tpyc` subprocess, about 7 CPU-minutes, so it stays a manual gate and is not in the regular run. `ref_sink_sweep` already has a `field_write` sink over the same positions but only on a local holder and only for reference kinds: add `self.f` and member-init sinks and the value-type slots (`str`, `bytes`, `StrView`, `Optional[str]`, `Optional[bytes]`, tuple, value union, scalars), answer them from its one-compile-per-program survey, then delete the subprocess sweep and its table. Only then may the cells join the regular run.
- **[thir][perf] A `str`/`bytes` param read inside a RESUMABLE body still reads as a VIEW, so the generic-slot materialize copies an already-owned buffer.** A generator/async frame captures such a param OWNED (`is_owned_in_coro_frame` -> `_CoroParamKind.OWNED_COPY`; the frame field is `std::string k`), but `_str_name_form` / `_bytes_name_form` answer BORROW for any name in `param_names` -- only `Own[str]` params are carved out (`prescan.owned_viewfam_params`). Most sinks do not notice (a decl `s = k` inside the frame renders `s = k;` bare), but the new generic-slot materialize does: `tests/cases/generics/generic_slot_view_form_positions` renders `std::string __tmp_N = std::string(k);` inside both the generator and the coroutine frame, where `= k` would do. Correct, one redundant allocation per call. Fix: seed `owned_viewfam_params` with the viewfam params of a generator/async body so the form predicates read the frame's storage, which is the fact `gen_async` already holds -- a form-fact change, so it moves renders across the corpus and wants its own snapshot pass. Found covering the positions for the view-at-a-generic-slot fix 2026-09-08.
- **[thir] Make `movable` a REQUIRED field on `THIRArgTemp`.** The field is the audited fact `banks_in_region` reads to decide whether a temp goes into a conditional operand's deferred slot, and it DEFAULTS to `None` ("never audited"), so a new row inherits the unaudited verdict by saying nothing -- exactly how eighteen already-spelled rows sat unaudited until the conditional-operand fix's second pass went looking for them. Dropping the default makes every one of the 43 construction sites in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` state the fact, so audit completeness is enforced by construction instead of by a sweep somebody has to remember to run. Ten sites omit it today and would pass `movable=None` explicitly: the eight unspelled rows (:2248, :2260, :2282, :2300, :14122, :14135, :14152, :14170), which cannot bank without a `cpp_type` anyway, and the two DELIBERATELY unaudited spelled rows -- **:14230**, whose `cpp_type` is a protocol-argument spec (sometimes literally `"auto"`), and **:14957**, a `@dynamic` adapter spelling -- neither of which holds a TpyType whose movability can be asked. Renders unchanged; the two unit constructions in `tpyc/thir/test_thir_validate_seams.py` need the argument too.
- **[thir][perf] The comprehension argument temp is spelled where the slot form does not require it, and a conditional operand then pays a `std::optional` slot for it.** A comprehension at a `const std::vector<T>&` slot renders `std::vector<int32_t> __tmp_1 = ({...}); sized("x", __tmp_1);` although a prvalue binds a const reference for the full expression (`argtemp.comprehension`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`); inside a conditional operand it becomes `std::optional<T> __tmp_N;` at statement scope plus an `emplace` after the guard. Two changes: key the row on the SLOT's form -- no temp where the slot is by value or `const T&`, a temp only where it is `T&` or an owning slot; and where a temp is still needed inside a conditional operand, declare it in a statement-expression block within the operand (`({ T __tmp = init; call(__tmp); })`) instead of the optional slot, whenever the call's result cannot borrow from the argument (`call_returns_cpp_ref` decides; a borrow-returning callee keeps the statement-scope slot, since the block-local temp would dangle). The block half also serves the argument temps that legitimately REMAIN -- a reference-typed generic instantiation, a container literal, a generator/coro factory's slot -- so it is the larger of the two. The generic `T`-slot half of this entry is done (the temp verdict `_generic_arg_slot` now carries, 2026-09-08): the verdict is taken at the instantiation, so a value-typed one renders its rvalue inline. Footprint at filing: 3 snapshot files with the plain-position container temp, 6 with a statement-level optional slot. Own analysis under `/tpy-fix-bug`; a render change, not for a fix branch.
- **[thir] A bytes literal's static-span render is decided at four sink sites; one read-only-position verdict would replace them.** A bytes literal lowers to the OWNED render by default and every view-shaped sink retags it (`_retag_bytes_literal_span`): the compare arm, the tuple-literal `in` chain, the `ranges::contains` arm and the `.contains` / user `__contains__` needle site, each with its own one-line reason (the comparison, the lookup and the `bytes` parameter slot all read through `::tpy::BytesView`). The fact they share is the POSITION -- a literal read once and never stored -- and it belongs on the literal's lowering as a form verdict keyed on the sink's use (`_ExprUse`), the way `Form` already rides the node; the four sites then collapse into the default and the `.contains` arm's older "bytes LITERAL at a BYTES-VIEW key target" admission row (now redundant with the unconditional retag there) folds with them. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the BytesView type change, 2026-09-11.
- **[thir] A bytes NAME needle at a `BytesView`-keyed container still rejects; the str twin lowers.** `k in s` with `k: bytes` and `s: set[BytesView]` / `dict[BytesView, V]` is kept out of the `.contains` arm by the `view_key_target(ct) is None` leg of the bytes-needle row, where a str name needle at `set[StrView]` renders bare (`binop.contains_view_key`). Since `::tpy::BytesView` carries the family's `==` and `std::hash`, the lookup would read the name by implicit conversion with no allocation, so the leg can go once a case pins it (`tests/cases/bytes/bytesview_dict_key` is the receiver-side sibling). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective of the BytesView type change, 2026-09-11.
- **[cpy-stub] `Deref`'s stub reads a wrapper's ANNOTATED field as the payload's.** `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py`'s `Deref.__setattr__` keeps a name on the wrapper only when it is underscore-prefixed or in the class `__dict__`; a field declared by annotation alone (`target: Point` then `self.target = target` in `__init__`) is routed to `self.__deref__()`, which reads the same field back through `__getattr__` -- a `RecursionError` under CPython for a wrapper the compiler accepts (the wrapper's own members win there). Cases work around it with an underscore-prefixed payload (`_inner`, `_target`). Fix: count `__annotations__` along the MRO as declared names; refreshes the `cpy_stubs` fingerprint.
- **[design] Rethink `Own[T]` at `str`/`bytes`: the explicit `Own[str]` spelling is not worth having, the generic `Own[T]` instantiated at `str` is.** Today a plain `str` parameter is `std::string_view` (a borrow) and `Own[str]` is `std::string` by value (the owned buffer), so `Own[str]` is the one spelling that lets a caller MOVE an owned string into a sink instead of copying it at the store. As a user-facing spelling it is obscure: nobody writes it, and a sink that stores a str copies once at the store either way. Where the owned form genuinely matters is a GENERIC slot -- `def push(self, v: Own[T])` on a container record instantiated at `str` must take the owned buffer, and today the instantiation's parameter form is decided on the open `T` (the same family as the view-at-a-generic-slot gap, which is closed at the CALL site by materializing an owned temp rather than in the signature -- see the param-form-as-template-argument entry below). Decide one rule for the value types that own a buffer: (a) `Own[str]` stays the owned-buffer form, documented as the exception, and generic instantiation at `str` derives it from the slot's `Own`-ness; or (b) `Own[str]` collapses to `str` (the view) like the scalars and the owned form is reached only through generic instantiation and the store-site materialization, with the move-at-last-use elision (`BUGS.md#own-str-slot-temp-copies-owned-source`) done at the store instead of the parameter. Either way the parameter form must be one channel read at instantiation. Raised by the user reviewing `str/own_str_arg_temp_in_while_condition` 2026-09-07.
- **[runtime] The static_assert pin blocks compile in every generated TU; they belong in a self-check TU.** `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/union_type.hpp` carries `union_pins`, `union_borrow_pins`, `union_buffer_pins` and `union_record_pins`, `variant_ref.hpp` carries `variant_ref_pins`, and `buffer_types.hpp` its sibling non-conversion and constructor asserts: 101 `static_assert` lines across the headers, five named pin structs of 121 lines, and nothing in the runtime or in generated code references any of them. A pin whose only job is to prove an invariant (layout parity, convertibility, a constexpr round trip, leaf well-formedness over packs no program uses) is a test, and the repo has the place for tests of that kind: a standalone TU under `runtime/cpp/tests/` registered in `tests/test_runtime_cpp.py`'s `_SELFCHECKS`, compiled and run once per toolchain. Move the pin structs and the pin-only asserts there; a header keeps only an assert that guards a definition at its point of use inside a template body. While there, add the missing `is_value_type<Union<Ts...>>` row -- true for a pack of value alternatives, false for a borrow pack and for a mixed one -- so a value union at a `param_val_or_ref_t<T>` slot would take the twin's `const Union&` form rather than a mutable reference if a generic at a union ever lowers (today every such instantiation rejects at `call.generic_arg_slot` / `decl.slot_type`). The row lives in `union_type.hpp`, not `type_traits.hpp`: `value_compare.hpp` (home of the pack predicate) includes `core.hpp` / `bigint.hpp` / `buffer_types.hpp`, all of which include `type_traits.hpp`, so the trait header cannot see the predicate without a cycle. Pin the three answers in the same TU.
- **[design] Declare a builtin type's view->storage construction and its coercions in the stub.** The generic parameter FORM question is SETTLED: `String`, `bytes` and `bytearray` each own a C++ type (`::tpy::String` / `::tpy::Bytes` / `::tpy::ByteArray`, derived from the std types), so `param_val_or_ref_t<T>` at a generic slot resolves to the monomorphic twin's own parameter form and no template argument is needed -- the second-template-argument design was rejected in favour of this. What is left is the second half of the same principle: the types are declared in the stubs (`@native("::tpy::String")`), but the compiler still owns their CONSTRUCTION and CONVERSION knowledge. A stub cannot yet declare: its view->storage construction (`view_to_owned_conv` and `view_owned_copy_init` in `tpyc/type_def_registry.py`, plus the five codegen lambdas that spell the same thing -- `str_to_string`, `strview_to_string`, `bytesview_to_bytearray`, `char_to_string` and `_any_storage_form` in `tpyc/coercions.py`); the implicit-conversion PAIRS between family members (`String` <-> `str`, `bytearray` -> `bytes`); `is_expensive_copy`; `param_needs_copy_for_reassign`; `boundary_marshal`; and `element_of`. The shape is a stub-declarable "construct my storage form from this view" hook -- a dunder -- that those sites read, so adding a fourth buffer type touches no compiler file.
- **[thir] `_container_method_call_supported` and `_record_method_call_supported` answer two different questions, so they were kept apart.** The record gate decides the receiver shape, the method resolution (single overload, MRO, native rename) and the return; the container gate decides only a resolved stub call's return -- widening the record receiver gate reroutes every container method call into the record member-call render. The mergeable half is the return admission, and it LANDED 2026-09-05: `_record_method_call_supported`'s result chain opens on `_stub_method_ret_ok` with the flag-free half enabled and its eight duplicated predicates are gone, so a value-result row added for the stub receivers reaches a user record's methods too. `storage_ret_ok` / `stmt_position` stay spelled in the record chain because those rows fire its own witnesses. Zero admissions gained over the whole case corpus (the shared core is a strict subset there), and the receiver/overload halves stay apart on purpose: routing a user record through the stub loop rejects loudly at `method.arg_shape` (the stub arg sink has no record pass-through row) rather than mis-rendering.
- **[thir] A user container's ELEMENT is not a native-arg source: `len(rows[0])` on `list[ArrayList[int32, 8]]` rejects at `call.native_arg.record_f1_slot`.** The NAME spelling (`len(al)`) already routes through the record arg row and renders `::tpy::__len__(al)`; only the SUBSCRIPT source is missing, and it is a record-row question rather than a container one -- `ArrayList.__getitem__` is an ordinary TPy method with no `native_function` / `native_name` / `cpp_template`, so the element family (membership = the receiver's `__getitem__` resolves to the builtin `::tpy::__getitem__`) correctly excludes it and forcing that spelling would be wrong code. Measured in the consolidation's stages 2 and 3.
- **[thir] `_container_slot_call_rvalue_arg` still enumerates its SLOT family, and silently excludes `bytearray`.** `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py` gates the concrete same-family container slot with `is_list or is_dict or is_set or is_array`. The row it serves is `d.update(mk_d())` -- a container-returning call at a stub method's same-family slot, which renders `::tpy::dict_update(d, mk_d())`. No `bytearray` reproducer reaches the gate today (measured 2026-09-05): `bytearray.extend` takes `Iterable[uint8]` / `Iterable[int32]`, which the concrete-family test refuses for every family, and the only concrete-`bytearray` slots left are the operator stubs (`__add__` / `__eq__`), whose call operand rejects one step earlier at the result gate (`b + mk_ba()` -> `call.ret_type.record_other`). So the exclusion is unwitnessable rather than wrong -- but it is still a family list, not an axis test. Widening it to `_f1_container_ref` is the shape; a case per family is the proof, and a bytearray leg needs the operator-operand row closed first.
- **[thir] Three more name-keyed gates the fold did not classify.** `_inst_call_rvalue_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) gates a call rvalue at an instantiation arg slot on `is_list or is_dict or is_set`; `_set_method_recv` (same file) is a set-only receiver branch; `_container_literal_inst_slot` (same file) is the `list([..])` / `set([..])` slot. Named in neither the deliberate-stop entries above nor BUGS.md -- each needs the same verdict the fold gave the others: an axis test, or an exclusion with a stated render reason.
- **[thir] `_comp_sized_iterable` enumerates the sized iterable families.** `tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py` decides whether a comprehension can reserve up front with `is_array or is_list or is_dict or is_set or is_dict_view`. The question is really "does this source report `__len__` in O(1)", which is a per-TypeDef fact rather than a family list; `bytearray` is sized and absent, and a user container that reports its size cannot opt in. Only affects the reserve, never correctness, which is why it survived the fold.
- **[thir] Fold the comprehension `_scrubbed_pointers` into `lc.shadow_scope`.** A comprehension variable is a real inner scope, but `_scrubbed_pointers` (`tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py`) strips the shadowed names from `lc.pointers` only, so the narrowing, movable, optional and frame facts of an enclosing name stay visible under a comprehension variable of the same spelling. `_LowerCtx.shadow_scope` is the one per-name strip nested defs and lambdas already take; route the comprehension heads through it (the loop-var names as the bound set) and delete the pointers-only scrub.
- **[thir] Make the inner-scope scrub structural, so a missed name-keyed field is impossible rather than detected.** `shadow_scope` strips the fields listed by hand in the `_SHADOWED_*` tuples (`tpyc/thir/lower/context.py`); the first version missed the `@overload` literal facts, a silent wrong-branch fold. `tpyc/thir/test_shadow_scope_fields.py` now fails on an unclassified field, but only detects. Option 1 (small): one container type for name-keyed facts (`NameFacts[T]`) that `shadow_scope` finds and scrubs by reflection, with an explicit opt-out marker for the inherited-by-design ones. Option 2 (the real fix): scope-structured lowering state -- name facts live in a scope chain like sema's `Scope`, a nested def / lambda opens a child scope and lookups walk outward, so shadowing holds by construction; the for-each and comprehension scrubs and `branch_scope`'s save/restore fold into it, and it fits the lowering-state move toward MIR. The guard test goes once either lands. The same move should settle the three "names this function binds" sets: `prescan.scope_bound_names` (own-scope bindings, the shadow set), `ScanResult.bound_names()` (also comprehension vars and lambda params: the synthesized-name fence) and sema's `scan.bound_names() | scan.reassigned` -- they answer different questions today and must not drift.
- **[thir] `_lower_into_any` / `_lower_from_any` name list/dict/set as EXCLUSION tests.** `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` refuses an `Any` round-trip for those three (the `make_any` wrap is a `{0}` placeholder that cannot express the paren copy a name/set/dict source needs, and the extraction has no container arm). Exclusions, not admissions -- so the risk is the reverse of the usual one: `bytearray` and `Array` are NOT named, so they fall through to a render nobody checked. Decide what those two do at an `Any` boundary, then state the fence on the axis.
- **[thir] The const-by-default param form is spelled twice: `_const_default_param_form` in the lowering and `to_cpp_param` / `to_cpp_const_param` in `typesys`.** The lowering predicate (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) asks the registry whether a TypeDef carries the `param_cpp_formatter` + `param_mut_cpp_formatter` pair; `tpyc/typesys.py` renders the same distinction. One `TypeDef` / `TpyType` property should carry it, with both readers consulting it, so a second type adopting the pair cannot get one of the two answers. The second half is the load-bearing one: `_const_param_rvalue_ctor_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) admits an rvalue at such a slot WITHOUT checking whether THIS constructor's slot took the MUTABLE spelling -- correct for `bytearray` today because no bytearray ctor slot is mutable, and a latent trap for the next type that adopts the pair. Add the mutable-slot check with the property. From /tpy-review of the container-family fold.
- **[thir] `TypeDef.subscript_borrows` is a redundant channel, and `_NATIVE_GETITEM` is a third spelling of the dunder table.** The element family now derives the element-borrow fact from the resolved stub's `fi.native_name`, which is the same fact `subscript_borrows` carries on the TypeDef -- wire the family to the TypeDef or delete the field, but do not keep two. Separately, `_NATIVE_GETITEM = "tpy::__getitem__"` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) hardcodes the string `tpyc/modules/defs.py`'s `DUNDER_CPP_TEMPLATES["__getitem__"]` already owns; derive it. From /tpy-review of the container-family fold.
- **[thir] `TypeDef` has `element_of` but no `key_of`, so the dict KEY is recovered from the stub instead of read off the registry.** `_native_getitem_key` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) matches the `__getitem__` stub's parameter against the record's type-param names and indexes `type_args` to find the concrete key. That is correct and better than a positional guess, but the fact belongs beside `element_of` as a first-class registry channel -- a new channel is a design decision, so it did not ride the container-family fold. From /tpy-review of that fold. The channel now exists: `TypeDef.native_members` (2026-10-02) records, from the stub, which type parameter iteration yields, which one a subscript returns and whether the subscript is keyed, so `element_of` (the dict's `args[1]`, Span's `_span_elem`), `_native_getitem_key` and `subscript_borrows` are derivable from it; migrate them and delete the static entries.
- **[codegen] Break a long container-literal initializer across lines.** `tests/cases/dict/nested_container_element_printers` emits a 225-column local declaration for one nested dict literal; break the initializer one element per line once the declaration passes 100 columns (`docs/PITFALLS.md#generated-cpp-readability`). The emitter has no line-wrapping helper yet, so this needs the same width-aware render as "A long call render has no way to wrap its arguments" below, not a tweak at one site.
- **[thir] One "may this operand render twice?" check on the lowered form.** Three sites answer it separately: the value `and`/`or` left operand (`_lower_value_select`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`: only a name skips the single-evaluation temp, by syntax, so `w: float = 0 or a` renders `auto&& __tmp_1 = 0; double w = static_cast<double>((__tmp_1 ? __tmp_1 : a));`), the chained-compare endpoint (`emit_prims.is_duplicable_expr`, a syntax walk whose own TODO asks for a purity bit) and the membership needle (`is_trivial_needle`). One predicate over the lowered THIR node -- a constant or a plain local read, no construction -- serves all three, and inlines a fixed-width literal there (not an `int` literal, which constructs a BigInt and may parse it). A literal-kind row beside the name row was built and backed out 2026-09-28: it widened a kind-keyed gate instead of adding the form-level fact. Raised by the architecture review of the generated-C++ readability branch.
- **[thir] One lowering fact for "this switch case block falls through".** Match arms carry `body_terminates` (set once in `_case_entry`, `tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`), but whether a whole case block can reach its closing `break;` is re-derived at emit with two formulas: `_emit_match_switch` asks for an unguarded entry and every entry terminating, `_emit_match_guarded_union` asks only whether the last entry is unconditional and terminates (`tpyc/thir/emit.py`). Decide it once per group at lowering and let both tiers read it. Raised by the readiness retrospective of the generated-C++ readability branch.
- **[thir] Post-cutover follow-ups, decided 2026-09-02 with the deletion's eight open questions.** Decisions taken for the deletion itself: `faces.py` stays and its zero-witness report prints unconditionally in the summary; the reject-reason journal (`note()` / `note_detail()` and the composed reason helpers) survives and only the fallback tally dies, because the strict diagnostic reads it; class-constant and `Final`-global initializers get the same strict treatment as bodies (an unlowerable initializer is a compile error, no runtime demotion, no escape hatch); `shape.py` stays but its per-run harness recording goes; the docstring rewrite is its own commit right after the deletion; `--dump-thir`'s reject column keeps its plumbing and reads "why did this raise"; `scripts/thir_migration/review/` stays in place as the fix queue; the unit-test conversion in the deletion commit is minimum-green only. What those decisions defer, each its own change -- (a) the unit-test consolidation, (b) `faces.py` and (c) `shape.py` are DONE 2026-09-06 by measurement rather than by classification: a coverage difference over the whole corpus (6062 programs: every case, every reject probe, both example sets) against the 304 unit files found 687 lowering statements only a unit reached; each was mapped to its test function through per-test coverage contexts, converted to a case (342 added, `error_` for a reject path) and proven reached, and the files were deleted; `faces.py` STAYS because the whole-corpus zero-witness census in `tests/conftest.py` is the live dead-arm detector; `shape.py` and its tally script went with the tests they measured; the 36 statements reachable by no program and by no test were decided 2026-09-07: the test-only emit seam went (the no-op `CommentSink` / standalone `TempSink` / local `ModuleCounter` bases each collapsed into their single ctx-backed implementation, so `emit_thir_body` and the two leaf emitters now REQUIRE their sinks), and with it the whole-module `lower_module` entry, `THIRModule` and the `dump_thir` renderer that only read it -- the pins lower per body through `lower_function`, the entry codegen itself calls. The constant position, the one product caller of the standalone sinks, got its own sink that rejects at the allocation (`const.needs_statement_scope`) instead of detecting a pending temp after the render. The rest STAYS: every remaining line is a reject, a guard or a lowering arm that an earlier gate makes unreachable rather than scaffolding, and dropping one turns a hypothetical gate bug into a silent miscompile -- the class this compiler keeps producing. Still open: (d) **Convert the 54 `None`-returning rejects** in the resumable and simple-generator lowerings to raises, so one raise formulation covers every reject and the journal can shrink to the raise's own message. (e) **Opt-in THIR snapshots**: a `snapshot_thir` key in `options.json`, mirroring `snapshot_lib_modules`, writing `expected/thir/<module>.txt` for a curated set of cases (moves, narrowing, resumable frames -- the shapes the deleted audits guarded). Not before the typing pass: today 101 of 537 node fields are pre-rendered C++ text, so a dump would duplicate the C++ snapshot and then churn on every representation step while the C++ stays byte-identical.
- **[thir][test] First-reject-wins: an `error_` case's annotation pins whatever body rejects FIRST.** The attempt driver raises at the first rejecting body of a module, so a case whose subject body is not the first to reject annotates an earlier, unrelated reject -- and keeps passing after its intended boundary is widened, the one regression it exists to catch. The harness validates the annotation on the REPORTED line, which makes the pin honest but not necessarily the intended one. Fix per case: narrow the program so its own shape rejects first (one reject per `error_` case; two rejects cannot share a module). The unit-suite half of this entry (the `*_stays_ast` / `*_falls_back` names) closed with the suite's deletion 2026-09-06. (ii) **`dump.py`'s `_not_routed` fallback arm is probably dead.** `--dump-thir` goes through `collect_thir` -> `generate_code_and_thir`, which now raises `ThirRejectError` on an unlowerable body, so the `<fell back to AST: reason>` line is unreachable for a real reject -- a bodyless binding and an overload stub both take the other arm. Confirm, then delete the arm with its `reasons` plumbing; if something does still reach it, its wording names an emitter that no longer exists. Surfaced by the post-deletion BUGS/docs pass.
- **[thir][test] `# tpyc: ok` is now refused in an `error_` case, and update mode validates annotations.** DONE 2026-09-07. `tests/test_case.py` rejects an `ok` annotation in an error case naming the line (compilation stops at the first error, so the leg is satisfied by a line the phase never reached), and `validate_annotations` runs in update mode too -- after the snapshot is written, in `test_case.py` and `test_interop_exec.py` alike -- so a regeneration can no longer rewrite `diag.txt` around a wrong annotation and leave the next plain run to fail on it. All 58 legs across the 38 pre-existing error cases went: 32 dropped as pure scaffolding (a `def` line, a stub `...` body, a `nums = [1, 2, 3]` fixture), 20 dropped with a header pointer to the normal case that already pins the happy path, and 6 moved into a section of one of five existing normal cases (`calls/overload_literal_int`, `generators/narrowed_value_opt_field_yield` x2, `generators/narrowed_value_opt_frame_faces`, `movability/pool_custom_move`, `union/union_field_const_read`). No new case was needed and no leg turned out false. The comp-only annotations (`type`, `non_null`, `bounds_*`, `div_*`, `cast_*`, `is_send`/`is_sync`, `frame_*`) keep their update-mode exemption, since they feed no snapshot; the same argument applies to them, more weakly. The residue is the GENERAL form of the gate: an annotation on ANY line the phase did not reach is still accepted (`type` / `bounds_safe` / `non_null` and friends in a body that rejected), which needs the harness to know which lines were analysed.
- **[thir] `_ConstPositionSink` (`tpyc/thir/constants.py`) implements the sink protocol by duck typing, and nothing pins the protocol.** It is the temp sink of a namespace-scope initializer: every allocation raises `const.needs_statement_scope`, the counters just count, `comments` is None. A method added to the ctx-backed `TempSink` (or a statement arm reaching the comment sink from expression emission) surfaces there as an `AttributeError` ICE where a reject is wanted. Cheap closure: a `Protocol` the two sinks both satisfy, checked by a unit in the kept machinery files, or a `__getattr__` that rejects.
- **[thir] A resumable's TERMINATOR rejects report the `def` line, not the offending one** (fixing it moves `tests/cases/async/error_narrow_post_if_across_suspend`, which commits the coarse `def`-line diagnostic)**.** `_lower_leaf` in `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py` stamps the rejecting statement's location on a `ThirUnsupported` that has none, which covers the frame-field statement arms. Three terminator paths raise outside it -- the branch condition, the await operand, and the finally-helper walk -- so a reject there reaches `fold_attempt` with no location and falls back to the enclosing callable's `def` line. Correct but coarse today; once `--thir-strict` is the only behaviour it is the line a user is shown, so each of the three wants the same set-if-empty stamp at its own leaf.
- **[thir] Small cleanups left over from the deletion.** Three: fold `Compiler._make_codegen` into `_run_codegen`, since the split existed to keep the two emit entry points routing identically and there is only one route left; extract the four set-if-empty `ex.loc` stamps in `tpyc/thir/lower/` into one helper; and dispatch `_strict_error`'s `where` phrasing on `component` before falling back to the node's name, so a `top_level` fold over a named node cannot be phrased as a function.
- **[thir] The call-arg position kind is still five booleans beside a one-member enum.** `_lower_call_arg` names its GENERIC caller through `CallArgKind`, the axis beside `_ExprUse.pos` for which argument loop is filling a slot -- the callee's shape, not the sink's. The other five kinds are still booleans on the same signature: `method_arg` and `method_arg_stub` (four spellings for three positions, the illegal fourth combination held only by convention), `protocol_slots`, `marker_arg` and `inline_template`. Fold each into a `CallArgKind` member so a new argument loop is a new member rather than a sixth flag; the rights beside them (`temp_args`, `nested_temps`, `readonly_target`, `frame_capturing`, `union_divergent_ok`) are not kinds and stay. The slot half of this entry landed: `slot_threaded` and the `target_type` keyword are one `_ExprUse.slot_target`.
- **[thir] "Operand lands in a C++ parameter" is decided at six operator positions, not by the call-arg path.** A `bytes` literal operand at a parameter slot renders the static span `::tpy::bytes_literal(...)`, and that retag is applied operator by operator: a binop and an augmented assignment (`_rb_bytes_literal_views`), a record `__getitem__` and `__setitem__` (`_retag_param_bytes_literal`), a compare dunder (inlined at the compare arm) and an `in` needle (`_bytes_literal_view_slot` at the membership arm) -- all in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` / `statements.py`. Each position resolves the dunder, finds the parameter type and asks `_bytes_literal_view_slot` itself, which the call-arg path (`_lower_call_arg`) already does for every ordinary argument. Route a resolved-dunder operand through `_lower_call_arg` against the dunder's parameter, so one mechanism decides what an operand at a parameter slot renders; a seventh operator position then needs no retag of its own. Found by the view-rule review (2026-10-01).
- **[thir] The validator's `THIRRaise` arm walks only `node.args`, so a non-call `raise <expr>` gets no form validation.** `_walk` in `tpyc/thir/validate.py` handles `THIRRaise` by walking the ctor argument list and RETURNING, which is right for `raise X(a, b)` (the args are the ctor's directly). The EXPRESSION form (`raise e` / `raise make_error()`) carries its subject on `raise_expr` instead, and the early return means that subtree is never walked -- no form check, no arg-temp check, on whatever it contains. Pre-existing; found while extracting the shared arg-list walk. Fix shape: walk the remaining children after the arg list instead of returning.
- **[thir] `_borrow_legal_return` and `_value_record_borrow` are two predicates joined at one `if`.** `tpyc/thir/validate.py`'s `THIRReturn` rule reads `not _borrow_legal_return(return_type) and not _value_record_borrow(stmt.value)` -- one question (may this BORROW value initialize this return slot?) split across a type-keyed half and a value-keyed half, so a reader has to reassemble it and a new row can land in the wrong half. Fold into one `_borrow_legal_return(return_type, value)`. Belongs in the deletion unit's cleanup sweep.
- **[cli] Five places stamp a `CodeGenError`'s filename, and only the compiler knows which file it is.** `tpyc/cli.py` wraps four codegen calls in the same `if e.filename is None and not compiled.is_entry_point: e.filename = os.path.relpath(compiled.path)`, and `Compiler._run_codegen` now does the same for a THIR reject -- so the rule lives once per call site instead of once. Consolidating it into the compiler (stamp every `CodeGenError` at the one place that holds the `CompiledModule`) would let the CLI drop all four wrappers. Held back because it changes the filename on EVERY codegen diagnostic, not just the ones that are unstamped today, and whether the entry point should stay caller-named is a design call rather than a refactor.
- **[test] Interop cases snapshot REGULAR emission, which is the corpus's job.** Each case under `tests/interop/` commits the module `.hpp`/`.cpp` alongside the CPython glue `_ext.cpp`, and the module half carries nothing interop-specific: `@export` affects the glue only, so an exported function's body renders exactly as the same source would in an ordinary case (checked on `floats`: no `PyObject`, no `Py_`, no export marking anywhere in the module `.cpp`). The interop-specific artifacts are the glue, `diag.txt`, the ext-exec `.so` build and driver run, and cpy-parity -- those are the case type's reason to exist. Consequences already paid: the THIR overlay there byte-diffs ordinary module emission and so duplicates corpus coverage, which is why it turned out to need no cutover successor after being scoped as a blocker. Worth narrowing the snapshot set to the interop-specific artifacts, which would drop roughly 68 committed files. **Do not act on the one-case check above** -- confirm across all 34 that no module emission differs from its plain-case equivalent before removing anything, since a shape where `@export` DID reach the module would be exactly the coverage worth keeping. Not cutover work; a cleanup that the cutover happened to expose.

- **[thir] The post-cutover fix queue: shapes that are now compile errors.** The primary queue is `scripts/thir_migration/review/` -- the BREAKS rows of `bins_*.json` (402 sites, each with a reproducer under `probes/<slice>/`) and the `BREAKS_AT_CUTOVER` entries of `program_verdicts.json` (478 programs). This entry holds what is NOT in those files: shapes found by two pre-deletion sweeps whose probe programs were not kept. Each is valid code that compiled and ran correctly before the deletion because a second emitter caught it; each is a `ThirRejectError` today. Close one by adding the lowering arm and landing an ordinary case, not a probe. The eight everyday witnesses from the guard-reading sweep (2026-08-31/09-01) all compile as of 2026-09-15 (three had closed on the way; batch 4 closed the nested `def` shadowing a module function, the covariant upcast into an Optional record field, `print(..., file=<subscript>)`, a `Final[tuple[...]]` class constant bound whole, and the truthiness of an Optional record field), so nothing is left here that the queue files do not hold.
  One of them is worth dwelling on: `tests/cases/class_const/final_tuple_constant` covered that constant only through the UNPACK position -- the whole-tuple bind beside it did not route, and no case reached it. Both positions route now, and the case covers the whole bind, the in-place subscript and a nested-tuple constant. **A covered feature is not a covered position**, and that is the shape this sweep keeps finding.
  **The other seven fold in front of an AST that emits ill-formed C++, and that reframes the class.** `if "yes":`, a genexpr over any dict view, a literal passed to a pointer-representation union parameter, extracting a container out of `Any`, a GUARD on a union match arm (the guard does not narrow though the arm body does), and an Optional match inside a generator (the arm body does not narrow though the plain-function form does) all fail the C++ build today; each is filed separately in BUGS.md (five at HIGH -- all common spellings). The seventh, a `for a, b in ...:` unpack inside a generator, lowers, builds and runs; the silent element copy that was left of it is fixed (the frame unpack lifts through `tuple_to_pointer` off the source lvalue). Probing also turned up a rejects-valid-code defect that is NOT a fold: the return-path analysis does not credit a break-free loop's `else` clause, so a function whose only `return` sits there is refused. For these the fence was doing the right thing; the deletion traded a bad-C++ error for a reject diagnostic, which is a UX change but not a correctness one. **The reusable heuristic: an unwitnessed fence is a good place to LOOK FOR AST BUGS.** THIR declined to mirror those renders, and in three of eight cases the reason is that the render is broken -- so triaging the remaining sites pays twice, once in cutover risk and once in defects that no test corpus reaches.
  **The METHOD is the durable half.** Probes aimed from reject TAGS found nothing: 0 folds from 13. Probes aimed after READING the guard condition found all sixteen: 16 folds from 58 that reached codegen. That rate is biased UPWARD -- the most ordinary-looking guards were probed first -- so read it as a bound on the per-guard rate, not an estimate of one. **Three KEYS are in play here and they must not be swapped**: 16 FOLDS (a probe whose body did not route), 9 WITNESSES (a folding shape that is valid code working today), and 10 new BUGS ENTRIES (filed defects, which include ones found while checking a shape rather than by a fold, and which sometimes cover more than one shape). Saying "the sweep filed nine bugs" pairs the witness key with the bug label and is wrong in both directions. Reject tags name where a reason was FORMATTED, not what blocks the shape, so a tag-driven triage of the remaining 358 sites will read as clean and be wrong. Two guard docstrings were also contradicted by probe: `_lower_with` states that a `with` nested in a branch or loop still rejects, and both spellings route -- treat every prose claim about what a fence still catches as unverified until a probe says otherwise.
  **Negative results are triage output too -- record them.** Several depth-0/1 fences turned out to be SEMA-GATED, so no valid program reaches them and they need no lowering work: `getattr`/`setattr` with a literal name on a declared field (sema redirects to `obj.x`), a `@dynamic`-protocol local without an initializer, a class pattern on a scalar Optional inner, a nested `def` containing `yield`, and `Final[list[str]]` as a class constant. A fence behind a sema diagnostic is unreachable by construction, not untested.
  **Thirty-nine more from the 2026-09-01 adversarial sweep** (162 hand-written probes; 23 of the 39 compiled and ran correctly, the other 16 were already broken in ways the sweep did not look at and are filed separately). They spread over 32 distinct reject reasons -- 1.2 probes per reason, the same flat tail the stdlib grind ended on, the largest `stmt.match` at 6. Not a set-cover problem: pick by what the shape COSTS a user, not by tag frequency.
  **Three more shapes, found by the asymmetry matrix and NOT in the 39** -- 7 probes, all rejected today: `case A() | B() as n:` on an `A | B` union subject (an or-pattern of class patterns carrying an `as` binding, with and without a guard); `case n if True:` on an `A | None` subject (a bare capture arm with a guard on an Optional); and a GUARDED capture or wildcard arm (`case s if ...:` / `case _ if ...:`) inside a match with enough string-literal arms to select the string-switch tier. **Five of the seven compile and run correctly today; the other two do not, and saying they did was wrong** -- the two that place the guarded arm FIRST are a silent miscompile the AST render drops on the floor, now filed HIGH. So this set splits like the 39 do: mostly working programs that lost their emitter, plus a couple that were already broken and only looked like routing gaps. Check before claiming a rejected shape works.
  **The 39 shapes, written out because the TAGS ARE LOSSY** -- they name the first reject, not the blocker, so a tag alone does not let anyone reconstruct what to re-probe. The probe programs themselves are gone (they were a second, weaker copy of what a test case does); each shape below is cheap to re-author, and whoever closes a gap should land it as an ordinary case rather than a probe.
  *match (the only cluster):* a call as the subject with no intermediate binding; a dict-subscript subject with 5+ literal str arms (string-switch tier, non-name subject); a match in a `for` whose arm mutates a captured reference field then breaks; a match inside `try` whose arm raises; a bool subject that is a call, exhaustive with no wildcard; a subscript subject of `int32 | None` inside a `while` with a guard on the int arm; a walrus subject (`match (n := compute(x)):`) with the name used after; a field-access subject whose pattern captures and mutates a reference sub-field; a `@dynamic` subject with two-level nested keyword sub-patterns and an `as` on the inner pattern; a `@dynamic` parameter subject with an or-pattern spanning two classes; a guard calling `isinstance` on a union-arm capture; a match in a generator on a `Ping | Pong | None` subject; `yield` in a match arm over a union-typed frame local read again after resume.
  *comprehensions and iteration:* a list comp over `dict.items()` whose element is a call, plus a comp-of-comp; a dict comp over `zip(enumerate(...), ...)`; a genexpr over `reversed(list)` consumed by `sum()`; `zip` over three uneven iterables as a comp source; a comp element that is a conditional expression producing a tuple, sourced from `enumerate()`; a walrus in a comp filter whose name is reused in the element expression and leaks to the enclosing scope; nested `for` loops reusing one loop-variable name at the same and at different types.
  *unions and narrowing:* a 3-member union list element narrowed by `is None` plus `isinstance` inside a loop; a tuple element of reference-type union narrowed after unpacking; a union as a generic type ARGUMENT (`Box[Dog | Cat]`) narrowed after extraction; a walrus binding `Dog | Cat | None` then narrowed in two steps; a value union narrowed by `==` against a str literal rather than `is None`/`isinstance`; a mixed value+reference union as a RETURN type narrowed by the caller; `list[Optional[tuple[int32, str]]]`.
  *calls:* `@overload` on a constructor; overload stubs shorter than the implementation with trailing params from defaults; an enum-member default crossed with out-of-order kwargs and an overload group; a call result subscripted then field-accessed then chained again; a chained subscript straight off a call return (`f()[i][j]`) and a subscript on a slice-of-a-slice; nested generics (a list of lists through a generic function, a generic class instantiated with another generic); two OS-divergent error classes in one `except` tuple with the `open()` result chained into `close()`.
  *records and module scope:* `super().__init__` with a value-type union parameter; mutually recursive records with an owned value moved into a list via `append`; a list comprehension at MODULE scope; a union-typed global narrowed at module scope; bytearray element mutation by index alongside bytes-vs-str indexing. Everyday spellings in the list include a list comprehension at module scope, a comprehension over `dict.items()`, `zip`/`enumerate`/`reversed` sources, a walrus in a comprehension condition, nested loops reusing a name, a match inside `try`/`except`, a match on a field access or a subscript, and `super().__init__` with a union parameter.
  **Four probes DIVERGE across the three widths.** At int32: an overloaded generator's const-mismatched narrowing, a generic class returning a narrowed `Optional[T]` field, and an int literal at an inherited overload. At BigInt only: a list-literal for-loop source, where the AST emits a bare `{10, 0, 1}` and THIR constructs each element -- **the first option-gated AST/THIR divergence anyone has caught**, and the whole justification for sweeping every width. Each is filed in BUGS.md. In the two that emitted C++ the AST could not compile, the deletion fixed them by removing the wrong author; the other two ran identically on both paths and are filed for the class, not the instance. None has a corpus witness.

- **[thir] Unverified: whether a movable union-typed source at the protocol-union identity row can pick up a THIR-side move the AST does not make.** `_struct_proto_union_arg`'s `at == pt` branch (same protocol union forwarded at its own slot) is justified by a documented LOAD-BEARING COINCIDENCE: the AST's consuming `own_iter(std::move(..))` rewrite keys on a bare `Iterable[Own[T]]` ptype and misses a `UnionType`, which is WHY both paths render the argument bare. The reasoning generalizes, and the row is pinned with a unit asserting `own_iter` does not appear (so it fails the day the AST's keying widens to unions) -- but a reviewer could not fully trace whether some movable union-typed source at that row picks up a move on the THIR side that the AST's blind spot does not cover. Evidence against it is strong rather than absent: the full corpus ran green with exec, and the move-verdict join -- since deleted with the AST path it compared against -- reported 0 divergences over 1010 joined nodes on its last reading. Filed as a known-unverified corner rather than chased, because the discriminating case would be a union-typed argument that is BOTH a last use and forwarded at its own protocol-union slot, and it is not obvious one is constructible. If any ArrayList or protocol-union-forwarding case ever regresses, start here. Raised by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, low confidence) on the 2026-08-28 stdlib grind.
- **[thir] `_optional_ptr_arg_face` returns an untyped string.** (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`, consumed in `expressions.py` x4 and `checks.py` x2) The face function returns one of eleven bare literals to six call sites, and the dispatcher has nine branches plus a documented silent fall-through that renders the bare un-addressed ctor -- a name added at the producer and missed at a consumer drops a temp with no type error. It classifies the ARGUMENT's shape rather than the sink's, so it is not part of the sink pair: make it a `StrEnum`, a mechanical swap over two files. Its sibling untyped field-read verdict, the `field_owned_str_ok` keyword, is priced in its own entry ("information-free at most of its call sites") -- same shape of defect, different fold.
- **[test] `tests/.session_fingerprints.json` is stale on master and every snapshot regeneration rewrites it.** `uv run python tests/update_snapshots.py -k <anything>` exits clean but modifies the `libtpy` and `runtime` keys, so a snapshot update silently drags an unrelated file into the change-set. Ablated against unmodified master `4ad40383c`, which produces the identical modification -- that commit touched `lib/tpy/` and `runtime/` and shipped a stale fingerprint file. Harmless today (`cpy_stubs`, the only key still gating a phase, matches, and the `libtpy`/`runtime` keys no longer gate anything per the CLAUDE.md testing notes), but it is a trap for anyone running `update_snapshots.py`. Either refresh the committed file or drop the two dead keys.
- **[thir] THE STDLIB FALLBACK BACKLOG is CLOSED (2026-08-30: 0 fallback bodies on both counting keys, 1245 routed over 2843 classified).** Kept for its lessons only -- the per-row instructions it used to carry describe rows that no longer exist. It ran 195 bodies (honest per-body key, 2026-08-25) -> 60 -> 21 -> 16 -> 0 over four rounds. **The reusable finding, learned separately four times on the way down: a per-row status assembled from reject TAGS rather than from an ABLATION was wrong every time, and always pessimistic.** `os::walk` was filed as a measured dead end and was four independent rows, each a sibling of an admission that already existed; the `asyncio._executor::poll` / `hashlib::_drain_blocks` pair was filed as zero-yield and flipped the moment it was priced as the shared row PLUS each body's own rungs instead of the shared row alone; `datetime::ZoneInfo.fromutc` was filed as blocked on a fence a fix days earlier had already made stale; and `http.client::HTTPSConnection.__init__` was filed as a DESIGN FORK and was three mechanical gaps with no design decision in it. Re-derive a row's blocker before ranking it, and never inherit a previous round's record of one. Three findings outlive the backlog itself: a shared raise SITE collapses the search without defining a LANE (one ctor-arg ladder held four unrelated predicates across two files), a collapsed sweep row is a SEARCH KEY and not a work unit (one row stood for four bodies that were three different questions at two sites), and two sibling predicates that CROSS rather than NEST -- one looser on containers, the other tighter on bytes -- have drifted apart rather than been deliberately split (that was `_ptr_union_member_wide` vs `_ptr_union_view_member_ok`, adjudicated and then closed 2026-08-30 by an audit of all 13 consumers).
- **[thir] A predicate that consults two members of a three-member family and silently omits the third has no mechanical guard.** It bit concretely: the resumable frame-param gate admitted value-repr `Optional[scalar]` and `Optional[view]` params but never the `Optional[Callable]` one, so a body fell back on a shape all three siblings capture and read identically. Fixed there. Five more functions under `tpyc/thir/lower/` still pair `_value_opt_scalar` with `_value_opt_view` and carry no callable leg -- at least one of them correctly, and that one is the trap worth naming: the binding-kind mapper has no callable leg because `ValueOptKind` is SCALAR/VIEW/RECORD, so the predicate family and the binding-kind enum are three members each and NOT the same three. Proposal: a family-completeness helper at the ADMISSION GATES -- the "is this family in scope at all" checks, not every predicate that legitimately wants a single member -- so the next omission is a type error rather than a silent fallback. Not urgent; the one live instance is closed.
- **[perf] Two `tplib.requests` renders that THIR now mirrors and that should not be the permanent shape.** `iter_content` copies the whole response body into an owned generator frame slot where a non-generator local would bind a view (a generator/non-generator behavior split); `items()` / `copy()` / `update()` pay four `std::string` heap copies per iteration where a borrow-form `pair` would pay zero. Observed 2026-08-25 during the stdlib grind, not re-verified since. Fixing either means changing the AST render first -- THIR has to mirror whatever the oracle emits.
- **[thir] The `self`-receiver deref residue, after the fact was made intrinsic (2026-08-29).** `THIRSelf.deref` is now set where the node is built, from `lc.self_is_pointer`, and the nine value-position retags are gone; a `receiver_through_pointer` property drives both the arrow-member clear and a `validate.py` rule, so the render and its guard read one predicate. Two residues remain. **(1) The raw-pointer slot class is NOT validator-guarded.** A borrow-tuple element binds the receiver pointer itself (`{1, this}`), and the clear there goes through a separate helper, because a value-typed record legitimately appears deref'd at a non-addr-of element -- so the guard that covers member access cannot cover this one. It is the position a future element row would forget, and the missing piece is specific: those nodes carry only `addr_of`, which conflates a pointer passthrough with a value slot, so a rule would falsely reject a value-typed record at a bare value element. A sound guard needs a new per-element pointer-slot channel on both nodes -- price THAT, do not re-derive 'no predicate exists'. The sibling `THIROptionalPtrArg` slot is guardable in about four lines, but it is not the forgettable site. **Before adding a third validator rule anywhere here, read the BUGS entry on `THIRValidationError` being uncaught:** every rule enlarges a filed crash-on-valid-code class whose newest trigger needs no flag and no macro. **And the invariant is still construction-site-enforced**, not unforgettable: the positioning helper wraps 3 of 14 field-access and 6 of 10 method-call constructions, and the unbound-base field access builds its receiver with a hardcoded non-deref rather than deriving it. The failure mode moved from a silent miscompile at a value sink to a crash at an arrow site -- louder and better, but a trade, not an elimination. **(2) The value-slot receiver arms (`cpp_template` / native free function) are pinned at the NODE level only**, because the shape is not constructible from source today: a `@native` class cannot carry a TPy body and a regular method cannot be `@native`, so `self` never reaches those arms. If either restriction ever loosens, that pin stops standing in for a real witness.
  **What the consolidation cost, worth knowing before the next one.** Three things the design brief had wrong, each caught by an adversarial probe rather than by a gate: the user-`__deref__` chain wanted `this->__deref__()` (the AST arrows the first hop), so making the deref intrinsic converted an ill-formed render into a DIVERGENT one -- and the fix, factoring the codegen's own indirect-name arrow test, turned up FOUR arms that had each dropped the self clause, not the two the brief named; a third consumer class (raw `T*` slots) existed that the brief did not name at all; and one of the three sites listed as wrong-today was not constructible. A survey that enumerates consumers by grepping one field name will miss the consumers that spell the same fact differently.
- **[thir] Reason-swallowing is a CLASS, and six-plus sites are still open.** A gate that catches `ThirUnsupported` and re-raises with a fixed tag discards the operand's own reason, so the fallback tally names the catcher rather than the blocker -- and every work-scoping decision taken off that tally is then wrong. Three sites were fixed 2026-08-27 and all three had been lying: `resumable.py`'s await-operand raised `from None` and hid three bodies that were really `method.arg_shape` (all three then routed on one row); `statements.py`'s if-condition catch replaced the reason with an operand-family tag, hiding three unrelated shapes under one `&&.scalar_scalar`; `_ptr_template_method_supported` had six untagged `return False` legs. This class is the plausible origin of the "asyncio is the always-last sink" belief this file later recorded as REFUTED. **The enumeration below was built by grepping `raise ... from None`, which MISSES the bare form** -- `except ThirUnsupported: return _reject(<literal>)` discards the reason just as thoroughly and matches no `from None`. One such site was found only when a reviewer swept for the CATCH rather than the raise: `simple_gen.py` (`sgen.cond`). Sweep by the catch next time, not the re-raise -- and sweep by SYMBOL, never by the line numbers a previous sweep recorded, which had all drifted within days. **Re-swept by the catch 2026-08-29: exactly ONE site was still open**, `simple_gen.py`'s bare `except ThirUnsupported: return _reject("sgen.cond")`, and that file went with the single-yield peephole on 2026-09-12, so NO site is open. Everything this entry previously listed now composes: `res.cond` (`resumable.py`), `expr.fstring` (`expressions.py`, which also routes its two direct rejects through `note_detail`), `stmt.while`, the four tuple-shape catches (`decl.tuple_literal_shape` x3, `return.tuple_source`) and the if-condition catch, which carries `ex.reason` behind its operand-family tag. **Yield when last measured, against 39 remaining stdlib fallback bodies: ZERO sat under any of these tags** -- measured, not estimated; the backlog reached ZERO on 2026-08-30, so that yield figure is history twice over -- re-measure against whatever a later sweep grows back rather than inheriting it. Do not pick this up expecting bodies; pick it up only to stop a future tag from lying. The general rule the branch learned the expensive way: an instrument fix is worth exactly the bodies currently under the catcher's own tag, and that is countable from the tag histogram before doing any work. Fix shape: compose `ex.reason` into the tag wherever a catcher re-raises, exactly as `stmt_reject_reason(stmt, ex.reason)` already does. Diagnostics-only, so no admission changes -- but re-measure after, because the tally will re-partition and some tags will turn out to be several shapes.
- **[thir] The receiver binding peel is still open-coded in two more predicates.** `_field_decl_type` and `_f1_record` were found deriving it twice and disagreeing -- first over `Own` (a false negative: every gate on the pair rejected an `Own`-param receiver's members), then over `Own[readonly[record]]` in the opposite direction, where the field-type half said yes and the receiver half said no. The second was LIVE: a sink that pre-checks its field (print args, field-write targets, match subjects, ~25 `field_prechecked=True` sites) never consults the receiver ladder, so the shape emitted on the strength of the lookup alone -- admitted and unwitnessed, byte-identical only by luck. Both now call a shared `_binding_peel`. **`_record_class_binding` open-codes the identical peel, and `_deref_wrapper_receiver_record` open-codes the re-unwrapping variant on both its field-type and receiver-binding legs.** Folding them in CHANGES ADMISSION at their consumers, so it is not a mechanical edit -- it needs the three units and a dualgen pass per consumer. The invariant worth stating: a question two predicates must answer identically should be derived once, because the tree has now produced this exact bug twice in one week from the same duplication.
- **[thir][test] Require a view-source-into-owned-slot CASE on any arm that decides a move off the LOWERED value.** An arm that both reads `.form`/ownership off the lowered value and makes a move/copy decision is blind to the AST-side move question that no longer exists, and a wrong-code move at exactly such a position was caught 2026-08-27 by the byte-diff alone. Clearing the marked corpus is a SET-COVER problem over the 376 distinct blocker constructs, and the greedy cover says the opposite of 'avoid the elephants': **7 constructs cover 253 of the 1014 marked cases (25%), and the first three of those seven ARE the elephants** (`expr.call` 67, `expr.method_call` 66, `decl.slot_type` 57 -- 190 cases between them). The successor cannot be a cross-path join; it has to be a THIR-INTERNAL invariant (assert the move verdict against the sink's own requirement rather than against the other path). - **[ci][verify] First macOS nightly must confirm the BigInt-literal ambiguity fix compiles.** The macOS `const BigInt` overload-ambiguity fix now lives in ONE chokepoint: `int_literals.render_int_literal_value` pins a target-less `>int32` literal to an exact BigInt-ctor width (`static_cast<int64_t>` for `<=int64`, `static_cast<uint64_t>` up to uint64, `from_str` beyond), so a bare `long`/`ull` token never reaches an ambiguous `long -> BigInt` / `unsigned long long -> BigInt` conversion (int64_t == long only on Linux; uint64_t == unsigned long long only on macOS). Both codegen paths share the function (THIR pre-renders literals through it). Verified by a C++ simulation of the macOS/Linux ctor layouts plus Linux-green. A real arm64 Mac build has since happened (Apple clang 21, 2026-07-29) but only over the `tests/interop` corpus, which touches none of the cases named below -- so this stays open on THOSE cases. So a red first mac-nightly on any BigInt-vs-literal site (`datetime.py`, `sys_maxsize`, the `int/bigint_compare_large_literal` / `int/bigint_list_large_literal` / `float/as_integer_ratio` / `builtins/sum_basic` / `stdlib/datetime_datetime` cases) is this fix's regression, not new breakage; conversely a green mac-nightly closes the verify loop. Rides the phase-2 mac row. Surfaced by /tpy-ready + /tpy-review of `fix-bigint-list-literal`.

- **[perf][cleanup] `render_int_literal_value`'s BigInt-TARGET arm has no `[2^63, 2^64-1]` case -- a threaded huge literal in that range renders `BigInt::from_str("...")` (runtime string parse) where the target-less arm now uses `static_cast<uint64_t>(...)` (compile-time, exact `BigInt(uint64_t)` ctor).** Add the symmetric `uint64` fast-path to the BigInt-target arm (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/int_literals.py`) so a value like `n: int = 18446744073709551615` avoids the parse. Rare range, correct either way -- pure perf/symmetry, not a bug. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the list-literal consolidation.

- **[test-gap] `_reindex_builtins_post_finalize` order-independence lacks a direct unit test.** The `threading/mutex_wrap_cross_module` regression guard reproduces the builtin-index ordering bug only because the module name `achan` happens to sort `tpy.sync` before `tpy._core._containers` in the Tarjan topo order (`tpyc/compiler.py:_compute_compile_order` ties-break via `sorted`); an unrelated future stdlib rename/reorder could silently stop reproducing it with no signal from the suite. Add a focused `tpyc/` unit test that constructs the two-module finalize order directly (no dependence on real stdlib module names) and asserts a builtin (`Ptr`/`uint32`) resolves in the consumer analyzer's registry regardless of finalize order. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `fix-channel-prereqs`.
- **[investigate] Known asymmetry in `_reindex_builtins_post_finalize`: it re-runs only ONE of the finalize loop's three registration steps.** `_finalize_declarations`'s implicit-module loop (`tpyc/compiler.py`) does builtin-type indexing + `register_protocol` + a non-builtin record auto-inject, all with the same "read a peer's not-yet-fully-populated exports at call time" shape; the post-finalize re-index re-applies only the builtin-type step. So a stdlib protocol or plain record reached via an edge-less `from tpy import X` could be stranded in a consumer's registry the same way `Ptr` was -- the same mechanism, half-covered. NO witness yet: named cross-module imports create module edges that force ordering, so it may be unreachable in practice (the gap is specific to implicit-stdlib entities that record no edge). Repro FIRST; only if reproducible, generalize the re-index (or the loop) to cover all three steps -- do NOT broaden it speculatively (snapshot/behavior risk without a witness). Kept in TODO (not BUGS.md) because it is an unconfirmed latent gap, not a reproduced defect. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) + the /tpy-ready retrospective of `fix-channel-prereqs`.
- **[feature] Extend `unsafe_interior_mutable` to an inline (non-`Ptr`) field -- a C++ `mutable` member.** Today the hatch is `Ptr[T]`-only: `tpyc/sema/registration.py` rejects a non-pointer payload ("only supported on a Ptr[T] field"), so an interior-mutable primitive must live behind a raw pointer to a heap block (`unsafe_take`/`unsafe_release`). Allow `unsafe_interior_mutable[T]` (T a concrete, non-`readonly`/`Own`/nested type) to lower to an inline `mutable T` C++ member: registration accepts the non-`Ptr` inner and sets `is_interior_mutable`; codegen emits `mutable T name;` and suppresses const-projection on the field's access (the inline case of the flag the `Ptr` pointee already uses). Sound -- inline `mutable` is the same escape as the `Ptr` form (mutate through a shared readonly handle), just inline storage; the `Ptr`-only reject is conservatism/YAGNI, not a soundness gate, and the rename commit's own doc names "C++ `mutable` member" as an intended hatch form. Payoff: a `@nocopy` interior-mutable primitive with NO external pointer into it (nothing needs a stable/shared address, unlike `Mutex`'s guard cell or `Rc`/`Arc`'s shared refcount cell) becomes allocation-free. First consumer: `tpy.sync.Condvar` -- its `_cv` currently heap-allocates (`unsafe_interior_mutable[Ptr[_RawCondvar]]`) only because the hatch forces a `Ptr`; inline `unsafe_interior_mutable[_RawCondvar]` drops that alloc and keeps `_RawCondvar` an honest non-const wrapper (vs. the alternative of faking const ops in the C++ wrapper). Design decision on the escape hatch -> own `/tpy-add-feature` pass; do NOT bundle into the channel work. Surfaced discussing the Condvar allocation.
