  **`Own[Opt[T]]` call/name lifts** (`decl.opt_slot_source` -- the
  `optional_to_ptr({slot} = ...)` is_opt_field forms); (d) **polymorphic
  subclass slots** (slot retyped to the rvalue's class; rebind case is a
  sema-error tier); (e) **lvalue-init reassigned optionals + lvalue reseats**
  (`decl.opt_reseat_source` -- the address-of reseat arm + reassigned bare
  record-name pointer alias landed wave 13; remainder is pointer-copy /
  storage-lift reseats); (f) **union reseats without a pre-declared slot** (the AST's
  inline-slot fallback) and **address reseats** (`decl.union_reseat_source`);
  (g) **non-record-member ptr-variant unions** (scalar/container members --
  `_eligible_ptr_union` keeps them out). The union decl/reseat emit arms are
  corpus-zero-witness until the call track lands union-returning calls and
  print-of-call args (their host bodies co-block there); the unit pins
  that covered them meanwhile went with the THIR unit suite.

- **[ergonomics] Allow a `Final[enum]` module constant as a default parameter (and field) value.** The enum-MEMBER default half is DONE (`def f(order: MemoryOrder = MemoryOrder.SEQ_CST)` works; the `tpy.atomic` sentinel was retired). The remaining half is a `Final[EnumType]` module constant used as a default: still rejected because `tpyc/typesys.py:2631` restricts `Final` to "only primitive types and tuple". Relax that restriction to admit `Final[enum]` (an enum member is a compile-time constant with a scoped-enumerator C++ form), then the existing `Final`-name default path (`codegen_cpp/functions.py` `default_to_cpp` `TpyName` arm) already emits it. Separable and lower-value than the member half was. Surfaced writing `tpy.atomic`.
- **[feature] Mutable (non-readonly) property getter -- unblocks a faithful lazy-cached `.content`.** Every `@property` getter is unconditionally marked `auto_readonly` (`tpyc/parse/parser.py:1792`), so `sema/method_expansion.py` clones it into a const + mutable overload pair and the body must type-check as BOTH -- a getter that mutates/caches into `self` (the requests `Response.content` lazy-drain idiom) fails the const clone ("Cannot call non-readonly method on readonly reference"). No current spelling produces a mutable-only property. Add one: a property getter that mutates self skips the const clone (or an explicit opt-out marker). Semantic cost to weigh in design: a mutable-only property makes `readonly[T].prop` uncallable (the getter demands a mutable receiver) -- the readonly system forbids read-mutation on purpose, so this is a deliberate narrowing, not a free win. Touches parser + `sema/method_expansion` + registration (type-system-adjacent) -> architectural, own `/tpy-add-feature` design. Payoff: `tplib.requests` `Response.content`/`.text`/`.json()` could auto-drain a `stream=True` body (matching real requests) instead of the current declared divergence (a streamed `.content` stays permanently `b""` -- never auto-filled; full-body via `r.raw.read()` / `iter_content`). Generally useful for any lazy-cached property. Surfaced designing requests streaming.
- **[diagnostic] Warn that a truthiness test is statically ALWAYS TRUE -- and stop rejecting `not rec` in the same change.** `if p:` on a user record with neither `__bool__` nor `__len__`, or on any plain enum value, is unconditionally true, and TPy says nothing: the user probably meant `p is not None`, an `== Member` compare, or a hook the type never defines. Sema ALREADY computes this exact fact, just to the opposite end -- it HARD-ERRORS on `not rec` ("Invalid operand type for 'not'") where CPython accepts it, the rejects-valid entry in BUGS.md. So one change closes both halves of the asymmetry: accept `not rec` (CPython-faithful) and warn that the test is always true, from the same no-truthiness-hook verdict. Design questions to settle FIRST (this is a new warning -- `/tpy-add-feature`, not a drive-by): (a) does it fire on an operand narrowed past None (`if p is None: return` then `if p:` -- always-true as a CONSEQUENCE of the narrowing, which defensive code writes deliberately; witness `tests/cases/bool/bool_narrowed_optional` `plain_if`), (b) generic `if x:` on a `T` monomorphized to a plain record would warn per instantiation, un-actionably, in code the author cannot change, (c) there is no escape hatch spelling today -- `bool(p)` is itself rejected for value types without `__bool__` (its own BUGS.md entry), so "I meant it" has no form but deleting the check. Churns `diag.txt` + `# tpyc: ok` annotations at roughly 19 corpus sites (the always-true renders, greppable as `static_cast<void>(...), true`). Belongs beside `OPTIONAL_VALUE_TRUTHINESS_WARNING` (`tpyc/diagnostics.py`, raised from `tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`), the existing member of this diagnostic family. Surfaced by the user reviewing the always-true renders after the constant-fold operand fix.
- **[thir] Enum-typed module globals are not seeded for reads, so any read falls the whole body back.** `_readonly_global_type` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:1300`) admits scalars, char, str/bytes, `Ptr` and value-tuples to the read-only value-global family but leaves "unions/enums unprobed", so `gc: Color = Color.RED` plus ANY read (`return gc`, `if gc:`) rejects at `name.global_read` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:2396`) -- while an `int32` global routes bare and a plain-record global routes through the pointer-slot family. An enum is a value type whose read renders bare, so admitting it looks like a small widening, but "unprobed" is a not-yet-verified marker rather than an oversight, so it needs its own byte-diff verification (unions likewise, and they are the harder half). Pre-existing; newly reachable from truthiness position because the plain-enum always-true arm now lowers its operand instead of returning early, so `if gc:` meets the same gate that `return gc` always did. Repro: `gc: Color = Color.RED` at module scope + `def f() -> Color: return gc` -- lower it and read `_thir_reject_reason` (`name.global_read`); swap the annotation to `int32` or a plain record and it routes. Surfaced removing the truthiness purity predicate.
- **[thir] Per-case blockers for the truthiness cases left ratchet-exempt (from the constant-fold operand fix) -- THREE OF THE FIVE ARE NOW ROUTED, two remain.** `bool/truthy_call_effects`, `match/guard_truthy_call` and `enum/enum_truthy_call_int` all flipped in the 2026-07-27 truthiness wave (`_ExprUse.truthy_discard` for the `@property` returning `Own[T]`; `_lower_match_guard` now going through `_lower_truthy`; the IntEnum shape gate deleted). STILL BLOCKED, each ONE construct and already measured: `typed_dict/typed_dict_in_call` -> `stmt.if:if.cond_binop.in.str_record_f1` (the TypedDict `in` fold is un-migrated -- the one of the three fold sites whose AST fix has no THIR mirror, since the construct rejects wholesale); `bool/truthy_walrus_binding` FLIPPED 2026-08-03 (long-tail wave 4: the ALWAYS_TRUE walrus mode + the enum first-decl walrus row).
- **[thir] The value-position `and`/`or` bare-literal truthiness form has no THIR shape, and no case for its temp-hoisted LHS.** `_gen_logical_value` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py`) calls `_truthy_for_rendered` WITHOUT an operand, so the fold emits the bare literal -- correct, because the LHS is either a bare name or already materialized into a temp before the truthiness test runs. THIR cannot reach that shape at all: a value-position `and`/`or` with a non-scalar/non-str LHS rejects at `valuesel.lhs_truthy` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` ~1466), which is why `THIRTruthy.operand` and `THIREnumWrap.operand` could be tightened to required and their bare-literal emit branches deleted. **The two are coupled**: widening `valuesel.lhs_truthy` to enum / plain-record LHS types needs an operand-less THIR form restored first, or the mirror cannot reproduce the AST's bare literal. Coverage gap on the AST side too -- `operators/logical_and_or_value` and `operators/logical_record_or_rvalue` both use a `TpyName` LHS (`use_lhs_temp` False), so the temp-hoisted variant of the always-true type family is unwitnessed. Safe by construction today (no dual-path divergence is possible while THIR rejects the position). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the constant-fold operand fix.
- **[thir][hygiene] Classifier/helper param order is inconsistent across siblings -- swap-prone once `_WalkState` is gone.** Removing the `_WalkState` bundle spread its fields (`declared`, `pointers`, `rebind_slots`, `storage_tuple_locals`, `narrowed`) as separate positional params across the remaining expression/comprehension helpers and the `for`/`match` classifiers in `tpyc/thir/lower/`, but the order is not uniform between siblings (e.g. `checks.py:_ref_field_write_ok(stmt, declared, analyzer, pointers, narrowed, prescan)` vs `_optional_record_field_write_ok(stmt, declared, pointers, analyzer, narrowed, prescan)` -- `analyzer`/`pointers`/`narrowed` swap positions). Since `pointers` and `narrowed` are both bare `set[str]`, nothing catches an accidental swap at a future call site. Options: (a) unify the arg order across the family, or (b) introduce a small FROZEN read-only carrier (a `NamedTuple`/frozen dataclass of the same fields, no `branch_copy`/mutation methods -- distinct from the deleted mutable `_WalkState`). The carrier-vs-flat call is a design choice; some of the ordering skew is pre-existing carry-forward. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of `thir-lower-reject-expressions`.
- **[thir][hygiene] `THIRGenExpr` stores pre-rendered C++ strings where the sibling node keeps facts structured.** `_lower_genexpr` (`tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py`) pre-renders `binding_cpp` (via `loop_var_binding`) and both `iife_captures`/`inner_captures` lists (via `_genexpr_captures`, called twice) into `THIRGenExpr` at lowering time, whereas the sibling `THIRComprehension` carries the equivalent facts structured (`var`, `elem_type`) and defers the `loop_var_binding`/capture render to `_emit_comprehension` in `emit.py`. Both nodes already store SOME rendered cpp (`container_cpp`, `slot_cpp`), so this is a lower/emit boundary-placement inconsistency, not a bug -- byte-identical today. Refactor to carry `var`/`elem_type` + a structured captured-names tuple and build the capture list once in `_emit_genexpr`. Non-trivial (moves the capture logic across the boundary). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the generator-expression cells.
- **[thir][post-deletion] Replace the pre-rendered-string node fields with structured type refs once the AST codegen is deleted.** The whole rendered-cpp family on THIR nodes -- `THIRCall.template_args_cpp`, `THIRMethodCall.method_targs_cpp`, `THIRVarDecl.cpp_type`, `THIRArgTemp.cpp_type`, `variant_cpp`/`callee_cpp`/the `THIRGenExpr` fields above -- stores resolver-rendered strings because (a) the spelling needs the lowering-time `TypeResolver` (cross-module qualification, pending-view resolution) and emit is deliberately a resolver-free printer (`_EmitState` carries only counters/sinks), and (b) rendering at lowering through the same functions the AST uses is what makes the byte-diff invariant checkable. AFTER the AST path is deleted that constraint relaxes: move the family to structured `TpyType` refs on the nodes and give the emitter a render context (a resolver handle or render callback), one boundary-move pass over the whole family -- not field-by-field, which would split sibling nodes across two conventions. Aligns with CLAUDE.md's LSP tie-breaker (introspectable/printable type representations) and IR_DESIGN's post-deletion end state (emitter becomes a printer over a real IR). User-agreed 2026-07-16 during the generics-foundation review.
- **[thir] Protocol boundary -- the rungs the param/arg cells deliberately left out.** The bare protocol param, the protocol-receiver method call, the protocol call-arg slot (Adapter / RefAdapter / concrete + `auto` rvalue temps) and `len(p)` are routed. Excluded, roughly by remaining mass: (a) **`Own[P]` params and returns** (~16 bodies, incl. 2 resumable) -- `T_p&&` / `std::unique_ptr<P>` slots whose reads move, whose method calls render `->` (`_receiver_is_own_dyn`), and whose call args take `::tpy::make_adapter<Base>` / `std::make_unique` (`_gen_dynamic_protocol_own_arg`); (b) **protocol RETURNS** (~8) -- `auto` (structural) / `Base&` (@dynamic); (c) **resumable protocol params** (21 blocked at `res.param_type`) -- need the two-phase `decltype` frame capture (`thir/lower/resumable.py`, `protocol_param_template_name`); (d) **`Optional[P]` / protocol-union params and arg slots** -- `_gen_protocol_arg`'s typed-null / `&(...)` / `optional_to_ptr` renders; (e) **protocol SUBSCRIPT** (~16 at `subscript.recv_type`) -- NOT uniform: `items[0]` emits `::tpy::__getitem__(items, 0)` while `items[i]` emits `items[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)]`, so the rung must first establish which dispatch the AST picks; (f) **protocol slots in the record-method arg loop** (`_record_method_call_supported` still rejects them as `method.arg_shape`, though `_gen_method_call`'s user-record loop does run the protocol pre-arms); (g) **for-each over a protocol iterable**, which rides the `stmt.for_each` rock (the corpus's #1 blocker, 333b/184sh). Landed on `thir-protocol-boundary`.
- **[thir][telemetry] `return`-of-record-source fallback reasons lost their sub-tags in the gate-removal inlining.** The inlined `TpyReturn` record-source reject in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` (~2056) now routes both the `Own`-typed-source-at-a-borrow-slot case (old `return.record_source.own_at_borrow`) and the non-F1-record bare-name source (old `return.record_source.name_notf1`) through the generic `_record_source_reject_detail` bucket (`return.record_source.name.{slot}`). Correctness is unaffected (accept/reject boolean unchanged; byte-diff green), but `$THIR_FALLBACK_JSON` triage can no longer distinguish these two return-source fallback causes. Restore the two `note_detail` calls at the collapsed branch if the distinction is still wanted for porting triage. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + architecture-fit) of `thir-read-only-admission`.
- **[thir][test-gap] Resumable leaf-shape rejects moved into `_lower_stmt_dispatch` are exercised only incidentally.** The predictive `_leaf_shape_reject`/`_gate_leaf` scan in `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py` was deleted; its rejects (`res.leaf_field_write` gated on `scope.in_branch`, `res.unpack`, `res.leaf_try`, `res.leaf_with`, `res.leaf_match`, `res.nested_def`; `res.leaf_return` ROUTED 2026-07-17) now fire inline in `_lower_stmt_dispatch` under `lc.resumable_leaf_mode`. No dedicated case pins the moved reject (e.g. a name-write nested two levels inside an `if` in an `async def` with no `await` in that branch); coverage rides on pre-existing `no_thir`-marked `tests/cases/async/*` cases being re-diffed by the overlay. Add a minimal case so the moved invariant is explicit, not incidental. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `thir-structural-plans`.
- **[thir] Assert emit idempotence directly -- the harness depends on it but nothing states it.** The THIR overlay re-emits each local user module a second time, so "a module emits identically every time" is now load-bearing for the whole corpus -- yet it is an emergent property of the overlay, not a tested invariant. `recursive_alias_cpp_names` violated it (a definer rendered its own generic recursive alias qualified on a second pass) and the overlay caught it only incidentally; the bug was not a THIR divergence at all and reproduced with THIR fully off. `tpyc/test_compiler.py::TestCodegenStateIsolation` pins the one map. Generalize: double-emit every module on the AST path and byte-compare, so the next per-module codegen map that forgets its reset fails directly instead of masquerading as a THIR bug. Needs no THIR, and covers cases THIR never touches. Surfaced by `fix-recursive-alias-name-leak`.

## THIR: a match arm in a void-returning body is rejected (2026-08-30)

**A match arm in a `-> None` body is rejected** (`body:stmt.match`). Isolated rather than assumed
-- the same arm in an `-> int32` body lowers, and the flat spelling of the
same match is rejected identically, so the trigger is the void return and not
the pattern shape or a container binding. It bites case authors directly: a
new case whose match arm returns nothing does not compile, so the fixture has
to be reshaped to return a value. That is a constraint on what the corpus can
express, which makes it worth closing rather than routing around.

## THIR: narrowed-name match subjects are rejected (2026-08-30)

`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py` returns `None` -- reject -- whenever a match
subject is a name in the narrowing map (`subj.name in narrowed`), and it does
so across ALL tiers, not just resumable ones. Verified with a plain sync
`def` holding a nested narrowed match: it is rejected with `body:stmt.match`,
no generator or async involved. That is ordinary valid Python that compiled
correctly before the deletion and is a compile error now.

Why nothing caught it before: no corpus case carries the shape, so every gate
was silent on it.

Sequencing note, now moot on its first half: the AST's own narrowed-subject
guard also rejected valid code, so the lane was ordered AST-first to avoid
mirroring a known-wrong rejection. That emitter is gone; what remains is
lowering the shape here, and it is wave-sized rather than a patch.

The lane must also re-check the non-lvalue capture gate in
`_select_match_route`. That gate guards a real use-after-free (a frame field
holding the address of a by-value dispatch local), and today narrowed subjects
never reach it because the reject above fires first. Routing them removes that
backstop. The gate's non-lvalue-only condition is believed to be the correct
final shape -- a narrowed subject that is an lvalue is frame-rooted, so it
should be admitted -- but that belief is untested precisely because nothing
reaches it, so it needs a witness once the shape routes.

## Architectural stabilization

- **[thir][cleanup] Two predicates answer "is element N of this tuple subscript a bare `T*`".** `_borrow_tuple_param_elem_subscript` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) answers it for a borrow-form tuple PARAM only and drives the sync REF_ALIAS decl's `deref=True`; `_subscript_yields_borrow_ptr` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) answers it for every receiver (param, borrow-form frame local, the borrowed half of a mixed slot, a mixed-own call) and now drives the resumable alias bind. Collapse the param-only one into the general one so the sync decl cannot miss a receiver shape the frame handles.
- **[perf] `_edges_reach_param` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`) scans every call edge of the callee per argument per call.** It replaced a truthiness check on `call_edges`; precompute the set of params the edges reach once, where `call_edges` is set (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`), so the per-call question is a set lookup -- an algorithmic-cliff site in a large body.
- **[codegen] A tuple-unpack target of a demoted `str` view copies twice:** `lbl, n = r.name, 1` with the view demoted renders `std::string __unpack_0_0 = r.name; std::string lbl = __unpack_0_0;`. Pre-existing for any owned tuple-unpack `str`; the rebind from the temp could move. **Stopped 2026-09-28:** the plain two-line spelling (`t = r.name` then `lbl = t`) copies twice too -- nothing moves an owned value-type local at its last use (sema's owned-local set excludes value types). The fix is a last-use move for owned value types, a move-model change, not a tuple-unpack row.

- **[codegen] A frame's `for` source is rendered twice; make the two renders one.** The frame struct spells the loop's fields off `decltype` of the source render produced at struct emission (`_for_source_aliases`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`, under the frame body scope with an unevaluated temp sink and the movable-locals seed), and the loop's setup renders the same expression again in its state block. They agree today because both go through the same lowered node, but nothing enforces it: a drift that keeps the value category (a frame-field shadow at the loop site, a `std::move` the seed grants at struct time that the loop site does not) would change the deduced type without a diagnostic, and `for_source_t`'s `static_assert` catches only an lvalue reaching an owning slot. Structural fix: render once, keep the render on the resumable state, and have the setup emit it (or compare its own render, modulo the `std::declval` stand-ins, and raise an internal error on a mismatch). The same holds for sema's const verdict on the source (`is_const_storage_source`, which still feeds the loop var's BINDING via `mark_frame_const`) against the C++-deduced field const: a disagreement is a loud C++ error in one direction and an over-restriction (a valid mutation refused) in the other; deriving the binding fact from the same source verdict removes the second answer. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective of the frame for-source unit, 2026-09-22.

Follow-ups from the 2026-09-14 architecture review at `4a28220b8b`,
recorded 2026-09-16. Retain TypeDef, THIR forms/conversions, shared argument
rows and the common frame machinery; make their contracts complete across
positions. These are design work items, not approved implementation choices.
Reproduce the motivating cases on the current tree before implementation.
Existing defects remain in BUGS.md; this section groups the architectural work.

- **[codegen] Nothing in the compiler may decide, or produce a form, by re-reading its own rendered C++ text.** A rendered string is an output, not an IR: a decision keyed on how something is SPELLED is disabled silently the day the spelling changes, and it is the consumer-re-derives-the-fact pattern THIR exists to remove. The frame emitter's cases are gone (the single-loop form, the re-dispatch-only case, the `inline` specifier of a small `__next__` are all decided on the CFG or passed into the renderer now). Still open, each in a different subsystem, none known to misbehave today: (1) `_merge_fn_into_header` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`) takes a rendered `template<...>` / `requires` header apart by string slicing (`tpl_line[len("template<"):-1]`, `startswith("requires")`) to splice the `Fn` template params in -- build the header from its parts once. (2) The adapter type qualifier in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/protocols.py` (`re.sub` over a rendered C++ type string, a lookbehind keeping it off names that already follow `::`) prefixes user type names with their namespace -- render the type qualified instead (`qualify_shadowed_nominals` is the existing mechanism for the same need). (3) Five `startswith("{")` tests on a rendered initializer recover "this is a brace literal" from the text: `tpyc/codegen_cpp/types.py` and `context.py` (one each), `tpyc/thir/emit.py` (three) -- the expression node, or the THIR literal node's own `typed_brace_cpp`, already knows. (4) `_slot_spellable` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) inspects a C++ type STRING for a trailing `&` or a leading `auto` to decide whether `std::optional<T>` is spellable -- ask the type. (5) `tpyc/thir/emit.py` builds a field-name suffix by stripping `.` and `*` out of a rendered parent expression. (6) The one that stays for now: `_CodeLineCounter` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`) sizes a generator's `__next__` in rendered code lines, skipping `//` lines so the verdict does not depend on whether source echo is on, for the 40-line inline-in-`_inl.hpp` limit. Size is a property of the output and the limit was measured in those units (the comment at `_INLINE_NEXT_MAX_LINES`), so replacing it means re-measuring against a structural size (CFG statements + terminators). Found 2026-09-21 by an audit of `tpyc/codegen_cpp`, `tpyc/thir` and `tpyc/interop` for `re.` / `startswith` / `endswith` / `replace` / line splitting applied to rendered text.
- **[design] A borrow-returning zero-arg METHOD call is a chain hop like a `@property` getter, and is not admitted as one.** The rooted-lvalue walkers (`chain_root_name` in `tpyc/prescan.py`, `_lvalue_chain_root` / `_chained_field_receiver_ok` in `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) walk through a property hop -- the read is a getter call that names storage the root owns, and `_lvalue_chain_hop_ok` proves per hop that it does, through `is_rvalue_source`. The identical proof holds for `o.made_m().pair` and the spelled call is refused anyway, so `a, b = o.made.pair` compiles while `a, b = o.made_m().pair` rejects `stmt.tuple_unpack` -- the same property-vs-method asymmetry the property-read normalization removed everywhere else. Admitting it is a widening of the chain vocabulary for every consumer of those walkers (the tuple-unpack source, the field-receiver ladder, the for-each iterable, the alias map), so it needs its own byte-diff over the corpus and its own case rather than riding a refactor. Keep the per-hop question where it is: the hop is admitted because it is not an rvalue, never because of the shape it wears. Three more rows are the same interim class -- admitted for a getter, refused for the spelled twin, for want of a call arm rather than a rule: `_is_len_call` (`len(f.items)`), the native container argument (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`), and `_field_over_call_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`, the merged successor of the property-only `_field_over_property_call_ok`: a field read off an accessor hop). `_augassign_recv_is_accessor` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) is the same walk once more: it descends a receiver chain and a subscript INDEX looking for an accessor hop, and it is the one that HOLDS rather than admits -- so when the walkers widen to the spelled twin, this one widens with them and the aug-assign hold has to cover both spellings or the evaluation-order decision covers neither. Two more joined them, both in the resumable YIELD-slot ladder (`tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py`), which has a field arm and an accessor arm and no call arm: the BORROW arm admits `yield self.<getter>` and refuses `yield self.<method>()` with the identical return convention, and the OWN arm does the same through `_own_return_getter_shape` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) beside its `_own_return_call_shape` sibling, which is spelled for a `TpyCall`. Both are master's verdict pair on both spellings, pinned by the `self_yield__{rec,items,own}__*` rows of the property x position table. The OWN pair is the one that says how this collapses: widening `isinstance(yv_src, TpyCall)` to accept a method call in that arm admits the spelled twin and lets the two predicates merge into one -- do it when the twin is MEASURED, not before, since nothing has said what `yield self.own_m()` should render. They widen with the walkers, in one change and one byte-diff. The with-manager disjunct that was a fourth member is gone: `is_lvalue` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) now answers the accessor question itself, so `manager_borrowed` asks one predicate again. Raised by the property-read normalization, 2026-09-18.

- **[design] Four positions REJECT a storage-ref `@property` read where a lift would render it.** A getter whose return is a pointer-repr `Optional[T]` hands back the FIELD's `std::optional<T>` BY REFERENCE (the storage-ref convention), which no plain method can return, so the positions that were never taught it are located rejects rather than renders: `print(s.o)` and `s.o.bump()` and `s.o.x` stop at `method.fi_kind` / `method.ret_type`, and a ternary arm at `expr.ifexpr` (`ifexpr.getter_arm_const_source`, which now covers RECORD and CONTAINER getter arms too -- they emitted `Rec& v = ((c) ? (s.r()) : (s.r()))` off a const receiver and failed the C++ build). That is master's verdict and no wrong code -- the branch's gate exists precisely to stop them spelling `print_optional(std::optional&)`, `deref_check(std::optional<Rec>&)` and `Rec* v = (c ? optional : optional)`, all of which failed the C++ build. The render each wants is the one the FIELD spelling already takes, over the getter call instead of the member read: `optional_to_ptr(s.o())` at the ternary and the print wrap, `deref_optional_check(s.o()).x` at the unproven receiver and the field-through. Three of the four already have their admission gate asking the convention (`reads_storage_form_optional` answers for both node kinds); what is missing is the lift arm each position renders. DEPENDS ON `BUGS.md#getter-source-const-not-tracked`: the lift was built and withdrawn because `optional_to_ptr` off a CONST receiver yields `const T*` while the position spells the pointee from the declared type, so it traded one ill-formed render for another. Lands with a condensed case `records/property_storage_ref_positions` -- Optional / record / container getters at print, method receiver, field-through, both ternary arms, if/while/assert truthiness and `is None`, each section mutation-observing with output == CPython. Probes `/tmp/agents/t1review/min_*.py` and `sweep*/`. Raised by the property-read normalization review, 2026-09-18.

- **[design] Narrowing over a pure zero-arg getter.** `if w.num is not None:` does NOT narrow `w.num` below it, and must not until two things exist. A getter is a CALL: nothing kills the fact when what backs it changes, so a global reassigned between the guard and the read keeps the key "proven" (probe `/tmp/agents/t1r2s/y9_global.py`), which needs a purity rule for the accessor and a kill rule for the key -- the same invalidation vocabulary the place work owes `BUGS.md#iter-borrow-place-needs-hops`. And the reads under a narrow do not lift: a narrowed `Optional[int32]` getter in a boolean context renders `if (z.num())`, the bare `has_value()`, so `if z.num:` prints truthy for 0 and `assert z.num` passes where CPython raises -- SILENTLY -- and `w.num + 1` spells `add_check<int32_t>(w.num(), 1)` over a `std::optional`, which does not compile. Both halves were measured on a branch that had the key speller and the resolver, and both are why it was reverted rather than patched (probes `/tmp/agents/r2/nt*.py`). The spelled METHOD twin is not narrowed either, so nothing is asymmetric today. Doing it means: a purity predicate over the getter body, a kill rule keyed on everything the body reads, and the storage-form lift at every read position under the narrow. Raised by the property-read normalization review round 2, 2026-09-18.

- **[design] A generator-returning `@property` is refused where the spelled method twin is admitted.** `for v in b.items:` with `def items(self) -> Iterator[int32]` stops at the getter call's own result gate (`expr.method_call:method.fi_kind`, pinned by `tests/cases/generators/error_property_generator_iterable`), while the identical generator METHOD iterable compiles -- the member-gen-call classifier passes `generator_ok=True` at the iterable position and the getter read does not reach it. That is a property-only reject under the one-node-kind invariant: the read IS a call, so it should take the same classifier. Needs its own byte-diff (the row changes which bodies route) and a happy case replacing the error one. Raised by the property-read normalization review, 2026-09-18.

- **[design] `forms=` REPLACES a sink's row, so a site that wants one extra verdict has to restate the whole row -- an additive `also=` channel would remove 21 restatements.** `_ExprUse.forms` is the site's override for the sink's `_POS_FORMS` row, and it is total: a site that spells `forms=` for the verdict it cares about silently drops every other verdict the row granted. That is how five transient sites came to REFUSE a lend their own sink's row admits (round 4's C15: a print argument, an f-string interpolation, a field-read receiver, an arithmetic operand, a coercion inner), each fixed by OR-ing `_LEND_OK` back in by hand. Measured 2026-09-18, and the metric is `forms=` OCCURRENCES (the keyword spelled at a call site), not distinct sinks or distinct call sites: 99 occurrences in `tpyc/thir/lower/*.py` outside `context.py`, of which 14 name `_LEND_OK` -- every one of them at a TRANSIENT sink, restating a verdict the row already granted -- and 3 name `_lend_forms`, the ARGUMENT sink's verdict, which is the callee's (`arg_lend_ok`) and not the row's at all. Shape: a second field beside `forms`, `also: frozenset[SinkForm] = frozenset()`, with `admits` reading `form in ((row if forms is None else forms) | also)`; a site then spells `also=_LEND_OK` and never has to know what else its sink grants. All 14 restatements would go; the 3 argument sites stay as they are, since a callee-derived verdict REPLACES the row on purpose. What moves with it: `tpyc/thir/test_arg_table.py`'s partition test asserts over `_POS_FORMS` alone and would have to read the pair, and the `forms=`-literal scan in the same file (the guard that no site re-admits `DYING_SOURCE_LEND` at a binding sink) would key on `also=` instead. Not urgent -- the 15 restatements are correct today and the scan now catches a missing one -- but the next form with more than one consumer pays the same tax. Raised as S12 by the property-read normalization review round 4, 2026-09-18.

- **[design] Re-analysing a property read builds a THROWAWAY field-access node to resolve through.** A body re-analyses expressions (a chained comparison's middle operand, the receiver of a write target, a lambda body under an overload dry-run), and a property read has already BECOME its getter call by then; the getter is pruned from the record's method table, so re-running method resolution on it would reject a read that resolved. `SemanticExpressions.analyze_expr` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) therefore mints a synthetic `TpyFieldAccess` carrying the same receiver and name and runs `_analyze_field_access` over it, stamping the type onto the real node (the stamp is load-bearing: a `trial_scope` rolls the type table back, and without it the lambda-under-dispatch position lost its admission). It reads back nothing, so it cannot be a cache read, and it cannot re-enter method resolution either -- but a synthetic node re-entering the FIELD path also re-runs the whole access analysis (narrowing lookups, borrow registration, the settable-property split) for a read that is no longer a field access, which is the wrong shape even though it is idempotent today. The fix is to share the getter-TYPING tail of `_analyze_field_access` as a helper both the first pass and the re-analysis call with `(receiver, name)`, leaving the field-specific work behind; the probe node then has nothing to carry. The one interim of the property-read normalization with no entry of its own. Raised by the property-read normalization review (W12/W18), 2026-09-18.


- **[design] A borrow DECLARATION is credited as a mutation of its source, so a read-only body pays `T&` where `const T&` is correct.** `_is_borrowing_auto_readonly_accessor` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) marks the RECEIVER mutated at the decl of any local bound off a borrowing `@auto_readonly` accessor, whether or not anything is ever written through the alias. Every `@property` getter is force-marked `auto_readonly`, so the rule now reaches property reads too and two corpus renders lost their const: `tests/cases/records/own_property_value_decl` emits `void use_view(Holder& h)` for a body that only iterates the view it read, and `tests/cases/records/property_union` emits `void describe(Canvas& c)` plus the mutable `::tpy::Union<Circle*, Square*>` / `to_ptr_variant` lift for a body that only prints. Both bodies are read-only; the marking is pre-emptive, because locals bind non-const references by default and the decl cannot see whether a later statement writes. The fix is to root the mutation on the WRITE -- the alias's first mutation, which the borrow graph already relates back to the source -- rather than on the bind, for methods and getters alike: one home, so the property face cannot drift from its spelled twin. Until then the pessimization is accepted rather than re-introduced as a property-only exception. **The ptr-Optional and union getter decls are the same widening one form deeper, and there it is SILENT** (2026-09-18, review round 4): `v = h.opt` on an `Optional[R]` getter emits `void f(Holder& h)` and `R* v` where the const twin returns `const R*`, and `v = c.shape` on a union getter emits `::tpy::Union<Circle*, Square*>` where the const receiver's twin returns `::tpy::Union<const Circle*, const Square*>` -- and because the const-borrow inference resolves the read to the MUTABLE `@auto_readonly` clone, no call site ever breaks and no diagnostic fires. The ternary flavour of the same disagreement is loud instead (`BUGS.md#getter-source-const-not-tracked`), which is the whole difference between them: the ternary has no decl to credit, so the two halves contradict each other visibly. It is NOT a one-line fix at the read. Picking the const twin when the body never mutates through the alias needs the body-wide fact the decl cannot have (the decl runs before the writes it must see), which is exactly the WRITE-rooted credit above; doing it at the read alone would flip the parameter to `const T&` while the decl's own `T&` binding still asks for the mutable one, trading a silent pessimization for a build failure. **The same credit costs an ordinary METHOD its inferred const face** (2026-09-18, review round 5): the mark is `mark_param_mutated` on the receiver ROOT, so a `@readonly`-eligible method whose body only binds a borrow getter and reads through it is credited with mutating `self` and emits without `const`. It is masked today -- sema's readonly gate rejects a decl off a borrowing accessor inside an explicitly `@readonly` method before the credit is reached, so only the INFERRED face can lose, and no call site breaks when it does. It unmasks the moment the gate is relaxed, so the write-rooted credit owns both faces or neither. Raised by the property-read normalization, 2026-09-18.

- **[design] A lambda is a nested `def` and must be ONE construct in sema: one capture rule, one escape rule, one warning.** A nested `def` goes through `_analyze_nested_def`, which stamps `captured_names` / `nonlocal_names` on the node and lets `_finalize_nested_def_escapes` decide move, copy, or copy-with-warning; a lambda bound to a `Callable` local takes its own capture path in the lambda analysis (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`), copies by default, and never reaches the escaping-closure warning -- so `read: Callable[[], int32] = lambda: len(data)` renders `[data]` silently where the identical `def` warns (`BUGS.md#callable-local-lambda-copies-capture-silently`). `TpyLambda.children()` also returns `[]`, so every sema walker that enumerates node kinds sees a def's body and not a lambda's: the last-use scan needed an explicit `into_lambdas` flag, a lambda inside a sibling def is invisible to the capture computation (`BUGS.md#nested-def-lambda-only-capture-missing`), and the transitive-capture entries (`BUGS.md#escaping-closure-sibling-capture-dangles`, `nested-lambda-no-transitive-capture`) each have a lambda spelling. Same shape as the property-read entry above: two node kinds carrying one meaning, every position taught twice. Design: normalize in sema so a lambda IS a nested def with an expression body (one node kind after analysis, or one analysis path both nodes enter), keep the genuine differences explicit (a lambda has no name and no statements; parameter types come from context), and delete the lambda-only capture path and the `into_lambdas` flag. Measure first: list every consumer that branches on `TpyLambda` vs `TpyNestedDef` and classify it as "would be the def arm" vs "genuinely lambda-only". Acceptance: `tests/cases/nested_def/escaping_local_copy`'s `make_lambda_reader` section starts warning like its def sibling; the `nested_def/` and `lambda/` corpora byte-identical otherwise. Nothing else touches lambda capture until this lands. Raised by the user 2026-09-18 reviewing the nested-def identity fix.
- **[codegen][sema] An unreferenced nested `def` is dead code: emit nothing for it, and let it contribute no later use to the escaping-closure rule.** A nested def that no statement, expression or sibling names after its definition is never run by CPython either, so dropping it changes no observable behaviour (TPy rejects defaults on nested defs, so there is no definition-time effect to keep); today it is emitted as an unused lambda AND counted as a later use of every local it reads, which forces a copy and a `copies local ... preventing move` warning on a closure that could have moved -- the `make_named_not_called` section of `tests/cases/nested_def/escaping_local_copy` pins that over-approximation deliberately ("proving it is unreachable is not this pass's job"). The test is REFERENCED, not called: a def passed as a value, stored, or returned is live. Reachability across siblings is the fixpoint `_names_used_after` already runs, so the fact is one pass away; emit side: skip the lambda. Acceptance: that section flips to a move with no warning and the emitted body loses the dead lambda; a referenced-but-never-called sibling keeps the warning. Raised by the user 2026-09-18 reviewing the nested-def identity fix; do after the lambda/def unification above so the liveness rule is written once for both spellings.
- **[design][first] Reconcile generic Optional callable representations.**
  Start with `def echo[T](o: T | None) -> T | None: return o`
  (`BUGS.md#generic-optional-return-committed-to-pointer`). The parameter uses
  `opt_param_t<T>` while the return commits to `T*`; parameter substitution
  strips the representation stamp that general substitution preserves.
  Define one consistent slot policy for declaration, return lowering, call
  result and receiving local, extending the existing renderers/traits and
  `THIRFormConvert`. Preserve alias returns for reference T and owned results
  for value T; replacing every pointer with `std::optional<T>` would copy
  reference types. Validate scalar/reference/view instantiations, direct and
  field returns, const sources, and generic/concrete twins across free calls
  and methods. This does not require MIR.

- **[design][first] Unify source attribution for mutation facts.** Direct
  writes follow `loop_var_iterable` as well as binding/borrow provenance;
  `_arg_storage_roots` for mutation-call edges reads only the borrow graph.
  Use one source-root query for both, preserving all roots of re-seated
  aliases and vararg packs. Start with `for p in ps: touch(p)` versus a
  direct field write, across list/varargs and ordinary/generator bodies;
  then check local const decisions against finalized call effects. Reuse
  the existing parameter-const verdict and the recently consolidated
  `const_frame_bindings`. Attribution is not invalidation: do not turn every
  source relationship into an invalidating loan. Coordinate with the
  import-component propagation item under "Deferred to THIR/MIR &
  workload-gated"; evaluation order and missing edges are separate problems.

- **[design] Complete the facts consumed by shared frame machinery.** Share
  concrete protocol-subframe deduction between inline await and generator
  delegation, deriving specialization and capture requirements from lowered
  arguments rather than bare annotations. Preserve readonly/borrow facts at
  the comprehension source-to-element boundary (the genexpr face closed when
  genexprs became frames: the frame's source param carries the readonly); do
  not propagate source readonly blindly onto arbitrary computed results. Pin the previously working
  protocol-delegation program lost when the single-yield shortcut was removed.
  These bounded repairs need not wait for the larger identity decision.
  Producer binding identity and movement belong to the existing "Producers
  are movable only while unstarted" and "Generator expressions lower to
  frames" entries below. Generators settled on ALIAS (2026-09-23: a second
  name is the same object); coroutines and genexpr locals are still open.

- **[design][MIR] Make loan extents and temporary owners explicit.** Extend
  the place/loan direction in `docs/IR_DESIGN.md`, starting with one scoped
  example such as match-arm bindings and direct/callee-mediated subject
  mutation. Compare advisory results with existing checks, covering missed
  hazards and absence of warnings after the borrow ends. Keep attribution
  separate from invalidation; OPAQUE match loans intentionally suppress
  invalidation checks whose extent the general graph cannot express.
  Temporary materialization should eventually carry its owner and required
  lifetime into lowering. This is architectural work, not a prerequisite
  for the Optional or mutation-edge fixes above.

- **[tooling] Freeze a small capability corpus across revisions.** Select
  representative existing cases and review witnesses; retain their sources
  unchanged when comparing revisions. Record correct output, wrong output,
  TPy rejection, compiler crash and C++ build failure separately. Include
  mutation-based alias checks, generic/concrete twins and protocol delegation;
  inspect materializations where immutable copies are output-invisible.
  Complement the existing rewrite-harness/copy-counter plans below. Growing
  test counts and shrinking reject counts alone do not measure retained
  behavior, and the sampled historical audit is not a regression-rate estimate.

- **[design][later] Carry admission decisions into argument construction.**
  The shared argument table returns bool, so lowering still reconstructs
  some source/slot choices. Trial a typed decision for one existing row/family,
  carrying its conversion and temporary requirement into construction; extend
  the current table rather than add another registry. Preserve row order,
  witness accounting, rejection behavior and conditional evaluation. Measure
  cost before generalizing. Success means deleting an independent decision,
  not moving the same conditionals to another file. Composite str/bytes view
  policies are a separate, lower-priority extension: coordinate with
  `BUGS.md#str-tuple-element-local-owned` and the existing tuple-view work,
  retaining ownership where values escape.

## Next
- **[tuple][gap] A tuple literal member that is a ternary of FIELD or SUBSCRIPT arms gets no copy rule.** `_ternary_member_copies` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) classifies NAME arms only, so `h.q = (1, g.c if k else C(5))` is not warned. Latent today: those arms reject in the lowering; the check must widen to every lvalue arm before they lower.
- **[tuple][gap] A lambda body returning a tuple literal into `Fn[..., tuple[.., Own[C]]]` gets no `Own`-element rule.** `app(lambda: (1, c))` for `def app(f: Fn[[], tuple[int32, Own[C]]])` has no member check -- the lambda's return is not routed through the RETURN sink the def body takes. Latent today: the body rejects at `expr.lambda:lambda.body:expr.tuple_literal` (probe `/tmp/agents/rv1cp/p81_lambda_own.py`); the check must land before that shape lowers, or the borrowed `c` is copied silently.
- **[tuple][consistency] Over an `Iterable[Own[C]]` loop, the scalar yield is silent where the tuple yield warns.** `for c in cs: yield (c, 1)` into `Iterator[tuple[Own[C], int32]]` warns "copies C into owned storage (tuple element 0)", while the scalar `for c in cs: yield c` into `Iterator[Own[C]]` is silent -- although it copies too (the `@nocopy` twin errors "cannot copy non-copyable type 'C' into owned storage"). The scalar's silence is the consuming-iteration suppression of the `BUGS.md` entry "The `Iterable[Own[T]]` copy-warning suppression is position-agnostic"; decide whether consuming iteration moves the element (then the tuple member should not warn either) or copies (then the scalar should warn). Probes `/tmp/agents/rv1cg/ownit.py`, `ownit_nc_s.py`.
- **[codegen] Generator expressions are frames: what is left.** Landed 2026-09-20 (docs/COMPREHENSION_DESIGN.md "Generator Expressions"): a genexpr is an anonymous generator function sema builds at the expression and analyzes once through the ordinary `_analyze_function` lifecycle; the closure emitter, `::tpy::genexpr_state` and `make_generator` are gone. Left over, none blocking: (1) `GenExprType` is still the sema type of the expression -- the consumers' protocol and overload rules key on it; typing the expression as the generator call it is would delete it. (2) NESTED `def` generators and nested `async def` are still rejected at sema, but the mechanism they were waiting for exists now: a frame takes reference captures as deduced-type forwarding slots (`TpyFunction.capture_params`, `_classify_params` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`). Lifting the reject needs its own matrix (`nonlocal`, a bound generator outliving the block it was created in, narrowing inside a body that runs later). (3) The in-place factory constructor is emitted for a genexpr's deduced source slot only; an `Own[T]` parameter of a non-movable `T` on a `def` generator or a coroutine could use the same constructor. (4) CONSUMER FUSION, the real speed lever: `sum` / `any` / `all` / `list` / `str.join` / a `for` head over a genexpr argument lower to a plain loop with no generator object at all. (5) The shapes that still reject: BUGS.md#genexpr-nested-source, BUGS.md#genexpr-source-needs-arg-temp (an owned source renders inside a by-reference lambda now, so threading the position's temp right is all it needs), a local bound to a genexpr, `min` / `max` / `in` / tuple-unpack over a genexpr, more than one `for` clause. (6) `TpyModule.has_header_genexpr` is decided by the parser, which cannot know a method's header-vs-source partition: a module whose only genexprs sit in methods too LARGE for the header still emits a `<mod>_inl.hpp` with no bodies (harmless; every consumer `.cpp` includes one empty file); a module whose only generators take `Fn` params does too, since their bodies are header templates now and `Compiler._compute_module_emits_inl` cannot see a param's resolved type). (7) The kept-genexpr rebind scan keeps its own line-based liveness range beside the last-use analysis and re-walks the body per hand-on round (BUGS.md#genexpr-kept-scan-consumer-binding has the fix shape).
- **[sema] One per-source loan-kind fact in place of `return_borrows_from` plus `held_whole_params`.** A genexpr's captures are the sources its frame keeps only as whole objects (ALIAS loan: growth allowed, moves gated), stamped as `FunctionInfo.held_whole_params` beside `return_borrows_from`; four readers (`_register_call_result_borrow`, `_provenance_storage`, `_call_result_sources`, the `calls.py` mutation-edge walk) re-check the subset. The loan kind per source index is one fact -- together with the per-callee ITER/ELEMENT choice `_register_call_result_borrow` makes off `iterator_source_callee` -- and belongs in the shape of `return_borrows_from` (index -> kind). The same fact would let a `def` generator stop filing an ITER loan on a param it only reads (`for v in g(xs, seen): seen.add(v)` warns today). Deferred as disproportionate to the genexpr loan fix: every reader of `return_borrows_from` changes.
- **[codegen perf] The single-loop emit form for `def` generators.** `_single_loop_plan` / `_emit_single_loop` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`) emit a frame whose only resume point is the head of its one loop as a plain loop with no `switch (__state)`, and closed the whole gap to the closure render for genexprs (gcc `user` 84 -> 77, `any` 85 -> 72 against the same frames without it; docs/COMPREHENSION_DESIGN.md "Emit shape" has both columns). It is written against the CFG shape, not against genexprs, but is ENABLED for `func.is_genexpr` only: a `def` generator of the same shape (`for x in xs: if p(x): yield f(x)`) would take it too, at the price of every such snapshot changing. Two things differ for a `def` generator: its body is lazy, so the loop seed stays at the first pull (the constructor seed is a genexpr-only right: CPython runs `iter(outermost)` where a genexpr is written), and its container may be mutated between creation and the first pull. Measure the snapshot churn first. This supersedes the "fall through to the next case" / `goto` loop-back lever in the perf entry below for that shape. The form is decided structurally (`_single_loop_plan`) and rendered through the transition seam (`_LoopForm`, `_transfer`), which today admits only the terminators a genexpr body has (`Fall`, `Branch`, `Yield`, `Unreachable`, the loop advance, no regions): widening it means teaching the seam a `def` generator's `return` (the `S_DONE` store in `_make_generator_resumable_return`) and deciding what a `try` region inside the loop does. A smaller leftover in the ordinary `switch` form: `_emit_state_machine` still RENDERS every case and then drops the ones `_redispatch_target` says only re-dispatch; now that the verdict is structural they need not be rendered at all, but `_emit_case` bumps `finally_guard_counter` before it renders, so skipping them renumbers the `__fin_ran_N` guards in every snapshot with a try region inside a frame -- do it together with another change that already moves those snapshots. The same widening would key the two `func.is_genexpr` gates beside it (`_builds_source_in_place`, the unpack holder's `aliasing_source`) on the source slot's classification instead.
- **[design] Producers are movable only while unstarted (Pin discipline, no allocation): what is left.** Landed 2026-09-23: every generator, genexpr and coroutine frame keeps its state in `::tpy::frame_state`, which deletes copy and assignment and panics on a move once the entry case has stored `S_DONE`, its first statement (pinned by `runtime/cpp/tests/test_frame_state_pin.cpp`); a generator object is a concrete frame type (`ConcreteGenType`) bound and aliased like a record, so a second name never copies; and a method call on a bound coroutine (`c.__poll__(w)`) marks it started, after which a move is a compile error. Left: (a) COROUTINE ALIASING. `d = c` still MOVES the handle (the documented divergence), so `d = c; create_task(c)` rejects where CPython accepts it. The design is the generator one: coroutine locals on the record slot model -- the name no longer owns an `std::optional<__coro_f>`; `await` polls through the binding with no reset; `create_task` moves out of the slot, only while unstarted -- with single-use tracked per possible OBJECT (the alias-rebind pass's origin sets), not per name, and the never-consumed / rebind-over-unconsumed warnings per object. About 75 sites key on the name-owns-the-slot shape: the sema bind rules, `THIRCoroHandleMove`, `coro_handle_slots`, the await `prebuilt_slot` payload, the protocol-arg `coro_handle` class. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. (b) The owning combinators are done (docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md "Temporaries at a lazy combinator"; the pinned residue is BUGS.md#separate-iter-temp-no-flush-slot): one over a random-access container is walked by POSITION and so is movable at any time, deliberately (an iterator pair seeded per pull cost 2x in a 20M-element `enumerate`), and one over a STARTED self-iterator source relies on the frame's move panic. Still open: the BORROWING flavors over a generator lvalue -- the eager `begin()` primes one element at `zip()` time, further from CPython (unobservable today: a bound `zip` of a generator does not lower). (c) Payoff: `gather` over concrete coroutines and `TaskGroup`-scoped tasks can embed child frames in the parent frame (allocation-free, like Rust's `join!`); `create_task` stays heap-backed and is documented as the one allocation. (d) Structure left by the generator half: `ConcreteGenType` inherits `is_protocol=True` from `Iterator`, so each structural-protocol consumer that must not treat a frame as a template slot carries its own `isinstance` exclusion (`_protocol_auto_slot`, `is_static_protocol_param`, `record_like`) -- audit the remaining `is_protocol` consumers, or make the concrete representation a first-class fact they read; `ExpressionAnalyzer._concrete_generator_call` and `StatementAnalyzer._concrete_coro_bind_type` derive the same frame identity at two sites (the call and the binding) and should be one helper decided at one site, together with (a); `frame_local_roots` (what a frame-holding local borrows) sits beside the argument-lending retention predicates (`arg_lend_ok` / `lends_from_dying_source`) and should share their borrow facts; the frame field order is the entry below; a generator with no spelled frame type aliases through a separate name-keyed `auto&` arm (`decl.iterator_object_alias`, keyed on `iterator_object_locals` by name -- the collision class of BUGS.md#frame-internal-names-collide) that goes away once such frames get a spelling. The lowering admits a generator-factory call through two channels at once: a type-keyed override (`generator_ok = generator_ok or builds_named_frame(e)` in `_free_callee_kind` / `_marker_call_kind`) that admits it at every sink, and the use channel's `use.admits(SinkForm.FRAME_FACTORY)`, which is dead for generators; one of the two should own it (`iterable_override` also reuses the ITERABLE-only `_member_gen_call_iterable_ok` for other sinks).
- **[design] Generator rebinds on the record path.** A name holding a generator is bound once today (BUGS.md#generator-rebind-rejects): `g = counter(0) ... g = counter(5)` is an error, and so are the tuple-unpack, `nonlocal` and inside-a-`for` rebinds. Records rebind through the same alias-rebind storage pass (`sema/alias_rebind.py`) -- in place when nothing holds the old object, a slot of the site's own otherwise -- and a generator object is already bound and aliased on that path, so a rebind can follow it too: the in-place write becomes `::tpy::frame_rebuild` (destroy + construct, since a frame is not assignable) and the own slot an `.emplace`, both of which the branch that introduced the ban had built and removed. The one generator-only rule: the new generator may borrow only storage that outlives the slot it fills (parameters, the receiver, module globals -- `_frame_slot_roots_ok` over sema's `frame_local_roots`), since a frame keeps references and runs a `finally` on destruction. Accepting this means accepting for generators the holder gap records already have -- a sync callee that hands the object to a task (BUGS.md#create-task-ref-param-escape) -- so it is a decision on whether generators may match records' soundness level, or wait for that gap to close (the Phase-2 callee escape fact). Deletes `error_frame_rebind`, `_unpack` and `_nonlocal`; `_while_iterating` stays (a running loop over the name). Gate: the ASan matrices (`/tmp/agents/narrow/m`, `/tmp/agents/narrow/m2`) with their rebind rows.
- **[sema] Admit a loop refill when the previous pass's generator is dead and closing it runs no user code.** A generator or async body rejects `for row in rows: xs = [row[0], row[1]]; g = inner(xs); for v in g: yield v` (`tpyc/sema/loop_frames.py`: the loop writes `xs`, which the previous pass's `g` borrows). When that `g` is not read again before its next binding (alias- and escape-closed, as the alias-rebind replay tracks) and `FunctionInfo.frame_close_runs_user_code` is False for everything it holds, destroying it never touches the storage it borrows: CPython destroys it at the rebind too, and no user code runs, so the write is unobservable and the everyday shape could compile whenever `inner` has no `finally`, `with` or `__del__`-holding local. A new admission rule, so present it to the user first; gate it on the ASan refill matrix (`/tmp/agents/fbo-int/m3`, `m4` generators) with the finally-less helpers added. The general case (a close that runs user code) stays the MIR consumer in docs/IR_DESIGN.md "Loop-bound generators that borrow storage the loop writes".
- **[docs] Write down how a resumable frame's exception unwinding cooperates.** `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py` unwinds through one C++ try level per cleanup action (`_unwind_levels`, `_emit_cleanup_level_catch`, `_emit_unwind_return`), and three mechanisms cooperate there: the per-case `__fin_ran_N` guards (exactly-once, and a typed handler rethrowing its own finally's exception), `__finally_stop` (a `return` in a `finally`, cleared when a later cleanup's exception cancels it), and the pending-return slot of a suspending finally; the abandonment destructor walks its own cleanup chain. Document the invariants in docs/ASYNC_DESIGN.md next to the region model, and close the ExceptRegion level gap for a suspending (CFG) finally (BUGS.md#frame-handler-skips-suspending-finally).
- **[codegen] Emit a non-template frame's abandonment destructor out of line.** A generator or coroutine frame that must run a pending `finally` or `__exit__` when destroyed mid-way gets `~__coro_X()` / `~__gen_X()` (the `switch (__state)` over the resume states, wrapped in the `tpy_panic` catch) defined inside the struct in the header (e.g. `tests/cases/async/task_abandoned_finally/expected/include/main.hpp`, 58 headers on master). For a frame that is not a template, declare it in the struct and define it in the `.cpp`, the split `__poll__` / `__next__` already use; a template frame keeps it inline. The emitter is `gen_async.py`'s destructor emission next to `_dtor_cleanup_cases`. Pure codegen placement: every snapshot with such a destructor churns, no output changes.
- **[codegen] Frame-layout rejects are decided in the printer.** `tpyc/codegen_cpp/frame_fields.py` raises the alias-cycle and untraced-generator-pulled-ahead rejects (`_raise_cycle`, the untraced loop `CodeGenError`) at C++ emission; they belong to sema (or a THIR fact) so they report with the other frame diagnostics. Also check `lifetime_closure`: it skips a field whose borrows are untraced, and an untraced field whose destruction runs user code keeps its declaration-order turn, so it could be destroyed before a frame that borrows it -- decide whether it should go last or reject.
- **[design] Generator lifetime: one decider per hazard, one write-effect predicate.** The generator-lifetime work (2026-09-24..27) left parallel paths a review named: (1) the plain-function checks of a generator used after its loop or block (`ExpressionAnalyzer.frame_scope_why`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`, read by `_check_frame_outlives_loop` and `StatementAnalyzer._frame_block_keeps`) decide by a syntactic durable-root rule while the frame check (`tpyc/sema/loop_frames.py`) decides the same hazard by the loop's writes, so the two positions drift (a parameter the loop appends to is admitted in a plain function, BUGS.md#plain-loop-generator-param-grown-in-loop); (2) `loop_frames._call_write` is another "may this call write its argument" predicate beside `calls.py` (`structural_mutated_params`, `_edges_reach_param`) and `mutation_propagation`, with its own deferred queue; (3) `LoopBindings.stores` / `effects` (`tpyc/prescan.py`) re-collect a loop's calls that the alias-rebind replay already walks in evaluation order; (4) `FunctionInfo.frame_close_runs_user_code` (`tpyc/sema/frame_close.py`, its own fixpoint) runs beside `frame_traits.py`'s recursive trait walk; (5) "the body keeps its locals in a frame" is re-derived inline in `alias_rebind.py` and `statements._frame_hoist_body`. Fold each into one site; the loop-write hazard's final home is MIR (docs/IR_DESIGN.md "Loop-bound generators that borrow storage the loop writes").
- **[codegen] A frame's loop fields release only what may run user code.** A resumable frame releases a loop's source, iterator and step fields on every exit from the loop, but only fields whose destruction may run user code (`TpyType.drop_runs_user_code`, with a generator or coroutine frame answering from `FunctionInfo.frame_close_runs_user_code`). A loop's ITERATOR field has no recorded type -- sema stores none on `TpyForEach` -- so `_loop_field_drops` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`) answers yes for any iterator a user `__iter__` returns; so such a loop resets its iterator on exit for nothing. Record the loop's iterator type in sema and read its `drop_runs_user_code()`; a static-protocol parameter's iterator stays a yes on purpose. A prerequisite of the finished-frame release (BUGS.md#finished-frame-keeps-locals), where the same noise touched about 55 of 157 releasing frames (measured 2026-09-25).
- **[codegen] Every position gets a statement-level slot for a pinned temporary.** A user-iterable temporary with a separate iterator at a lazy combinator (`zip(Noisy(2), xs)`) is bound to a local, and the combinator borrows it and stays movable, only where the position has a statement-level slot and the temporary is a constructor or free-function call (`argtemp.separate_iter_source`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`). Everywhere else the combinator owns the record in place and is pinned: a nested call argument, a member init, module level, an `and`/`or` operand, a method / static-factory / field-of-temporary source, a non-movable record. Nothing miscompiles -- a pinned combinator iterates in place -- but handing one to an OWNING consumer fails (BUGS.md#separate-iter-temp-no-flush-slot, and its genexpr face `genexpr.pinned_into_owning`). Work: flush an arg temp from a nested argument to the enclosing statement; a module-level and a member-init slot; the `and`/`or` operand banked like the ternary arm already is (`std::optional<T> __tmp; emplace`); an admission rule each for the method, static-factory and field-of-temporary sources (what the result may borrow from decides whether the receiver temporary must be hoisted with it). A non-movable record banked in a conditional operand cannot go through `optional::emplace(T&&)`; it needs construction from a factory, the mechanism a genexpr frame's in-place source constructor already uses (`_builds_source_in_place`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`). Closes BUGS.md#separate-iter-temp-no-flush-slot and retires `genexpr.pinned_into_owning`; BUGS.md#argtemp-no-flush-slot-wording and BUGS.md#record-rvalue-protocol-temp-unspelled sit on the same render arms. Rare on three axes, zero occurrences in the corpus and the stdlib -- hence not tagged. Filed 2026-09-20 as the deferred alternative of the pinned-source decision.
- **[HIGH][tooling] Runtime counters for reference-type copies and heap allocations, committed per case and ratcheted.** Every class in `docs/PITFALLS.md` that the suite is blind to is a copy or an allocation the output does not show: the cpy phase compares stdout, the snapshot pins whatever was emitted, and a reviewer reads. Under a test-build macro, the copy constructor of every emitted record and the runtime containers increments a counter, and a global `operator new` hook counts heap allocations; the harness prints both per case and commits them as a ratchet, so a change that adds a copy or an allocation to a case fails even when its output is byte-identical. Copies must reconcile with the diagnostics in BOTH directions (`silent-copy-vs-alias`, `copy-warning-at-wrong-site`): copies == explicit `copy()` calls + warned sites. **The heap counter is BLIND to `str`/`bytes` materialization**: `std::string("b")` fits the small-string optimization and never reaches `operator new`, so the `view-not-copy` class (the 2026-09-06 needle regression, the set-literal lookups that still built a string per C literal) shows zero. That class is countable only at the CONSTRUCTION site: either the emitted-C++ scanner below, or -- the exact form -- route every codegen-authored materialization through one runtime helper (`tpy::owned(view)` or similar) that the macro counts and the scanner greps, instead of spelling `std::string(` / `bytes_copy(` at each site. Deciding that routing is a design fork for the counter branch, not a detail. Filed 2026-09-07 from the corrections audit (`docs/PITFALLS.md`).
- **[HIGH][tooling] Three pure-Python checks over the corpus and the lowering, each replayed against the case it was filed from.** (1) A hidden-allocation SNAPSHOT SCANNER in `/tpy-ready`: a hunk that adds `std::string(` / `bytes_copy(` / a container construction / a `BigInt(` temporary where the previous line had a bare literal or a view is a finding, never churn to acknowledge -- the `dict.setdefault` double allocation and the `list.remove` owned needle both showed in the snapshot diff and nobody read them against the mapping. This is the instrument for the SSO-blind class above. (2) A HARDCODING RATCHET over `tpyc/thir/`: the 119-site survey (method names, runtime symbols, `is_list or is_dict or ...` family enumerations, `container_gates.py`'s count) as a committed script with a ceiling that must not grow; catches the special-cased stub methods of 2026-09-06 and the per-kind bytearray legs. (3) NOCOPY-ABLATION as a pytest flag over new or changed happy cases: recompile the case with every user record marked `@nocopy`; a case that still passes could not have seen a copy and needs the marker or a mutating leg, one that fails names a real copy. Twelve cases in one three-day window passed three specialist rounds and the readiness gate while unable to distinguish a move from a copy; the CLAUDE.md prose rule did not hold. One cheaper lint rides along and landed first (`tests/test_diag_text.py`): (4) `no-cpp-in-diagnostics` / `no-internal-names-in-diagnostics` as a grep over every diagnostic string in `tpyc/` and every committed `diag.txt` (`std::`, `::tpy::`, `int32_t`, `string_view`, `Tpy[A-Z]\w+`; baseline debt is the two escaping-closure `string_view` files, allowlisted until reworded). (`error_` cases are never run under CPython -- decided 2026-09-07 -- so `reject-valid-python-only-as-documented-divergence` stays a reviewer probe, not a harness check.) Filed 2026-09-07.
- **[diagnostics][decision] `ThirRejectError` messages name the lowering's reject TAG (`expr.method_call`, `stmt.var_decl`, `ctor.mil_reads_unready_field`, ...), which is a compiler-internal code in a user-facing diagnostic.** Measured 2026-09-07 over the committed corpus: about 130 `diag.txt` lines carry a tag (`expr.method_call` 16, `expr.list_comp` 15, `stmt.var_decl` 11, `method.arg_shape` 10, `stmt.return` 6, ...). The tag is also the key the step-6 reject queue and its `error_*` witnesses are organized by, so `tests/test_diag_text.py` does NOT police it: a ratchet would fail every batch that adds a witness. Decide whether the user-facing text names the Python construct with the tag demoted to a `--explain`-style detail (the `docs/PITFALLS.md` `no-internal-names-in-diagnostics` reading) or whether the tag stays while the reject queue is being worked; the diagnostic-codes entry below is the natural vehicle for the former. A known instance: a lambda stored into a field from a method rejects as `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.lambda)` (`tests/cases/records/error_method_lambda_field`), where the reason is a language rule (the closure would copy its captures silently), not a codegen gap. Filed 2026-09-07.
- **[MED][diagnostics] Give every diagnostic a stable code, registry-backed, and let tests pin the code instead of the wording.** Today 698 diagnostic sites emit free text, the corpus holds 1866 distinct diagnostic lines, and 2283 `# tpyc: error(/regex/)` / `warning(/regex/)` annotations pin WORDING, so every rewording churns annotations and a message can drift from its siblings unnoticed. A registry entry per diagnostic -- a slug in the `BUGS.md` style (`copy-into-field`, `unsupported-pattern-form`), not an opaque number -- with the canonical template and a one-paragraph explanation: annotations accept `error(copy-into-field)` beside the regex form; `tpyc --explain <code>` prints the explanation next to the existing `--explain-send` / `--explain-sync`; `tests/test_diag_text.py` checks the registry's templates instead of the reached corpus, so an unreached diagnostic is covered too; per-code suppression and an LSP get a key for free. Land it incrementally: the registry plus the annotation form first, a code REQUIRED for every new diagnostic from then on, existing sites back-filled in sweeps by module. Relates to `docs/PITFALLS.md` `no-cpp-in-diagnostics` / `no-internal-names-in-diagnostics` (the template review becomes the single check). Filed 2026-09-07.
- **[LOW][tests] Convert one per-shape case family into the exemplar condensed case.** CLAUDE.md now prescribes one case per fix with a section per position, but no committed case has that shape yet. The bytearray legs from the 2026-09-06 batch (`bytes/bytearray_own_param` and its list/dict siblings) are the obvious first fold: one reference-type case per slot with a leg per container kind. Filed 2026-09-07.
- **[MED][tooling] A semantics-preserving REWRITE harness: the same seed program at every position and every wrapper, compiled, run and compared.** From seed cases, generate variants -- the body moved into a method, a constructor, module scope, a generator, an async body, a comprehension, a closure; the subject wrapped as `(x,)` and `(x, 1)`; `str` swapped for `bytes` -- and assert identical output under TPy and CPython, the same diagnostic class, and (once the counters exist) the same copy and allocation counts across variants. This is the mechanical successor of `same-construct-every-position` and `tuple-equals-scalar` in `docs/PITFALLS.md`, and the only instrument that reaches shapes no case has: `dualgen.py` diffs one hand-supplied file and nothing in the repo generates programs. Design fork: corpus-driven mutation of existing cases (cheap, biased to shapes the corpus already has) vs a grammar-driven generator over the type and wrapper space (more work, finds what no case reaches). Filed 2026-09-07.
- **[HIGH][tooling] Stand up compiler-CODE coverage over `tpyc/`, right after the cutover. We have never measured it, and every instrument we do have answers a different question.** The reject-site reach census, the arg-table family reach and the face/witness census all measure LANGUAGE-SHAPE coverage -- which shapes some test exercises. Nothing measures which compiler code no test executes. The two are not substitutes, and the 2026-09-01 sweep is the clean illustration: 39 probes fell back because no case covers those shapes, while the fallback machinery those probes ran through is heavily exercised, so line coverage would have reported those regions green. Plain `coverage.py` line/branch over `tpyc/` from the suite is cheap and would be a genuinely new signal.
  **Do it AFTER the flip, not before, and the reason is not scheduling.** With two emitters, an unreached arm in one of them is ambiguous -- it may be dead, or it may be live-but-shadowed by the other path taking the body. With one emitter that ambiguity is gone: an unreached render arm is dead code, full stop. So the same tool answers a much sharper question the day the AST body emitters are deleted, and the deletion itself is the largest coverage event this codebase will ever have. Expect the first run to be noisy -- `tpyc/` holds error paths, `@native` arms and option-gated branches no ordinary case reaches -- so budget for a triage pass, and treat the output as a worklist rather than a ratchet until it has been read once.
- **[codegen, rejects-valid and LOUD -- not a miscompile] A for-loop variable and a `with` target sharing one name collide in the frame layout.** `gen_async._frame_layout` collects `source_form_fields` from `for_loop_info` then `update`s it with `with_target_payloads`, so the with payload wins and the loop's own `pointer_form_loop_var` classification is never reconciled with the plan verdict. **Severity adjudicated 2026-08-29:** two entries described this site and were read as disagreeing (silent miscompile vs loud failure). They do not disagree -- both bodies say the advance step writes one form against a field declared as another, which is a hard C++ type mismatch. It fails loudly at `frame_slot<T&>::emplace(T&&) = delete`; only one entry's HEADLINE said miscompile, and that word was wrong. Reachable only when one name is both a source-form loop var and a `with` target. Reproduces on master, so it is pre-existing. Fix shape: make the two producers disjoint or state which wins and why -- the current resolution is an accident of dict ordering, not a decision, and master's only precedence pin covers source-form-vs-pointer-alias, not source-form-vs-source-form. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) and by the FrameLayoutPlan merge's semantic-conflict pass.
- **[thir] `with.opt_slot_target` has zero witnesses -- determine whether the shape still exists and delete the arm if not.** The `WithTargetArm.ASSIGN_OPT` row (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) mirrors a `with` target that an enclosing branch-decl pass hoist-predeclared into OPTIONAL_STORAGE, and the whole-corpus face census reports it unwitnessed. That is the same shape whose AST defect the with-target storage work closed (the hoist-predeclared `std::optional<Record>` target that COPIED `__enter__()`'s result where CPython aliases, fixed by binding an alias instead), so the arm may now be unreachable by construction -- but `_with_manager_needs_hoist` still tests `item.target not in self.ctx.optional_locals`, which reads as though a with target can still land there, so the causation is NOT established. Resolve it in one direction: either produce a case that witnesses the arm, or confirm the AST can no longer emit an optional-storage with target and delete arm + face together. An arm that can never route is exactly the unwitnessed admission the THIR contract's routing pin exists to prevent. Direct evidence from the with-family waves (2026-08-03): the one former candidate shape now provably takes the pointer arm, not ASSIGN_OPT (the unit that recorded that verdict went with the THIR unit suite) -- an ever-owned with-target name (borrow_only False at the branch-decl pass) is the remaining path that could still reach OPTIONAL_STORAGE; probe that shape first. Surfaced by /tpy-ready after merging master's THIR waves.
- **[tests] Cover two untested `with`-target frame shapes.** The with-target storage work pinned the aliasing, residency and single-slot rules, but two shapes still have no case: (a) a `with ... as t:` inside a `for`/`while` in a generator/async body, which re-enters `__enter__` and re-emplaces the frame slot each iteration; (b) a REFERENCE-typed target reassigned after the block (the existing `with_target_rebound_after_with` rebinds a value-typed `int32`, so the pointer-reseat of a with-target frame field is unexercised). Both are plausible homes for a wrong storage form, and (a) in particular re-runs the emplace path the aliasing fix changed. (The former multi-item shape is covered by `control_flow/with_target_multi_item_mixed`.) Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the with-target storage branch.
- **[CPython interop] the newly-buildable `default before required keyword-only` shape is unpinned at the `@export` boundary.** `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md` documents `def f(a, b=10, *, c)` as building (the positional-defaults fix materializes that default at the call site instead of emitting it on the declaration), but no `tests/interop` case carries the shape -- the nearest is `combine(a, *, b, c=5)` in `tests/interop/defaults/src/defaults.py`, where no default PRECEDES the required keyword-only param. So a documented capability rests on the plain-TPy cases only, and the extra `PyArg_ParseTupleAndKeywords` interaction at the boundary is unverified. Adding it edits an existing interop case's committed snapshot, so it wants the snapshot-policy heads-up rather than a drive-by regen. Surfaced by the /tpy-review meta-review of the positional-defaults fix.
