- **[CPython interop] Optional boundary -- deferred slices.** `Optional[T]` crosses at `@export` fn / exposed-class method / `__init__` / property params and returns for every admitted `T` (branch `export-optional`; `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md` "The None gate"). One peel (`boundary_optional_inner` / `boundary_optional_is_pointer` in `type_def_registry.py`) serves admission, the form checks, the copy warnings and the glue; the `T*` form reuses the exposed-class borrow / identity / view ladder and the container copy-in, the value form goes through `optional_from_py` / `optional_to_py` (`marshal.hpp`) with `T`'s leaf lambda. Tests `tests/interop/optionals/`, `tests/cases/interop/error_export_optional_*`. **Deferred (each a located error today):** (1) **an Optional REFERENCE-class getset FIELD** (`root: Optional[Node]`) -- the value form (`limit: Optional[int32]`, str, enum, value class) crosses as a read/write getset since 2026-09-22; the reference form is rejected (a view through the gate would alias the storage slot across a None/value rebind). The one admissible slice: a `root: Optional[Node]` set exactly once in `__init__` and never rebound could cross as "view or None" under the same never-reassigned gate a bare class field uses (`exposed_view_field` peeling the Optional, the getter returning `none_to_py()` on an empty slot); the everyday rebinding field stays a documented divergence, since a rebind-aware view would either observe the CURRENT payload or go stale, both divergent from CPython. (2) **an Optional in a DUNDER slot signature** (`__eq__(self, other: Optional[Cls])`, `-> Optional[T]` from `__getitem__` / `__next__`) -- the slot validators pin operand and return shapes; `__next__ -> Optional[T]` is the one everyday shape worth a design (today `__next__` ends by raising `StopIteration`). (3) **Optional as a container ELEMENT** (`list[Optional[int32]]`) -- `_is_marshallable_element` does not peel; the storage-form element is `std::optional<T>` for every `T` (a reference class element would be a copied `std::optional<Cls>`, the same copy a plain class element is), so the element arm is the value-form `optional_from_py` with the element's leaf -- small, but unasked-for until a user hits it. **The structural debt (2026-09-22 review):** `is_function_boundary_marshallable` now peels Optional for EVERY caller, and each position without a gate emit subtracts it back by its own mechanism in its own file -- a getset FIELD through the non-peeling base predicate (`_exposed_form_error`'s role check), a dunder SLOT through `slot_unmarshallable_reason` (export_shape, consulted by the sema-side dunder validator), a container ELEMENT because `_is_marshallable_element` does not peel. One fact ("does this position emit the None gate?") decided at three consumers. Fix shape: a position argument on the admission predicate (param / return / field / slot / element) so the peel is decided where the position is known; that is also the home for (d): a `__getitem__` / `__next__` RETURN of `Optional[T]` already routes through the shared return ladder and is refused only by the slot rule -- admitting returns slot by slot (params stay out: `_value_in_decl_expr` has no gate) is the first slice to lift. (The round's other follow-ups -- the `AliasCandidate` NamedTuple, the one `_boundary_peel`, the pointer-container arm folded onto the value arm -- landed in the branch.) **Plain-TPy rejects the case had to route around (not boundary work; the rows are in the reject queue):** `return self._label` / `return lbl` for an `Optional[str]` field or local at an `-> Optional[str]` return (`return.opt_view_source`, `BUGS.md#optional-str-return-view-source` covers the view-VALUE half; the whole-optional field/local passthrough is `bins_stmt3` "opt_view_source"), `self._limit = v` storing an un-narrowed `Optional[int32]` param whole (`name.optval_unproven_read`, `bins_expr1`), and `-> Optional[V]` returning a value-class PARAM or FIELD whole (`return.storage_opt_source`, `bins_stmt3`; only fresh construction lowers, which is all `tests/interop/optionals` pins for the value class) -- all everyday shapes, and they rank above the deferred slices here.
- **[CPython interop] Span buffer boundary -- deferred slices.** `Span[readonly[T]]`/`Span[T]` (`T` a fixed-width int or `float`) cross the `@export` FUNCTION boundary as a PARAM ONLY (never a return -- return numeric data via `list[T]`), via the buffer protocol: `span_from_py<T>` (`marshal.hpp`) calls `PyObject_GetBuffer(PyBUF_ND | PyBUF_FORMAT)` (1-D, C-contiguous), strictly validates itemsize/format against `T` (no coercion), copies into a fresh `std::vector<T>` that implicitly converts to the function's `std::span<T>`/`std::span<const T>` param (the same owned-copy-converts-to-borrow-param trick as `str`/`bytes`), and releases the view. New predicate `is_span_boundary_param` in `type_def_registry.py` (param-only, checked at the `_validate_ext_module_exports` call site and the `assert_marshal` drift-guard in `extension.py` -- NOT folded into `is_function_boundary_marshallable`, which stays direction-symmetric for every other boundary type). Facade (`cpython_abi.hpp`/`cpython_h.hpp`) gained `Py_buffer` + `PyObject_GetBuffer`/`PyBuffer_Release` + `PyBUF_ND`/`PyBUF_FORMAT`, verified against real `Python.h` in the facade self-check. **v1.0 is copy-in for BOTH `Span[T]` and `Span[readonly[T]]`** (no `PyBUF_WRITABLE`, no write-back) -- a mutated `Span[T]` (non-readonly) param **warns** (the renamed `_warn_export_copy_boundary_mutation`, same `mutated_params` mechanism and no-escape-hatch bar as the list/dict/set container-mutation warning); `Span[readonly[T]]` can never warn (writing through it is already a compile error). Tests: `tests/interop/span_numeric/` (round-trips per width + float via `array.array`/`memoryview`/`bytes`/`bytearray`; `ext_checks.py` for format/itemsize mismatch, non-buffer arg, non-contiguous buffer, copy-in-mutation-invisible), `tests/cases/interop/{warn_export_span_mutation,error_export_span_return}`. **Deferred:** (1) **zero-copy** (both read-only and writable) -- phase 3.5, IR-gated (the foreign-borrow primitive; a spike showed the escape machinery can't fence a foreign-source param at all sinks). (2) **`bool`/`int` (BigInt)/`char` elements** -- excluded; `bool`'s buffer format (`'?'`) is inconsistent across exporters and rarely used as a numeric buffer, BigInt has no fixed-width buffer representation. (3) **`float32` elements** -- excluded because the scalar `float32` type itself isn't yet a boundary type at all (unrelated, orthogonal gap -- `Span[float32]` will "just work" once that scalar rung lands, since the admission predicate reuses `is_boundary_marshallable`). (4) **multi-dimensional / non-C-contiguous buffers** -- rejected (`PyBUF_ND` without `STRIDES` requires 1-D contiguity); no `ndim > 1` support. (5) **Span at the exposed-class METHOD boundary** -- DONE (the method-boundary rung; a `Span` method/`__init__` PARAM is admitted via `is_span_boundary_param`, return stays rejected, the mutation warning covers it); a Span getset FIELD is not a thing (a view field doesn't marshal; stays base-rejected). (6) **Span as a container element** (`list[Span[float]]`) -- not admitted, not a design goal. (7) **format-code table completeness** -- `span_from_py_impl`'s per-width accepted-code lists (e.g. int32 accepts `'i'` and `'l'`, int64 accepts `'q'` and `'l'`) cover the common numpy/`array.array` cases per-platform but are not an exhaustive `struct`-module mapping; revisit if an exotic exporter's format code is rejected in practice. **Post-/tpy-review (2026-07-01):** the buffer-view exception-safety leak (a `bad_alloc` during the copy skipped `PyBuffer_Release`) and the silent non-native-byte-order acceptance (a `'>i4'`-style buffer copied verbatim instead of rejected) were both found and FIXED in review (RAII guard + a native-byte-order check in `span_format_matches`); the transitive-mutation-warning gap (a `Span[T]` mutated only via a helper call gets no warning, unlike `list`/`dict`/`set`) was filed as a `BUGS.md` defect (needs `/tpy-fix-bug`, touches shared `mutation_propagation.py` infrastructure) rather than patched inline. Remaining cleanups from that review: (8) **`span_elem_type()` dedup** -- `is_span_boundary_param` (`type_def_registry.py`) and `_span_elem_cpp` (`extension.py`) both duplicate the "strip Own/Ref, assert Span, pull `type_args[0]`, unwrap readonly" sequence; extract one shared helper. (9) **widen `span_numeric` test coverage** -- DONE in part: added `peek_int32` (a mutable, non-readonly `Span[int32]` param that only reads), round-tripped in `driver.py` via `array.array`/`memoryview`, proving the mutable form marshals correctly and that a read-only *use* of it doesn't warn; mirrored with a `peek` case in `tests/cases/interop/warn_export_span_mutation` (declared-but-never-mutated `Span[int32]` stays quiet, unlike `scale`). STILL OPEN: only 4 of the 9 `span_from_py<T>` specializations (`float`/`int32`/`uint8`, now also exercised via `peek_int32`) get a happy-path test; the dual-format-code branches for the untested widths (`int8_t`/`int16_t`/`uint16_t`/`uint32_t`/`int64_t`/`uint64_t`, e.g. `int64_t` accepting `'l'` alongside `'q'`) remain unexercised. (10) **the native-byte-order rejection (review fix, item above) has no regression test** -- and, unlike the width/format-mismatch cases already in `ext_checks.py`, it can't be added cheaply: `array.array`/`memoryview.cast()` only ever expose a NATIVE format string (no stdlib-only way to construct a Py_buffer with an explicit non-native `<`/`>`/`!` prefix), so covering this branch needs either a numpy test-only dependency (the one common exporter that does emit explicit byte-order codes) or a from-scratch C++-level unit test calling `span_format_matches` directly (`runtime/cpp/tests/` currently has only the facade self-check, no general header-logic unit-test harness). Small infra/scope decision either way -- pick one before adding the test, don't assume it's a five-minute addition. Surfaced by the `/tpy-ready` retrospective for `interop-span-buffer`.
- **[CPython interop] exception bridge follow-ups (built-in types DONE).** Built-in TPy exceptions raised in an `@export` body now cross as the matching `PyExc_*` with the message (`tpy/interop/exc_bridge.hpp`; glue catches `const tpy::BaseException&`). Remaining, all tracked Planned in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`: (1) **user-defined exception classes -- TYPE crossing DONE** (`PyErr_NewException` per ext_module-defined exc class at `PyInit_`, registered `typeid -> PyObject*` in an `ExcRegistry` the glue passes to `set_py_err_from`; own importable type, inheritance chain, catchable as base). Still deferred under this rung: (1a) **faithful data-field crossing -- DONE** (branch `interop-exc-data-fields`): a data-carrying user exc's fields (scalar/str/bytes/exposed-enum) cross as instance attributes via a per-type generated setter threaded through the `ExcRegistry` (`typeid -> PyObject* + ExcSetErr`; `extension.py::_emit_user_exc_setters`, `exc_bridge.hpp`); the setter constructs `pytype(e.what())`, sets each field via `PyObject_SetAttrString`, then `PyErr_SetObject`. `str()`/`args` reflect the message only (acknowledged, unavoidable -- the C++ exc holds typed fields, not the original arg tuple). Container/exposed-class exc fields = located error (the user-exc field validator (tpyc/interop/module_validators.py)), deferred. Full `args` fidelity (opt 1, needs `super().__init__` modeling) declined. The crossing is *transitive* (registry-driven, fires wherever raised) AND covers INHERITED user data fields (a subclass crosses its own + inherited fields via `TypeRegistry.user_declared_fields`, which skips native-base fields like `BaseException.message`; found+fixed in /tpy-review -- the first cut only marshalled own fields, a silent-drop divergence). The setter is `noexcept` + wrapped in try/catch degrading to `PyErr_NoMemory()` (a field marshaller can throw under OOM). Cross-module exposed-enum exc field = located error (routes through `_exposed_form_error` for the locality check). Two DEFERRED follow-ups filed from /tpy-review: (1a-i) **admit VALUE-TYPE exposed-class exc fields** -- the getset path admits an immutable value-type exposed-class field, but exc fields reject ALL exposed-class fields; admitting them reuses `_value_out_expr`'s `instance_to_py` arm (now safe under the setter's try/catch, since `instance_to_py` can throw) + needs a test; (1a-ii) **dedup the "is user exception" predicate** (`not is_native and implements_throwable and inherits_base_exception`) -- now spelled at 4 sites (`compiler.py`, `analyzer.py`, `registration.py`, `extension.py`); fold into a `RecordInfo.is_user_exception()` / registry helper. AND (higher value, /tpy-ready 2nd-opinion): the load-bearing drift is admission-vs-EMIT, not validator-vs-validator -- the user-exc field validator (tpyc/interop/module_validators.py) admits `is_boundary_marshallable(_, False) and not is_exposed_class`, but the setter EMIT is in `extension.py::_emit_user_exc_setters`; widening the shared marshallable predicate would auto-admit a type the setter cannot emit -> broken glue TU. Co-locate the "admissible exc-field type" predicate WITH the emit so admission+emit cannot drift (the exposed-class exc-field reject is already test-pinned by `error_export_exc_class_field`). Tests +`tests/interop/user_exc_inherited/` (hierarchy + transitive raise), +`tests/cases/interop/error_export_exc_cross_module_enum_field`; (1b) **the `str()`/`args` divergence is documented, not warned** -- a per-raise warning was shipped then REMOVED in /tpy-review: it was non-actionable (unavoidable under TPy's model, no escape hatch, no author-side fix -- making the exc message-only would drop the very fields, worse) and landed on the TPy author, not the Python consumer who reads `e.args`; so it is a doc-only divergence like the other no-escape-hatch ones (`_warn_export_user_exc_data` and its `warn_export_user_exc_data` test were deleted). (1c) **cross-module user exceptions** -- only classes DEFINED in the ext_module get a Python type; an imported user exc raised at the boundary still degrades to its built-in base (a data-field exc field typed as a cross-module enum is already a located error; the raise-through-an-imported-exc case is the remaining gap). (1f) **test gaps** -- bare user exc (no `__init__`), `py_exc_by_name` unknown-built-in-base fallback (e.g. inheriting `CancelledError` -> `PyExc_Exception`), and the `PyInit_` module-init (top-level) raise path are unexercised. (2) **`@error_return` Err -> raise** across the boundary. (3) **panic -> exception** (convert `tpy_panic` to a Python exception instead of `abort()`ing the host). (4) **exception chaining** (`__cause__`/`__context__`) not carried. (5) **`CancelledError` (and other `async.hpp` `BaseException` subclasses) degrade to `PyExc_BaseException`** -- no `PyExc_CancelledError` stable-ABI singleton exists (asyncio.CancelledError is Python-level), so bridging it needs importing `asyncio.CancelledError` at `PyInit` and stashing the type; deferred. (6) **test gaps**: the `PyInit_` (module-init raise) catch path needs a dedicated expected-import-failure interop case; broaden the cascade test with user-raised `RuntimeError`/`OverflowError`/bare `LookupError` (the latter exercises degrade-to-listed-base). (7) optional: extend the facade self-check to validate the new `PyExc_*` decls. (8) **low-prio perf:** `py_exc_for` is a linear `dynamic_cast` cascade (O(depth) RTTI probes). Fine -- it's a cold path (runs only when an exception crosses the boundary) -- but if ever revisited, the clean form is a virtual kind-tag on the `Throwable`/`BaseException` hierarchy switched on in the interop header (one vcall, keeps the Python C-API out of `core.hpp`), best bundled with the user-exc-class rung since that adds per-type metadata anyway. Not a faster cascade.
- **[CPython interop] exposed classes (`PyType_FromSpec`) -- deferred slices.** The baseline rung ships: `@export class` -> a CPython type built at `PyInit_`, instances embedding the TPy payload after the `PyObject` header (`tpy::interop::Instance<T>`, `class_bridge.hpp`); `tp_init` runs `__init__`, `tp_dealloc` runs the C++ destructor; plain instance methods + annotated fields as read/write getset; instances cross as free-fn/method params (a borrow of the live payload via `instance_payload` -- mutation writes through) and returns (a `self`/param-sourced borrow return crosses as the ORIGINAL PyObject -- see the identity-preserving-returns entry above; other sources copy via `instance_to_py` and warn; `Own[Cls]` is the always-fresh form). The type is final (no `Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE`), no instance `__dict__`. The ext-module validator (`_validate_exposed_class` in `tpyc/interop/module_validators.py`) rejects, with a located error, what the glue can't emit yet -- this is the deferred matrix: **(1) dunders** (Q4) -- **checkpoint 1 DONE** (`__repr__`/`__str__` -> `Py_tp_repr`/`Py_tp_str`; `__eq__`/`__ne__`/`__lt__`/`__le__`/`__gt__`/`__ge__` -> one `Py_tp_richcompare`, `__ne__` auto-derived from `__eq__`; `__hash__` -> `Py_tp_hash`, `PyObject_HashNotImplemented` wired when a richcompare dunder is defined without `__hash__`; new `_validate_export_class_dunders` in `analyzer.py` mirrors `_validate_dyn_dunder_kind`'s decorator/kind rejections plus per-dunder param-count/type/return-type checks; fixed a real pre-existing gap surfaced by the first class-typed non-self method param: `_boundary_inner` didn't strip `ReadonlyType`, so `def __eq__(self, other: Vec2)` -- whose `other` arrives as `readonly[Vec2]` -- failed `is_function_boundary_marshallable`/`is_exposed_class` even though `Vec2` is exposed; tests `tests/interop/class_dunders/`, `tests/cases/interop/error_export_class_dunder_{return,arity,staticmethod}`, `warn_export_class_dunder` repointed to `__call__`). **checkpoint 2 DONE** (arithmetic/ordering operators -> `Py_nb_*`: binary ops -- `__add__`/`__sub__`/`__mul__`/`__truediv__`/`__floordiv__`/`__mod__`/`__pow__`/`__lshift__`/`__rshift__`/`__and__`/`__or__`/`__xor__` -- each wire ONE wrapper handling both the forward dunder and its reflected counterpart if defined, since CPython invokes the same slot with `(a, b)` regardless of which side is `self`; the non-self operand marshals as whatever type the dunder declares -- another `@export` class OR a scalar/enum (e.g. `def __mul__(self, scalar: int64)` for `vec * 3`), NOT restricted to the record's own type -- and a type mismatch downgrades to `NotImplemented` via a new `catch (const MarshalError&) { if (!PyErr_ExceptionMatches(TypeError)) return nullptr; PyErr_Clear(); }` pattern (a real error, e.g. `OverflowError` from a right-typed-but-bad-value operand, still propagates); `__pow__`/`__rpow__` use the ternary `nb_power` signature and reject a real 3-arg modulus; unary ops (`__pos__`/`__neg__`/`__invert__`) reuse the repr/str shape; in-place ops (`__iadd__`... the `CONST_PARAMS_METHODS` set) mutate self and return the SAME PyObject (`Py_IncRef`+return, no `instance_to_py` copy) since TPy already requires them to return `self` -- the borrow-return-copies warning is suppressed for this group specifically since identity IS preserved here (unlike every other dunder). New facade: `Py_nb_*` slot ids (25 constants) + `unaryfunc`/`binaryfunc`/`ternaryfunc` typedefs (`cpython_abi.hpp`, self-check-verified) + `PyErr_ExceptionMatches`/`PyErr_Clear` (`cpython_h.hpp`). Dunder-name tables (`_NB_BINARY_OPS`/`_NB_UNARY_OPS`/`_NB_INPLACE_OPS` in `extension.py`) are derived from the canonical `BINOP_TO_METHOD`/`BINOP_TO_RMETHOD`/`AUGOP_TO_IMETHOD`/`UNARYOP_TO_METHOD` tables (`modules/defs.py`), not a hand-rolled duplicate. Tests: `tests/interop/class_operators/` (same-type `__add__`, scalar-mixed `__mul__`/`__rmul__`, unary `__neg__`, in-place `__iadd__` with an identity check, ternary `__pow__`), `tests/cases/interop/error_export_class_dunder_arith_{arity,return}`. Verified end-to-end via a manual `.so` build+driver (forward/reflected/unary/inplace/wrong-type-TypeError/3-arg-pow-TypeError all matched). **checkpoint 3 DONE (Q4 fully landed)** (container protocol -> `Py_mp_*`/`Py_sq_*`/`Py_tp_iter*`: `__len__` wires ONE wrapper to both `Py_mp_length` and `Py_sq_length`; `__getitem__` -> `Py_mp_subscript` (a wrong-typed key's `TypeError` propagates directly -- no `NotImplemented` fallback, unlike arithmetic operators, since subscripting has no reflected side; slicing, `__getitem__(self, s: slice)`, is out of scope); `__setitem__`/`__delitem__` share ONE `Py_mp_ass_subscript` wrapper (`value == nullptr` means `del obj[k]`; if only one of the pair is defined, the other direction raises `TypeError`); `__contains__` -> `Py_sq_contains` (omitted entirely when undefined -- `in` then falls back to CPython's own iterate-via-`tp_iter` behavior for free); `__iter__` -> `Py_tp_iter` (reuses the checkpoint-2 unary-op emitter directly -- no self-identity special-casing needed: `__iter__` may legitimately return a fresh iterator object, not `self`, so it's marshalled like any other exposed-class-returning dunder, with the usual borrow-vs-`Own` warning); `__next__` -> `Py_tp_iternext` -- `__next__` is implicitly `@error_return(StopIteration)` (the parser default: `parse/parser.py`'s `if node.name == "__next__" and error_return is None: error_return = "StopIteration"`), so the compiled method returns `std::expected<T, StopIteration>` rather than throwing on exhaustion; the wrapper checks `.has_value()` and calls `set_py_err_from` on the `.error()` value directly (`StopIteration` is already in the exception bridge's built-in list, so no new bridging code needed) -- exempted from the blanket `@error_return` rejection the other dunders get. `list(x)`, `iter(x)`/`next(it)`, and a `for` loop all round-trip through CPython's own sequence/iterator machinery once these are wired -- verified end-to-end via a manual `.so` build+driver. New facade: `Py_mp_*`/`Py_sq_*`/`Py_tp_iter*` slot ids + `lenfunc`/`objobjargproc`/`objobjproc` typedefs (reuses `binaryfunc`/`unaryfunc` from checkpoint 2 for `mp_subscript`/`tp_iter`/`tp_iternext`), self-check-verified. Tests: `tests/interop/class_container/` (len/getitem/setitem-mutation/contains/iter+next via `list()`+manual+for-loop), `tests/cases/interop/error_export_class_dunder_{getitem_arity,setitem_arity,len_return}`. Never in scope for Q4 at all: `__call__`, `__bool__`, async iteration (`__aiter__`/`__anext__`), context managers (`__enter__`/`__exit__`), descriptors (`__get__`/`__set__`), and pickling (`__reduce__`) -- file separately if ever wanted. **Post-/tpy-review fixes (same session):** one Critical found and fixed, one Critical claim DISPROVEN by direct testing -- (a) [DISPROVEN] the review flagged `Py_tp_hash` being omitted whenever ANY richcompare dunder is defined without `__hash__` (not just `__eq__`) as a silent divergence from real Python's `__eq__`-specific unhashable-on-override rule. Building and running an actual `.so` showed this ISN'T a bug: `PyType_Ready` (the mechanism behind `PyType_FromSpec`, used for every exposed class) nulls `tp_hash` whenever `tp_richcompare` is populated AT ALL, with no way to tell which specific dunder populated it -- verified by removing the explicit `PyObject_HashNotImplemented` wiring entirely and confirming the type stayed unhashable regardless (a plain-`__len__`/no-richcompare class stays hashable, confirming richcompare-presence, not the explicit wiring, is what triggers it). So a `__lt__`-only class DOES become unhashable once exposed, unlike its plain-Python source (which stays hashable) -- this is a genuine, unavoidable, now-DOCUMENTED acknowledged divergence (comment in `extension.py`, `Ordered` class + `ext_checks.py` assertion in `tests/interop/class_dunders/`), not something fixable in TPy's glue. (b) [FIXED, confirmed real] richcompare codegen hardcoded the "other" operand's C++ type as the record's own type regardless of what the compare dunder actually declared, so a legal-per-sema `def __eq__(self, other: int64)` passed comp but failed the `.so` build with a confusing internal g++ error; fixed by requiring a compare dunder's operand type equal the record's own type at sema (`_validate_export_class_dunders`), +`error_export_class_dunder_compare_wrong_type`. **Known limitation from this fix (documented in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`/`LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`, not yet filed as a TODO before now):** unlike arithmetic operators (checkpoint 2), a comparison dunder can only compare against the record's OWN exposed-class type -- `__eq__(self, other: int64)` or `__eq__(self, other: SomeOtherExposedClass)` are both rejected at sema, even though sema's `is_function_boundary_marshallable` check would otherwise admit them. Lifting this needs richcompare codegen to marshal per-op-declared-type with a `NotImplemented`-on-mismatch fallback (mirroring `_value_in_decl_expr`'s already-built arithmetic-operator pattern) instead of the current single type-guard-then-switch shape shared by all 6 ops -- a real codegen redesign, not a quick follow-up. Also added from the review: `__delitem__`-actually-implemented coverage (`Slot` class in `tests/interop/class_container/`), an `OverflowError`-propagates-not-swallowed-by-NotImplemented test and an asymmetric `__sub__`/`__rsub__` pair (operand order matters, unlike the previously-only-tested commutative `__mul__`/`__rmul__`) in `tests/interop/class_operators/`, and `error_export_class_dunder_{contains_return,iter_return}` cases. **Post-/tpy-ready fixes (same session, second-opinion agent caught this before merge):** `compiler.py`'s per-method loop unconditionally skips all non-`__init__` dunders, so its `type_params`/overload/param-form rejections never ran against ANY dunder -- confirmed as a LIVE gap (not just theoretical) by direct reproduction: a generic dunder (`def __len__[T](self) -> int32:`) and a defaulted dunder param (`def __eq__(self, other: C = None)`) both passed comp-phase cleanly then failed the actual `.so` build with confusing internal g++ errors (`no matching function for call to ... __len__() const` / `could not convert 'nullptr' to 'const C&'`) -- the exact failure shape already fixed once for richcompare in this same round. Fixed: `analyzer.py::_validate_export_class_dunders` gained a `type_params` check and a new dunder param-form helper (since resolved: both homes now live in `interop/export_shape.py` and share their message tails, split as `unsupported_wrapper_param_form` vs `unsupported_slot_param_form` because the two emit shapes genuinely admit different forms). Tests: `error_export_class_dunder_{generic,default_param}`. The `@overload`-grouped-dunder case the second-opinion agent also flagged was checked and found to be ALREADY correctly rejected (the existing `is_overload_stub` check fires on the first stub before the impl is ever reached) -- not a live gap, no fix needed there.

**@export class single-value marshal duplication:** `extension.py`'s `_value_in_decl_expr` (operand/key/setter decode) and `_value_out_expr` (getset getter + exc data fields; dunder RETURNS now route through `_emit_call_return`) duplicate `_emit_marshal_in`/`_emit_call_return`'s (statement-form) branch structure -- two marshalling dispatch chains to keep in lockstep when a boundary type is added. Same-family: the `-1`-sentinel BaseException/catch-all block is hand-inlined three times (tp_init, field setter, property setter -- the field variant lacks the BaseException arm); a tiny shared `-1`-catch emitter would collapse it. (low confidence) `_value_in_decl_expr` always binds a `const&` for an exposed-class non-self operand regardless of Phase-2 mutation analysis; a dunder that legitimately mutates a non-self operand would hit a const-mismatch build failure rather than a clear diagnostic -- not confirmed against a concrete case. **(2) inheritance -- DONE** (branch `interop-class-inheritance`: single exposed same-module base -> real `tp_base` via `PyType_FromSpecWithBases`; see the dedicated deferred-slices entry); **(3) `@property` -- DONE** (branch `interop-class-properties`): a property crosses as a *computed* getset -- the getter is a zero-arg method return site (reuses `_emit_call_return`, so it admits the full method boundary set incl. containers), the setter a one-param method param site (reuses `_emit_marshal_in` via an `a0` alias; a non-value setter param is Own-auto-wrapped, so the marshalled owned local is `std::move`d in). Getter-only property = `nullptr` setter (`AttributeError` on write, as CPython -- message text differs). Shape checks route through `export_method_shape_error(allow_property=True)` (async/generator/generic/`@error_return` accessors still reject); a setter typed as an exposed class -- value-type OR reference (the property Own auto-wrap runs before a user record's ValueType flag is known, so both arrive Own-wrapped) -- is a dedicated located error steering to a plain method; a `Span[T]` setter is a located error (a setter stores, and the buffer copy-in dies at the call -- store `list[T]`); `del` on any property or field raises `AttributeError` via a `value == nullptr` guard in both setter emits (CPython's getset delete protocol; previously segfaulted); `_`-prefixed properties are internal (uniform `_`-attribute rule, borrow-return warn loop included); a borrow-return getter warns via the existing `_warn_export_class_return_alias` (labeled `property 'x'`, const-clone deduped). Tests `tests/interop/class_properties/`, `tests/cases/interop/{error_export_class_property_class_setter,error_export_class_property_value_class_setter,error_export_class_property_span_setter,error_export_class_property_setter_unmarshallable,error_export_class_property_error_return,error_export_class_property_unmarshallable,warn_export_class_property_borrow_return}`. Deferred follow-ups: (3a) **enable value-type exposed-class property setters** -- rejected today only because `_apply_property_setter_wrapping` (sema/method_expansion.py) runs before the protocol pass sets a user record's ValueType flag, so the param is Own-wrapped and the borrowed argument payload can't feed it; fix = defer/reorder the wrap decision (plain-TPy-wide, own design pass) or copy-emit at the boundary for a value-class `Own` setter; (3b) property accessors skip `unsupported_wrapper_param_form` (a defaulted setter value param passes unvalidated -- harmless today, the getset protocol always supplies the value; add for uniformity with the method path); (3c) test gap: no runtime (ext-exec) witness of an exposed-class-VALUED getter (`-> Own[Inner]` copy-out read; the borrow-form warn case is comp-only) -- needs a second exposed class in an interop case. The warning-dropped-on-error residual is now its own BUGS.md entry; **(4) class-typed fields** -- the ENUM half is DONE (branch `interop-class-typed-fields`: an exposed-enum getset field round-trips value-correctly, singleton-preserving -- see the enums entry item 2c). The CLASS half is now split by the borrow-view gate (branch interop-field-borrow-views): a NEVER-REASSIGNED public reference-class field crosses as a READ-ONLY aliasing borrow-view getset (write-through, registry-deduped identity), while a REASSIGNABLE one stays a located error (a view aliases the storage slot, so the rebind would show through it); the diagnostic steers to dropping the post-__init__ reassignment or making the field **internal** (a `_`-prefixed name -- see the internal-fields entry below -- kept as payload state, never a Python attribute) plus an accessor method (mutating through `self`) or an explicit `copy()`. A *public* `@nocopy` or cross-module exposed-class field stays rejected for the usual reasons (internal fields have no interop gate, so a `_`-named `@nocopy` member is fine). **Internal (`_`-prefixed) fields DONE** (branch `interop-internal-fields`): a field whose name begins with `_` never crosses as an attribute at EITHER site (exposed-class getset via the `extension.py` getset loop + `_validate_exposed_class`; exception data-fields via `_collect_user_exc_classes` + `_validate_user_exc_data_fields`), gated by one shared predicate `type_def_registry.is_internal_boundary_field`. It stays live payload state, so an exposed class can now hold ANY-typed internal member (reference class, container, `@nocopy`) reached through a method -- the pattern the reference-class-field diagnostic already recommended, now actually reachable. Divergence (acknowledged, like `e.message`): a `_`-field is an ordinary attribute under plain Python but absent on the `.so`, so drivers must not read one. Test `tests/interop/internal_fields/`; migrated `class_container`'s `_i` cursor (its pointless mutable getset drops). FILED-NOT-BUILT: replace the C++ `nothrow_move` static_assert on the payload with a located sema pre-check for a non-movable exposed payload (a `_`-field can now make a class non-movable, hitting the assert as a raw build error rather than a diagnostic). **(4a) exposed VALUE-TYPE fields -- DONE** (branch `interop-class-typed-fields`): a field typed as an @export `ValueType` record (`origin: Point`) is admitted -- value types are immutable, so copy-out is behaviorally invisible (the same safe bucket as enum, not the reference-class footgun). Two parts landed: (i) an exposed value-type class emits READ-ONLY getset (getter only, `nullptr` setter -- gated on `info.is_value_type` in `extension.py`; also fixed the pre-existing r/w-mutable fidelity gap that was filed in BUGS.md, now removed); (ii) the field reject narrowed to `is_exposed_class(typ) and not _boundary_inner(typ).is_value_type()`, so a value-type field falls through to admission -- getter copy-out via `instance_to_py`, the OUTER holder's field-set stays r/w (whole-value replacement). CPython parity: chose read-only `.so` + ext-only divergences (mutation-raises-AttributeError and copy-out `is`-identity in `ext_checks.py`, driver stays parity-clean) over freezing the `lib/cpy` `ValueType` stub -- no `no_cpython.txt` needed, consistent with the shipped strict-by-type/final/no-`__dict__` pattern. Equality gate resolved: value types have NO implicit structural `==` (it's a compile error without a defined `__eq__`), and a user-defined `__eq__` is already wired by the Q4 richcompare rung. Test `tests/interop/value_typed_fields/`. char fields (no marshaller) and tuple fields (value type, but the getset has no container/tuple emit -- pairs with the container-getset-field work) remain separate small gaps; **(5) static/classmethods**; **(6) generic exposed classes / generic methods**; **(7) faithful exception data-field crossing (exc TODO 1a)** -- DONE (branch `interop-exc-data-fields`); reused the getset single-value marshal helper (`_value_out_expr`) for each exc data field, not an exception-only path; container/exposed-class exc fields deferred (located error); **(8) `copy.copy`/`pickle`** (a C type with no `__reduce__`/`tp_copy` fails both where the source class succeeds -- track as a declared divergence); **(9) overloaded methods / `__init__`** (now *rejected* -- the glue emits one positional wrapper, so an `@overload` group would silently expose only the first arity; supporting it needs per-arity dispatch in the wrapper); **(10) `tp_traverse`/GC** -- not emitted (fields are scalar/str/bytes/enum or a nested value-type class, all held by value with no `PyObject` reference, so no reference cycle is possible -- an enum field holds an interned int, a value-type field an inline immutable value, not a Python ref). NOT triggered by the enum-field work, and NOT by the borrow-view rung either: a view holds exactly one strong ref (its owner) while no exposed instance references a view, so the graph stays acyclic by construction and refcounting suffices; tp_traverse becomes relevant only if exposed instances ever hold arbitrary PyObject refs (e.g. Python-side subclass attributes, currently rejected at instantiation); **(11) `Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE`** -- a LEAF exposed type stays non-subclassable from Python (honest `TypeError` at the class statement); a class that is another exposed class's base carries BASETYPE (required by `PyType_FromSpecWithBases`) with a tp_init exact-type guard rejecting Python-subclass instantiation, and the `PyType_IsSubtype` branch in `instance_payload` is now LIVE (a base-typed param accepts a derived instance); **(12) throwing re-`__init__`** leaves the instance with a destroyed payload reachable via getset (UB if then touched) -- exotic (catch an `obj.__init__()` failure, then read a field) and CPython is also ill-defined there; revisit if it bites. Code organization: DONE -- the glue emitter is now `tpyc/interop/extension.py` (`ExtensionGenerator`, wired as `CodeGenerator.extension`; `generate_extension_glue` is a thin delegator), and `boundary_cpp_type`/`boundary_unmarshallable_msg` moved to `type_def_registry.py` (next to `is_boundary_marshallable`), so both the sema validator and the glue import them from one neutral home. Byte-identical codegen. Full design in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md` phase 4. **Review follow-ups (from /tpy-review):** DONE in round 2 -- non-`__init__` dunders now *warn* (`_warn_export_class_unexposed_dunders`); `Own[<exposed class>]` params, `@nocopy` exposed-class borrow-returns, and class-typed fields are now *located errors* (`Compiler._exposed_form_error`, renamed from `_exposed_class_form_error` when it gained the enum cases) instead of opaque C++ failures (the `@nocopy` borrow-return suppresses the duplicate identity warning). Round-3 (ready gate): `@overload` method/`__init__` groups now reject (item 9) -- the silent-first-arity drop the rest of the branch was eliminating. (A plain *duplicate* `def __init__` was already rejected upstream; the new check covers the `@overload` group case codegen's `[0]` would otherwise truncate.) STILL OPEN: (a) keyword arguments -- DONE (positional/keyword, defaults, keyword-only and positional-only all cross). (e) cross-module exposed classes have no same-defining-module guard -- DONE (branch `fix-cross-module-exposed-class`): `Compiler._exposed_form_error`'s class branch now checks the class is locally `@export`-defined in the current module (mirrors the pre-existing enum-branch guard), resolved via `registry.imported_record_qualification_for_type` (qualified identity, not a bare short-name set -- a name-collision variant of this exact check was caught live by `/tpy-review`'s `cpython-parity`/`architecture-fit` passes and fixed before merge), so a foreign exposed class used as a param/field/return is a located error instead of a misbuild; tests `tests/cases/interop/error_export_class_cross_module_{param,return,name_collision}`. **Cleanups:** rename `type_def_registry._boundary_inner` -> `boundary_inner` (now a cross-module API); dedupe the dunder-exclusion predicate spelled at 3 sites (compiler/generator/analyzer); unify `is_exposed_class` (`td.record.exposed_to_host`) and `is_boundary_marshallable` (`td.boundary_marshal`) onto one canonical check (the `boundary_cpp_type`/`boundary_unmarshallable_msg` relocation is DONE -- now in `type_def_registry.py`). **Test gaps:** round 2 added `error_*` cases for the Own-param / class-typed-field / @nocopy-borrow-return rejects + a `warn_export_class_dunder` case; still missing `error_*` for the remaining `_validate_exposed_class` reject paths (throwable/generic/static/async; the inheritance rejects got their own cases on the `interop-class-inheritance` branch) + the `@export`-outside-`ext_module` ParseError + `@export("renamed") class`, and a happy-path for multiple exposed classes in one module or an empty class (no fields/no non-init methods).
- **[CPython interop] enums + constants boundary -- deferred slices.** An `@export` enum in an ext_module is recreated at `PyInit_` as a **real** CPython enum (`enum.IntEnum`/`enum.Enum` via the stdlib functional API with `module=` set; `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/interop/enum_bridge.hpp` `make_enum`/`enum_dict_add`) -- CPython-parity-verified observably identical to a source-level class-statement enum. Module-level `Final` constants of a boundary scalar (`int`/`IntN`/`bool`/`float`/`str`) become init-time module-attribute snapshots (read after `__tpy_init`; Final => immutable so the snapshot can't go stale). Enums are `@export`-gated (consistent with classes/functions; the enum parser accepts bare `@export` in an ext_module); constants are auto-exposed via `Final` (no decorator syntax exists for a binding, and Final is the only snapshot-safe global form). Validator (`_validate_exposed_enums` in `tpyc/interop/module_validators.py`) rejects `@export` on a `@native` enum or a nested enum; the glue collectors `ExtensionGenerator._exposed_enums`/`_exposed_constants` filter the exposable surface. Facade += `PyImport_ImportModule`/`PyObject_GetAttrString`/`PyObject_Call`/`Py_BuildValue`/`PyDict_New`/`PyDict_SetItemString`; `marshal.hpp` += `to_py(std::string_view)` (a `Final[str]` resolves to `StrView`). Tests: `tests/interop/{enums,constants}/`, `tests/cases/interop/error_export_{enum_outside_ext,native_enum,nested_enum}`. Deferred: (1) **enum *values* as `@export` function param/return types** -- DONE (branch interop-enum-values): an exposed enum crosses as a fn param/return via `enum_bridge.hpp` `enum_from_py`/`enum_to_py` against the module-static enum-type handle (promoted from a PyInit-local). OUT reconstructs the member (`EnumType(value)`, identity preserved); IN is strict-by-type (bare int -> TypeError; documented int-vs-member-vs-source divergence, ext_checks-tested). Admission = `boundary_marshal` on the exposed enum's TypeDef (sema registration) + `is_exposed_enum`. `int(enum)` inside a body is still unsupported (orthogonal TPy conversion gap, not the boundary). (2) **nested enums** (inside a class) and **cross-module enums** -- nested still rejected; a cross-module exposed-enum param/return is a located error (`_exposed_form_error`, checks the enum is locally @export-defined) rather than a misbuild -- the exposed-CLASS cross-module path now has the same guard too (DONE, branch `fix-cross-module-exposed-class`; see the exposed-classes entry's item (e)). From /tpy-review (treat as ONE deferred cross-module unit, all low-reachability today): (2a) the cross-module guard branch was UNTESTED -- DONE (branch `fix-cross-module-exposed-class`): a 2-file `src/main.py` + `src/enum_mod.py` fixture under `tests/cases/interop/` works fine (the "single-source-per-case" limit only applies to the `tests/interop/` ext-exec harness, not the plain comp-phase `tests/cases/` one); see `error_export_enum_cross_module` (and the class analog `error_export_class_cross_module_{param,return}`). (2b) DONE for both classes and enums: the class guard resolves by qualified identity (`registry.imported_record_qualification_for_type`, the same type-object-based "is this local?" helper codegen already uses to qualify a cross-module record) instead of a bare short-name set -- a module that imports a foreign exposed class under an alias while also defining its own same-named local one no longer defeats the guard; regression test `error_export_class_cross_module_name_collision`. The ENUM guard was similarly hardened (reads `EnumInfo.module_name` off the resolved type object rather than `registry.imported_enum_qualification`'s name-keyed lookup) and the underlying general enum name-resolution bug that initially blocked verifying it (an aliased cross-module enum import getting confused with a same-canonical-name LOCAL enum, no `@export` needed to reproduce) is now fixed too (branch `fix-enum-alias-collision`: `parse/type_resolver.py`'s enum branch now mints a qualified `NominalType` from the import tuple instead of trusting a bare-name registry lookup, mirroring the pre-existing record branch; `codegen_cpp/generator.py`'s `native_cpp_names` population gained the qname-keyed entry records already had plus a local-shadow guard on the bare-name compensating write). Regression tests `tests/cases/enum/enum_alias_local_collision` (general) and `error_export_enum_cross_module_name_collision` (interop). (2c) **enum getset field on an exposed class** -- DONE (branch `interop-class-typed-fields`): a locally-defined exposed enum is a valid read/write getset field; the getter/setter reuse the same single-value marshal helpers (`_value_out_expr`/`_value_in_decl_expr`) the operator dunders use, so the field round-trips `enum_to_py`/`enum_from_py` against the module enum handle (member singleton preserved, strict-by-type set). A cross-module exposed-enum field stays a located error (the same cross-module guard, now covering the field role -- retargeted `error_export_class_enum_field`). Tests: `tests/interop/enum_typed_fields/`. (2d) `is_exposed_enum` reads `td.boundary_marshal` as an exposed proxy rather than a first-class `EnumInfo.exposed_to_host`; correct today (boundary_marshal set only when exposed) -- fold into the existing "unify is_exposed_class / is_boundary_marshallable onto one canonical check" cleanup, don't add the field standalone. (2e) DONE: asymmetric enum signatures (enum-IN-only `is_red(c: Color) -> bool`, enum-OUT-only `default_color() -> Color`) now exercise each marshal side independently in tests/interop/enum_values. (3) **`bytes`/`BytesView` and `char`/`tuple` constants** -- a `Final[bytes]` resolves to a view with no `to_py(span)` overload, and `char`/`tuple` aren't boundary types; all are silently left unexposed (like a non-`@export` function), documented in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`. A `bytes` constant would need either `to_py(BytesView/span)` or forcing the owned form. (4) **the auto-exposed-`Final` surface is implicit** -- there is no per-constant opt-in marker (unlike `@export` on enums/funcs/classes); a user intending to export a `Final[tuple]` gets silent non-export. Acceptable as the opt-in-parallel framing (only boundary-typed Finals form the surface), but if it bites, a future explicit constant-export spelling (or a warning on a skipped non-boundary `Final`) is the escape hatch. (5) **`_exposed_constants` re-resolves the Final type** via `resolve_stmt_type_cascade` (the generator's `seen_globals`/compiler's `ModuleVarInfo` already hold it) -- a small "consumer re-derives the fact" smell; fold onto a shared resolved-globals source when one is threaded to the glue. (6) **test gaps** (from /tpy-ready retrospective): an unannotated `X: Final = 5` constant (may carry an unresolved int-literal type that fails `_constant_exposable` where the annotated `Final[int]` form passes -- the item-5 materialized-type fix would also erase this) and an `auto()`-valued `@export` enum (the parser materializes `auto()` to concrete values at parse time, so the path is correct but untested) are both unexercised.
- **[CPython interop] str/bytes boundary -- deferred slices.** The str/bytes rung ships only the owned, immutable value forms by copy. Excluded, by design: (1) **`StrView`/`BytesView` (zero-copy view input)** -- a view param would borrow into the live PyObject for the call's duration; making that escape-sound for a *foreign* source is the phase-3.5 foreign-borrow primitive (IR-gated). Currently rejected with the standard "not marshallable" diagnostic; `str`/`bytes` (copy) are the workaround. (2) **`bytearray` (mutable buffer)** -- shares `bytes`' C++ representation (`std::vector<uint8_t>`) but is a reference type; marshalling it by copy as a `PyBytes` would silently drop the aliasing a CPython caller expects, so it is rejected (admission judges the `Own`-unwrapped inner type's `is_value_type`, so `bytearray` and `Own[bytearray]` both reject). Could later be supported as an explicit copy with a documented "no aliasing" note, or mapped to a real `PyByteArray` if a mutable round-trip is wanted. (3) **`str.upper()`/concat etc. produce fresh owned strings** -- fine today; no action. All three are in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`.
- **[CPython interop] PIC stdlib `.o` cache for ext-exec builds.** The exec phase reuses a shared precompiled stdlib `.o` set, but the ext-exec `.so` build is `-fPIC` so those objects don't apply -- `tpyc -b` recompiles the runtime + imported stdlib fresh on every cache-miss build (correct, just slower; ccache warms most of it). If interop build time grows, add a PIC-`.o` stdlib cache variant (or build the `.so` from the non-PIC set where the linker permits) so ext-exec re-verifies as cheaply as exec. Deferred until interop case count or build time justifies it.
- **[CPython interop] `error_`-style interop cases.** The ext-exec harness snapshots front-end diagnostics (`expected/diag.txt`) but still fails hard on a nonzero tpyc exit, so a compile-error ext module cannot be a case (the main harness's `error_` convention: expected-to-fail source with the error pinned in `diag.txt`). Add when a rejection is worth pinning at the interop level; comp-phase rejections live in `tests/cases/interop` today.
- **[CPython interop] auto-emit `__text_signature__` into the exposed-class docstring.** CPython parses a leading `Name(sig)\n--\n\n` out of a type's `tp_doc` into `__text_signature__`, so `help(Cls)` renders a real constructor signature line (this is how `help(dict)` shows `dict(mapping)`). TPy knows `__init__`'s signature statically, so the glue could synthesize that prefix into the emitted `Py_tp_doc` -- **zero runtime cost** (it is a string already being emitted) and strictly better `help()` output than the plain Python source gives. It also gives the dunder-docstring exclusion a positive story: the constructor's documentation lands somewhere useful instead of merely being warned about. Verified the bare `(x)` form parses and populates `__text_signature__` at the abi3 3.12 floor; NOT verified whether annotated/defaulted parameter forms survive CPython's signature parser, which is the first thing to check. Open question: whether to merge a user's `__init__` docstring into the class doc automatically (convenient but magic -- the author did not write it there) or only synthesize the signature line and leave prose placement to the author. Surfaced investigating why dunder docstrings cannot cross.
- **[CPython interop] follow-ups from /tpy-review.** (1) **Facade function-signature self-check.** `test_cpython_facade_selfcheck.cpp` validates struct layouts + constants but NOT the `extern "C"` function decls in `cpython_h.hpp`, so a wrong signature surfaces only at link/ABI corruption. Add `static_assert(std::is_same_v<decltype(&::PyFn), decltype(&tpy::cpy::PyFn)>)` per decl. (2) **Boundary-marshalling render helpers live in `codegen_cpp/generator.py`** (`boundary_cpp_type`, `boundary_unmarshallable_msg`) but are consumed upward by `the ext-module validator (tpyc/interop/module_validators.py)` via a local import -- a layering smell; move to a neutral `tpyc/codegen_cpp/ext_boundary.py` (or similar) both sides import. (The admission predicate itself already moved to `type_def_registry.is_boundary_marshallable`, and `BOUNDARY_CPP_TYPES`/`boundary_type_ok` were deleted, so only these two diagnostic-render helpers remain.) (3) **`_Py_NoneStruct` is not a named stable-API symbol** -- it is binary-exported by every CPython and the only way to reach `Py_None` from the no-`Python.h` facade at the abi3 3.12 floor (the documented `Py_GetNone()` lands in 3.13). Marked "don't use directly" upstream; swap to `Py_GetNone()` once the abi3 floor rises to 3.13. (Done in this round: void-return `@export` and the `to_py` overload-ambiguity, now resolved by a `requires`-constrained integral `to_py` template that never competes with the `int64_t`/`double`/`bool` overloads.)
- **[design question, open -- discussion stage, no decision] Revisit the `# tpy:` directive surface: comment pragmas vs in-language spellings.** Comment directives (`# tpy: ext_module`, `macro_module`, `namespace(...)`, `link("pcre2", managed=True)`, ...) are poorly visible in code (dim highlighting) even though typos already warn (parser.py's unknown-directive ParseWarning). Candidates discussed 2026-07-12: (a) status quo -- honest "metadata, not semantics", matches `# coding:`/`# type:` pragma precedent; (b) marker import `from tpy import __extension_module__` -- the `from __future__` precedent, loud typos, highlighted as code; no parameter channel, and linters flag it as an unused import (F401) unlike the special-cased `__future__`; (c) dunder assignments `__ext_module__ = True` / `__tpy_namespace__ = "..."` / `__tpy_link__ = [...]` -- declarative, statically scannable pre-execution (required by `macro_module`, which decides whether the module RUNS under CPython at compile time), CPython-inert without stubs, param-capable via literals, linter-quiet; (d) a call form (`tpy.extern.ext_module()`) -- rejected in discussion: looks like an import-time side effect but would never execute (a declaration in a call costume). Constraint: whatever is chosen must cover the WHOLE surface in at most two coherent forms (flags + parameterized), not fork per-directive; migration would touch every directive consumer, all tests, and docs. Whole-surface redesign, own /tpy-add-feature design pass if picked up.
- **[CPython interop] ext-exec harness robustness gaps (from /tpy-review).** (1) `discover_interop_cases` (conftest) silently drops a `tests/interop/<case>/` dir that has a `driver.py` but no `# tpy: ext_module` source, and picks only the first such `.py` -- a mis-named or future multi-module case is underbuilt with no diagnostic; warn/fail loudly instead. Relatedly, if discovery ever returns nothing, `_INTEROP_CASES` is empty and the module collects zero tests silently -- add a module-load guard asserting at least one case so a broken discovery fails loudly instead of no-op'ing. (2) `compute_ext_exec_fingerprint` doesn't key on the Python version (`sys.version_info`/`sys.executable`): the ext-exec marker stays green across a CPython minor-version switch, so a driver-output divergence between versions stays invisible until `--force-exec`. Fold the version into the fingerprint. Both deferred -- low bite with one case.
- **[CPython interop] ext-exec THIR overlay follow-ups (from /tpy-ready).** (1) **The overlay's AST side is anchored to nothing.** In `tests/cases` the overlay's AST emission is itself byte-compared to the committed snapshot (`tests/conftest.py`, the `all_modules` loop), so any drift between it and the real emission is loud. `run_interop_thir_overlay` instead compiles in-process and never compares its AST side to what the `tpyc` CLI actually wrote, so the overlay could emit a slightly different program than the case really builds and a divergence unique to the CLI shape would be missed. Exposure is nil today -- `options.no_main = True` is the whole ext-module derivation (`tpyc/cli.py`, the `ext_module_build` branch) and the overlay mirrors exactly that -- so this is structural hygiene, not a live defect. Cheap anchor: diff the overlay's AST output against the CLI's `gen_hpp`/`gen_cpp`/`gen_ext` with `// #` comment lines stripped. (2) **Module-scope diagnostics cannot be annotation-validated.** A module-level warning (e.g. the ext_module NUL-docstring drop) formats without a line number, so no `# tpyc: warning(/../)` annotation can attach to it and `tests/cases/interop/warn_export_docstring_nul` pins that site through `diag.txt` alone while its other six sites carry annotations. Either give module-scope diagnostics a line (the directive or docstring line) or teach `validate_annotations` a module-scope form.
- **`urllib.parse` v2 follow-ups (deferred from the v1 stdlib add).** Tracked per-item in STDLIB_ROADMAP.md's urllib.parse table: `parse_qs` (dict-of-lists; needs `dict[str, list[str]]` build), bytes variants (`quote_from_bytes`/`unquote_to_bytes`/`SplitResultBytes`), `urldefrag`, and the extra params/forms (`urlencode(doseq=)`, `quote(encoding=)`). Also the namedtuple-compatibility gap: results are records, so integer indexing (`r[0]`) and unpacking (`a, b, ... = urlsplit(u)`) are unavailable -- all-str components mean `__getitem__(int) -> str` is feasible to add if a parity need surfaces. Each is a focused `/tpy-add-feature`. Surfaced building urllib.parse v1.
- **`urllib.parse.unquote` invalid-UTF-8 -> U+FFFD divergence (silent, documented).** `unquote`/`unquote_plus` of a percent-sequence that decodes to invalid UTF-8 (e.g. `unquote("%FF")`) returns the raw bytes; CPython defaults to `errors='replace'` and substitutes U+FFFD. Matching it needs a lossy UTF-8 decode (`bytes.decode(errors=...)` or equivalent) the runtime does not yet expose -- a small runtime/stdlib feature, not a urllib fix. Well-formed URLs never hit it. Documented in the module header + LANGUAGE_FEATURES. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of urllib.parse v1. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (lossy UTF-8 decode).
- **[codegen perf] A constant container of literals should lower to a static/compile-time structure, not a runtime-rebuilt or runtime-initialized heap container.** Two rungs: (a) a set-literal membership in a function body (`x in {"a", "b", ...}`) rebuilds a fresh `ordered_set<std::string>` on EVERY call; (b) hoisting it to a module-level `set[str]` global (the current urllib.parse workaround) builds the heap set once at `__tpy_init` but is still a runtime-initialized heap object, not a compile-time constant. For a container of compile-time literals (esp. string sets used as lookup tables), codegen could emit a truly static structure -- a sorted `constexpr std::array<std::string_view>` + binary search, a perfect hash, or a `string_view` switch -- with zero per-call and zero startup heap cost. Surfaced by /tpy-review of urllib.parse's scheme tables. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[feature] Support `Final[set[...]]` / `Final[frozenset[...]]` (container constants) for module-level constants.** `Final` is currently restricted to primitives + tuple (`Final[set[str]] is not supported; only primitive types ... and tuple are allowed`), so a constant lookup table must be spelled as a plain mutable module global `set` -- which works but loses the immutability/intent `Final` documents (`frozenset` would be the natural CPython spelling). Pairs with the constexpr-lowering item above: a `Final` constant container is exactly what should lower to a static structure. Surfaced building urllib.parse's scheme tables (had to use a non-`Final` global). Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[feature] `collections.namedtuple` / `typing.NamedTuple` support.** A type that is simultaneously a tuple (indexable `r[0]`, unpackable `a, b = r`, iterable) AND carries named fields + methods/properties. TPy has no such type today, which forces stdlib results CPython returns as namedtuples -- `urllib.parse`'s `SplitResult`/`ParseResult` (and future `os.stat_result`-shaped results) -- to be plain records, losing indexing/unpacking (a deliberate, compile-visible divergence). Namedtuple support would let those be true namedtuples and close the divergence. Likely a `@class_macro` synthesizing `__getitem__`/`__iter__`/field properties over a backing tuple, or a first-class type-system construct. Surfaced building urllib.parse v1 (user: "eventually we should handle namedtuples"). Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[feature][small] An unannotated lambda local is a nested def: `k = lambda: 0` compiles as `def k() -> <inferred>: return 0`.** Today `k = lambda: 0` is refused (a lambda has no type of its own; it takes the slot's -- `Callable[...]` captures by value, `Fn[...]` by reference) with a message about parameter types (BUGS.md#lambda-local-needs-slot-type-message), while the same closure spelled `def k() -> int32: return 0` compiles as a by-reference nested def (`auto k = [&]() { ... }`). The feature: sema rewrites `name = lambda <params>: <expr>` with no annotation into a `TpyNestedDef` named `name` whose return type is the expression's, and lowers it through the existing nested-def path -- same capture, same liveness pin (a captured name is never moved in the enclosing body), same C++; no new form. A lambda WITH parameters still needs their types (Python lambda syntax has no annotations): a located error naming the remedies, `def k(x: int32)` or a `Callable[[int32], int32]` annotation; a lambda in a typed slot (`sorted(key=...)`, an `Fn` parameter, an annotated local) keeps today's path. Storing such a `k` into a `Callable` field copies the capture, as a nested def does. `/tpy-add-feature`, localized: the var-decl / assignment arm in `tpyc/sema/statements.py` plus the reworded message in `_analyze_lambda`. Surfaced in the REPL 2026-10-01; filed on request, not scheduled.
- **Multi-base ctor inheritance with a generic init parent -- test-coverage gap.** `_find_unique_init_parent` now accepts a generic-base instantiation as the unique init parent, and the `inheritance/generic_base_inherited_ctor` case covers single-base + generic-subclass shapes, but the multi-base mixin shape (`class Sub(Base[14], Mixin)` where `Mixin` contributes no `__init__`) is untested -- it exercises the `found is not None` uniqueness path with a generic init parent specifically. Add a case. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the generic-base inherited-ctor fix.
- **[IR migration] Keep a hoisted str/bytes tuple view target zero-copy when its source provably outlives the hoist scope (precise lifetime analysis).** Today a str/bytes tuple-unpack target hoisted out of a branch is unconditionally owned (`promote_hoisted_views`, the Option-A conservative rule): the hoisted slot outlives the per-branch `__tup` temp and any branch-local by-ref source, so a view would dangle. But when the by-ref source itself outlives the hoist scope, owning is an unnecessary copy. Two instances: (a) the source is a pre-existing function-scope local (`tuple_unpack_stable_name_keeps_view`, just hoisted); (b) the source is assigned on all branch paths under one shared name (`if c: t = make(); a, b = t else: t = make2(); a, b = t`), so the predecl machinery hoists `t` to the *same* outer scope as `a`/`b` -- the source is then function-lifetime and a view stays valid (every read of `a`/`b` happens while `t` is alive). The conservative rule over-owns both; the precise rule -- own iff the source does NOT outlive the target's hoist scope (accounting for same-scope declaration/destruction order) -- is place/loan escape analysis, which belongs on MIR's `Place`/`LoanInfo` model, not a codegen/sema heuristic. Until then the conservative copy is correct, just occasionally non-optimal. A loop `else` clause over-owns more than a branch does: it owns every unpack target the clause binds, even one read only inside the clause, where the identical `if` arm keeps the view (a target read AFTER the loop is decided at the read site, `own_view_if_block_sourced`). Surfaced fixing the tuple-unpack hoisting bug (Option B deferred).
- **[perf] The view hoist rule over-owns two loop heads whose element is lent.** A generator / genexpr yielding a tuple with a borrow-form reference member (`Iterator[tuple[Rec, int]]`, unpacked `for r, n in pairs(rs): y = r.name`) is treated as a by-value yield, because `yield_always_borrows` answers False for a tuple, so `y` copies (output unchanged). And a loop over a `set[str]` or `dict[str, ...]` PARAM (`for w in st: o = w`) records no iteration roots, so a view of its element hoisted past the loop copies too. Both are safe over-copies; the fix is asking the yield / container form per element.
- **[cleanup] Materialize the tuple-unpack "owned-temp source" fact as a `TpyTupleUnpack` AST field.** Sema (`_analyze_tuple_unpack`, `source_binds_by_ref`) and codegen (`_gen_tuple_unpack`, the bind-by-ref guard `isinstance(stmt.value, TpyName) and not any(stmt.is_owned)`) independently re-derive the same "does the source materialize an owned `__tup` temp vs bind by-ref" predicate; a comment pins the pairing today, but it is a sema/codegen mirror that will drift if codegen's bind conditions evolve. Set it once on the node (alongside `is_owned`/`is_ref`) and have both read it -- matches the "first-class AST facts over consumer-side re-derivation" rule + the THIR direction. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the tuple-unpack-view UAF fix.
- **[THIR migration] reach analysis excludes `enum_member_of` by field NAME -- make the exclusion structural before the next stamped type fact.** `sema/reach_analysis.py::_iter_typed_children` walks every `TpyType`-valued node attribute; `TpyFieldAccess.enum_member_of` (the sema-stamped binding fact for `E.A`) is skipped by a hardcoded key check, because surfacing it re-adds the defining module's include past the aliased-re-export dedupe (`tests/cases/imports/package_alias_reexport_enum`). It is the FIRST stamped fact that is an actual `TpyType`; the next one (any binding/codegen fact stamped as a type) will silently get walked and over-include unless someone remembers to extend the skip list. Options: a field-naming convention the walker checks (e.g. a `_binding` suffix), a wrapper marker type, or an explicit per-node allowlist of reach-relevant fields. NB the skip is by KEY over every node's `__dict__`, so the inverse failure exists too: a future unrelated attribute coincidentally named `enum_member_of` gets silently reach-skipped (under-include). Both failure modes surface as visible include diffs in snapshots, not silent miscompiles. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the value-binding frontier.
- **[THIR migration] value-binding hygiene one-liners (spend when the next enum/scalar cell lands).** (a) `_lower_call_arg` carries three boolean context flags (`temp_args`/`readonly_target`/`method_arg`); bundle into a small ArgCtx-style dataclass if a 4th arrives. (b) ~10 gate sites hand-write the `_eligible_scalar(t) or _eligible_enum(t, analyzer) is not None` disjunction -- fold the plain-disjunction sites into one combined value-scalar predicate when the next enum cell (cross-module/@native/nested) re-touches them anyway. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective of the value-binding frontier.
- **[THIR migration] THIR emit duplicates three AST-codegen leaf decisions verbatim (transitional, do NOT extract yet).** `tpyc/thir/emit.py` mirrors the AST path byte-identically by design (dual-mode during migration), duplicating: `_is_elif` source-column elif detection (vs `StatementGenerator._is_elif`), the `div_check`->`div_floor` / `mod_check`->`mod_floor` swap (vs `expressions.py` `_gen_binop`'s `divisor_non_zero` branch), and the comment-emission ordering. These collapse when the AST codegen path retires (THIR becomes the only emitter), so extracting a shared helper now would couple two paths meant to diverge-then-one-dies -- premature. Until then a change to an AST heuristic must mirror into emit.py; the byte-identical corpus run catches a divergence. The `Mirror ...` comments in emit.py are the intentional signposts -- keep them. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the THIR scaffold.
- **[THIR migration] THIR lowering depends on `codegen_cpp/type_resolution`.** `tpyc/thir/lower.py` imports `resolve_stmt_binding_type` from `codegen_cpp/` to capture a local's sema-deduced type onto `THIRVarDecl`. That helper is a sema-query (reads the analyzer, emits no C++) misplaced under codegen, so THIR -- the sema->codegen boundary -- inverts the layering by reaching into the codegen package. When the IR boundary hardens, move `resolve_stmt_binding_type` (and siblings) to `sema/` or `typesys`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the THIR scaffold.
- **[THIR migration] range-`for` slice deferred cells (increment 2).** `tpyc/thir/lower.py`'s `_for_range_eligible` covers only `range(stop)` / `range(start, stop)` step-1 counter loops over a fixed-int loop var not used after the loop. These richer shapes stay on the AST path and are the next breadth for range-`for`: (1) **3-arg / stepped ranges** (the `literal_pos != 1` / `literal_neg` / variable-step branches of `_gen_range_counter_loop`, incl. `range_check_step_nonzero` + `range_check_overflow`); (2) **hoisted loop var** (`hoist_loop_var` -- the `__range_N` hidden-counter + body-assign form); (3) **`for/else`** (the `__after_else_N` label + `orelse` block); (4) **bounds that are binops / calls / `int32(k)` ctors / negated literals** -- need the byte-identical net to confirm `gen_range_args`' `_gen_expr_deref(arg, ptype)` matches `_emit_expr` with the param-type context (the literal/name shapes are confirmed); (5) **loop var shadowing an outer local** (`was_declared` handling); (6) **non-`_eligible_scalar` element types** (e.g. BigInt, float32 range -- different overflow/`__step_N`/`f`-suffix handling; the gate is `_eligible_scalar`, which already admits bool/float, so only these stay out). Each is additive in `_for_range_eligible` + `THIRForRange` emit; the byte-identical net (`TPY_THIR_CODEGEN=1`) gates each. Surfaced building THIR increment 2.
- **[THIR migration] expression-statement slice deferred cells (increment 32).** The expr-statement cell (`tpyc/thir/lower.py` `_stmt_eligible` `TpyExprStmt` branch) routes `print(<scalar/str-literal args>)` + bare same-module free-function call statements. Deferred, additive behind the byte-identical net: **(1) docstring-opening bodies** -- a function/method whose body OPENS with a docstring stays fully AST, because the `TpyExprStmt` branch has no docstring carve-out, unlike the ctor M3c-trivia rung which treats `is_docstring(stmt) or TpyPassStmt` as inert `THIRNoOpStmt` trivia (`lower.py` ~2130). Reusing that precedent (a docstring/`pass` expr-statement -> `THIRNoOpStmt`) would route the common `def f(): """doc"""; print(...)` pattern -- a real routing gain, the self-contained tail of this cell. Deferred (not just "cheap, later") because it carries a design fork CLAUDE.md forbids settling autonomously: scope the no-op arm to docstring-position-only (a leading string-literal expr-statement) vs ANY bare string-literal expr-statement -- they differ on a mid-body bare `"str"`. **(2) bare numeric-literal print args** (`print(0)` / `print(1.5)`) -- an `IntLiteralType`/`FloatLiteralType` fails `_eligible_scalar`, so only named/typed scalar exprs route as print args; the literal-arg boundary is intentional (same reason bare-literal locals stay out). **(3) print f-string / container / BigInt args** -- ride the str/BigInt/form rungs. The `sep=`/`end=` kwargs LANDED (wave-2 tails: str-literal + resolved-str-NAME sources, `_print_kwarg_token`); still out there: `file=`/`flush=`, kwargs on an empty arg list, and non-literal/name kwarg sources -- note the emit renders sep-then-end (AST renders end-then-sep; unobservable until a temp-hoisting source is admitted, flagged in `_emit_print`). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + test-coverage) of the print cell. Drive the docstring carve-out via `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[thir][consolidation debt] Finish the name-read classifier: the DEREF half is consolidated, the ARROW half and a few stray copies remain.** `_name_read_deref` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) is now the single resolution point for whether a bare NAME read renders `(*name)`, position-keyed via `_ExprUse.indirect_read` (ledger: "Indirection consolidation"). Remaining hand-written copies of adjacent verdicts: (a) `THIRUnionArgLift.deref` recomputes `_ptr_read_derefs(name)` inline (expressions.py, the union-arg lift) -- fold by lowering the value under `indirect_read` and reading the node's own deref (the `_lower_ptr_name_src` pattern). It no longer needs a self-aware rung: the self-receiver deref became intrinsic to `THIRSelf` on 2026-08-29, and the lift's own comment now records that it must not stack a second one; (b) the ARROW half (receiver `->` vs `.`) is still per-site: ~6 `_ptr_read_derefs` receiver-arrow conditions -- a full classifier would answer bare/deref/arrow per name from one point; (c) manual `not in lc.pointers and not in lc.narrow.narrowed` pairs at guard sites (grep the pattern); (d) the resolver's plain (non-indirect) branch still relies on the non-local invariant that spelled/narrowed reads return early from the name arm and never reach it. **Adjacent but a DIFFERENT axis, do not fold blindly:** `_already_pointer_source` (predicates.py) answers "does this EXPRESSION already evaluate to `T*` at a pointer sink, so no `&` lift" -- expression-keyed and about the sink, where this item is name-keyed and about the read. A unified classifier should absorb it as a second question, not collapse the two into one. Surfaced by the thir-wave-next8 retrospective; deref half landed 2026-07-29.
- **[consolidation debt] Two predicates now answer "is this call a constructor" by different rules.** `is_constructor_call` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) was extracted so the AST and both THIR mirrors ask the iterable-lvalue question identically, and it consults `resolved_function_info.is_constructor` -- needed because `cls(...)` inside a `@classmethod` names no record. Its sibling `is_rvalue_source`'s `TpyCall` arm (`tpyc/value_category.py`) still tests only `get_record(func_name)` / `call_type`, so it does not recognise that spelling; the two agree on `cls(...)` only because that arm's fallthrough happens to be `return True` ("default: rvalue"). Benign today, and `is_temporary_expr` (which routes through `is_rvalue_source`) is consequently unaffected by the extraction -- but it is the duplicated-predicate shape that CLAUDE.md calls out, and the accidental agreement is exactly what makes a future divergence silent. Fix shape: have the `TpyCall` arm of `is_rvalue_source` delegate to `is_constructor_call` rather than re-deriving it. Surfaced by the merge-master semantic check on the loop-var storage-form branch.
- **[consolidation debt] Always fully-qualify local type references in generated C++ -- retire the conditional shadow-qualification (and CLOSE the member/type collision class uniformly).** Today local record/enum/@dynamic-protocol type *references* render bare (`day`) and only qualify (`::tpyapp::mod::day`) inside a record whose member shadows the type -- the `RecordInfo.shadows_local_type` sema fact + `_qualify_shadowed_nominals` flag + per-render-path flag-awareness (`_cpp_base_name` for records/enums, `get_dynamic_base_name` for protocols) + the THIR whole-record reject (`docs/THIR_COMPLETION_LEDGER.md`). This is the "parallelize" side of generalize-vs-parallelize: it added a SECOND qualification toggle beside the existing cross-module one (`native_cpp_names`, which ALREADY always-qualifies), and it needs a NEW flag-aware branch for every shadowable type kind -- proven by the recursive-union-alias-wrapper residual (BUGS.md), a 4th kind whose separate render path (`recursive_alias_cpp_names`) the conditional fix does not cover. Always-qualifying local references (extend the cross-module path to local) would DELETE the shadow fact + flag + all per-path branches + the THIR fallback cell AND close the collision class for every type kind at once -- collision-proof by construction, one uniform rule that subsumes the alias residual. Costs to weigh: whole-corpus snapshot churn; generated-C++ verbosity; it stays "qualify references, not DECLARATIONS" (struct/forward decls + out-of-line-def class name stay bare); and the THIR win needs THIR emit changed to bake qualified names too (coordinated AST+THIR). Verify no emit site breaks under blanket qualification (friend operators / ADL, templates, CRTP). This is the RIGHT closure of the collision class -- prefer it over adding a 5th flag-aware render path. Route via `/tpy-add-feature`. Surfaced by the user + the /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion of the member/type-name collision fix.

All low-risk, byte-diff-gated. **Not yet routed generic-record cells** (deferred, byte-identical fallback): a `T` LOCAL decl (`x = self.value`) and `Own[T]` METHOD params (not in `_f1_param_eligible`, so an `Own[T]`-param move-write falls back). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + test-coverage) of F5.

- **[THIR migration] Audit the remaining `_eligible_scalar(analyzer.get_expr_type(...))` gate sites toward `_resolved_scalar`.** Increment 34 added `_resolved_scalar` (`tpyc/thir/lower.py`: readonly/ref unwrap + `resolve_int_literals`) and migrated the ~7 sites the container-literal cell provably needed (method ret/args/slots, subscript results, print args, binop result, for-each elem); ~14 other `_eligible_scalar(get_expr_type(...))` sites remain (return values, assign RHS checks, condition operands, ...) that could equally see an unresolved `IntLiteralType` from a literal-seeded container's use sites. Safe today -- a stale site just returns False and the function conservatively stays on the AST path -- but it drifts: a future gate reaching for `_eligible_scalar` out of habit silently under-routes. NOT a mechanical rename: each conversion WIDENS what routes and needs its own byte-diff scrutiny (the increment-34 no-paren literal-operand binop reject is exactly the kind of emit fork such widening surfaces), so do it as a deliberate audit pass -- classify each site (needs resolution / genuinely literal-free), migrate the needed ones in one batch under the whole-corpus byte-diff. **Trigger: run the audit before opening the F3 form-ladder resumption** so drift doesn't accumulate across more statement-shape cells. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the container-literal-locals cell. NB: THIR deferral notes of this kind belong in `docs/THIR_COMPLETION_LEDGER.md`'s deferred-cell registry -- migrate the THIR paragraph-entries there when next touching them, keeping TODO.md a priorities list.
