- **[THIR migration] truediv (`/`) eligibility decision -- the `/` in `_ARITH_OPS` is dead.** The parser emits true-division as `TpyBinOp` op `div`, not `/`, so the `/` token in `tpyc/thir/lower.py`'s `_ARITH_OPS` never matches; `_binop_eligible` rejects truediv via the op-name miss, NOT a missing cpp_template (float and int truediv both carry `::tpy::truediv({self}, {0})`). Float increment 3 exposed this: pre-float, truediv's float result was rejected by `_eligible_scalar`; now only the op miss keeps it out. Decide: (a) **enable** truediv -- replace `/` with `div` in `_ARITH_OPS`, byte-verify via the net (float `a / b` emits `(::tpy::truediv(a,b))` identically per probe; ALSO verify int `a / b` -> float and any div-by-zero handling), or (b) **drop** the dead `/` token. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective (the float-`/` exclusion comment had the wrong reason).
- **[THIR migration] Unify the mixed-sign comparison predicate.** `tpyc/thir/lower.py`'s `_mixed_sign_compare` reproduces `tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py`'s `_mixed_sign_fixed_int` (both over the shared `int_traits_of`). They reach the same verdict by different literal-handling -- codegen has an `IntLiteralType` skip clause (`expressions.py` ~2131), while the THIR side resolves operand types first (`_operand_type`), so literals never reach the predicate. Net-gated today, but the divergent reasoning bites if either side's literal handling shifts. Hoist one predicate into the type layer (`type_def_registry`, where `int_traits_of` already lives) and have both phases call it. Surfaced by /tpy-review meta + /tpy-ready retrospective.
- **[THIR migration] The fallback-purity invariant is load-bearing and unguarded.** Generate-and-assert rests on lowering being side-effect-free w.r.t. shared analyzer/codegen state: when a body raises `ThirUnsupported` partway through, the partial attempt is discarded and the AST path re-emits that body. This holds today (`_LowerCtx`/`declared` are per-attempt; `movable_locals` is copied at `tpyc/thir/lower/context.py`; lowering only reads analyzer state), but nothing enforces it -- a future lowering arm that writes back into an analyzer set would corrupt the AST oracle on every fallback, with no test to catch it (fallback emits byte-identical AST, so the corruption surfaces as an unrelated miscompile elsewhere). Add an explicit invariant note at the four `except ThirUnsupported` boundaries (`lower_function` / `lower_constructor` / `lower_resumable` / `lower_top_level`) and a guard test that lowers a body which rejects mid-way and asserts the analyzer state is unchanged. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion of the gate removal.
- **[THIR migration] Defense-in-depth test: a later match arm / with-body / try-body falls back.** The sequential-lowering commits replaced the batch preflight walk over arm/handler bodies with `_lower_stmts`, which raises on the first unroutable statement after earlier ones already lowered. The mechanism is shared with flat bodies and covered by `test_sync_lowering_reports_first_reject_in_source_order` + its ctor twin (`tpyc/thir/test_fallback.py`), so this is a guard against a future local-catch regression, not a coverage hole -- optional. Unreachable today (`_body_eligible` rejects record-field writes), but if the eligible-field-write set ever grows, add an `assert isinstance(ftype, OptionalType)` before that node so the invariant is self-documenting and a gate gap fails as an AssertionError, not a cryptic emit crash. **scalar field writes** (`recv.field = <scalar>`) -- DONE (increment 10, `_scalar_field_write_ok`): a value-scalar field off any F1-record receiver lowers to a plain `THIRAssign`. **augmented assignment** (`recv.field += x` / `x += y`) -- DONE (increment 11, `_scalar_aug_assign_ok`): lowers to `target = (target OP value)` via `THIRBinOp` (+ a `paren_wrap` flag for the AST aug-assign's no-paren RHS), gating out in-place dunders / `str +=` / `FixedInt += BigInt` / subscript / class-constant targets. NB the `FixedInt += BigInt` gate became reachable when increment 75 admitted BigInt to `_eligible_scalar`; it is covered by the error case converted from the unit suite's BigInt aug-assign pin. The non-template `resolved_binop` gate stays defensive-only. **static / property / dunder-operator methods** -- DONE (increment 48); **generic-record methods** (templated `self`) -- DONE (F5 stages A-C, see `docs/THIR_COMPLETION_LEDGER.md`; residual: `T` local decls + `Own[T]` method params); **nested-record methods** still deferred (`iter_module_callables` walks top-level `module.records` only -- nested-record methods stay on the AST path, safe-by-omission). Surfaced building the THIR method frontier (M1).
- **[THIR migration] method frontier reuses the `_f1_is_const` / `_is_move_source` reproduce-mirrors unchanged (corpus net now restored).** M1 routes the F1/F2 mirror helpers (`_f1_is_const` vs `_is_const_indirect`, `_is_move_source` vs `_is_last_use_movable`; TODO entries above) over real corpus method bodies, so they are now corpus-validated, not just unit-tested -- the better moment to hoist them into shared analyzer-pure helpers (per "Hoist reproduce-style mirrors into shared helpers per-rung, NOT at F-final" above). M1 deliberately reused them as-is (routing, not refactoring); the extraction is a follow-on, lower-risk now that the net catches drift. Surfaced building the THIR method frontier (M1).
- **[THIR migration] `_f1_is_const` mirrors `_is_const_indirect` (transitional).** `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`'s `_f1_is_const` re-derives the field-source subset of `StatementGenerator._is_const_indirect` (the ReadonlyType reads on the optional inner / the init's raw sema type / the var_types entry, plus the storage-optional const bump) and uses a `const_locals` analog of the walk-built `const_indirect_locals`. Documented mirror needing manual lockstep if `_is_const_indirect` grows a new branch applicable to F1 field sources -- lowering can't call the ctx-bound method directly. Same transitional-mirror family as the emit.py increment-mirror entries above; dissolves when the AST form-codegen retires (F-final) or `_is_const_indirect` is hoisted to a shared analyzer-pure helper. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of F1.
- **[THIR migration] Hoist reproduce-style mirrors into shared helpers per-rung, NOT at F-final.** The byte-identity-to-AST contract is the oracle that validates THIR -- and it is DELETED at F-final (when the AST form-codegen retires). So the *reproduce*-style mirrors (`_f1_is_const` vs `_is_const_indirect`; the F2b `_gen_assign` optional-field-write branch; `_is_move_source` vs `_is_last_use_movable` -- F2e, with the extra sema-set-vs-walk-built-`movable_locals` equivalence to re-audit on each slice expansion (M3b-move generalized `_is_move_source` to take a `movable_names` param mirroring the AST helper, the ctor MIL passing `own_param_names` -- so the two now share that shape and must move in lockstep); `_mixed_sign_compare` vs `_mixed_sign_fixed_int`; `_positional_only_template` vs `expand_cpp_template`'s brace grammar (incr 37 -- a gate-side re-parse, so a grammar miss only under-routes or fails loudly, never mis-emits); `_str_name_form`/`_resolved_str_value` vs `_is_str_view_source`/`_resolve_view_storage` (incr 38 -- EMIT-load-bearing: the name-form tag drives the owned-sink `std::string(x)` copy, so this pair is in the high-risk mirror class; when the next str owned sink lands, also fold the twice-spelled decl-init/return wrap condition into one `_wrap_view_to_owned` helper); the emit.py increment-mirrors incl. the F2d two-slot `__slot_N` emit vs `_gen_pointer_local_init`) do NOT "die" at F-final -- they become the canonical and only implementation exactly when their validating diff vanishes, baking in permanently any subtly-wrong behavior that neither a unit test nor an organic corpus case exercised. Contrast the *extract* pattern (`classify_local_binding`, `resolve_stmt_binding_type` -- both paths call one helper, identical by construction), which carries no such risk. Action: prefer extract over reproduce-mirror for each new sema->codegen fact, and hoist each existing mirror into a shared analyzer-pure helper as part of the rung that needs it, so reconciliation is incremental-and-oracle-checked rather than a big-bang at F-final after the net is gone. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion of F2.
- **[design territory] Fix the stale-resolved-twin at its source in sema, not at each codegen consumer.** The const-rooted-receiver arms (`_is_const_indirect` + `_f1_is_const`) and the sibling `val_or_cref_t`/`val_or_ref_t` TypeParamRef-return gate (`statements.py:2397` / `thir/lower/statements.py:4050`, filed in BUGS.md) all compensate for the SAME root cause: sema resolves a self/receiver call to the MUTABLE twin before the enclosing method's readonly-ness is inferred in Phase 2, so `resolved_function_info` no longer matches what C++ overload resolution picks on a const receiver. Each codegen/THIR consumer re-derives receiver-constness to paper over the stale `fi`. A cleaner fix re-resolves (or flags) affected self/receiver calls' `resolved_function_info` right after `infer_method_const` runs in `tpyc/sema/mutation_propagation.py`, so every present and future consumer of `fi.is_readonly` sees a correct fact instead of special-casing "peek at the receiver instead of trusting `fi`." Design territory (a Phase-2 re-resolve may carry its own fixpoint ordering concerns); discuss before implementing. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the inferred-readonly borrow-const fix.
- **[THIR migration] `THIRAssign.target` is a bare `THIRExpr` (no lvalue guarantee) -- weigh a Place-precursor for F3/F4.** F2b widened `THIRAssign.target` from `THIRName` to `THIRExpr` to carry the optional-field-write target (`recv.field` / `recv->field`), chosen on byte-identity grounds (emit renders both via `_emit_expr`). It is looser than MIR's `Place(Local/Field/Index)` and gives no structural guarantee the target is an lvalue. F3 tuple-unpack and subscript-write targets will pile onto the bare-expr target; revisit a thin lvalue-shaped target node (a Place-precursor) when those land, rather than accreting more shapes onto a bare expr. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion of F2.
- **[THIR migration] F3 storage-tuple alias decision is reproduce-mirrored, not extracted.** `forms.is_storage_tuple_alias_decl` (the `auto&& t = <storage tuple field>` arm) is co-located with the binding classifiers as the shared home, but the AST path (`statements.py` `_gen_var_decl_code` ~2157-2186, the `storage_form_tuple_locals` `auto&&` return) still decides this arm inline -- so two implementations co-exist, with the whole-corpus byte-diff as the only anti-drift net. Extending the THIR subset (Subscript / storage-form-Name alias sources) requires updating BOTH the predicate and the inline AST arm in lockstep. Per the "prefer extract over reproduce-mirror" rule (above), the clean fix is to refactor the AST arm to call `is_storage_tuple_alias_decl` (a verified zero-diff extract-method, like `classify_local_binding`); fold it in when the next F3 alias-source cell lands, or at F-final. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of F3. **UPDATE 2026-07-28: that cell LANDED (`fd519dddb`) and the extract was DEFERRED, so the mirrored surface is now wider, not narrower** -- the predicate gained the Subscript and storage-form-Name sources plus a `storage_tuple_locals` param. Note the entry's own lockstep warning did NOT apply: the AST arm already admitted all three shapes, so the widening only brought THIR up to it. The extract is an AST-side refactor and must land as its own change-set (AST and THIR changes never share one), which is why it was not folded in here.
- **Nullable static-protocol param in a ctor member-init field initializer -- test-coverage gap.** `seed_param_locals` now seeds `pointer_locals`/`const_indirect_locals` for a nullable static-protocol ctor param (e.g. `Optional[Sized]`) in the member-init-list context, but no test exercises a MIL-eligible ternary field-init on one (`self.count = len(items) if items is not None else 0`); existing protocol-optional-param ctors branch via `if/else` in the body, which is body-emitted not MIL-hoisted. Same `pointer_locals` deref mechanism the optional-ptr/union cases cover (`records/ctor_field_init_*`), distinct type path. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the ctor-MIL-deref fix. `seed_param_locals` now seeds `pointer_locals`/`const_indirect_locals` for a nullable static-protocol ctor param (e.g. `Optional[Sized]`) in the member-init-list context, but no test exercises a MIL-eligible ternary field-init on one (`self.count = len(items) if items is not None else 0`); existing protocol-optional-param ctors branch via `if/else` in the body, which is body-emitted not MIL-hoisted. Same `pointer_locals` deref mechanism the optional-ptr/union cases cover (`records/ctor_field_init_*`), distinct type path. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the ctor-MIL-deref fix.
- **`raise E(own_arg)` Own[T]-move -- test-coverage gap.** The raise path now shares the bare-name ctor arg-lowering loop, so the protocol / covariant / optional-ptr / union / mutated-temp arms are covered from a raise site (`exceptions/raise_ctor_*`). Still untested: a `raise E(own_arg)` where `__init__` takes an `Own[T]` param -- the move-at-last-use lives in the `gen_call_arg` fallback, not a dispatch arm, so it's a separate cell; make `T` `@nocopy` so a silent copy is a build error, cover both throw and return tier. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the raise-arg coercion fix.
- **`unsafe_interior_mutable` fields -- deferred scope (v1 shipped Ptr-only, field-level).** The interior-mutable field marker (`unsafe_interior_mutable[Ptr[T]]`, dual of `readonly`; landed for `Rc`/`Weak` refcount cells so `clone`/`downgrade`/`upgrade` are readonly-callable and yield readonly-payload clones) deliberately ships a subset: (a) **value-field interior** -- `unsafe_interior_mutable[T]` on a non-pointer field (a memoized/cached value mutated through a readonly getter) is rejected today; supporting it needs codegen to emit the C++ `mutable` keyword on the member (the Ptr case needs no codegen change since const doesn't cross a raw pointer). (b) **type-level interior metadata** -- instead of a per-field marker, declare a *type* as interior-mutable (e.g. `@unsafe_interior_mutable` on `_RcCellBase`) via library-declared `TypeDef` metadata, so every `Ptr[InteriorType]` field inherits it with zero per-field annotation (more CLAUDE.md-aligned, but broadens the hatch to every appearance of the type -- weigh against the field-level opt-in's auditability). Both are `/tpy-add-feature`-sized. (c) **reject `unsafe_interior_mutable[Ptr[readonly[T]]]`** -- the validation accepts a `Ptr` to a readonly pointee, but `unsafe_interior_mutable` on a const-pointer field is meaningless (the pointee is already inside the readonly boundary); add a reject branch + an `error_` case. Surfaced building the interior-mutable readonly-`Rc.clone` feature.
- **Zero-copy `json.dumps` over typed container shapes -- BLOCKED on protocol-conformance coverage.** Goal: dumping a *typed* container variable (`d: dict[str, int32]`) serializes in place with no `JsonValue` wrapper (the current behavior is a clean rejection -- `error_json_dumps_concrete_container` -- after the implicit `to_union` deep-copy was reverted as a footgun). The clean way is a pure-stdlib type-directed serializer (a `ToJson` protocol + `dumps[T: ToJson](obj: T)`), but that needs built-in/container types to conform to a protocol, which TPy can't express today -- see "Protocol conformance for built-in and generic-container types" under Open feature gaps. A json-specific C++ writer + compiler routing was considered and rejected: it just duplicates the same compiler coupling we want to remove from `print`. So this stays blocked on that foundational capability; keep the clean rejection until then. Surfaced designing zero-copy json.dumps (reverted `to_union`).
- **`PostSemaFunctionMacroContext.note_param_mutated` is shaped for the single-overload free-function host.** The method-body host surface has begun landing (deferred method macros are now driven by `_drain_deferred_sema_macros`), so `note_param_mutated` now explicitly rejects a method host (`if self.is_method: error(...)`) rather than mis-targeting a free function -- but the real method-aware support is still open, and multi-overload targeting was always broken: (a) it writes `direct_mutated_params` on `registry.get_function(name)[-1]`, the last overload by position -- wrong target for a multi-overload host, and the method case needs a `record.get_method`-aware lookup instead; (b) the no-FunctionInfo guard is defensive and untested because it is unreachable through supported usage today (only the out-of-range guard and the new method-host guard have `error_*`/unit coverage); (c) for a *method* host, seeding `direct_mutated_params` can flip Phase-2 `is_readonly` inference and structural-protocol conformance, not just local const-ness. Revisit overload targeting, method-aware resolution, and the readonly/conformance interaction to lift the method-host rejection. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective of the post-sema note_param_mutated addition; method-host guard added by /tpy-review of feat-method-function-macros.
- **Unify the two empty-literal/generic-constructor annotation blocks (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py` ~457 and `tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~3430).** The empty-`[]`-against-a-hint logic is duplicated near-verbatim across the call-arg/hint path (`analyze_expr_with_hint`) and the annotated-assignment path (`x: T = []`): both compute `hint_matches`/`annotation_matches`, both build the `ListLiteralInfo` with `has_explicit_annotation`/`explicit_type`, and both now carry the same recursive-union list-member branch (`needs_wrapper()` + `_find_list_member`). They must be kept in lockstep -- the union branch was added to expressions.py first and the statements.py copy was the source of a half-fixed bug (`x: JsonValue = []` rejected while `json.dumps([])` worked). Fold into one shared helper (statements.py could delegate to the expression path, or both call a common `_resolve_empty_literal_against(target)`). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the empty-list recursive-union fix.
- **Coordinate the two "generic container vs recursive union" dispatches in `compatibility._check_compat`.** The concrete-std-container rejection guard and `_check_union_member_type_args` (immediately below it) share the same outer condition (same-name `NominalType`, differing `type_args`) and are non-overlapping only by construction (the guard requires a std container + a `needs_wrapper()` union element + `a_res != e_res`; the other handles the accept path). Any future change to either has to know about the other. Consider folding the std-container deep-conversion check into `_check_union_member_type_args` (or a shared classifier) so the accept/reject decision lives in one place. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the cross-module recursive-union literal fix.
- **Unify non-generic recursive-union (`AliasRef`) C++ rendering onto the qname-keyed map.** The non-generic path renders via the short-name `native_cpp_names` channel (`AliasRef.to_cpp` + the imported-recursive-union registration in `generator.py`), which is collision-prone when two different modules export same-short-named recursive unions both reached cross-module without import -- mitigated today by a first-write-wins skip-guard + the documented same-short-name limitation. The generic path (`RecursiveAliasInstanceType`) is already collision-proof via the qname-keyed `recursive_alias_cpp_names` map. Clean end-state: route non-generic `AliasRef` rendering through the same qname-keyed map (key `{module}.{name}`), retiring the short-name channel for recursive-union wrappers. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective of the cross-module recursive-union literal fix.
- **[LOW perf] str/bytes view->owned wrap is redundant in direct-init contexts.** The shared `_view_source_to_owned` chokepoint wraps a view source uniformly (`std::string(view)` / `::tpy::bytes_copy(view)`) because it can't see its consuming context. In a *direct-initialization* context -- a tuple literal `std::tuple<std::string,...>{view, ...}` -- the str element's explicit `string_view` ctor is already reachable, so the old `{tag, ...}` built the element IN PLACE; the wrap now materializes a temporary + move-constructs it (`{std::string(tag), ...}`), adding one cheap `std::string` move (buffer steal, no extra allocation/char-copy). Function-arg sinks (`push_back`, etc.) genuinely NEED the wrap (the explicit ctor doesn't fire on implicit conversion -- that was the original build failure). Skipping the wrap in tuple-literal str contexts would reintroduce a str-vs-bytes asymmetry (bytes still needs it: `std::vector` has no ctor from `span`), so a clean fix is context-aware (the chokepoint, or its callers, knowing direct-init vs copy-init). Negligible; only worth it if tuple-of-str-from-view turns up on a hot path. Surfaced reviewing the view->owned unification snapshots. **Tuple-unpack TARGETS now reach this sink too**: fixing `get_resolved_type`'s unresolved `var_types` return made them view-form, so `take((x, y))` off `x, y = src` went from the in-place `{x, y}` to `{std::string(x), std::string(y)}`. Same one-move cost, but it widens the shape set a context-aware chokepoint would have to cover, and it is the second source kind to land here -- if a third arrives, build the fix instead of re-noting it.
- **[MED design] Warn at the mixed-tuple module GLOBAL as a stopgap, before the global slot learns the borrow form.** The storage-form wave made `G: tuple[Box, Box] = make_mixed(B)` reachable (it failed the C++ build before) and it now copies SILENTLY -- a new silent CPython divergence, filed in BUGS.md (now MED, narrowed to the mixed global after the all-borrow half closed). The full fix (a borrow-form global slot mirroring the local's machinery) was deferred as too large, but the cheap half was NOT taken: firing the same per-element copy warning the container and field sinks already give would make the divergence acknowledged rather than silent, at the cost of a new warning site. Wants a decision rather than a patch -- it is a diagnostic the deferred fix would later remove, and the pinning case `tuple/element_vs_singleton_global` would need its expectations updated twice. Tracked separately so it reads as the one cheap thing that would stop the wave shipping a new silent divergence, rather than as part of the deferred full form.
- **[design][low] Module scope is the body of __tpy_init: a module global takes the form its local twin would** (plain storage for a single assignment, the reassigned local's pointer-over-per-assignment-storage for a rebound or aliased one), its C++ type fixed once from all module-level writes and read by importers off the exported binding -- replaces 'every reference global is a pointer slot' for scalars and tuples alike; absorbs `BUGS.md#global-tuple-ref-storage-form` and the tuple-global rebind-after-unpack refusal. PRIORITY (user decision 2026-09-23): module globals are the least important position -- serious programs rarely use them -- so global-position work ranks LAST and is not patched per position or per shape: a global divergence is filed against this entry, not fixed on its own branch. A per-shape fix (tuple-of-references globals as pointer slots over per-write static backing) was built on `u1-tuple-meds` and removed again before merge: correct, but a parallel mechanism this redesign would delete. Filed here 2026-09-25: a module-level receiver of a user `__getitem__` (`R = Rows()` then `R[0].append(3)` or `len(R[0])` at module scope) rejects at `method.recv.subscript` / the record-getitem arm, whose index/receiver gate admits a global pointer slot only at a plain element read, while the builtin twin (`B["m"].append(1)` on a `dict[str, list[int32]]` global) compiles.
- **[MED] Make the tuple RENDER 3-valued instead of stacking booleans over it.** `is_storage_form_source(expr)` returns a boolean for what is really a 3-valued render -- BORROW / MIXED / STORAGE -- so the storage-form wave had to bolt `renders_own_borrow_tuple` beside it and derive `needs_tuple_storage_lift = not storage or mixed` on top, two booleans encoding three states with the redundancy unstated. Three separate bugs on that branch came from one predicate answering two questions, which is what forced the split. The clean shape is `tuple_render_of(expr) -> {BORROW, MIXED, STORAGE}` with all three booleans as one-line derivations; that is also exactly `docs/IR_DESIGN.md` Q9's form-as-IR-fact, so it should land AS the THIR lowering rather than twice. NOT a fold of `owned_tuple_storage_type` into `collapse_tuple_own_elements` -- that was proposed and correctly rejected, since the two encode OPPOSITE facts (borrow-form unification vs owned-storage form) at disjoint call sites. ~15 `is_storage_form_source` call sites.
- **[MED] Sema mirrors codegen's tuple-render pair at a different breadth.** `_is_owning_tuple_call` (sema) duplicates `is_storage_form_source`'s call arm, and `_borrow_carrying_tuple_return` (sema) mirrors `renders_own_borrow_tuple` (codegen) but tests `has_ref_elements()` where the codegen side tests `is_mixed_own()`, with the ternary composition rule copy-pasted between them. They agree today by compensation, not by construction -- the 're-derive the fact at the consumer' pattern CLAUDE.md warns about, across the sema/codegen boundary. Folds into the 3-valued render item above. Diagnostic wording from U1 worth a pass: a mixed container ternary at an `Own` tuple element says "parameter, attribute, or non-last-use variable" even for a last-use local arm, and its `@nocopy` hint suggests auto-move, which never applies to a ternary arm; `return (d := c)` at the last use of `c` warns "use copy()" where `return c` is the better remedy. A third instance, from U1: `_LAST_USE_MOVES_SINKS` restates a lowering decision in sema. The tuple-literal member walker (`check_tuple_literal_members`, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) exempts a last-use `@nocopy` member only at the FIELD and YIELD sinks, because the lowering MOVES a last-use member there and lifts the literal through `tuple_to_storage` (a copy even then) everywhere else. That is a fact about the render kept in sync by hand: if a lowering arm starts moving at a container sink (or stops at a field), sema's verdict silently disagrees with the C++. The same debt: `arrives_borrowed` leaves a MIXED-arm ternary with a RECORD or protocol result (`c if k else C(5)`) out of every scalar `Own`-slot check because the lowering refuses that shape today (a container result lowers and is checked per arm); the day a record one lowers, the copy of the name arm is silent unless the check learns it. The fact belongs on the sink's form, decided once and read by both sides.
- **[MED] Tuple-element storage-form sinks with no corpus coverage.** The wave's eight-sink claim is pinned unevenly: a plain field assign OUTSIDE a ctor (`h.t = make_mixed(b)`; only the ctor member-init path is exercised), a local reassign, `list.insert()`, a set comprehension, and the POSITIVE arg-lift direction (a mixed result into a fully-owned tuple param -- the param case pins only the negatives) have no case. The `@nocopy` element error is pinned at `append` alone. A regression at the mixed-param sink already shipped past a green full suite for exactly this reason.
- **[LOW] The tuple copy warning states a cost, not a consequence.** `copies B into owned storage (tuple element i); use copy() to make this explicit` reads as an allocation nit, but the thing that matters is that a later write through the stored value will NOT be seen on the original -- these are CPython divergences. The scalar sibling has the same wording. Family-wide rewording, not specific to tuples.
- **[HIGH design] A tuple element does NOT behave like the same type would as a singleton at that position -- and it should.** The rule: element `i` of `tuple[T1, T2, ...]` at position P behaves exactly as `Ti` would as a standalone value at P -- same copy/reference rules, same view rules, same ownership rules. Today the per-position rules are written for top-level values and do not reach inside the aggregate, so each element kind re-derives its form from a different place. **Known instances.** (1) A `str`/`bytes` element of a tuple PARAM is storage form: `def f(t: tuple[str, str])` renders `const std::tuple<std::string, std::string>&`, so passing two views costs two allocations plus two char-copies where `def f(a: str, b: str)` passes the same data as `std::string_view` for free -- visible in one call site: `takes_scalars(a, b)` beside `takes_tuple(std::tuple<std::string, std::string>{std::string(a), std::string(b)})`. The tuple element table (`docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`, the borrow/storage row) defines a borrow form only for `T | None` and plain NON-VALUE slots, while the `str`/`bytes` param-view rule is a documented exception to value semantics applied only to a TOP-LEVEL param. (2) A per-element-`Own` tuple (`tuple[Own[A], B]`): storing one now materializes the borrowed element BY VALUE at every storage sink and warns per element with `copy()` as the acknowledgment -- step (a) below, DONE. The borrow-POSITION decl paths (rebind, walrus, hoisted local, branch/loop-carried, generator and async frame local), the method-producer const disagreement, and the `| None` element are DONE -- step (b) below. A reference member nested inside an inner value tuple warns at every sink too, naming the depth as an element path (the copy check walks nested value tuples). What remains is the `Optional`-WRAPPED producer, whose return ABI is a design fork rather than a fix; and one sink that still copies SILENTLY -- the MIXED module global (the all-borrow tuple global is a tuple of pointer slots now). Both are filed in BUGS.md. The inferred container element type now takes the owned storage form, so a fixed `Array` and a `vector` no longer disagree about alias-vs-copy at the same store. **Caveat on the rule:** it is same SEMANTICS, not same C++ spelling -- a singleton borrow is `T&`, but a tuple of references is non-assignable (exactly what makes the container shape fragile), so elements keep the `T*` stand-in. **Sequencing.** (a) make storage agree with the annotation rule (sema) -- DONE for the bare mixed tuple; (b) fix the borrow-position decl paths -- DONE, AST-first per the THIR contract (sema keeps the per-element `Own` on a mixed local instead of collapsing it onto a unified borrow it has no form for, and every decl path spells the mixed render); the `Optional`-wrapped return is carved out of it as its own design question; (c) unify onto ONE elementwise "what form does element i take here" question, which is what THIR's form-as-IR-fact design exists for (`docs/IR_DESIGN.md` Q9) -- do that AS the THIR lowering, not twice. Cost to expect: element form changes tuple param SIGNATURES for `str`/`bytes`, so wide snapshot churn plus an ABI change. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. **Ordering and release split:** `docs/TUPLE_COMPLETION_PLAN.md` -- step (c) is its U5, instance (1) its U6, both 0.7.0; the silent cells and everyday rejects are U1-U2, 0.6.0.
- **[LOW codegen readability] A bytes literal coerced to owned bytes/bytearray still renders the nested `::tpy::bytes_copy(::tpy::bytes_literal("...", N))`.** The storage-form literal path now emits the single `::tpy::bytes_literal_owned(...)`, but a bytes literal reaching an owned slot via a COERCION (`bytesview_to_bytes` / `bytesview_to_bytearray` in `tpyc/coercions.py`) -- notably `bytearray(b"...")` -- still gets the nested form: the literal renders as a view (`bytes_literal(...)` span) and the coercion lambda, which only sees the already-rendered string, wraps it in `bytes_copy(...)`. Correct, just verbose. Clean fix: render a bytes-literal source whose target is an owned bytes/bytearray slot directly via `cpp_bytes_literal_owned` (so no view->owned coercion fires) -- a sema/coercion-insertion change, NOT a codegen-helper swap, and NOT a string-sniff of the coercion arg. Surfaced finishing the readable-bytes-literal work (~8 snapshots still show the nested form, all `bytearray(b"...")`). Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[LOW codegen readability] A long call render has no way to wrap its arguments, so qualifying same-module callees pushed 386 snapshot lines past 100 columns (max 146).** `thir/emit.py` joins a call's arguments into one line unconditionally; the `::tpyapp::<mod>::` prefix every same-module free call now carries added ~20 columns to each of them, and a nested call or a synthesized lambda (the coroutine-factory wrapper is the worst at 146) compounds it. `generated-cpp-readability` in docs/PITFALLS.md asks for one argument per line past an editor width, but no emitter-side mechanism exists to do it -- the render is a single f-string. Fix shape: a wrapping helper in `thir/emit.py` that every call-shaped render (free call, method call, constructor, native helper) routes its argument list through, breaking one argument per line at the indent of the open paren once the joined form exceeds the width. Whole-corpus snapshot churn, no behavior change. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the ADL requalification.
- **[LOW] Fold the str/bytes view->owned-into-Optional-slot decision into the one chokepoint.** The view->owned unification routed three sites through `_view_source_to_owned`, but a FOURTH decider remains: `_maybe_convert_opt_str_param` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py:486`, called at :1318) handles an `Optional[str]` param flowing into an `Optional[str]` slot (emits `s ? std::make_optional(std::string(*s)) : std::nullopt`), and it is str-ONLY (no bytes sibling). Not buggy today -- the bytes-Optional-into-Optional-slot shapes build and run via the optional/coercion machinery -- so this is cleanliness, not a defect. The clean end-state: the chokepoint's bare-slot arm uses `_is_*_view_source OR _expr_uses_optional_*_param`, while the `_wrap_for_owned_slot` Optional residual uses only `_is_*_view_source` (to avoid double-wrapping a whole-optional source); both could instead key uniformly on `_is_narrowed_value_optional(expr)` (`:570`, declared-Optional + analyzed-non-Optional = a narrowed deref vs a whole optional), collapsing the param-name augmentation and `_maybe_convert_opt_str_param` into the single chokepoint and giving bytes parity for free. A consumer-side re-derivation today; folding it onto the first-class `_is_narrowed_value_optional` fact is the per-CLAUDE.md direction. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion of the view->owned unification.
- **[cleanup] The str/bytes view->owned copy spelling lives in two helpers.** `view_to_owned_conv` (`tpyc/type_def_registry.py`, the bare `std::string` / `::tpy::bytes_copy` callable, wrapped by `view_owned_copy_init` for the coro/generator-frame ctor-init + init-capture) and `_view_owned_copy_expr` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py`, the expression-site chokepoint + optional-param assign) both encode the same str->`std::string` / bytes->`::tpy::bytes_copy` mapping. Collapse to one source -- `_view_owned_copy_expr` could delegate to `view_to_owned_conv`, or the mapping could become a `copy_conv` field on `ViewTypeFamily` that every consumer reads. The two serve different layers (registry frame-capture vs codegen expression-site), so it is a cross-module consolidation, not a mechanical swap; relates to item folding `_maybe_convert_opt_*_param` onto `_is_narrowed_value_optional`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the bytes view-family param unification.
- **Compound view-source residual optimization (core DONE).** The COMPOUND view-deduction work (ternary / `and`-`or` / nested) is done: a view deduced from a compound owned-borrow source now registers EVERY storage root via the shared `walk_view_source_leaves` traversal (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`), so mutating any root demotes it to owned -- this closed a silent UAF (a compound view tracked no roots before) -- and a narrowed `str | None` param deref is now a zero-copy view (the `std::string(std::string(...))` double-wrap is gone). One residual *optimization* remains, currently resolving OWNED (sound, just not zero-copy): **mixed pending-view + owned-borrow compound arms** (`x = a if c else d[0]`, `a` a pending-view local) conservatively resolve owned (the pending arm forces owned in the fresh-from-owned branch) -- a view tracking both the `source_var_ids` and the borrow-root channel would reclaim the copy. Folds naturally into the provenance-classifier consolidation (next item). Surfaced finishing the compound-view-roots fix.
- **[cleanup] Unify the view-source structural recursion shape.** THREE independent walks of the same TpyCoerce / TpyBinOp `&&`-`||` / TpyIfExpr arm shape: `walk_view_source_leaves` (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`, drives pending-source + borrow-root collection), `is_view_compatible_source`'s own and/or+ternary recursion (same file, the view-safety predicate -- guarded today only by a keep-in-sync INVARIANT comment), and `addr_taken_roots` (`tpyc/sema/context.py:46`). A future node kind (e.g. walrus) needs all three updated in lockstep; a miss between the predicate and the leaf walk yields a stale view (UAF). Route `is_view_compatible_source` through `walk_view_source_leaves` (a leaf-fn returning view-safe-ness combined with `all()` -- non-trivial: the predicate uses AND/short-circuit + PendingViewType early-exits vs the walk's list return, so it's a small design step, not mechanical), and move the shared walker into `context.py` (it only needs parse nodes; `local_deduction` imports `context`, so verify no import cycle) so `addr_taken_roots` shares it too. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, safety-model) of the compound-view-roots fix. (Breadcrumb: routing reassigned `str`/`bytes` PARAMS through this same view-source machinery -- so a param reassigned only to borrow-valid sources stays a view like a local does, retiring the coarse `param_needs_copy_for_reassign` for view types -- was probed and DEFERRED as not-worth-standalone: near-zero corpus payoff and a silent-dangle risk if mis-classified (a `span` param is implicitly constructible from an owned vector, so a wrong call dangles with no build error). Only fold the param-reassign path in if doing this consolidation anyway.)
- **[cleanup] DRY the for-loop / comprehension iterable-render call sites onto one `(code, type)` helper.** The narrowed-value-Optional fix routes every iterable-render site through the pair `_maybe_unwrap_narrowed_optional(expr, gen_expr_deref(expr), is_indirect_name(expr))` + `narrowed_value_optional_iter_type(expr, get_resolved_type(expr))` -- repeated inline at ~3 comprehension sites in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py` (`_gen_comprehension_iife`, `_gen_comp_begin_end_loop`, the array/general comp paths), plus the sync for-loop's `_for_iterable_deref` and the resumable `gen_async._for_src_access` / `gen_generators._analyze_for_strategy`. A single helper returning `(rendered_code, dispatch_type)` would collapse the repetition and make a future missed iterable-render site (the recurring decay pattern) impossible. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the narrowed-Optional for-loop fix.
- **[cleanup] `_enter_comp_scope` queries the un-narrowed iterable type when registering the comprehension loop var.** `tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py` -- `_enter_comp_scope` calls `get_resolved_type(gen.iterable)` (not `narrowed_value_optional_iter_type`), so for a narrowed value-Optional iterable `get_iterable_element_type` returns None and the comp loop var is left unregistered in the var-type table. No live symptom for `str`/`bytes` (the element is `char`/`uint8`, never an Optional needing a deref), so it is latent; route it through the same narrowed-type helper for consistency with the corrected outer dispatch. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the narrowed-Optional for-loop fix.

- **[design] Derive 'contains a borrow' for TPy records.** The HANDLE half is declared: a native value type whose every value is a borrow handle carries `@native(..., borrowing_view=True)` on its stub (`StrView`, `BytesView`, `Span`, `varargs`, `SpanIter`, the dict views), latched onto `TypeDef.is_borrowing_view`, and `is_borrowing_view_type` reads only that flag -- the compiler holds no list of view types, and what a handle borrows stays on the producing call (`return_borrows_from`). What remains is a TPy record that CONTAINS a borrow (a `StrView` / `Span` / `Ptr` field): it declares nothing, so a record built over a local and returned dangles silently (`BUGS.md#record-view-field-escapes-local-buffer`). Deriving that fact needs four decisions first:
  (a) a HANDLE-vs-CONTAINS split. Several consumers must keep reading only the declared handle fact, because their rule is about a value that IS a handle: the view-constructor-borrows-its-first-argument rule (`sema/iter_loans.py:95`, `sema/compatibility.py:2749` `_view_constructor_arg`, `sema/local_deduction.py:165`, `sema/calls.py:3688` / `:3709`); the receiver-alias rule (`value_category.py:237`, `sema/local_deduction.py:159` / `:178`, `codegen_cpp/context.py:2734`, `thir/lower/statements.py:2752`); the member-is-a-handle rule (`sema/context.py:3119`); and the const-ness projection (`typesys.py:4410`). A contains-a-borrow fact is a second predicate for the lifetime checks (return, yield, field store, closure capture), not a widening of this one.
  (b) a POINTER tier: `Ptr` is a borrow at a return but copied into frames like a value, and `tpy.coro.Waker` is the one stdlib `ValueType` with a `Ptr` field -- a derivation that treats every `Ptr` field as a borrow classifies it.
  (c) per-INSTANTIATION derivation for generics: `W[StrView]` contains a borrow where `W[int32]` does not. The `Send` derivation's default for a field mentioning a type parameter (`contains_type_param` -> OK) is the UNSOUND direction for a lifetime fact.
  (d) `Ptr` is also used to OWN (`Box`, `Rc`, `Arc` hold their payload through one), so a reference-type record cannot be classified by field type alone; the derivation applies to value types, or needs an owning marker on those wrappers.
  A stale claim went with the rewrite: the frame-temp rule's `frame_temp_arg_source` / `frame_temp_arg_slot` no longer consult the borrowing-view predicate. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.

- **[design] Callable-level borrow annotation for native stubs: the remaining users.** `borrows=(...)` / `element_of=(...)` (keywords of `@native` / `@cpp_template`) (rule 37 of `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md`, docs/NATIVE_INTEROP.md) has landed on free functions: a bodyless binding names the parameters its result IS (`borrows=`) or whose element it is (`element_of=`), registration stamps `return_borrows_from` / `element_borrows_from`, and sema decides per call whether the result binds as a borrow or is a fresh value -- a borrow only when every named argument lends storage that outlives the call (an lvalue; for `element_of=`, a container -- an iterator never lends) -- which a binding or owning slot holding it warns about (`TpyCall.result_form`, `copy_observable`). Its users are `min` / `max` (two or three operands, and one iterable with and without `key=`) and `next(it, default)`. What remains: (1) METHODS -- rejected today because the method-call path does not take the call-site stamp: the method-call path takes the same call-site decision (`stamp_result_borrow` on `TpyMethodCall`, the receiver as lent operand -1, the argument hoist round 5 added for the free twin) and a declared `borrows=` REPLACES the receiver inference (an omitted "self" denies it); first consumer `dict.get(key, default)` (its own entry, "`dict.get(key, default)` should return a BORROW" below, becomes a stub-only change). SCHEDULED: the first follow-up unit after the borrow-result branch merges, before the builtin keyword-argument unit (user, 2026-10-04). (2) `copy_iter()`'s borrow, a value-category-dependent fact (it borrows a container passed as an lvalue but moves in and owns an iterator passed as an rvalue) that `@native(..., borrowing_view=True)` on the `CopyIter` type cannot express (`BUGS.md#copy-iter-send-while-borrowing`).
- **[design] `@cpp_template` folds into `@native`** (one binding decorator: a C++ name OR a template, plus the declared facts -- `transient=`, `checks_signals=`, `borrows=` / `element_of=`, ...). The user's stated direction (2026-10-04), after the borrow facts moved from a separate decorator onto the binding's own; today the two decorators carry the same function-level keywords in parallel. docs/NATIVE_INTEROP.md "Declaring what a result borrows" cites it.
- **[design] View constructors borrow their arguments; a view root is durable by its emitted storage.** Two coupled halves, one branch. (1) The constructor rule: a borrowing view's constructor borrows every argument with borrowable storage (anything but a bufferless scalar, `Own[T]` included -- an owned view still points into its source), replacing the positional "a view's constructor borrows its FIRST argument" guess (`_view_constructor_arg`, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`, and its consumers in `iter_loans.py` / `local_deduction.py`), which also misses user `@native(borrowing_view=True)` constructors entirely (they carry no `call_type`), so `return Cursor(xs)` over a PARAMETER is rejected today (documented in `docs/NATIVE_INTEROP.md`). Better still, stamp it as a signature-derived `return_borrows_from` on the constructor's FunctionInfo at registration (like `_stamp_iterator_retention`), which removes the separate constructor arm and the two recognition paths (`call_type` vs `fi.is_constructor`). (2) Durability: whether a view's root outlives the call must be ONE fact decided from the local's emitted storage form, not from `safe_to_return` / `bp_is_param_derived` (`BUGS.md#view-root-owned-local-dangles` has the shapes). Tried on `native-borrowing-views` (reverted, 5e46c10db3 / 111bacb632): the rule alone reached predicates that judged an owned local durable; each strictness patch exposed another shape across two review rounds -- an owned local from `sorted(p)` / `p.copy()`, the `Own[Span]` deny-list, a local rebound from a parameter being a copy, a generic `ys = p` at `T=str`, and a false reject of `s = p[0]; return StrView(s)` when an unsettled `str` local was taken as owned (the direct-return path already defers it through `pending_view_storage_checks`). The durability half therefore comes first; it needs `/tpy-fix-bug`, and `BUGS.md#native-ctor-return-unlowered` must not open the direct native-constructor return before it lands.

- **[safety] Re-key the pre-existing view lifetime rules on the declared borrowing-view fact.** Several rules older than `@native(..., borrowing_view=True)` still name the `StrView` / `BytesView` families instead of asking `is_borrowing_view_type`, so a user borrowing view (and `Span`, `SpanIter`, the dict views, wherever the rule is family-specific) skips them: an explicit annotation bound to a temporary (`_analyze_var_decl` in `tpyc/sema/statements.py`, "Cannot bind ... to a temporary view") -- `c: Cursor = temp()` is not rejected; the local-deduction view-source rules (`is_view_compatible_source` and `_is_static_view_leaf` in `tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`); and the THIR validator's borrow-legal return slot (`_borrow_legal_return` in `tpyc/thir/validate.py`). Audit each: a rule about "a value that is a borrow handle" re-keys on the fact; a rule about the str/bytes owned-vs-view pair (promotion to an owned `str`) stays family-keyed and says why. Found reviewing the borrowing-view declaration, 2026-09-24.

- **[cleanup] Remove `_iter_yields_ref_tuple_proxies`: the runtime picks a frame loop's element binding.** An internal stopgap kwarg on the `dict_items` stub (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_dict.py`), read in one place: the generator/async frame's `for` loop (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_generators.py`, and the borrow-tuple loop-var sets it feeds in `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py`). A frame keeps the loop element across a suspension as a pointer (`__for_tup = &(*__for_it)`), which is ill-formed when the iterator yields a tuple of references BY VALUE, so the flag switches to `__for_tup = ::tpy::tuple_to_pointer<...>(*__for_it)`. Whether `*it` is an lvalue or a prvalue proxy is the iterator's C++ reference category (`std::iter_reference_t`), a fact the runtime already has: emit one form (e.g. `__for_elem = ::tpy::elem_borrow(*it)`, the frame field declared as its `decltype`, element reads through one accessor valid for both shapes) and delete the flag, the kwarg and the pointer-vs-borrow-tuple fork in the frame lowering. Generator/async cases looping over tuples change their C++. Natural home: the collections.defaultdict unit that makes dict views first-class values, which reworks dict-view loops; otherwise its own small branch.

- **[cleanup] Resolve builtin generics from their stubs instead of the type resolver's factory table.** The dict views are spelled from their stubs now, but the compiler still knows them through `TypeDef.type_factory` (`make_dict_keys_view` / `make_dict_values_view` / `make_dict_items_view` in `tpyc/typesys.py`), which `tpyc/parse/type_resolver.py` calls for an annotation like `dict_keys[str, int32]`. Making a builtin generic annotation resolve from its `@builtin_type` stub's record removes that table, and with it the last compiler-side knowledge of which builtin generics exist. Found reviewing the borrowing-view declaration, 2026-09-24.

- **[feature] `typing.KeysView[K]` / `ItemsView[K, V]` / `ValuesView[V]` (and the `collections.abc` names) as aliases for the dict views.** A TPy class that forwards a dict's views (`def keys(self) -> ...: return self._d.keys()`) must be spellable in valid Python, and the only spelling TPy accepts, `dict_keys[K, V]` / `dict_values[K, V]` / `dict_items[K, V]`, is not a CPython builtin name: `-> dict_keys[str, int32]` raises `NameError` at the `def` under CPython 3.12. Resolve the `typing` and `collections.abc` names to the same view types (note `KeysView[K]` / `ValuesView[V]` carry one type argument where TPy's views carry both `K` and `V`, so the alias must recover the missing one from the value it annotates or the view types must be re-parameterized). Returning a view is itself still a lowering reject (`BUGS.md#dict-view-return-yield-rejected`); the spelling is needed as soon as that lands. Requested by the user, 2026-09-24.

- **[cleanup] One path for a native type's C++ name.** A `@native` record is named by codegen's `native_cpp_names` map (`CodeGenerator`, the `get_native_builtin_records()` loop in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py`), which skips every builtin with a `type_factory` and exists only while codegen runs; the dict views, which have a factory and no `cpp_formatter`, are named instead by a fallback in `NominalType._cpp_base_name` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) that reads `TypeDef.record.native_name`. Dropping the factory exclusion puts them on the map with zero corpus churn (measured 2026-09-24 over `stdlib_render` and the dict/view cases), but the map is empty at sema and outside a compilation, where a dict view is rendered too -- `tests/test_runtime_value_type_parity.py` then spells `dict_keys<...>` -- so the fallback stayed. The one path is the TypeDef-owned name (it has no short-name collisions and works in every phase): retire the generator's builtin loop onto it, checking `_emits_own_cpp` and the NominalTypes built by bare name that reach no TypeDef today. Retiring the `Span` / `varargs` / `SpanIter` `_ViewTemplateFormatter`s (`tpyc/type_def_registry.py`) belongs to the same change: their C++ template name is written twice, in the stub's `@native` and in the formatter, with `latch_declared_native_flags` failing the compile when the two disagree; they spell `readonly[T]` as `const T` without the TypeDef only because a type still renders outside a compilation. Found reviewing the borrowing-view declaration, 2026-09-24.

- **[perf] The uniform frame-temp hoist is type-blind, so it also hoists temporaries the frame slot COPIES anyway.**
  `async def msg(tag: str)` copies its view param into an owned `std::string tag` frame field, yet an inline
  `await msg(a + "x")` in another coroutine emits `::tpy::String __coro_arg_0;` on the awaiting frame plus
  `__coro_arg_0 = (::tpy::str_concat(a, "x")); __sub_0.emplace(__coro_arg_0);` -- an extra owned field and a second copy
  for a temporary the callee's slot never borrows. The narrowing is keyed on the SINK rather than on a view taxonomy:
  skip the hoist when the frame's param classification says the slot is an owning copy (the OWNED_COPY / by-value
  kinds -- a copied slot cannot dangle). (`str` / `bytes` LITERAL sources already pass bare: `frame_temp_arg_source`,
  `tpyc/value_category.py`.) Behaviour-neutral, snapshot churn in the shrinking direction; do it as its own small
  change with a `--dump-code` of that shape as the before/after.

- **[cleanup] Pin the moved reject tag for `SpanIter` / dict-view frame params.** The one `is_borrowing_view_type` arm in `_res_param_ok` admits `SpanIter[T]` and the three dict views at the frame-PARAM gate; they then reject at the CALL SITE arg shape. The verdict is unchanged (reject before, reject after), but the tag moved from `res.param_type:*` to `call.arg_shape.*` and no corpus case observes either. Add a section to an existing `error_` case rather than a case per family member. Surfaced by /tpy-ready on the borrowing-view frame-param slice.
- **[harness] An `error_` case whose sources are all frontend-plugin files cannot exist.** `error_case_annotation_problems` and the per-file annotation validation in `tests/test_case.py` both glob `src/*.py`, so a `tests/cases/pascal/error_*` case fails the gate with "Error test must have at least one '# tpyc: error(...)' annotation" -- there is no `.py` file to carry the leg, and an annotation in the `.pas` is never read. That is why the driver-error regression is pinned as a harness test (`tests/test_failure_reporting.py`) rather than a case. Fix shape: read the case's plugin-extension sources too (the registry knows the extensions) and settle how a `# tpyc:` annotation is spelled inside a plugin language's comment syntax -- a design call, not a mechanical widening. Surfaced by /tpy-ready on the driver-diagnostic harness fix.
- **[harness] The comp-only fact annotations are silently vacuous in an `error_` case.** `error_case_annotation_problems` refuses `ok`, `mir(...)` / `mir_summary(...)` and the line-level `mir_*` fact family there, but `type`, `non_null` / `nullable`, `bounds_*`, `div_*`, `cast_*`, `is_send` / `is_sync` and `frame_*` are still accepted and never validated (`tests/test_case.py` reads those facts only off a successful compile). Generalize the gate: refuse every fact annotation in an error case with the `ok` wording, after moving the existing legs to a normal case (one today: `type(readonly[Point])` in `readonly/error_auto_readonly_result_mutate`). A second vacuous position: every fact annotation, `mir(...)` and the `mir_*` facts included, is read from the entry module's `main.py` only, so one written in a helper module of a multi-module case is silently ignored. Surfaced adding the `mir(...)` annotations.
- **[cleanup] `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py` carries five inline copies of the `default_emittable` / `default_to_cpp` suffix pairing.** Lines ~470, ~481, ~511, ~564 and ~618 each spell the same `if emit_defaults and defaults and default_emittable(...): part += f" = {default_to_cpp(...)}"` pair, so the param-index-to-slot mapping and the "is it emittable" question are re-derived per signature emitter. The resumable emitter consolidated exactly this into one `_default_suffix` helper (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`), which is what let the factory declaration and the frame constructor carry byte-identical default sets by construction; the same helper shape is wanted here so the five plain-signature emitters cannot drift either. No behavior change -- verify with the corpus byte-diff. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the resumable-factory default fix.
- **[cleanup -- HARDER THAN IT LOOKS] The `nonstmt_borrow_bindings` override in the borrow snapshot is LOAD-BEARING, not a redundant epicycle.** An aliasing match-capture of an lvalue subject records a stmt-borrow (`sema/match.py`) AND adds the name to `nonstmt_borrow_bindings`, which `analyzer.py`'s function-end snapshot OR's back in to cancel the `nonstmt_bound_names` exclusion. It LOOKS like add-to-exclusion-then-cancel, but the override is function-level on purpose: the match-arm codegen emits the capture *unconditionally in borrow form* (`q = &subject`), so the variable's single C++ declaration must stay pointer form for the WHOLE function -- even if the same name is later bound by an owned `with...as` / for-loop var (which re-adds it to `nonstmt_bound_names`). A naive cleanup that drops the override (or lets the later owned binding win) makes the decl owned (`Box q`) while the arm still binds a borrow -> the two disagree and codegen reads garbage. Verified: removing the override regresses `tests/cases/match/borrow_capture_then_with_rebind` from `99/7/99` to `0/7/0`. A real cleanup must unify the match-arm capture's emitted FORM with the variable's decl form (make the arm defer to owned when the name is later owned-bound, accepting the copy/parity implications), not just simplify the snapshot bookkeeping -- bigger work, likely IR-era (the place/loan model makes "this name's form" a single fact). Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the attempted cleanup, which a regression test caught. The guard test now exists.
- **[codegen readability] `print(v)` of a narrowed `str|None`/`bytes|None` name renders `print_optional_val(v)` instead of dereferencing the proven-non-None value.** The print path (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/builtins.py` ~332) branches on `get_resolved_type(arg)` -- the *declared* Optional type -- not the sema-narrowed analyzed type, so inside `if a is not None:` a `print(a)` still routes through `print_optional_val`. NOT a defect: output is correct (the optional is present, so the value prints). Cleanliness only -- a narrowed NAME arg could deref + print directly, but the fix must preserve the deliberate field-case `print_optional_val` (field storage stays `std::optional<T>`). Sibling of the (now-fixed) dict-value narrowing skip, same root (declared-vs-narrowed type at a value sink). Surfaced fixing the dict-value narrowed-Optional bug. **Stopped 2026-09-28:** dropping the print-specific rows (the `_print_optval_opt` locals arm and two dead rows in `_print_arg_ok`) and reading the narrowed name generically renders `std::cout << (*a)` correctly for str, scalar, `String`, walrus and frame locals, but breaks three shapes: a None-narrowed name has no generic read (`control_flow/elif_arm_bound_local` and `inference/reassign_numeric_widen` reject at `print.arg.other_nonetype_name`), BUGS.md#async-await-bound-narrowed-optional-read-bare surfaces as a compile error, and tuple/`Span` inners mis-render because the print name arm keys on the declared type. Keying that arm on the narrowed read type instead would also newly admit narrowed value records, which is its own decision.
- **Borrow/storage chokepoint -- test-coverage gap.** One regression guard not yet written (no observed failure): a `Send[T | None]` / `Sync[T | None]` marker over a pointer-repr Optional -- guards the `_make_marker` -> `with_inner` `force_pointer_repr` preservation (no `send_sync/` case exercises a pointer-repr Optional inside a marker). Add under `tests/cases/send_sync/`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the chokepoint branch.

Add: (a) a 3+-element await tuple with two `Own` elements (multiple move-outs from one `auto&& __tup`); (b) an await-tuple unpack inside a `try`/`except` body across a suspension (frame cleanup interleaving with owned-element destruction). - **owned-tuple PARAM -- test-coverage gaps.** The owned-tuple-param feature (`tuple[Own[A], ...]` -> `std::tuple<...>&&`) is covered for 2-element sync functions (unpack/forward/return, never-consumed warn+suppress, use-after-move, mixed exclusion). Add: an owned-tuple param on a **generator/async** function (interaction with frame-struct promotion -- the param is seeded into `movable_locals` + `storage_form_tuple_locals`) and on a **class method**. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the owned-tuple-param feature.
- **owned-tuple never-consumed warning is per-tuple, not per-element.** `_warn_unconsumed_own_params` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) suppresses the warning for a `tuple[Own[A], ...]` param when ANY owned element is `@nocopy`/value-typed (`any(...)`), so a mixed `tuple[Own[NocopySock], Own[BigInt]]` that is never consumed is silenced even though the `BigInt` element is genuinely unconsumed -- weaker than the scalar per-param model. Whether to tighten to `all(...)` (warn unless EVERY owned element is drop-legitimate) is a warning-semantics design question, not a mechanical flip: tightening could newly warn on legitimate consume-one/drop-the-other patterns. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, safety-model) of the owned-tuple-param feature.
- **Tuple-element BigInt-overflow panic -- test gap.** `int/panic_int_to_fixed_aggregate_overflow` covers an out-of-range `BigInt` element in a *list* literal, but the *tuple*-literal element path is a separate sema route (`_analyze_tuple_literal` via `_materialize_narrowing_element_coercion`, vs the array path's inline check). Add a panic case for an overflowing `BigInt` element in a `tuple[..., int32]` literal/return so the tuple route's runtime `to_fixed_check` is guarded too. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `fix-aggregate-literal-elem-coercion`.
- **Variadic tuples (`TypeVarTuple` / `*Ts`, and variadic-arity tuple returns).** TPy has fixed-arity tuple types + unpacking (FEATURE_ROADMAP A10) but no variadic-tuple generics: a function can't take/return a tuple of statically-unknown arity, nor splat `*args` of heterogeneous types into a fixed-arity tuple. Substantial type-system + codegen feature (the C++ side is `std::tuple` with parameter packs); warrants `/tpy-add-feature`. **Blocks `itertools.chain` / `product` / `permutations` / `combinations`** (chain/product take `*iterables`; product/permutations/combinations yield tuples whose arity depends on the inputs) and the *variadic* `starmap` (the fixed two-argument `starmap` is separately blocked on the simple-peephole dangling-capture bug -- see BUGS.md). Surfaced scoping itertools v2.
- **asyncio I/O reactor follow-ups (post-M2 + smaller gaps).** The M1 epoll reactor + M2 `sock_accept`/`sock_connect` + the client streams layer (`open_connection` -> `StreamReader`/`StreamWriter`) shipped (`EpollReactor` + `get_running_loop().sock_recv`/`sock_sendall`/`sock_accept`/`sock_connect`; see `docs/ASYNC_DESIGN.md` "I/O reactor" + `tplib/async_echo_*` in the `tpy-examples` repo). Remaining, roughly in priority order: (1) **Swap-in reactor** -- make the executor's `reactor` field `@dynamic Reactor`-typed (it's concrete `EpollReactor | None` today; the `Reactor` Protocol already exists in `_executor.py`) and let `asyncio.run` take a reactor factory, so a user-provided / alternative backend can replace it. NOTE: cross-platform readiness polling is already handled *below* the TPy line -- `epoll_impl.cpp` is dual-backend (epoll on Linux, kqueue on macOS/BSD) behind the flat `tpy_epoll_*` ABI via `#ifdef`. So this is NOT needed for kqueue; the real motivator is a fundamentally different model (io_uring, completion-based) or a user-pluggable pure-TPy reactor. Low priority / speculative until such a need is real. (2) **Independent read+write waiters on one fd** -- the reactor is single-waiter-per-fd (one direction at a time); two coroutines awaiting different directions on the same fd needs `_waiters` keyed by (fd, direction) + a combined epoll interest mask with MOD. (3) **Scaling**: `EpollReactor._waiters` is a `dict[int32, Waker]` and the executor `runnable_q` is still O(n) `pop(0)` (pre-existing, tracked separately) -- fine for now, revisit under a 10k-connection workload.
- **asyncio reactor M1 -- EINTR handling.** Two gaps, both low-frequency (EINTR is rare on non-blocking fds): (a) `tpy_epoll_wait` (`runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/epoll_impl.cpp`) retries `epoll_wait` on EINTR with the *original* `timeout_ms`, not adjusted for elapsed time, so a timer can fire late by up to one timeout per EINTR -- recompute the remaining time from a deadline on each retry; (b) a signal-interrupted `recv`/`send` in `_SockRecv`/`_SockSendAll` (`lib/tpy/asyncio/__init__.py`) returns EINTR, which falls to the error branch and raises `SocketError`, where CPython retries -- treat EINTR like a retry (re-issue the syscall) rather than a fatal error. Surfaced by /tpy-review (runtime-cpp-correctness + cpython-parity).
- **asyncio reactor M1 -- test-coverage batch (residual).** Most of this batch is now covered (cases under `tests/cases/async/`): cancel of a parked `_SockRecv`/`_SockSendAll` (`reactor_cancel_parked_io`), `sock_sendall` non-EAGAIN error (`reactor_sendall_error`), `get_running_loop()` outside `asyncio.run` -> `RuntimeError` (`get_running_loop_outside_run`), multi-fd `EpollReactor.poll` batch n>1 (`reactor_multi_fd_poll`), and negative `sock_recv` -> `ValueError` (`socket_recv_negative_size`). Two internal branches remain untested because they are not deterministically reachable from user-level TPy code: (d) `EpollReactor.register_fd` MOD re-arm (an fd re-registered while still armed -- the reactor unregisters on wake, so the same-fd re-arm path needs an internal scenario, not a user program), and (e) `_next_timer_timeout_ms` "already due" (`delta <= 0` -> 0) -- timing-dependent (a timer already past when the timeout is computed), so any test would be flaky. Add if a deterministic harness for internal reactor state lands. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage).
- **asyncio reactor M2 -- test-coverage batch (residual).** Most of this batch is now covered (cases under `tests/cases/async/`): sync `socket.recv(-1)` -> `ValueError` (`socket_recv_negative_size`, alongside the async path), `BlockingIOError` catch semantics -- catchable, caught by `except OSError`, not by `except ValueError` (`socket_blocking_io_error`), cancel of a parked `_SockAccept` (`reactor_accept_cancel_timeout`), and a direct `getsockopt_int`/`setsockopt_int` roundtrip on `SO_REUSEADDR` (`socket_getsockopt`, `no_cpython` -- TPy-only method surface). The `_SockConnect`-side paths remain untested because loopback connect behavior can't be steered from a portable test: (c-connect) cancel of a parked `_SockConnect` needs a connect that stays EINPROGRESS without completing (an unresponsive remote -- network-dependent/flaky), and (d) the `_SockConnect` synchronous-success branch (connect returns 0 on the first poll) is dead on loopback, which always returns EINPROGRESS for a non-blocking connect. Add if a deterministic connect-stall harness lands. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the asyncio M2 branch.
- **asyncio reactor M2 -- hardening / known gap.** A non-blocking stdlib gap surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion: **socket closed mid-await** -- `_SockRecv`/`_SockSendAll`/`_SockAccept`/`_SockConnect` hold a raw `Ptr[socket]` across suspension with no tie to the socket's lifetime, and `socket` has an explicit `close()`/`__del__` that flips `fd` to -1 -- a socket closed while its awaitable is parked leaves the awaitable polling `fileno() == -1` into the reactor (sharper than the generic `Ptr`-across-await exposure that `Ptr[Lock]`/`Ptr[Queue]` already carry). No compile-time enforcement; v1 accepts it. (The other two gaps from this entry are now fixed: the `socket._accept_fd` fd-leak on a peer-resolve failure closes the accepted fd before re-raising; `_SockSendAll` sends via a growing offset through `socket._send_from` instead of re-slicing a fresh `bytes` per park -- regression-guarded by `reactor_sendall_large`.) Surfaced by /tpy-review + /tpy-ready of the asyncio M2 branch.
- **asyncio streams -- deferred pieces.** The streams layer shipped `open_connection` -> `StreamReader` (`read`/`readexactly`/`readline`/`at_eof`) + `StreamWriter` (`write`/`drain`/`close`/`wait_closed`) + `IncompleteReadError`, and `start_server(handler, host, port)` -> `Server` (`serve_forever`/`close`/`wait_closed`/async-with + `server.sockets[0].getsockname()`; background accept loop spawning the async `handler` per connection, on the async-fn->Callable coercion). Deferred: (a) **`StreamReader.readuntil` `limit` / `LimitOverrunError` + multi-fill coverage** -- `readuntil(sep)` itself SHIPPED (the `bytes` coro-param gap is fixed via the `OWNED_COPY` capture kind); like `readline`/`read` it enforces no buffer limit, so CPython's `limit=`/`LimitOverrunError` surface is still absent. Also untested: the `readuntil` fill loop *iterating* (separator split across two `sock_recv` chunks) and a multi-byte separator spanning a chunk boundary -- the shipped `stream_readuntil` test sends all bytes in one `sock_sendall`, so the separator is found on the first buffer and the `while` loop body never runs (the loop logic is shared-shape with `readline`, which is also single-chunk in tests). Deterministic multi-fill over loopback TCP needs the server to send in pieces with a client read between -- add when there's a harness for it. (b) **`start_server` remaining CPython-parity gaps** -- both lifecycle tests now run under real CPython asyncio. One documented `Server` divergence remains (no test exercises it, so it is not behind `no_cpython`): **`wait_closed()` is a no-op** -- CPython awaits in-flight connections to drain; matching needs `Server` to track its spawned per-connection tasks (a task registry populated by `_accept_loop`) and await them in `wait_closed()`/`__aexit__`. (`__aenter__` now returns `self` as a borrow -- `async with server as s` aliases, CPython parity.) Also: `Server.sockets[0]` hands out a *readonly* socket borrow (only `getsockname`-style reads; mutating socket methods aren't exposed). The interior-mutable readonly-`Rc.clone` has since landed, but by design a clone from a readonly receiver yields a *readonly*-payload handle (no readonly->mutable laundering), so exposing a *mutable* socket still needs the proxy to hold and clone a *mutable* `Rc` via a non-readonly accessor path, not the readonly clone. A CPython `sock=` param to `start_server` is also still unimplemented. Sub-cells of the coercion still open: a bound async *method* ref (`obj.handler`) is the general no-method-value gap; the `Fn`-template target + intermediate `Own[Cancellable]` local are in BUGS.md; a sync (non-async) fn passed where a coroutine-factory `Callable` is expected should get a sema diagnostic (today only a downstream C++ error -- add an `error_` case once the diagnostic lands); `docs/CLOSURES_CALLABLE_DESIGN.md` should gain an async-fn->Callable coercion section (covers the coercion semantics + the bound-method/`Fn`-template limits). Also deferred: `StreamReader.readuntil` limit / `LimitOverrunError`, `StreamWriter.get_extra_info`, `start_server` backlog (multiple listening sockets, `reuse_port`, `ssl`), the streams buffer's O(n) per-fill `bytes` concat (mirror `_SockSendAll`'s offset gap). Surfaced building the asyncio streams layer.
- **asyncio: graceful SIGTERM shutdown (TPy enhancement; CPython-divergent).** `asyncio.run` now handles **SIGINT** (Ctrl-C) gracefully -- cancel the root task, run its `finally`/`__aexit__`/`wait_closed` cleanup, then raise `KeyboardInterrupt` -- matching CPython's asyncio.run (signal layer in `runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/signal_impl.cpp` + `lib/tpy/signal.py` + the executor's `_SignalScope`/`shutdown_armed`). SIGTERM is deliberately NOT handled, matching CPython (default terminate). Servers under k8s/Docker typically want graceful SIGTERM too; adding it is a deliberate divergence from CPython's asyncio.run, so it needs the acknowledged-divergence treatment (doc note + ideally an opt-in spelling like a `shutdown_signals=` arg to `run`) rather than silently installing a SIGTERM handler. The C signal layer already saves/restores via sigaction and the eventfd wakeup is signal-agnostic, so wiring a second signal is small once the divergence is acknowledged. Surfaced building the SIGINT graceful-shutdown feature.
- **asyncio: deadlock guard ("no progress possible") is suppressed during a signal-armed run.** `asyncio.run` registers the SIGINT wakeup eventfd in the reactor, so `wait_for_event`'s fd count is always >= 1 and the "no coroutine made progress, no timers, no I/O" RuntimeError never fires while shutdown handling is active -- a genuinely deadlocked root now blocks until Ctrl-C instead of raising. This matches CPython (which has no such guard), but loses a useful debugging signal. Restoring it would need the executor to distinguish the control eventfd from real work fds (the "dedicated executor wakeup fd" design, vs the chosen "eventfd in the reactor"). Low priority. Surfaced building the SIGINT graceful-shutdown feature.
- **asyncio streams -- coverage + small parity gaps (from /tpy-review).** Non-blocking follow-ons on the shipped streams layer: (a) test gaps -- `readline` multi-fill (newline arrives in a later chunk), `readline` at EOF with no trailing newline (partial-line return), `at_eof()` with EOF flagged but data still buffered (returns `False`), `is_closing()`, `drain()` with an empty buffer; (b) `IncompleteReadError` message text differs from CPython's "N bytes read on a total of M expected bytes" (the `.partial`/`.expected` fields match -- only the formatted message diverges); (c) `drain()` on an empty buffer returns without yielding a scheduling slot (CPython's `_drain_helper` is near-noop here too, so marginal). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the streams layer.
- **`async with StreamWriter` ergonomics (TPy-only enhancement).** Give `StreamWriter` `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` (returning self / `close()` + `await wait_closed()`) so users can write `async with writer: ...` instead of the explicit `writer.close(); await writer.wait_closed()` two-step. NOTE: this is a deliberate divergence -- CPython's `asyncio.StreamWriter` has NO async-context-manager support (no `__aenter__`/`__aexit__`; the documented cleanup is exactly the two-step), so code/examples using it would not run under stock CPython. Weigh against the streams module's CPython-faithful-mirror goal before building. Surfaced reviewing `tplib/stream_client.py` in the `tpy-examples` repo.
- **io.BufferedReader / FileIO / socket.makefile v2 follow-ups.** v1 shipped `io.FileIO` (fd adopt) + `io.BufferedReader` (concrete, wraps a `FileIO`) + `socket.makefile("rb")` -- the binary-read layer `http.client` builds on. Deferred, each a separate add: (1) **`BufferedReader.readinto(buf)` / `FileIO.readinto(buf)`** -- write into a caller `bytearray`; blocked on mutable-buffer write support (slice-assignment / memoryview not on the surface), so http.client v1 should use `read()`. (2) **`BufferedReader.peek(n)`** -- non-consuming lookahead. (3) **Text mode** -- `makefile("r")` / a `TextIOWrapper` over a binary buffer (encoding/newline translation); v1 `makefile` rejects non-binary modes with `ValueError` (TPy-only, `no_cpython` case `socket_makefile_unsupported`). (4) **`makefile(buffering=0)` unbuffered** -- CPython returns the raw stream; our fixed `Own[BufferedReader]` return can't, so unsupported. (5) **`makefile` dup vs CPython shared-fd -- the faithful fix is a SOCKET-LAYER design, pure library, NOT THIR-gated.** v1 dups the socket fd (reader/socket close independently); CPython shares the fd via an internal refcount (`_io_refs`) and keeps the socket object alive while a makefile reader exists. Observably equivalent for request/response reads, so dup is fine for v1. (The sharper divergence than fd-count/refcount: the socket and the dup share ONE kernel byte-stream -- dup'd fds share the open file description -- so interleaving reads on both handles steals bytes from the other; benign for http.client's write-via-sock / read-via-fp split, a footgun if a user reads from both.) The blocker on a faithful share is purely an ownership-shape problem (no compiler gate): `makefile(self)` only *borrows* `self`, so it can't move the caller's owned `@nocopy` socket into an `Rc[socket]` -- the async `StreamReader` only gets to share `Rc[socket]` because `open_connection` *constructs* the socket into the Rc. The clean fix is to refcount the fd in a shared cell (CPython `_io_refs` model) so `makefile` clones it -- but forcing that `Rc`/heap cell on EVERY socket fights `@noalloc`/primitive-cleanliness (the cost is the per-socket alloc + losing the trivial-RAII value, not throughput -- socket I/O is syscall-bound). Preferred shape (design, build when a workload needs faithful shared-fd or a lean primitive -- per the don't-build-infra-ahead-of-demand stance): a two-layer split -- a lean **`tplib.net.Socket`** raw-fd `@nocopy` zero-overhead primitive (reactor + hot paths + `@noalloc` target) and the stdlib **`socket.socket`** as an `Rc`-backed CPython-faithful facade on top (where `makefile` shared-fd + refcount-close live). The lean primitive has value independent of makefile. Until then dup stands. (HTTP keep-alive has since landed -- SSL_DESIGN.md's former precondition for the Rc-unify cleanup -- and dup remains sufficient: the drain-before-next-request discipline never reads through socket and reader concurrently.) (6) **`readline(size)` `_MAXLINE` cap usage** -- the `size` arg works; http.client should pass it to bound header length once built. (7) **`makefile` return-type overloads (the eventual full-parity shape, once TextIOWrapper/BufferedWriter/BufferedRWPair exist)** -- mirror the existing `open()` pattern in `lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_io.py`: `@overload` on a `Literal[...]` mode arg returns the precise concrete type (`"rb"`->`BufferedReader`, `"wb"`->`BufferedWriter`, `"r"`->`TextIOWrapper`, `"rwb"`->`BufferedRWPair`, `buffering=0`->raw `SocketIO`), so a literal call needs no narrowing; a runtime `mode: str` call hits the catch-all overload returning the union of those types, which the user narrows/asserts. v1 returns only `BufferedReader` and raises on the rest. (8) **`asyncio.StreamReader` still appends each fill to `_buf` and re-slices it on every take** (`_buf = _buf + chunk`, `bytes(self._buf[n:])`) -- quadratic over a large read, the shape `io.BufferedReader` dropped for an unread offset (`_pos`) plus join-once fills. Porting that to StreamReader keeps the rule both depend on: materialize an owned head (`bytes(self._buf[a:b])`) before reassigning `_buf`, since a no-wrap slice borrows the buffer being replaced. (9) **`BufferedReader` raw source is `Box[RawBinaryIO]` unconditionally** -- the `@dynamic` raw protocol (added for `ssl.SSLRawIO`/`makefile`) type-erases EVERY source via `make_adapter`, so the common concrete-`FileIO` path (the http.client/requests read loop) now pays a heap alloc per reader + a vcall per ~8KB fill it didn't before (was a concrete inline field). The decision is right -- a generic `BufferedReader[S]` would push a viral type param up http.client/requests, and the slicing wall blocks a bare protocol field -- so this is a perf-tracking note, not a back-out.
