If an HTTP read-throughput workload ever demands it, de-erase the concrete path via a static-generic + dyn hybrid (`BufferedReader[S]` for a statically-known source, the `Box[dyn]` form only when the source is polymorphic). Negligible at 8KB granularity for now. Surfaced by /tpy-ready of the ssl makefile increment.
- **http.client / http.HTTPStatus v2 follow-ups.** v1 shipped `http.HTTPStatus` (full CPython code set; `.value`/`.name`/value-lookup/int-compare) + `http.client` (`HTTPConnection`, `HTTPResponse`, `HTTPException`/`BadStatusLine`) -- plaintext HTTP/1.1 over a `socket.makefile`-backed `io.BufferedReader`, byte-parity with CPython on the implemented subset (tests `stdlib/http_status`, `http_client`, `http_client_framing`, `http_client_bad_status`, all gold parity via socketpair + `conn.sock` injection). Deferred, each a separate add: (1) **HTTPS / `HTTPSConnection` -- SHIPPED** (`HTTPSConnection(host, port=443, timeout=None, context=None)` runs the HTTP/1.1 flow over an `ssl.SSLSocket`; secure-default context, caller `context=` captured by value; a *sibling* of `HTTPConnection` -- not a subclass, since TPy method dispatch is static -- both satisfying a `@dynamic _Connection` protocol so a caller holds either behind one `Box[_Connection]`; request-building extracted to module free functions; test `stdlib/https_client`, `no_cpython`, real TLS handshake via the `_tls` injection seam). Residual: `http.client` now imports `ssl`, so every program importing it links mbedTLS -- see the use-driven-linking follow-up below. Test gap: the `@dynamic _Connection` protocol ships with NO committed test of `Box[_Connection]` virtual dispatch, and `_Connection` currently has zero consumers (a structural-conformance forward-declaration for Increment 5). DECISION (with user, post-merge): Increment 5 switches HTTPConnection/HTTPSConnection to NOMINALLY inherit `_Connection` (`class HTTPConnection(_Connection)`) -- explicit conformance, direct base storage in `Box[_Connection]` (no `Adapter`, so it sidesteps the structural-conformance incomplete-`Adapter` bug in BUGS.md entirely; no factory workaround needed). Cost is a vtable pointer per instance (concrete calls devirtualize -- no per-call cost) + regenerating the `http_client*` snapshots (vtable added to HTTPConnection's emitted C++). SHIPPED in Increment 5. (2) **Low-level incremental request API** -- `putrequest`/`putheader`/`endheaders`/`send`; v1 has only high-level `request()`. (3) **Non-bytes request bodies** -- v1 takes `bytes | None`; CPython also accepts `str` (encoded), file-like (`.read`), and iterables (auto-chunked) -- needs str->bytes at the boundary (and the `String.encode()` gap, BUGS.md) plus chunked *sending*. (4) **`HTTPResponse.headers` as an `email.message`-style object** -- v1 exposes `getheader(name, default)` (case-insensitive, dup-join) + `getheaders()` only; `.headers[...]` subscript / `HTTPMessage` methods are absent (a class can't reproduce `email.message.Message`). (5) **`HTTPStatus.phrase`/`.description`/`.is_success`-style helpers** -- TPy enums can't carry per-member data; accessing them is a compile error (signaled, not silent). Needs the per-member-data enum feature or a parallel `phrase(status)` free function. (6) **`str(HTTPStatus.OK)`** -- CPython 3.11+ returns `"200"`; align TPy enum `str()` if a test prints a member directly (tests use `.value`). (7) **Header continuation/folding** -- `_read_headers` treats each line independently; obs-folded continuation lines aren't joined (rare, legal). (8) **`Content-Length` > 2GB single read** -- `_length` is `int` but `read()` narrows to `int32` for `BufferedReader.read`; loop the read for very large bodies. (9) **connection reuse -- SHIPPED** (HTTP/1.1 keep-alive: the socket persists across request()/getresponse() cycles; `HTTPResponse.will_close` mirrors CPython's `_check_close` -- Connection-header substring match, HTTP/1.0 default-close, unframed-body fallback; the caller drains each response and closes on will_close; `request()` after `close()` reconnects; test `stdlib/http_client_keepalive`, gold parity). Declared divergence: `getresponse()` does NOT auto-close on will_close as CPython does -- TPy's `SSLSocket.close()` sends close_notify immediately, which would race a still-unread TLS body; the close happens at the caller after draining. Residuals, each a separate add: no `CannotSendRequest`/`ResponseNotReady` state machine (a next request on an undrained connection silently corrupts the stream where CPython raises; needs the connection to see response state it hands away -- an Rc back-ref or a drained-callback shape), no pipelining, no `Proxy-Connection` (HTTP/1.0 proxy) keep-alive token. **Successor design (user-endorsed direction): will_close as ownership transfer.** CPython's `getresponse()` auto-close ("this effectively passes the connection to the response" per its own source) is a MOVE expressed via refcounts; TPy can express it directly -- on will_close, `getresponse()` moves the transport out of the connection into the response (owned closable slot beside the reader), so the connection divests immediately (`sock is None`, next request() reconnects = CPython observables restored), close stays eager everywhere, and the close-after-drain happens at the response owner with no TLS close_notify race. Removes the declared getresponse-no-auto-close divergence AND enables the misuse-guard residual above (the connection knows it has no transport). GATED on the `take()` Optional-field-move builtin (Ownership & Consuming Iteration section); once that lands this is a localized http.client change. Remaining corner after the redesign: an explicit user `close()` of a keep-alive connection mid-read (document as "you closed it"). `set_tunnel`/proxy still missing; redirect following ships at the requests layer. (`timeout=` now ships: `HTTPConnection(host, port, timeout=)` threads a socket timeout through `create_connection`.) (10) **status-line whitespace tolerance** -- v1 splits on single spaces (`split(" ", 2)`); CPython splits on whitespace runs (`split(None, 2)`). (11) **`http.HTTPMethod` enum** -- CPython exposes it alongside `HTTPStatus`; not implemented. (12) **perf** -- the `_read_chunked` O(total*chunks) accumulation is FIXED (bytearray + extend, amortized O(n)). Remaining: `_build_request` allocates a fresh `bytes` per header line (`data + ln.encode() + b"\r\n"`, two `bytes_concat` + a `bytes_literal_owned("\r\n")` each) -- bounded (few headers), fine. Surfaced building `http.client`.
- **`tplib.requests` / `urllib.request.urlopen` v2 follow-ups.** v1 shipped `tplib.requests` (`get`/`post`/`put`/`patch`/`delete`/`head`/`request` + `Response` + `Session` + Basic `auth` + `RequestException`/`HTTPError`/`ConnectionError`) and a simplified `urllib.request.urlopen` (GET/POST shim, `URLError`), both pure TPy over `http.client` (tests `tplib/requests_{get,post,session,errors}`, `tplib/error_requests_json_inline`, `stdlib/urlopen`; all `no_cpython` -- `requests` has no CPython module and the offline test seam injects a socket, so the wire-layer parity is covered by `http.client`'s gold tests). Deferred, each a separate add: (1) **`timeout=` -- SHIPPED** (`get`/`post`/.../`request`/`Session.*` take a `timeout: float | None`; threads through `_connect` -> `HTTPConnection(timeout=)` -> `socket.create_connection`; a slow connect/read raises `Timeout(RequestException)`, the socket layer's `TimeoutError` re-wrapped in `_request_on`; test `tplib/requests_timeout`). Residual: the requests `(connect, read)` two-element timeout tuple is not supported (single float only); and `Session.request(timeout=)` is silently ignored when `Session._connection` is pre-set (the injected connection is used as-is, so the per-call `timeout=` never reaches `_connect`) -- TPy-only module, no parity contract, but a silent no-op worth closing if the pre-set-connection path outlives the test seam. (2) **redirect following -- SHIPPED** (`allow_redirects=` on `get`/.../`request`/`Session.*`, default True; `head()` defaults False; follows 301/302/303/307/308 via `Location` resolved with `urljoin`; `Response.history` holds the intermediate responses, `Response.url` is the final URL; 301/302/303 coerce non-HEAD method to GET and drop the body, 307/308 preserve both; a redirect across a host/scheme/port change drops `Authorization` (`should_strip_auth`); `Session.max_redirects` default 30 -> `TooManyRedirects`; http->https redirects are followed and a redirect to a non-http/https scheme (e.g. `ftp`) raises `ConnectionError`; recursion-based, since a loop-carried `Own` local trips the return borrow check; tests `tplib/requests_redirect{,_disabled,_method,_too_many,_cross_host,_bad_scheme,_https}`). Residuals: the per-hop connection-queue seam `Session._redirect_connections` is offline-test-only (now underscore-prefixed, internal); `params` apply only to the first hop (redirect targets carry their own query); the build needed the recursive-record copyability fix (`is_type_non_copyable` guard, separate branch) because `Response.history: list[Response]` is self-referential. Test-coverage gaps (filed by /tpy-review, low value -- logic is cpython-parity-verified): the HEAD-exception path (a 302/303 redirect of a HEAD request keeps HEAD) and the Location-absent-on-3xx branch (a 3xx with no `Location` header returns as-is) have no dedicated case. (3) **cookies -- SHIPPED** (`cookies=` dict on `get`/.../`request`/`Session.*`; a `CookieJar` + `Cookie`; `Set-Cookie` parsed into `Response.cookies` and accumulated in `Session.cookies`, resent domain/path/secure-matched -- so a cookie set by one host never leaks to another across a redirect; tests `tplib/requests_cookies_{send,set,session,domain,delete}`). Deferred cookie sub-items, all declared narrowings: (a) `cookies=` accepts a `dict[str, str]` only (not a whole `CookieJar`) -- a reference-type union param `CookieJar | dict` was avoided; (b) the jar is keyed by name only, so a same-name/different-domain collision is last-wins (CPython keeps both, keyed by (domain, path, name)); (c) the RFC 1123 and RFC 850 `Expires` forms are parsed (matching CPython's `http.cookiejar`); the asctime form is not (an asctime `Expires` is ignored -> the cookie is session-lifetime). Real expiry is otherwise honored (Max-Age precedence over Expires, past-expiry/`Max-Age<=0` delete, malformed `Max-Age` discards the whole cookie like CPython, expired cookies withheld from send; via `time.time()` + `datetime.strptime`); (d) the default cookie path is `"/"`, not the request-URI directory. Compiler bugs surfaced building this (all worked around in the library): two new BUGS.md entries -- `k in` a const/readonly dict with a non-Equatable value type is rejected; a named reference-type local bound off a const container read (`c = d[k]` / `d.get(k)`) drops const -- plus a new dict reproducer of the pre-existing "resumable generator METHOD that iterates a `self` field" entry (a generator over a const dict can't store the const key-iterator in its frame; `__iter__` yields from a materialized `keys()` list instead), and a Safety/borrow-checker entry (a const method call on a container-subscript element blocks const inference for the enclosing container, so `update`/`header_for` are emitted mutable). Test-coverage residuals filed by /tpy-review (low value, logic is exercised elsewhere): no case supplies a comma-bearing `Expires=` Set-Cookie (guards the `_ingest` split-before-CID-join rationale) or a negative `Max-Age` (only `Max-Age=0` covered). (4) **`json=` inline-literal ergonomics** -- today the caller must bind `payload: JsonValue = {...}` first (the compiler rejects an implicit concrete-dict -> `JsonValue` conversion; clear error, documented); closing this is the recursive-union literal-coercion direction, not a requests fix. (5) **`Response.headers` case-insensitive -- SHIPPED** (`Response.headers` is now a `CaseInsensitiveDict` defined in `requests.py`: case-insensitive `[]`/`in`/`get`/`del`, original casing preserved in `items()`/`keys()`, `__eq__` does case-insensitive content compare; test `tplib/requests_headers_ci`). Now a full mapping: duplicate response headers joined with `", "` (at the `getheaders()` collect site, like urllib3's `HTTPHeaderDict`), `__iter__` (generator over original-case keys, so `for k in headers` works), and the mutable-mapping surface (`update`/`copy`/`pop`/`setdefault`/`popitem`/`clear`) all shipped. Sole residual: `headers == {plain dict}` is a type error (only CID==CID compares); CPython CID `==` accepts any `Mapping` -- a signaled compile error, not silent, low value. (6) **form-dict `data=` + multipart `files=` -- SHIPPED** (`data=` now accepts `bytes | dict[str, str]`: raw bytes sent verbatim, a dict urlencoded as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`; `files=` (`dict[str, FileField]`) uploads `multipart/form-data` -- each value a `FileField(filename, content, content_type="application/octet-stream")`, so a file part always carries a `Content-Type` (unlike a requests bare 2-tuple, which omits it); any dict `data` folds in as plain form parts; wire format byte-verified against real `requests._encode_files`; tests `tplib/requests_form_data`, `tplib/requests_files`). Declared narrowings: no str body / file-like / iterable / list-valued form field; the files value is a `FileField` record, not a bare `(filename, content)` / 3-tuple like requests (a `tuple | FileField` union was prototyped to keep the bare tuple but dropped: the union element type read badly AND a bare-tuple literal won't coerce through the `dict[str, ...] | None` param -- the terse case wouldn't compile); `data=bytes` is ignored when `files=` is given (only a dict `data` folds in); an empty dict `data` is falsy so it is treated as no body (matching requests' `elif data:`); the multipart boundary is a fixed token (not randomized) with no content-collision scan (deterministic wire bytes, like urllib3's no-scan). Compiler bug surfaced while prototyping the dropped `tuple | FileField` shape (filed anyway, real defect): literal-index subscription (`v[0]`) of a tuple narrowed out of a variant emits raw `operator[]`; BUGS.md. Perf residual (from /tpy-review, deferred): `_encode_body` returns a `tuple[bytes|None, str|None]` that `_request_on` destructures without a move (Optional-wrapped tuple slots miss the whole-tuple-unpack `Own` optimization -- a pre-existing compiler gap, repro `tests/cases/tuple/own_tuple_per_element_param`), so the body bytes are copied once more on the hot path; same body-copy family as (13)(a). Not worth distorting the lib (inlining `_encode_body` into `_request_on`) to dodge a compiler gap; fix the tuple-unpack move opt instead. (7) **`.text` charset sniffing** -- v1 decodes UTF-8; `.encoding` is fixed (no `Content-Type` charset / chardet). (8) **streaming -- SHIPPED** (`stream=True` on all verbs + `request`/`Session.*`; the `Response` holds the live `HTTPResponse` and exposes `iter_content(chunk_size)` (required chunk_size, no default -- dodges the generator-default-drop bug in BUGS.md), `iter_lines()`, `.raw`, `.close()`, `with resp:`; only the terminal hop streams -- a followed redirect is fully drained + poolable, faithful to requests; a streamed connection is dropped, never pooled; the reader keeps its own dup'd fd so it survives the connection close; tests `tplib/requests_stream{,_lines,_redirect}`). Declared divergence: `.content`/`.text`/`.json()` do NOT auto-drain a streamed body (requests' lazy-`.content` needs a mutating `@property`, which TPy's readonly model forbids -- see the mutable-property-getter feature item above); the body is reachable via `iter_content` / `iter_lines` / `r.raw.read(-1)`. Compiler bugs surfaced building this (all worked around; filed in BUGS.md): a generator method narrowing an Optional reference-type `self` field is mis-inferred const (drops its default param + const-poisons the narrowed local); a `with EXPR as v:` whose call materializes a union-typed default arg emits the temp in an invisible scope; storing a generator's yielded reference-type value to an outer variable aliases the dead frame (silent UAF -- copy with `bytes(chunk)`). `/tpy-review` residuals: `iter_content`/`iter_lines` now also chunk over `.content` on a NON-streamed response (matching requests, added post-review); `iter_lines` strips a preceding `\r` so CRLF bodies don't leak a trailing `\r` (lone-`\r`-as-terminator is a declared divergence from full splitlines). Deferred parity follow-ups (declared in the `Response` docstring): (8a) a mid-stream socket failure surfaces as the RAW socket exception, not a wrapped `requests.ConnectionError`/`ChunkedEncodingError` -- wrapping needs a `try/except`+`raise` inside `iter_content`'s generator (the fragile resumable-frame surface with open BUGS.md entries), so it is `/tpy-add-feature` work, not a review fix; it also interacts with the qualified-`except`-name-shadow compiler bug (BUGS.md) that made the raw exception mismatch reachable; (8b) a second iteration after exhaustion silently yields nothing rather than raising requests' `StreamConsumedError` (narrow misuse, low value). Also filed to BUGS.md this round: close/`with`-exit UAF of a `.raw`/`iter_content` handle taken before close (Safety); try-scoped-`Own`-local can't be moved (worked around via the `_send_recv` helper); borrow-form-`Optional[bytes]`-param forwarding copies the body per send (perf, the `_send_recv` extraction newly triggers it). (9) **`Session` connection pooling / keep-alive -- SHIPPED** (`Session._pool: dict[str, Box[_Connection]]` keyed `scheme|host|port|verify-token` via the `_pool_key` free function; pop -> use -> put back; a will_close response closes the socket but the pooled entry stays as a lazy-reconnect handle, since `HTTPConnection.connect()` reconnects when `sock is None`; same-host redirect hops reuse the pooled connection within one call; `__exit__` closes the pool; module-level `get`/`post` use a fresh Session per call like CPython requests; test `tplib/requests_pool`, which seeds `_pool` directly as the pooling seam). Residuals: a pooled connection keeps its creation `timeout=` (a later per-call value does not re-apply -- same family as the `_connection`-seam residual in (1); closing it = a `set_timeout` on the `_Connection` protocol, re-applied at pop time); the `_connection` injection seam stays single-use and unpooled (a Box cannot be moved out of an Optional field into the pool -- probe-verified reject). Test-coverage gap (filed by /tpy-review; low value -- the pop/put-back logic is hop-agnostic and covered at hop 0): the hop>0 pool branch (redirect target served from the pool) has no case -- feasible offline via dual seeding (`_connection` for hop 0, `_pool[_pool_key(redirect_target)]` for hop 1; two sockets, so no reader read-ahead conflict). (The pool FAILURE path -- a raise on a popped entry drops it instead of restoring -- is covered by `requests_pool`'s `failed_request_drops_entry`, a SHUT_WR peer -> `BadStatusLine`.) (10) **proxies -- TLS SHIPPED** (`verify: bool|str` + https routing + `requests.SSLError`, Increment 5; tests `tplib/requests_https`, `tplib/requests_verify_context`, `tplib/requests_redirect_https`); `proxies=` still missing. (11) **auth schemes beyond Basic** -- digest, bearer-token helper, custom auth objects. (12) **`urlopen` response surface** -- `.geturl()`/`.info()`/`.getcode()` (v1 returns a bare `HTTPResponse`; use `.status`/`.reason`/`.read()`/`.getheader()`). (13) **exception tree roots at `OSError` -- SHIPPED** (`RequestException` re-based on `OSError`, so the whole tree -- `HTTPError`/`ConnectionError`/`Timeout`/`SSLError`/`TooManyRedirects` -- is caught by `except OSError`, matching CPython requests' `IOError`/`OSError` root; `urllib.request.URLError` re-based likewise; `_request_on`'s own `except` arms are unaffected -- its try-body raises only wire-level exceptions and sibling handlers don't catch each other's raises; test `tplib/requests_errors` pins the `except OSError` arm). Surfaced building the REST-track ergonomic layer. Two code-quality follow-ups from /tpy-review (both low priority): (a) **request-body bytes are copied at each call layer** (`post`/`put`/... -> `request` -> `_request_on`), the context-blind `bytesview_to_bytes` coercion (pre-existing, tracked separately) plus `_request_on`'s initial `body = data` copy that could be deferred to the json-only branch -- fine for small JSON payloads, revisit before a large-body path; (b) **`_request_on` binds `reason = resp.reason` as a `string_view` local** then constructs `Response` after `conn.close()` -- safe today (the local `resp` outlives the view and `close()` only nulls the socket), but a fragile reused-view pattern; passing `resp.reason` directly to the constructor removes the intermediate view. (The offline test seams -- `urlopen`'s private `_urlopen(..., injected: Box[_Connection])` impl and `Session._connection` / `Session._redirect_connections` -- are underscore-prefixed / off the public surface; a stricter method-based entry point was considered and rejected as over-engineering for a test seam.)
- **Use-driven (symbol-granularity) managed-lib linking.** Module discovery and managed-lib linking are import-driven at MODULE granularity with no tree-shaking: `reach_analysis.py` seeds every imported module as reached regardless of use, and `collect_third_party_deps` (`compiler.py`) walks the full discovered module set and links every `managed=True` directive. Consequence surfaced by HTTPSConnection: `http.client` imports `ssl` (for `HTTPSConnection`), so EVERY program importing `http.client` -- even pure-plaintext ones -- links the vendored mbedTLS objects (build-size cost only; ccache + the cached stdlib `.o` set amortize build time; no correctness/runtime impact). CPython avoids this via lazy `import ssl` inside the method; TPy has no lazy import. The fix is use-driven linking: link a managed lib only when a *used* symbol pulls it in, not merely an imported module -- reverse the "imports => reached" seeding, track re-exported-but-unused symbols, and preserve the transitive TYPE closure (a module whose type appears in a signature must still link even if no call uses it). Generalizes to any `managed=True` lib (pcre2/re, mbedtls/ssl); the THIR/MIR migration is the proper foundation for the reachability machinery (don't build it ahead of demand -- plaintext binary size has to actually bite first). When it lands, `http.client`'s `ssl` import becomes free for non-HTTPS users with no API change. Surfaced building HTTPSConnection (Increment 4). The bundled CA store (`cacert_data.c`, ~230 KiB of `.rodata`) rides the same no-tree-shaking payload: it links into every binary whose module set reaches `ssl`, including plaintext-only `http.client` users -- use-driven linking would drop it from non-HTTPS binaries too.
- **Bump mbedTLS to 3.6.7 and drop the local RSA-PSS backport.** We vendor 3.6.6 (latest as of 2026-07) and carry `runtime/cpp/third_party/mbedtls.patches/001-tls12-accept-rsa-pss-rsae-sigalgs.patch` for the upstream #10668 regression (TLS 1.2 clients rejecting `rsa_pss_rsae_*` ServerKeyExchange -- breaks PSS-picking servers like Windows/Schannel with RSA certs). When the release carrying the fix ships (expected 3.6.7), bump `VERSION`+`SHA256` in `scripts/vendor_mbedtls.py` and drop the patch (the vendor procedure in `third_party/README.md` walks the patch-review step). Blocked on the upstream release; recheck periodically.
- **`socket.settimeout` v2 follow-ups.** v1 shipped `settimeout`/`gettimeout`/`getblocking` timeout mode (recv/send/accept/connect wait in `poll()` on one deadline per operation, composed in `socket.py` over the `_interrupt` module's waits, which blocking mode shares so a Ctrl-C ends a blocked call; a timeout raises `TimeoutError("timed out")`, now an `OSError` subclass to match CPython where `socket.timeout is TimeoutError`; the `makefile`/`BufferedReader` read path is timeout-aware via a `FileIO(timeout_mode=)` flag that re-raises `os.read`'s EAGAIN-`BlockingIOError` as `TimeoutError`). Tests `stdlib/socket_{timeout,gettimeout,connect_timeout}` (CPython-parity), `tplib/requests_timeout`. Deferred: (1) **`setdefaulttimeout`/`getdefaulttimeout` + the `_GLOBAL_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` sentinel** -- CPython's `create_connection`/`HTTPConnection`/`urlopen` default to that process-wide sentinel, distinct from explicit `None`; TPy defaults to plain blocking (`None`), so a process-wide default can't be set. (2) **Proposal: make blocking and timeout-mode sockets permanently `O_NONBLOCK`, as CPython does** -- today they are blocking at the OS level. `accept()` polls the listener, then calls a blocking `accept()`; it does not flip `O_NONBLOCK` for the call because the flag lives on the open file description, shared with other threads and `setblocking()`. So with several threads accepting on one listener, one can lose the race for the connection its `poll()` saw and block in `accept()` past its deadline, deaf to Ctrl-C, until the next connection (`socket._accept_fd` in `lib/tpy/socket.py`). The proper fix is CPython's: keep blocking and timeout-mode sockets `O_NONBLOCK` at the OS level for their whole life (`getblocking()` reports the Python-level mode), so every blocking-mode call retries on `EAGAIN` and none can block outside `poll()`; `makefile()`'s reader over a dup of the fd then needs its own wait (today it relies on `SO_RCVTIMEO` on a blocking fd). (3) **connect-timeout *expiry* is not deterministically tested** -- the success path is covered on loopback (`socket_connect_timeout`), but triggering an actual connect timeout needs an unresponsive remote (network-dependent/flaky), same gap as the asyncio `_SockConnect` cancel test; add if a deterministic connect-stall harness lands. (4) **`SO_LINGER` (struct linger) setsockopt** -- still int-only (`setsockopt_int`); add a struct path when needed. (5) **`socket.timeout` alias** -- CPython aliases `socket.timeout` to `TimeoutError`; TPy doesn't export it, so `from socket import timeout` fails (and `except socket.timeout:` fails on the qualified-type-in-except limitation regardless). Low value -- code should use `except TimeoutError`. (6) **`timeout=` threading above `HTTPConnection` is compile-only-tested** -- `HTTPConnection(timeout=)` -> `create_connection` -> `settimeout` reaching the socket is now exec-tested over loopback (`stdlib/http_client_timeout`, parity), but the one-line forwardings above it (`urlopen(timeout=)`, `requests.get/post(timeout=)`, `Session.*(timeout=)` -> `_connect` -> `HTTPConnection`) are verified only by compilation: their offline test seam (`_sock=` / `Session._connection`) makes `connect()` a no-op, so an end-to-end requests/urlopen exec test would need a loopback HTTP server, which the http test suite avoids by policy (socketpair seams only). (7) **structured `.errno`/`.strerror` on `OSError` -- SHIPPED** (fields on `tpy::OSError` exposed via `native_field` renames -- `errno` is a C macro, the C++ members are `error_number`/`strerror_text`; needed a codegen fix so `native_field` renames resolve through TPy-level subclasses of `@native` records, walking `mro_ancestors`; populated by `_raise_errno`/`_raise_io`/`_maybe_raise_connection_error` and the asyncio `sock_connect` completion, which now routes through the shared PEP 3151 mapping and raises `ConnectionRefusedError` on a refused async connect like CPython asyncio; `gaierror(OSError)` ships for name-resolution failures with the EAI_* code in `.errno` via the `tpy_last_resolve_code()` shim; a minimal `errno` module (`EAGAIN`/`EWOULDBLOCK`/`EINPROGRESS`/`EPIPE`/`ECONNRESET`/`ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNABORTED`, host-correct via the `tpy_const_*` globals) enables `e.errno == errno.ECONNREFUSED`; tests `stdlib/socket_errno` (parity), `exceptions/os_error_attrs`). The "CPython-exact OSError" follow-up SHIPPED (branch `oserror-exact`): `(errno, strerror[, filename])` ctor overloads on the whole native family (per-overload `@cpp_template` stubs; `raise X(...)` and inherited-`__init__` construction resolve overload groups sema-side), ctor-time CPython-exact `str(e)` formatting, `.filename`/`.filename2` fields, os/file C++ raise sites populated via the shared `tpy::raise_mapped_os_error` PEP 3151 table (os error messages drop the `op:` prefix), socket factories retired to direct ctors, file-domain errno constants (`ENOENT`/`EEXIST`/`EACCES`/`EPERM`/`EISDIR`/`ENOTDIR`/`EBADF`/`ETIMEDOUT`), and a warning on errno-form construction of the BARE `OSError` class (CPython's `__new__` subclass mapping divergence); tests `exceptions/os_error_ctor`, `stdlib/os_error_exact`. Remaining residuals: post-hoc attribute assignment doesn't reformat `str(e)` (declared; ctor-time formatting), message-kwarg construction (`SSLError(message="x")`) of an inherited-overload-ctor subclass no longer resolves (kwargs skip the overload-group path; loud arity error, rare form); user subclasses keep a single `(errno, strerror)` `__init__` (user-class `@overload __init__` is accepted-then-silently-dropped, so it can't express the per-form ctor pair -- see BUGS.md). Coverage gap: `ConnectionResetError` (ECONNRESET) and `ConnectionAbortedError` (ECONNABORTED) are mapped in `_maybe_raise_connection_error` but have no exec test (hard to trigger deterministically without a cooperating peer / `SO_LINGER` RST); a compile-phase-only case exercising `except ConnectionResetError:`/`except ConnectionAbortedError:` would at least guard the names compile and are recognized as `OSError` subclasses. Surfaced building the REST-track reliability layer; (5)/(6) and the coverage gap by /tpy-review.
- **Annotation validator: explicit `__deref__()` calls aren't recognized as Ptr deref sites.** `# tpyc: nullable(p)` on `print(p.__deref__())` fails with "no ptr dereference found" -- the validator only matches auto-deref field/method access. Affects test authoring only (pointers/panic_ptr_deref_null stays unannotated because of it). Note: annotations are skipped in `--update-snapshots` mode, so a bad one only surfaces on the next normal run.
- **Subscript-keyed narrowing (`if items[i] is not None: use(items[i])`).** No narrowing fact is established for subscript expressions -- `_expr_to_narrowing_key` returns None for `TpySubscript`, so the guarded re-read warns and re-checks even for value-type elements with an unchanged index (verified by probe; the `warn_subscript_narrowing_*` test names notwithstanding, the unmutated sibling also warns). Sound but pessimistic; the documented bind-to-a-local pattern is the workaround. If added, the fact key must include the index expression identity and be killed by ANY container mutation, index reassignment, or a mutation through any name the may-hold relation (`prescan.InPlaceWrites`) relates to the container (the kill-set machinery from the flow-fact work covers the meets). CPython-semantics note: a repeated `items[i]` read is a real second `__getitem__` call, so eliding is only sound for builtin containers with no user `__getitem__` side effects.
- **Move an owned reference-type local into a comprehension element at last use.** NARROWED: container *method* inserts (`xs.append(x)`, `s.add(x)`, `d[k] = x`), the list/dict/set *literal* element forms, AND list/set/dict comprehensions over an `Own[T]`-yielding source now move a bare owned element -- the comprehension's last-evaluated sink (list/set element, dict value, including the filtered `[x for x in g() if p(x)]` shape) moves unconditionally (`_comp_elem_moves(is_last_sink=True)`, `_move_comp_sink`). Two gaps remain: (a) **consuming a temporary owned container** like `[w for w in [a, b]]` where `a`/`b` are owned locals -- iterating the fresh list literal does not yield `Own[T]` (the elements are borrows of the temp's slots), so the move-gate (`gen.owns_elements`) does not fire and the elements copy. Closing it needs consuming-iteration of the temporary source (move out of `[a, b]`), distinct from the Own-yielding-source path already handled; (b) a **sub-expression sink inside a filtered comprehension** -- `[take(node) for node in g() if p(node)]` where `node` is consumed by `take`'s `Own[T]` param: the element is the call result (not the bare loop var), so the move runs through `_maybe_move`'s `all_last_uses` gate, which the filter's extra `node` occurrence defeats, so `node` copies into `take`. Rare (the bare-var last-sink cases are covered); closing it needs the sub-expression move to recognize the post-filter last use too. Surfaced by the owned-Optional-local-move-out feature and the comprehension-sink move work.
- **[LOW] Materialize the comprehension bare-loop-var sink fact instead of re-deriving it in sema and codegen.** `_comp_elem_moves` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) and `_move_comp_sink` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py`) each re-derive "this sink is the bare loop var" with the same `TpyCoerce`-unwrap + `inner.name == gen.var` shape check. The two are adjacent and well-commented (and gate on the same `is_last_sink`/`all_last_uses` facts, so they don't drift today), but per the CLAUDE.md "prefer first-class AST facts over consumer-side re-derivation" direction this could be one shared util (or a fact on the comprehension node set during sema). Low urgency; THIR lowering will force it. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, codegen-correctness) of the dict-comprehension move.
- **Match codegen `_SwitchEntry` tuple -> dataclass.** `tpyc/codegen_cpp/match.py`'s `_SwitchEntry` is now an 8-field positional tuple (`guard, body, cap, as, raw_names, loc, type_facts, bind_modes`) unpacked at ~15 sites; growing it positionally is fragile (a file-local `@dataclass` already exists as precedent). Convert to a dataclass so field adds don't touch every unpack. Pre-existing debt, widened by the match-binding-form fact. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the match scalar-copy fix.
- **Match guarded-switch dedups bindings using the first entry's bind mode.** In `_emit_switch_groups`' multi-entry guarded arm, a binding shared across same-label entries is emitted once with `entries[0]`'s `bind_modes`; correct today because sema enforces same-value/same-label arms have a compatible binding type, so the free-copy-scalar verdict is identical across entries. Latent if that sema rule ever loosens to allow heterogeneous types per label. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the match scalar-copy fix.
- **Borrow-alias branch-decl follow-ups (from the @error_return borrow-alias fix).** Test gaps: a dict/set borrow from an `@error_return` callable (list+record covered); a borrow-then-borrow rebind (two branches binding different borrow sources, mutate after, observe the right source); a match-capture of a non-value subject guarding the `nonstmt_bound_names` exclusion (existing match tests pass with zero churn, a weak implicit guard only). (a) Const-predicate drift: sema's `record_stmt_borrow_binding` (`sema/context.py`) computes borrow const from ReadonlyType + readonly-fi only, while codegen's `_is_const_indirect` additionally consults codegen-populated const sets (`deep_const_borrow_params`, `const_ref_params`); a mismatch is a LOUD C++ compile error (`&const` into `T*`), not silent -- unify when those const facts move sema-side. (b) Single-target for-loop vars are not in `nonstmt_bound_names` (only with-as/unpack/match are); a loop-var-only name never enters the stmt-borrow fact so today's behavior is correct, but a name that is BOTH a loop var and stmt-borrow-bound elsewhere in the function now gets cross-statement pointer-form leakage at the loop pre-decl (the deleted walk was stmt-scoped); decide whether loop vars should be marked (which would change the old in-body-reassign behavior) or the fact made per-stmt. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the borrow-alias fix and the borrow-fact materialization.
- **Unify cross-module C++-name qualification (sema overlay vs codegen's native_cpp_names).** `_cross_module_cpp_overlay` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`) re-derives a slice of codegen's `native_cpp_names` population (`generator.py`, ~130 lines) to qualify cross-module records at sema-time cpp_template rendering -- the two paths can drift (the @native subcase already had to be added to match codegen). Root cause is that `NominalType.to_cpp()` renders cross-module names via a codegen-populated ContextVar map, and sema renders C++ before that map exists. THIR-aligned end-state: push cross-module qualification out of `to_cpp` into a shared renderer that takes an explicit module-qualification context, so both phases call one path. Pre-existing smell (sema renders C++ at all); IR-migration-adjacent. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of `fix-cpp-template-cross-ns-qualify`.
- **Cross-module cpp_template qualification: `set`/`dict`/`{cpp}` coverage.** The sema overlay that qualifies cross-module element types in `@cpp_template` substitution is covered for `list()` (`imports/list_cross_module_own_iter`) and the same-module non-regression (`iterators/list_same_module_own_iter`). Untested through the same code path: `set(cross_module_iter())` (`set_construct<{T}>`), `dict(...)` (`dict_construct<{K},{V}>` -- the two-param path), and the `{cpp}` substitution branch (`result_type.to_cpp()`) with a cross-module result type. Same `{T}`/`{cpp}` render, lower risk, but a regression would silently emit unqualified C++. Also a cross-module `@native` record in a cpp_template arg (the overlay now mirrors codegen's native_name handling, but it's untested). Add guards when next touching this area. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage + architecture-fit) of `fix-cpp-template-cross-ns-qualify`.
- **`heapq.merge` manual-append guard for a reference-type `Own[T]` yield.** `tests/cases/stdlib/heapq_merge` exercises the reference-type (`Item`) yield only via `list(merge(...))`; the `for x in merge(...): r.append(x)` manual-append path is covered for value-type `int32` but not for a reference-type `Own[T]` element, so a codegen regression in that append branch would be invisible. Add a small ref-type manual-append case. `list()` already covers the same yield boundary, so this is guard-completeness, not a known gap. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the merge `Iterator[Own[T]]` flip.
- **`Iterable[Own[T]]` conformance test-coverage gaps.** The Own-symmetric-strip fix is covered by `iterators/own_iter_to_iterable` (`list()` + a user `Iterable[Own[T]]` param fed an `Iterator[Own[T]]`) and `iterators/iter_copy_into_owned_warns` (the still-warns guard for a non-Own actual). Untested: `set(iter_of_own)` / `dict(iter_of_own_pairs)` sinks, and the concrete-container exact-match branch in `compatibility.py` with an actual carrying `Own` in a type arg (e.g. `dict[K, Own[V]]`). Add when next touching that area. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the symmetric-strip fix.
- **Move `_register_call_result_borrow` out of `statements.py`.** It is local-imported inside `_analyze_named_expr` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) to dodge the `expressions` <-> `statements` circular import; move it to a shared module (`sema/iter_loans.py` holds its helpers) so it imports at top level. Low value; do when next touching either site. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the with-manager-borrow fix.
- **Converge the explicit method call with the implicit-dunder chokepoint (`tpyc/sema/receiver_calls.py`).** `g.m()` (`MethodAnalyzer`) shares the loan check, the mutation credit and the readonly-receiver predicate (`receiver_is_readonly`) with `credit_implicit_receiver_call`; the TIMING differs: the explicit call rejects a readonly receiver on the callee's declared `is_readonly` at once, while an implicit dunder waits for the emitted const-ness in the finalize pass, so an unannotated non-mutating method passes as `for x in g` and fails as `g.m()`. the readonly-receiver reject and the "does this call mutate the receiver" decision (`call_mutates_receiver`) are still decided at the method-call site, and it looks invalidation up by name rather than from the resolved callee (BUGS.md#explicit-inherited-method-no-loan-warning). One entry point for both.
- **Route `del`, slice assignment and the builtin element-hop store through the receiver-call chokepoint.** `del g[k]`, `g[a:b] = v` and the element-hop check of a builtin `g[k] = v` still carry their own loan and mutation code in `tpyc/sema/statements.py`; each is a call on the receiver (`__delitem__`, `__setitem__(slice)`, `__setitem__`) and belongs on `credit_implicit_receiver_call`.
- **Make the receiver-call chokepoint's modes explicit.** `credit_implicit_receiver_call` takes `callee=None` (callee unknown), `eager` (no Phase-2 deferral) and an opt-out `check_loans`, and `credit_receiver_mutation` an `edges_recorded`; a small mode value (or separate entry points) would say which combination a site means. (The readonly-receiver test is derived from the receiver itself, `receiver_is_readonly`, and its verdict is queued to the finalize pass.)
- **Fold `with_borrowed_fields` into the `with_fields` tuple (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/resumable_cfg.py`).** The async with-region prescan tracks borrowed (`T*`) vs owning (`frame_slot<T>`) context-manager frame fields via a parallel `with_borrowed_fields: set[str]` keyed by field name, alongside `with_fields: list[tuple[str, str]]`. A string-keyed side-set is the "string-key => not designed yet" smell; widen `with_fields` to `list[tuple[str, str, bool]]` (or a named triple) so the borrow flag is self-contained and the `fname in with_borrowed_fields` membership test at emit time disappears. Both are populated in the same prescan loop, so no ordering obstacle. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the with-manager-borrow fix.
- **Disentangle `FunctionInfo.is_readonly` for callable-value calls (`tpyc/sema/methods.py`, `tpyc/sema/calls.py`).** The synthetic FunctionInfo for a callable-value call is `is_readonly=False` so the borrow/mutation consumers treat the callback's ARGS as mutable -- but `is_readonly` is also read as "the RECEIVER may be mutated", so `methods.py` needs two `and not expr.is_callable_field` guards (at the readonly-receiver rejection and the receiver-mutation marking) to stop a callable field from demoting its holder. Each new `is_readonly` consumer that cares about receiver vs arg mutation will need another `is_callable_field` patch. Cleaner: split the two facts -- either a separate `receiver_readonly` flag on FunctionInfo, or set the synthetic FI `is_readonly=True` and carry arg-mutation conservatism through a dedicated channel. Relatedly, `analyze_callable_value_call`'s eager opaque-callee mutation loop re-expresses the per-param filtering (`ReadonlyType` / `param_has_mutable_borrow_surface` / `TypeParamRef`) that the call-edge recorder already has; an `_eager_mark_opaque_callee_mutations(expr, param_types)` helper would give the "opaque mutating callee" pattern (also wanted by unknown-body constructors) one home. Effort: S. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + safety-model) of the callable-values fix.
- **Borrow-conflict warning is not last-use aware (`BorrowTracker.has_element_borrow`, `tpyc/sema/context.py:271`).** The "passing borrowed container to non-readonly parameter" warning (`_check_borrow_arg_conflicts`) fires whenever the container has ANY element/iter/ptr borrower registered in scope, regardless of whether that borrow is still live at the call site. So `p = xs[0]; print(p.v); mutate(xs)` warns even though `p`'s last read precedes the call and the mutation is provably safe -- a false positive. Sound (it never misses a real cross-call invalidation, only over-approximates), but noisy on the dead-borrow shape, which is common (`tests/cases/calls/warn_callable_borrow_invalidation` exercises exactly it). **Fix shape:** gate the warning on the borrow being live across the call -- intersect `has_element_borrow` with the existing last-use set (`all_last_uses`), or expire element borrows from the BorrowTracker at the borrower's last use. The latter is the cleaner end-state and aligns with the MIR loan-expiry model; the former is a cheap intersection at the warning site. Either way verify it doesn't suppress the genuine live-across-call case (read after the call). Effort: S. Surfaced reviewing the callable-values warning coverage.
- **One borrow-invalidation warning per statement.** `g[1] += 1` (`__getitem__` and `__setitem__`) and `with g:` (`__enter__` and `__exit__`) each warn twice when both dunders grow `g`; report the statement once, naming the dunders. Low value; `tests/cases/records/warn_mutating_dunder_invalidates` would lose a duplicate line.
- **Callable-value test backlog (`tests/cases/calls/`).** Coverage additions from the callable-values fix, none guarding a known live bug: (a) `error_` case for the readonly-contract rejection from the callable-value direction -- a function with a non-readonly list param stored into a `Callable[[readonly[list[T]]], None]` field/param should reject at the store; (b) a `Fn[[T], R]` generic combinator forwarding a reference-typed arg, asserting it does NOT over-warn (the generic-slot eager-mark exemption); (c) return-covariance positive test (callee returns a concrete subtype, contract expects a supertype -- current variance tests use `None` returns on both sides); (d) a mutate-through-and-read-back case for the `star_unpack_generic_fn` / generic `Callable[[Box[T]], R]` shape (the const->mutable flip is currently exercised read-only); (e) a Callable-field-from-`@readonly`-method happy path (the `is_callable_field` receiver exemption is exercised only indirectly). Effort: S. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage + cpython-parity) of the callable-values fix.
- **Self-iterator `Iterable[T]`-param test-coverage gaps (`tests/cases/iterators/gen_selfiter_param`).** The resumable self-iterator fix (drive a move-only generator source in place rather than copying it into the iterator slot) is covered for a sync generator consuming a generator via a for-loop + comprehension, a temporary source, and the `Iterator[T]`/list inverses. Untested, none guarding a known bug: (a) an **async** consumer (`async def f(it: Iterable[T]): for x in it: ...; f(gen())`) -- low priority, the async coro's *sync* `for` reuses the identical `resumable_iter_*` emit already covered by the sync test, so this is guard-completeness for the 8 regenerated `async_*proto_param*` snapshots, not an untested path; (b) a generator **method** consuming an `Iterable[T]` whose arg is a self-iterator (the `record_name` frame adds a `__self` field + distinct struct name); (c) **two-level chaining** (`take(take(repeat_n(...), m), n)`) -- a resumable generator consuming another resumable generator; (d) an **empty** source (`times=0`, loop body never entered). Add when next touching this area. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the self-iterator-copy fix.
- **`match` sequence patterns (`case [a, b]:` / `case (a, b):`).** The biggest user-expected pattern-matching gap and fully feasible in TPy's static model: `tuple` has compile-time arity, `list`/`Array`/`Span` need a length check + element bind, `str`/`bytes` excluded (matches CPython). No representation change, no RTTI. Listed under `MATCH_CASE_DESIGN.md` "Future Extensions"; this is the one worth scheduling first (mapping `{"k": v}` and star `[x, *rest]` patterns can follow -- star needs a rest-binding decision: sub-tuple for tuples, view-vs-copy for `list`/`Span`). Steering note: prefer growing `match`'s pattern surface over back-porting expression subjects into `isinstance`, so each surface keeps a clear job (isinstance = bare-name test-and-narrow; match = expression-subject test-and-destructure).
- **Checked downcast for polymorphic / `@dynamic` sources.** Today the only runtime downcast is `isinstance`-narrowing inside a branch; there is no one-shot "assert this is a `Dog` or panic." Feasible by mirroring `any_cast_or_panic` (emit a checked `dynamic_cast` / `dyn_adapter_cast`). Open decision: `typing.cast(T, x)` is a static no-op in CPython, so overloading it to mean "checked downcast" diverges -- a distinct spelling (e.g. a `downcast()` helper) may be cleaner. Pairs with the `Any`-extraction path that `cast()` already has. Lower priority than sequence patterns; revisit when a real use appears.
- **Materialize vararg slot const-ness on `TpyVarargPack` at sync time.** `_gen_vararg_pack` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py:5308`) takes an optional `slot_type` and re-derives whether to wrap the element type in `ReadonlyType` at codegen by combining the pack's substituted base with the slot's current readonly-ness. Cleaner THIR-aligned shape: when `_sync_inferred_vararg_readonly` flips a slot, also walk the module's call sites and update `TpyVarargPack.element_type` for each call to that callee -- codegen then reads a single fact, no consumer-side re-derivation. Needs a TpyCall/TpyMethodCall walker that knows which packs target which callee FI. Not blocking; the current shape works.
- **Auto-readonly inference for `*args` (parallel to non-vararg auto-const).** Non-vararg reference-type params auto-const-infer based on body mutation (`def take_one(item: Box)` with a non-mutating body emits `const Box& item`); varargs don't -- `*items: Box` always emits `tpy::varargs<Box>` (mutable elements) regardless of whether the body mutates. The asymmetry is the underlying reason the caller-side marking fix landed on `fix-vararg-const-arg`: a non-mutating mutable vararg slot forces every caller to provide non-const sources, instead of the callee's slot collapsing to `varargs<const T>`. The proper symmetric fix is to track vararg-element mutation in the body (mirror the param-mutation tracking for non-vararg params) and have `_vararg_span_type` / the codegen render path emit `varargs[readonly[T]]` / `varargs<const T>` for inferred-readonly slots. That subsumes both the recent caller-marking fix (which becomes unnecessary for non-mutating callees) and the const-source family in BUGS.md. Real feature work -- design surface (interaction with the explicit `*items: readonly[T]` form, with generic varargs, with mutation propagation), and many existing snapshots would shift (mutable vararg signatures flip to `varargs<const T>` for non-mutating bodies). Probably warrants `/tpy-add-feature`. Surfaced when reviewing the `fix-vararg-const-arg` test outputs.
- **Mutating property getter has no escape hatch.** Every `@property` getter is forced `auto_readonly` (`tpyc/parse/parser.py` sets `auto_readonly=True` on getters unconditionally), so the getter *body* cannot mutate `self` or call a non-readonly method -- a lazy-memoizing getter (`if not self._cached: self._cached = compute()`) is rejected. CPython getters mutate freely. (Cloning an `Rc` from a getter body now works -- `Rc.clone` is `@auto_readonly` since the interior-`_cell` change -- so that is no longer an example of the gap; body-side mutation of a plain field still is.) (Returning a mutable object from a getter and modifying *that* DOES work -- auto_readonly's dual const/mutable overloads hand back a mutable reference on a mutable receiver; the gap is purely body-side mutation.) Possible: a `@mutating_property` / non-const-getter form, or a getter-body opt-out of auto_readonly. Interacts with the auto_readonly dual-overload clone (probably `/tpy-add-feature`). Effort: M.
- **Vararg address-take marking: consolidate sites + use `effective_storage`.** Five sites in `tpyc/sema/{calls.py,compatibility.py}` share the "this expression's address is taken into a `T*` slot, so the source must be a non-const lvalue -- mark its root mutated" pattern: `_validate_lvalue_params` (~calls.py:2549), `coerce_expr`'s `record_to_ptr`/`upcast_to_ptr` (compatibility.py:1252), the `value_ptr_coercion` path (~calls.py:4606), and the two vararg packing branches added on the readonly-varargs / fix-vararg-const-arg work (`_analyze_and_pack_varargs` non-unpack and *unpack branches). A small `_mark_addr_taken_root` helper on `CallAnalyzer` would tighten them. Additionally, the two vararg branches use raw `_root_name_of_expr(arg)` rather than `borrow_tracker.effective_storage(...)` -- the other three sites resolve alias chains first, so the vararg pair currently misses element/field/ptr borrows back to their source param. No real bug surfaced yet, but the asymmetry will rot. THIR-friendly final form: tag `TpyVarargPack` with `address_takes_elements: bool` at construction so codegen + the mark sites consult a single fact instead of each re-deriving from `elem_type.is_value_type() and not TypeParamRef`.
- **Codegen-side vararg lvalue/hoist dispatch consolidation.** `_gen_vararg_pack`'s non-unpack branch (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py:5337`) now classifies each arg as lvalue/rvalue inline (`TpyName`/`TpyFieldAccess`/`TpySubscript` after `TpyCoerce` peel) to decide between direct `&arg` and temp-hoist. The classifier duplicates `_match_subject_is_lvalue` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/match.py:25`. Two follow-ups: (a) push the per-arg hoist decision back to sema as `TpyVarargPack.args_need_hoist: list[bool]` -- THIR-aligned, single source of truth (codegen reads, doesn't re-derive a structural fact); (b) extract a shared `codegen_cpp/lvalue.py:is_addressable_lvalue` helper once a third caller appears. Worth doing before the next varargs-touching feature. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `fix-vararg-generic-ref`.
- **Resumable generator yielding `tuple[..., RefType]` with 2+ yields.** No test exercises a resumable-frame generator (multi-yield) yielding a tuple that contains a pointer-form element -- the interaction of the new borrow-form-loop-var deref at the yield-return and `_maybe_wrap_tuple_to_pointer`. The tuple path is unchanged by the deref fix (gated on `generator_borrow_form_loop_vars`, scalar names only), so it's coverage hardening, not a known defect. Add under `tests/cases/iterators/`. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the generic-vararg-iteration work.
- **Materialize the owning-tuple generator-local fact instead of re-deriving it in codegen.** `CodeGenContext.owning_generator_tuple_locals` body-scans `func.body` to classify which resumable-frame tuple locals are owning (`Own[tuple]` call, never reassigned) vs aliasing, and is called twice per async function (the struct field-decl in `gen_async.py` and `setup_resumable_frame_locals`). Sema already tracks the owning fact in `owning_storage_tuple_vars`; THIR-aligned shape: materialize an owning-tuple-locals set on `TpyFunction` (analogous to `generator_locals`) so codegen reads one fact, no body rescan or double-derivation. Not blocking. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the tuple owning/alias-mix work.
- **Materialize the borrow-alias frame-local classification on the AST instead of the codegen prescan.** `_classify_pointer_alias_locals` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`) body-scans the resumable body to classify which frame locals are borrow aliases (single-assign of an lvalue, tuple-unpack `is_ref` targets from a safe source) -> `T*`/`const T*` frame slots, re-deriving the borrow-vs-own decision via `_is_plain_nonvalue` / `is_rvalue_source` / `_is_const_indirect`. Same family as the owning-tuple item above: sema's `_analyze_var_decl` / `_analyze_tuple_unpack` already decide indirection (`ref_bound_locals` / `pointer_locals`); THIR-aligned shape is an `is_borrow_alias` (+ const) fact on `TpyVarDecl` / per-target on `TpyTupleUnpack` so codegen reads one fact. The for-loop `pointer_form_unpack_targets` machinery is also a codegen prescan, so the eventual unification covers both. Not blocking. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the borrow-alias-across-suspension fix.
- **[LOW] Send/Sync of a promoted loop-body frame local takes the loop-variable bucket.** `frame_loop_var_names` (`_stamp_frame_materials`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) is every name in `pending_loop_vars`, and `local_slot` (`tpyc/sema/frame_traits.py`) answers not-Send / not-Sync for all of them -- right for a loop variable that may be a raw pointer or view into the iterable, over-conservative for a promoted body local the frame OWNS (`::tpy::frame_slot<T>` after 2026-09-14): a generator holding only `c = Cell(n)` in a while body read after the loop flips from Send+Sync to neither. Route owned-value promoted locals through `_value_slot_traits` like the other frame fields; the view/pointer-form ones keep the bucket.

- **Only hoist resumable-frame locals that are live across a suspension.** `_collect_generator_locals` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py:1250`) hoists EVERY function-level local into a frame field -- its only exclusions are params, `self`, and `global`-declared names -- so a local that is born and dies entirely within one straight-line segment (no `await`/`yield` between its last write and last read) still becomes a frame field. The docstring claims "locals living across a yield/await suspension become frame fields", but there is no cross-suspension liveness filter; the claim is aspirational. Example: a tuple-literal unpack desugared in an async body emits hidden `__unpack_N_*` temps that bind the targets before the first `await` and are dead by the suspension, yet they appear as `T* __unpack_0_0 = nullptr;` frame fields (`tests/cases/async/tuple_literal_unpack_alias_across_await`). Cost is frame-size only (extra pointer/value slots, written once) -- zero runtime cost -- so not blocking. Proper fix: compute per-local cross-suspension liveness (the resumable CFG in `resumable_cfg.py` has the suspension points) and field only locals live across >=1 suspension; the rest stay block-scoped locals in their segment. Correctness-sensitive (a local used after a suspension that is wrongly NOT fielded becomes stale/UAF), so design it as its own `/tpy-add-feature` pass, not an inline tweak. Benefits all async/generator bodies, not just unpacks. Since 2026-09-14 a loop-body local read after the loop joins the class for both loop kinds (a promoted body local stays in `pending_loop_vars` so a read after a SUSPENDING loop lands on the frame at all; a `while` body's locals used to escape the collector): csv's `DictReader.__iter__` (`name`) and the requests body reader (`end`) each carry one such field that a liveness filter would drop. Surfaced reviewing the tuple-literal-unpack desugar's async frame fields. A LOOP VARIABLE of a loop the frame does not drive is the same class and the cheapest face to check: a `for` whose body does not suspend keeps its block-local `auto&& x = *__beg_1;`, yet the hoist takes `x` out of `func.pending_loop_vars` all the same and the struct declares a `::tpy::frame_slot<Cell> x;` nothing ever names (verified 2026-09-21 on `/tmp/agents/loop_src_loan/r1_single.py`) -- the liveness filter answers it, and so would asking the frame prescan whether this loop is CFG-decomposed.
- **Materialize alias-local const-ness as a sema fact instead of re-deriving the source's const-ness in codegen.** `_is_const_indirect` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/statements.py`) decides a non-value alias local binds `const` by inspecting whether its init reads a const-inferred source (name in `const_ref_params` / `const_indirect_locals` / `deep_const_borrow_params`), and the `T&`-branch propagation at the call site (statements.py ~2119-2139) re-derives the same for subscript/name sources. The two are NOT redundant today -- `_is_const_indirect` tests the un-unwrapped `TpyName` and adds `deep_const_borrow_params`, while the inline `T&`-branch block unwraps `TpyCoerce` and handles subscript -- so neither can be deleted in isolation; they need manual lockstep if either const set grows. This is the consumer-side re-derivation the IR migration aims to remove: sema already knows (post-Phase-2) whether the alias local is ever mutated through its borrow chain, so the const verdict should be a single fact on `TpyVarDecl` (and per-target on `TpyTupleUnpack`) that codegen reads once, replacing both sites. Folds into the `is_borrow_alias (+ const)` fact in the item above. Not blocking. Surfaced completing the single-assign alias const-precision fix (BUGS.md const-source family).
- **Tuple-literal-unpack desugar test-coverage gaps.** The aliasing desugar (`a, b = (e0, e1)` -> per-element temps + binds) is covered for sync function and async bodies, but: (a) no snippet exercises it inside a SYNC GENERATOR (`yield`) body, where the temps/binds interact with the resumable-frame ABI (pointer-form frame locals, frame-slot hoist) -- add a `tests/cases/iterators/` case that aliases a reference element across a yield and observes a mutation at the source; (b) the const-precision half (`_is_const_indirect` const-inferred Optional/pointer-local source) is regression-guarded only by the `warn_auto_move_optional` snapshot -- add an exec case where a read-only `Optional[T]` alias is passed to a `@readonly` method, so a silently-dropped `const` becomes a C++ build failure; (c) add a `TestDesugarShape` unit case for an arity-mismatched tuple-literal RHS (`a, b = (int32(1),)`) to pin that the length guard skips the desugar (falls through to TpyTupleUnpack + sema arity error). Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage).
- **Tuple-literal-unpack desugar does not reach macro-generated statement fragments.** `parse_fragment(kind="statements")` parses via `_parse_body` at `_fn_body_depth == 0`, so a flat tuple-literal unpack emitted by a macro fragment won't desugar (stays a copying TpyTupleUnpack). No current macro emits such a fragment; revisit if the macro API grows one. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit).
- **Generator-delegation limitation family: what is left.** The frame embeds its `for` source by value and spells every field of the loop off the source expression's own type (2026-09-22: `using __for_src_N_t = decltype((...))` in the frame struct), which lifted the spelling rejects -- a protocol-param callee, an iterable that is not a direct generator call (a combinator, a genexpr, a call through a variable), a named `Iterator[T]` source with a non-value element. What remains is not spelling: a *mutually delegating cross-module pair* (neither header is complete for the other, `error_gen_delegate_cross_module_cycle`) and *bounded recursive delegation* (tree walks) both need heap indirection for the embedded frame -- an `Own[Iterator[T]]`-style boxed handle the frame can hold without knowing the callee's size. A local bound to a generator call is a concrete frame, aliased like a record (2026-09-23).
- **Cross-kind resumable-ordering test: `async def` consuming a sync generator call.** The unified `_emit_resumable_structs` sort orders coro structs after the sync generator structs they embed (`for x in gen_call():` with `await` in the body allocates a `__for_src` field typed as the generator struct), but no test exercises the cross-kind edge -- the coro-before-generator seed order would mask a missing edge until declaration order flips it. Add under `tests/cases/async/`. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `fix-generator-for-src`.
- **Unify `sema/compatibility.py::is_lvalue` with `codegen_cpp/context.py::is_temporary_expr`.** Logical complements classifying the same expression taxonomy with one diverging TpyCoerce sub-case; the for-src materialization work deepened the codegen-side usage. A shared lvalue predicate would keep the two from drifting. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `fix-generator-for-src`.
- **Shared coro-param frame-slot classification predicate.** `tpyc/sema/frame_traits.py::param_slot` is a hand-maintained conservative mirror of `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py::_classify_param_kind`: every new coro param storage shape must be added to both, and a missed sema-side update silently classifies the new shape non-Send (the safe direction, but degrades Send coverage). Extract a shared classification (a kind enum or an "is stored owned" predicate over types) both sides consult -- natural to fold into the generator-onto-resumable-frame migration, which restructures the codegen side anyway. While there, refine the over-conservative (never-unsound) cases that degrade Send coverage: (a) value-type `Optional`/`Union` slots (`int32 | None` lowers to owned `std::optional<int32_t>` but classifies non-Send); (b) `_value_slot_traits` gates the tuple-borrow check on `TupleType.has_ref_elements()`, wider than codegen's actual borrow test `has_pointer_repr_element()` -- a tuple with a *union* element is stored owned by codegen but classified non-Send; (c) **str/bytes params are now stored OWNED in the frame** (codegen `OWNED_COPY`, gated on `is_owned_in_coro_frame`), but `param_slot` still classifies a `str` param by `StrView` traits (non-Send) -- so an owned-str/bytes-param coro/generator frame is conservatively non-Send when it is actually Send. The shared predicate to consult here is `is_owned_in_coro_frame` (already used by codegen + `generator_borrow_param_indices`); `param_slot` should classify those by the owned type's traits. All three are safe-direction; tightening any is the risky direction (a wrong tightening reintroduces a false-Send), so verify against codegen shapes, not casually. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `send-sync-phase2` (a,b) and the str/bytes coro-param owned-copy fix (c).
- **Share the sync `_gen_call` arg-coercion pipeline with async `_gen_coro_emplace_arg`.** `_gen_coro_emplace_arg` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`) hand-mirrors a subset of sync's `_gen_call` arg cascade -- `_gen_optional_ptr_arg`, `_gen_dynamic_protocol_arg`, `_gen_union_arg`, then `gen_call_arg` -- but omits `_gen_protocol_arg` (sync's nullable/multi static-protocol coercion). Not a reachable defect today: nullable/multi-protocol static-protocol async params are rejected up front by `_protocol_template_parts` (gen_async.py:458, clean "not yet supported" diagnostic), single required protocols flow through the `gen_call_arg` fallthrough, and rvalue ref-param temps are now hoisted by `_lift_borrowed_rvalue_args`. The hazard is drift: the manual mirror can silently fall behind when sync gains a new coercion. THIR-friendly final form: one shared arg-coercion entry point both the sync call site and the async emplace path call, so neither re-derives the cascade. Touches the hot sync `_gen_call` path -- warrants its own `/tpy-fix-bug`/`/tpy-add-feature` pass, not an inline patch. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `fix-async-emplace-rvalue-dangle` (was the "shape half" of a BUGS.md entry whose silent-miscompile framing didn't hold up once the lifetime half was fixed and the protocol case shown to be guarded).
- **Async-def factory param for an `Own[T]` param emits `T` by-value, not `own_param_t<T>`.** An `async def` method/function with an `Own[T]` param (e.g. `asyncio.Queue.put(self, item: Own[T])`) generates the coro-factory wrapper param as `T item` rather than `::tpy::own_param_t<T>` -- unlike the sync side and unlike `put_nowait`/`get_nowait` which use `own_param_t<T>`/`own_return_t<T>`. Non-failing today: `Own[T]` args are moved (not copied), so `@nocopy`/reference element types still work (`Queue[Box[int32]]` compiles + runs). It's a codegen consistency gap that could bite a future genuinely-uncopyable-AND-unmovable type, or diverge from the sync param shape in some edge. Fix: route the async factory's param lowering through the same `own_param_t<T>` path the sync method path uses. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `asyncio.Queue`.
- **Unify MRO-bound-ancestor resolution between `coro_struct_owner` and `protocols.py::resolve_ancestor_instantiation`.** Both walk `RecordInfo.mro_ancestors` to find the bound ancestor `NominalType` for a given defining record. They differ in how they match (`coro_struct_owner` in `tpyc/typesys.py` matches by qname string and stays registry-free; `resolve_ancestor_instantiation` uses a registry for per-ancestor `get_record_for_type` identity checks). Not unifiable as-is, but if the MRO-rebase pattern grows a third caller, hoist a single qname-based free function into `typesys.py` both consult. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the generic-base inherited-async fix.
- **`asyncio.BoundedSemaphore.__init__` duplicates `Semaphore.__init__` instead of `super().__init__()`.** The subclass re-runs the `value < 0` guard and re-initializes `_value`/`_waiters` by hand (then sets `_bound`), because TPy's MI `super()` support is only partial. If `Semaphore` ever gains a field, `BoundedSemaphore` silently misses it. Low-risk today (2-field parent); switch to `super().__init__(value)` once MI super() resolution is dependable. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `asyncio.BoundedSemaphore`.
- **Support nullable / multi-protocol static-protocol params on `async def`.** `async def f(x: SomeProto | None)` / `async def f(x: ProtoA | ProtoB)` (static protocols) is rejected at codegen (`_protocol_template_parts`, gen_async.py:458) -- only single required static protocols like `Own[Awaitable[T]]` are supported in coro frames. The sync side handles these via `_gen_protocol_arg`; lifting the async restriction needs the coro struct's template-header + frame-field shape to encode the nullable/multi-protocol case, plus the matching emplace-arg coercion (see the pipeline-sharing item above). Feature work, no current demand; the diagnostic is clean so it's not blocking. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `fix-async-emplace-rvalue-dangle`.
- **Group generator-frame-state save/restore in `gen_async.py`.** The generator-body scope contextmanager manually saves/resets/restores ~12 fields (`generator_field_names`, `generator_optional_fields`, `generator_frame_slot_locals`, `generator_borrow_form_loop_vars`, `generator_for_loop_info`, ...) at three separate sites with no mechanical check that all three were updated -- each new frame-scoped field extends the list in three places. Collapse the generator-specific fields into a single `GeneratorFrameState` dataclass with one save/restore pair. (These fields are populated mid-setup by `setup_resumable_frame_locals`, so they stay mutable sets -- not a frozen snapshot; the win is the single save/restore pair, not immutability.) Not blocking; do before the next frame field lands. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the yield-deref narrowing. **Related incomplete-save/restore hazard** (surfaced by /tpy-review of the await-arg field-type-spelling fix): `_resumable_frame_ctx` routes through `setup_body_scope` -> `reset_scope`, which wipes ~30 scope fields (`declared_vars`, `var_types`, `optional_locals`, `ptr_variant_locals`, `slots`, `reassigned_vars`, ...), but the ctx manager only saves/restores ~12 of them. Harmless today because the only build-time entry (`_build_resumable_cfg` wrapping `builder.build()` in the ctx so the await-arg field-type `gen_expr` gets `self`->`__self` / `frame_slot` deref) runs at top level where those fields are empty, and the CFG is cached. But it is not nesting-safe: a future call site that builds a resumable CFG from *inside* an active body-emit scope would silently corrupt the outer scope's narrowing/declared-var state. Fix: make `_resumable_frame_ctx` save/restore the full `reset_scope` field set (the durable root fix; preferred over relocating the build-time entry, which does not remove the build-vs-emit phase mixing anyway).
- **`_is_templated_coro` omits `_fn_template_parts` despite its "single source of truth" docstring (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`).** The predicate decides header-vs-cpp placement for coro/generator structs from `func.type_params`, `_protocol_template_parts`, and the enclosing record's params -- but NOT `_fn_template_parts`, so an `Fn`-only generator (no type/protocol params) returns `False`. Behavior is currently correct: such generators land in the header via another path (verified -- single-module AND cross-module `Fn`-only generators compile/run, nothing leaks to the `.cpp`), so this is a latent inconsistency, not a live defect. The hazard is a future refactor consolidating placement on this predicate would reintroduce a cross-module gap (an `Fn` generator's template body emitted out-of-line in the definer's `.cpp`, un-instantiable by importers). Fix: add `or bool(self._fn_template_parts(func))` once the placement paths are understood/consolidated (verify no snapshot churn -- should be a no-op for current placement). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the Fn-param-in-generator fix.
- **Borrow-form-yield-deref regression guard (BLOCKED on the bare-Optional-yield compile gap).** The yield-deref is gated on `generator_borrow_form_loop_vars` specifically so pointer-repr Optional/Union frame locals are NOT deref'd (a broad `pointer_locals` gate would `(*name)`-strip their None/variant case -- a Critical caught in review). Today the only guard against re-widening that gate is the comment at `tpyc/codegen_cpp/statements.py` `gen_yield_value`; a real regression test (a resumable generator yielding a bare `P | None` local) can't be green because direct `yield opt` hits the pre-existing bare-Optional-yield compile gap (see the `std::expected<std::optional<P>, ...>` narrowing entry in BUGS.md). Add the guard once that gap is fixed. Surfaced by /tpy-review test-coverage.
- **Reference-element exec coverage for generic generator/vararg iteration.** `gen_generic_for` only instantiates the generic generator with a value-type `T` (int) at exec; `varargs_generic_iter_ref` only does pass-through counting (no `args[1:]`). Add: a ref-type `T` call site for `gen_generic_for` (behavioral guard for the borrow-form ref-yield path beyond the snapshot), a `varargs_generic_iter_ref` variant exercising `args[1:]` for a reference-type `T`, and a direct `yield it` on a `pointer_form_unpack_target` (tuple-unpack loop var) to cover that membership of `generator_borrow_form_loop_vars` directly rather than via snapshot. Surfaced by /tpy-review test-coverage.
- **Regression guard for the call-macro `expr_type_hint` clearing.** `_run_call_macro` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`) clears `ctx.expr_type_hint` while analyzing the macro's own args so the slot type can't leak into arg sub-analysis, then restores it for `CallMacroContext.expected_type`. The `call_macro_expected_type` case only passes string-literal args, whose `analyze_expr` is hint-independent (int literals are `IntLiteralType` at analyze time too -- the IntN coercion is later), so the clearing is currently a no-op in every test. A faithful guard needs a *hint-sensitive* arg whose `MacroArg.type` would differ if the hint leaked -- e.g. a nullary generic call whose `T` is pinned by the return hint (`poly(empty())` where `def empty[T]() -> list[T]`), plus a purpose-built reporting macro that emits something observable from `arg.type`. Non-trivial test scaffolding (needs a new reporting macro + a hint-sensitive callee). Surfaced by /tpy-review test-coverage of `feature/call-macro-expected-type`.
- **`@function_macro` test + API coverage gaps.** The spike has no `error_*` cases for its diagnostic paths: unknown function macro (a resolved decorator that isn't a registered `@function_macro`), a macro raising `MacroError` / an unexpected `Exception` (`tpyc/sema/function_macros.py`), `FunctionMacroContext.annotate_local`'s two failure modes (no introducing statement / local already typed), and `replace_expr`'s "node not found in body". Also missing: a regression guard for the parser behavior change (an unknown *resolved* free-function decorator now defers to sema's "Unknown function macro" instead of erroring at parse); a `-> None` function to exercise the `return_type is None` branch the smoke test never hits; `test_macro_loader.py` unit coverage for `MacroRegistry.get_function_macro` / `_is_function_macro` registration; an `annotate_local` target nested inside an `if`/`while`/`for` body (the `_annotate_in` recursion is untested -- all cases have flat bodies); and a `FunctionMacroContext.module_qname` exercise. Separately, `macro_api.py` re-exports `VarDecl`/`Name`/`StrLiteral`/`BoolLiteral` but not an `IntLiteral` alias, so a macro inspecting integer literals must reach for the internal `TpyIntLiteral`, breaking the "macros import only from `tpyc.macro_api`" contract -- add the alias. The frontend function-macro path (lowered `Function.decorators` -> `TpyFunction.pending_macros` -> sema pass-5.5) has no end-to-end test exercising the seam: `tpyc/test_frontend_lower_macros.py` stops at `lower_module` output and the `function_macro_resolve_type` snippet uses the source-decorator path, so the lowered->sema integration is untestable until a frontend actually emits decorated functions -- add a guard when the first such frontend lands. Surfaced by /tpy-review test-coverage of the `@function_macro` spike.
- **Unify `warning`/`error` on the remaining macro contexts.** `_MacroContextBase` (macro_api.py) hosts the shared diagnostics + registry introspection for `CallMacroContext` and `FunctionMacroContext`; `BuilderContext` (anchors at `_call_loc`) and `ClassInfo` still carry duplicated `warning`/`error`. Mechanical follow-up: alias their loc into `_loc` and inherit -- they would also gain `get_field_type`/`get_method_return_type` for free.
- **`lookup_imported_name` / `enum_members` / `lookup_function_signatures` coverage gaps.** (a) `lookup_imported_name` lives on `_MacroContextBase` so it is reachable from `CallMacroContext`/`BuilderContext`, but only the `@function_macro` path is exercised; add a `@call_macro` (or builder) case that resolves a module-visible record/enum by name. (b) `enum_members` is only tested on a module-local plain `Enum`; the imported-enum route (an enum imported from a sibling module) and the `IntEnum` subclass route are untested. (c) `lookup_function_signatures` has the same shape -- on `_MacroContextBase` but only exercised from the `@function_macro` path; add a `@call_macro`/builder case that reads a callee's signatures. (The per-module visibility contract -- a sibling-module type not imported into the host resolves to `None` -- and the `resolve_type_info` dedup are now done.) Surfaced by /tpy-review of `feat-function-macro-lookup-name`.
- **`lookup_function_signatures` param-shape gaps + `Signature.params` typing.** (a) `Signature.params` projects each param to `(name, TypeInfo.from_tpy_type(p.type))`, silently dropping `ParamInfo.keyword_only` / `is_variadic`; no test covers a callee with a keyword-only or `*args` param, so a macro can't tell those shapes apart and the projection could lose them unnoticed -- add a case and decide whether the flags belong on `Signature`. (b) `Signature.params`' element type is `tuple[str, TypeInfo | None]`, but `lookup_function_signatures` always sources non-optional `ParamInfo.type`, so the `None` slot is unreachable from this caller (inherited from `FunctionMacroContext.params`, the parser-phase shape where an unannotated param really is `None`). Decide whether to keep the type uniform against a future method-overload lookup or tighten it for the registry-phase caller. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `feat-function-macro-lookup-params`.
- **Refine vararg lvalue classifier to use `ctx.is_temporary_expr`.** The current ad-hoc include-list is over-permissive on two unreachable edges: `make_obj().field` (rvalue-rooted field access -- `&make_obj().field` would fail), and a user-record subscript whose `__getitem__` returns by value (`&call_returning_value()` would fail). The canonical `ctx.is_temporary_expr` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py:1916`) already handles the subscript case explicitly via its `TpySubscript` arm. Switch the classifier to `if not ctx.is_temporary_expr(arg): &arg else hoist` to absorb those edges. Current code is correct for everything reachable; this is hardening for future cases. Surfaced by /tpy-review safety-model.
- **Residual vararg arg-marking test variants.** Three primary variants are now covered (`method_varargs_nonmutating_ref_arg`, `varargs_generic_nonmutating_ref_arg`, `varargs_loop_var_ref_arg`).
