Lower-priority gaps remaining: mixed individual + `*unpack` args in the same call (currently rejected by sema -- could only be tested as a positive case if the rejection is relaxed); field/subscript source as a vararg arg (`f(self.box, items[0])` -- `_root_name_of_expr` returns the root, so marking would flow to `self` / `items`; works but unguarded).
- **Readonly-vararg test coverage hardening.** New code paths from the readonly-`*args` work lack regression guards (all routed and working, just untested): (a) the value-type const-view converting ctor in `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/varargs.hpp` (value specialization) -- forwarding a mutable value-type vararg into a readonly value-type vararg; (b) the "Cannot unpack into *args: element type ... needs a conversion" diagnostic branch in `tpyc/sema/calls.py` -- confirmed reachable (e.g. unpacking `Span[int32]` into `*args: int64`), not dead, but no test hits it; (c) generic readonly vararg `def f[T](*args: readonly[T])`; (d) method readonly vararg `def m(self, *xs: readonly[Box])`; (e) keyword-only + readonly vararg; (f) empty unpack into a vararg (`xs: list[Box] = []; f(*xs)`). Add `tests/cases/calls/` cases. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the support-star-unpack-varargs branch.
- **Regression guard for `raise <expr>` last-use (blocked).** The liveness fix tracks reads in both `raise Foo(args)` and `raise <expr>` (raise_expr) forms, but only the arg form is tested (`error_raise_read_after_consume`). A clean raise_expr test (`raise make_err(h)` where `make_err` reads a consumed `h`) is blocked by the `Own[<Exception>]` return diagnostic bug in BUGS.md; add the guard once that lands.
- **Type alias re-export through intermediate module.** General TPy limitation surfaced while adding generic-alias tests: `lib_a` defines `type Foo = ...`; `lib_b` does `from lib_a import Foo`; `main` then does `from lib_b import Foo` and fails with `'Foo' not found in module 'lib_b'`. Affects both generic and non-generic type aliases. Root cause: `compiler.py::_extract_decl_exports` iterates `compiled.ast.type_aliases` (parser-output) which only contains locally-declared aliases, not imported ones; re-exporting modules don't add imported aliases to their `ModuleExports.type_aliases`. Records / functions / enums have separate re-export paths that work (see `tests/cases/imports/*_reexport`). The line-less module-level diagnostic shape (`main.py: error: ...`) means today's `# tpyc: error()` annotation can't pin it as a regression guard; once the re-export path is fixed, add a `generic_alias_reexport` happy-path test.
- **`Own[Optional[Tree[T]]]` field/param coverage.** Only the *return* shape is pinned today (`generic_recursive_own_optional_return`, `error_generic_recursive_optional_return_dangle`). No test exercises `Own[Optional[Tree[T]]]` as a record field or a function parameter, so the chosen storage/borrow rep for those positions can shift silently. Add field + param cases (likely under `tests/cases/union/`) to lock the rep. Surfaced by audit of the generic-recursive-alias followups list against tracked items.
- **Unify the recursive-alias-wrapper emit-ordering predicate sites in `generator.py`.** Three coordinated sites in `generator.py` key on `recursive_union_names` + `type_params` + `module.protocols`: (1) the pre-concept loop in `_generate_forward_decls_and_concepts` emits fwd-decls for ALL wrappers (generic template header / non-generic `struct X;`) when `module.protocols`; (2) the before-records loop in `_generate_definitions_and_reexports` emits the same fwd-decls when NOT `module.protocols` (sites 1 and 2 are complementary on the `module.protocols` axis); (3) the post-records type-alias loop emits non-generic wrapper *full definitions* and unconditionally skips generic ones (those emit before records). The split risks predicate drift if `_gen_recursive_union_struct` or the criteria change. Collapse into a single classifier (`GENERIC_RECURSIVE` / `NON_GENERIC_RECURSIVE` / plain) with explicit "fwd-decl before concepts / before records; full def before records (generic) / after records (non-generic)" intent in one place; also consider tightening the pre-concept fwd-decl to only wrappers actually referenced by a protocol signature (records use the precise `protocol_referenced_records` set; wrappers over-approximate). Surfaced by /tpy-review of `fix-recursive-alias-wrapper-gates` (codegen-correctness + architecture-fit).
- **Single-home the per-module codegen render-map resets in `clear_codegen_state()`.** Four maps carry per-codegen-module perspective and must reset on every `CodeGenerator.generate()` pass: `native_cpp_names`, `union_alias_names`, `recursive_alias_cpp_names` (all three reset in `clear_codegen_state()`, `tpyc/typesys.py`) and `local_qualified_cpp_names` (reset inline at `generator.py:236`, immediately above its own populate loop, and unmentioned in `clear_codegen_state`). A reader who takes `clear_codegen_state` as "where per-module maps reset" will add a fifth map there and miss nothing -- but one who copies the `local_qualified` pattern scatters the invariant further. That scattering is exactly how `recursive_alias_cpp_names` came to be un-reset (it rendered a definer's own alias qualified on any second emit of the module). Nothing reads `local_qualified_cpp_names` between `clear_codegen_state()` (`generator.py:173`) and the inline clear, so moving the clear up is behavior-neutral. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion on `fix-recursive-alias-name-leak`.
- **Unify the generic-recursive finalize-coverage sites into one registry-signature walk.** `_finalize_generic_recursive_aliases` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) rewrites `AliasRef -> RecursiveAliasInstanceType` across a hand-maintained list of registration-time signature snapshots: AST function/method/field annotations, then `RecordInfo.init_params`, then record method `FunctionInfo`, then protocol `MethodSignature` (AST + registry). The **same omission recurred three times** while building `fix-recursive-alias-wrapper-gates` -- each missed snapshot category was a distinct reachable bug (ctor args, method return/params, protocol signatures). A per-category list is structurally footgun-shaped: the next signature snapshot added anywhere in sema silently reintroduces the bug class. Replace with a single pass that finalizes every registration-time signature snapshot (ideally driven off one place that enumerates them), so a new snapshot store can't be forgotten. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective on `fix-recursive-alias-wrapper-gates`.
- **`@dynamic` protocol method typed with a *non-generic* recursive union coverage.** The generic-alias cross-module case is now covered (`dyn_recursive_alias_method`). Still untested: an `@dynamic` protocol whose method takes/returns a non-generic recursive union (`Expr`). Probe whether it works before writing the case. (Note: the *same-module* protocol-method-with-recursive-alias emit-ordering failure found while covering the generic case is filed as a compiler bug in `BUGS.md`, not here.) Surfaced by /tpy-review of the W1 + F2 commits (test-coverage).
- **FEATURE_ROADMAP D19 status refresh.** `docs/FEATURE_ROADMAP.md:96` still labels D19 "generic recursive in progress" and the detail section (~line 707) lists generic recursive aliases under "Not yet supported". With qualified/aliased cross-module use landed, the remaining generic-recursive gaps are narrow follow-ups (`isinstance(x, Tree)`, `Tree[list[int32]]` nested-ambiguous, mutual recursion across generic aliases) rather than "in progress" -- refresh the row + detail bullet to reflect substantial completion. Surfaced by /tpy-review (docs-sync); pre-existing, broader than the cross-module diff.
- **Precise generic-recursive-alias render registration (THIR cleanup).** Codegen registers *every* imported user module's generic recursive aliases into `recursive_alias_cpp_names` by qname (`generator.py`, the per-module setup loop), not just the ones an actual use site references -- tracking exact uses would need a finalize-time side-table. Correctness-safe (idempotent, qname-keyed, harmless over-registration), but it is a "consumer re-derives the fact" pattern: the finalize pass already knows which generic-recursive aliases a module instantiates, so the registration could be driven from there instead of a blanket import scan. Tighten when the THIR migration gives finalize a natural place to record per-module wrapper uses. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective (second-opinion flip).
- **Refactor `_resolve_own_source_type` to reuse `substitute_type_params`.** `tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py:_resolve_own_source_type` (Box[P] Phase 3) does manual `dict(zip(...))` + `.get(name)` lookups in two places (function `inferred_type_args` and record-receiver `type_args`) instead of delegating to the established codegen helper `substitute_type_params` (used at line 2461). Not blocking; the duplication will rot as the helper grows. Cleanup: collapse both branches into one call through `substitute_type_params(fi.return_type, subst)` and let the existing helper handle the TypeParamRef walk. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the Box[P] Phase 1-5 work.
- **Box[P] test coverage gaps.** Missing test cases identified during tpy-review: `tests/cases/protocols/dyn_box_generic_protocol` (Box[Container[int32]] where Container[T] is `@dynamic` and generic -- exercises the partial-template `is_dyn_protocol_base` specialization for generic protocols + unique_ptr<Container<int32>> construction); `tests/cases/protocols/dyn_box_return_from_function` (`def make() -> Own[Box[Pet]]: return Box(Dog(...))` -- pins return-site coercion for structural conformers, not just inheritance). The multi-hop inheritance case landed as `dyn_box_nested_dyn_inherit`; Rc[Box[Pet]] now resolves through both the intermediate-local form (`rc_dyn_box_workaround`) and the nested-call form (`rc_box_pet_nested`); the explicit-typearg form is still pinned by `error_rc_dyn_explicit_typearg`.
- **Bounded factory / single-allocation Rc loose ends.**
  - **`Own[U] -> Own[B]` / bare `U -> B` coercion.** Not implemented -- single-cell `Rc.new` only needs `Ptr`. Add only when a real use appears.
  - **Complete the `satisfies_bound` migration + unify the substitute-then-check step.** The inference path (`type_ops.py::infer_type_params_for_function`) and now `validate_type_param_bounds` (explicit-args path, fixed by `fix-generic-bound-substitution`) both substitute the bound by the resolved params before validating via `satisfies_bound` -- but they hand-inline the *same* substitute-then-check logic separately (`type_ops.py:1436` vs `calls.py`'s `validate_type_param_bounds`); collapse them into one shared helper. Remaining sites still call `type_conforms_to_protocol` on the *raw* bound (so a sibling-referencing bound like `[R, T: Proto[R]]` mis-checks there): `calls.py` overload pre-check + the three record-ctor sites, `expressions.py` Fn/Callable inference, `bound_check.py` class-param-shadowed method. Route them through the shared helper. The shared helper must also guard `substitute_type_params`'s `SemanticError("Unknown type parameter")` and rewrap it as a located `ctx.error` (today both fixed call sites are handed a complete subst, so it can't fire, but a future caller with a partial subst would crash unlocated). Correct for protocol bounds (all that reaches them today -- record-level class bounds are still rejected at registration), so the record-ctor sites are only latently affected; verify reachability of `class Stack[R, T: Proto[R]]` in the fix pass. Also guard the bound-collection loop in `codegen_cpp/generator.py` (it adds non-protocol bound names to protocol-include lists -- harmless no-match today) with `is_protocol_type`.

The `None` return is intentional (lets overload resolution try other candidates); a clean fix surfaces bound-miss as a distinct outcome. Pinned by `tests/cases/generics/error_bound_factory_inference` AND `tests/cases/protocols/error_rc_dyn_nonconformer` (both accept either wording via regex).

Existing `for_iterable_bound` uses a concrete type-arg, so substitution is a no-op there. Add when a real use surfaces.

- **Cross-cell `Weak[OtherT]` test coverage.** Current `weak_cycle_breaks` / `weak_outlives_payload` / `weak_basic` all exercise self-referential cells (a `Weak[Node]` field inside `Node`). The new `_RcCell[U]::release_strong` comment claims "a nested `Weak.__del__` triggered by payload destructor sees `weak >= 2`" -- but no test exercises the case where U's destructor fires a `Weak.__del__` on a *different* cell (e.g., `Rc[A]` whose A holds a `Weak[B]`). The cross-cell sequencing should be correct by construction (each cell tracks its own counters), but the gap means a future change to the destruction order would not be caught by the canary suite. Add a focused case under `tests/cases/tplib/`. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` of `feat-single-alloc-rc` (test-coverage specialist).
- **Extend `@dynamic` protocols to allow fields.** Currently `@dynamic` protocols can declare methods but not fields (gap noted in `docs/DYNAMIC_PROTOCOL_DESIGN.md:559-561`). That forced `_RcCellBase` in `lib/tpy/tplib/rc.py` to expose strong/weak counters as virtual methods. The fused-release API on the cell keeps each Rc/Weak operation to at most one vcall, so the perf delta from this is small (~the indirect-call cost on the final cell teardown, plus an icache + vtable-slot reduction from 5 methods to 1). The bigger payoff is shape clarity: a `@dynamic` base with `strong: uint32` + `weak: uint32` fields + a single virtual `release_payload(self) -> bool` matches `std::shared_ptr`'s control-block shape exactly. TODO comment in `lib/tpy/tplib/rc.py` flags the migration site. Also unlocks other polymorphic-cell patterns (any future tagged-union / type-erased control block).
- fix Box/Rc TODOs
- Add generic-holder (`class Holder[U]: shared: Rc[U]`) and Weak-via-downgrade variants of rc_field_default_init -- pin the broadened using-decl invariant.
- Protocol-side parallel handling of `IMPLICIT_AUTO_READONLY_METHODS`. Today `sema/registration.py::register_protocol` applies `IMPLICIT_READONLY_METHODS` to protocol method signatures (so e.g. `Deref[T].__deref__` becomes implicitly `is_readonly=True`), but doesn't parallel-treat `IMPLICIT_AUTO_READONLY_METHODS`. Harmless currently because protocol matching only asks "does the type have a signature with this name/shape" -- the type's dual mutable/const overload pair from method_expansion offers both, and the protocol's single const signature matches the const one. Becomes load-bearing if protocol-driven dispatch is ever extended to pick between the two overloads (e.g., `&p_borrow.__deref__()` resolving to the const overload vs `&p_owned.__deref__()` resolving to the mutable one). Surfaced by the parallel review of the `IMPLICIT_AUTO_READONLY_METHODS` split.
- Strict reachability for module compile + include set (workstream B of the include-propagation fix). Today: `import a` adds `a` to the build set and to consumer hpps regardless of whether anything from `a` is referenced. Goal: a module is built/included iff one of its symbols is reached, with implicit stdlib (tpy, typing, builtins) still always in. Three concerns to keep separate per Codex's review: semantic visibility (sema discovery is import-graph-driven today and changing it breaks `_register_user_module_import`'s "module already in registry" invariant), header/include visibility (already reach-driven post-fix, but currently still seeds from `user_module_imports`), and runtime side effects (`__tpy_init` is emitted from literal `TpyImport` AST nodes in `codegen_cpp/statements.py`, so dropping unused imports changes init semantics). Add `--keep-unused-imports` escape hatch for callers that depend on top-level side effects.
- CallMacroContext API redesign: current API grew ad-hoc from test cases (get_field_type, get_method_return_type, qualified_name, first_param, self_type, etc.). Needs a principled design pass: call site context (function params, method vs free), type introspection (fields, methods, qualified identity), and diagnostics. Consider whether type introspection belongs on TypeInfo (needs registry access) or stays on ctx. Unify get_record_fields (string name, match_args gated) with the TypeInfo-based path. See MACRO_DESIGN.md future extensions.
- `@overload` impl without annotations: arity-variant stubs + impl currently require the impl to carry full annotations. Could infer impl param types by merging stub signatures, or re-analyze the impl body per stub so the stubs become the sole source of type info. Blocked on restructuring sema body analysis; nice-to-have follow-up to the arity-overload work.
- range function/type defined in .py and generic
- range Sequence API: `Range[T]` is iterable but missing CPython's Sequence surface -- `__len__`, `__getitem__(int32)` (O(1) `start + i*step`), slicing (returns another `Range[T]`), `__contains__` (O(1) arithmetic check, currently falls back to linear scan which is wrong-performance for `x in range(10**10)`), `__eq__`, eventually `__reversed__`. Consider folding with "range defined in .py" to avoid adding methods twice. Quick win independent of the rest: add O(1) `__contains__` now.
- Overloads with bodies (no dispatch function): allow `@overload` variants to have bodies directly, removing the need for a separate implementation function. TPy dispatches at compile time so this is straightforward. For CPython compatibility, `tpy.overload` could build a runtime dispatch table (pick by arity/types). Would simplify stdlib modules that mix `@native` and TPy overloads.
- Overloaded generic methods: free functions support a mixed generic/non-generic `@overload` set under one generic impl (each overload emits per its own type params), but methods reject any overloaded-generic outright (`sema/methods.py`: "Overloaded generic methods are not supported", three sites). Lift the method guard to reach parity with free functions -- the codegen path (`_gen_overload_specialized_method`) has the same impl-vs-stub type-param asymmetry the free-fn path resolves, so it needs the same stub-derived template-ness. While there, unify the free-fn emitter's `in_header` flag with the method emitter's `MethodEmitMode="def_hpp"` -- both encode "emit with `inline` because the definition lands in the header". `/tpy-add-feature` (it removes a guard + extends codegen, not a pure bug fix).
- Ptr null-provenance warning: consider warning when accessing through a Ptr with unknown provenance (similar to Optional access warnings). Design question: warn on all unknown-provenance access (noisy for function params) vs only when provenance is lost (was non-null, then reassigned from unknown source)?
- Source-order conflict resolution for module-scope name binding. Today, when a module both imports and locally defines `X`, the local definition always wins regardless of source order (the local `register_*` re-binds the `module_attributes` cell to `defining_module=None` and clears any prior `registry.functions[X]` entry). CPython's "last module-scope binding wins" requires per-statement order tracking: `class X: ...; from c import X` -> imported X wins; `from c import X; class X: ...` -> local X wins. Affects the `source_order_local_then_import` and `source_order_import_then_local` tests deferred from the per-module attribute table refactor (Phase 8). No current user impact (the "local wins" rule is sane and predictable); a Python-faithfulness improvement. Likely lives at the `register_*` sites + bind_imports interaction; needs a per-name source-line ordering map and a final pass that picks the latest binding.
- Reach analysis migration to bindings. Pairs with the strict-reachability entry above. Today's reach seeds from `module.user_module_imports` (the AST-level import statements). Migrating to consume a per-binding `requires_include` flag would let reach be driven by *which symbols are actually referenced*, not by which modules were import-statemented. The flag was trimmed when no reader existed; re-add when this work starts.
- Cycle-peer enum re-export `using` emission. Codegen currently suppresses cycle-peer enum re-exports (`generator.py` re-export emit loop) while cycle-peer record re-exports do emit a `using` through `<peer>_fwd.hpp`. Forward-declared enum classes are declared with their underlying type in `_fwd.hpp`, so the `using` would be safe; the suppression is a holdover from the legacy extraction-ordering accident. Flipping it means a small snapshot delta in `mutual_cycle_with_enum` (and possibly siblings) -- not blocking until a concrete use case forces consumer-side qualified enum-type access through a cycle peer.
- Define decorators as .py functions: readonly/noalloc/nocopy/pure/dynamic/error_return (tpy), native/cpp_template/builtin_type (tpy.extern), overload/override (typing) are currently parser keywords with empty stub files. Want them as real function definitions eventually so the parser doesn't need special handling. Blocked on: functions need type annotations to compile, and decorator signatures have no meaningful type (identity function over any callable).
- ContextManager[T] protocol
- **Consolidate the isinstance lowering-mode flags on `TpyCall` into one kind/enum.** `isinstance` lowering is now selected by several mutually-exclusive booleans/ints on `TpyCall` -- `isinstance_is_protocol`, `isinstance_deref_depth > 0`, `isinstance_type_param`, plus the default variant/typeid/dynamic_cast paths -- each consumed by a new branch at every consuming site (`_emit_call`'s isinstance lowering in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py`, and `_extract_isinstance_facts`). The fact-extraction site already missed one mode (`isinstance_type_param`) and would have emitted `std::get` on a non-variant had sema not independently blocked the trigger -- a single `isinstance_lowering` enum/Literal field would make the per-mode handling exhaustive-by-construction and kill that class of omission. THIR-aligned (one materialized fact, no consumer-side mode re-derivation). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the type-param-isinstance trait lowering; same family as the cpp_shape/`has_field_condition` materialization items above.
- Reject `isinstance(self, ...)` transitively reachable from `__init__` / `__del__` bodies (low priority). The direct case is rejected at sema by the `self-isinstance-dispatch` branch (`tpyc/sema/calls.py::_analyze_isinstance`), but a method called *from* `__init__` that internally does `isinstance(self, Sub)` would compile and run -- and silently diverge from CPython, since the C++ ctor/dtor dynamic-type rule sets `*this`'s dynamic type to the enclosing class for the entire ctor/dtor call graph. **Detection shape:** walk the intra-module call graph during Phase 2 (mutation-propagation fixpoint already does this) flagging methods reachable from any `__init__` or `__del__` body; emit a warning (or error) when one of those methods contains a polymorphic `isinstance(self, ...)`. Cross-module calls are out of scope for the local call graph; document as a known transitive footgun. Low priority -- unusual pattern, sema rejection on the direct case catches the obvious mistakes. Filed during /tpy-review of the `self-isinstance-dispatch` branch.
- The sync function/method signature emitters in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py` (`gen_function_def`, `_gen_literal_specialized_function`, `_gen_overload_specialized_function`, `_gen_method`) each recompute `_get_reassigned_params` + `_get_*_mutated_params` + `_get_*_addr_escapes` and feed them to `decide_param_const` (~491, ~607, open-coded at ~582/~595), where the call site reads the materialized `FunctionInfo.const_borrow_params`. Collapse them onto that fact; `reassigned_params` is the blocker (it is not on `FunctionInfo`), so hoist it there first. Watch out for the method site at `functions.py:1601` -- `_get_method_genuine_mutated_params` feeds the const arm of the signature and `_get_method_mutated_params` the non-const one; they are not interchangeable. This is the SYNC half of the collapse named in "A resumable frame answers" (the frame half deletes `compute_body_const_sets` rather than migrating anything onto it) and in "Param-const verdict: collapse the body-side re-derivation". Surfaced by /tpy-review of `async-scope-reset`.
- Explicit upcast to silence the narrowing warning: currently the "upcast narrows 'Child' to 'Parent'" warning has no escape hatch. Add an explicit cast syntax (e.g. `cast(Parent, child)` or `Parent.upcast(child)`) that acknowledges the intent and suppresses the warning. Needed once users have legitimate "I know this narrows, I only want the Parent view" patterns. Pairs with the warning added for implicit value upcast in `compatibility.py`.
- `@dynamic` on concrete classes: the upcast-narrowing warning and the method-hiding warning both suggest "make '{Parent}' a @dynamic protocol for runtime polymorphism", but `@dynamic` currently applies only to protocols. Users with a concrete base class must refactor it into a `Protocol` first, which the warnings don't acknowledge. Options: (a) allow `@dynamic` on concrete classes (opt-in virtual dispatch, vtable for that hierarchy only); (b) update the warning wording to say "convert '{Parent}' to a @dynamic protocol" and accept the refactor burden. Option (a) is closer to Python semantics but adds vtable overhead to any hierarchy that opts in.
- **Polymorphic + wrappers + isinstance: broad composition landscape.** Investigated 2026-05-25. **Phase 1 landed** (bare `Pet` / `Ptr[Pet]` borrows dispatch `isinstance` via `dynamic_cast`; `Optional[Pet]` at parameter position; fresh `Own[...]` rvalue lent to a borrow param). **Phase 2 landed** (`/tpy-add-feature`, on `dyn-protocol-wrapper-compose`):

Rides `narrowed_types` under a distinct key (`prescan.deref_view_key`); `TpyCall.isinstance_deref_depth` + the access nodes' `deref_narrowed_to` tag the AST; codegen casts the deref payload pointer. A non-owning handle (`Weak[Pet]`) is rejected with an `upgrade()`-first hint.
  - **Adapter-aware `isinstance` for structural conformers** -- `tpy::dyn_adapter_cast<P,U>` (in `dynamic.hpp`) tries both `Adapter`/`RefAdapter` shapes and projects `.inner`; `ProtocolGenerator.dynamic_narrow_cast_rhs` picks `dynamic_cast` (inheritance) vs `dyn_adapter_cast` (structural) for all sources (bare/Ptr/Optional/wrapper). Flipped `error_isinstance_dyn_structural` to positive `isinstance_dyn_structural`.
  - **`Own[Pet]` rvalue param** (inheritance + structural) works; locked in by `own_polymorphic_param`.
  - **`Optional[Pet]` init-only function-local** allowed (lowers to `const Pet*`); rvalue rebind stays rejected (shared slot can't retype). Unified `polymorphic_subclass_into_optional` to cover direct @dynamic inners.

Threading it through is the follow-up; use `Optional[Box[Pet]]`.

The deref-view if-init cast-and-cache landed (`deref_view_init_locals`: the condition + every narrowed access in a branch share one `Sub*`, same shape as the bare/Ptr/Optional sources). Two related cleanups remain, both the same silent-divergence hazard (a fix to one emit block missing the other -- the shape that produced this branch's only Critical):

Reuse the cached local when present -- naturally folds into the same read-path helper.

  - **`list[Box[Pet]]` literal element upcast -- RESOLVED** (`covariant-list-literal-upcast`; test `list/covariant_wrapper_literal`): covariant-generic wrapper elements now upcast to the annotated element type in list literals + comprehensions via `CompatibilityChecker.is_covariant_generic_upcast`, which exempts the per-element anti-slicing guard; value/reference slicing + invariant generics stay rejected. Workaround: `.append(...)`, or annotate elements. Sibling: any covariant-element list literal (`list[Rc[Pet]]`, `list[Ptr[Parent]]`) hits the same guard.

Container-level invariance is unchanged (a whole `dict[str, Box[Dog]]` still can't be passed where `dict[str, Box[Pet]]` is expected). Original analysis kept for history: the `dict` literal entered contextual mode with `expected_value` but the value-unification's else-branch peer-unified the values (`Box[Dog]` vs `Box[Cat]` -> "mixed value types"; single value -> `dict[str, Box[Dog]]` -> container mismatch) instead of checking each against the annotated value type.

Surfaced by /tpy-review of Phase 1.
- **Phase 20 cleanup: `cpp_concept` semantic overloading.** `ProtocolInfo.cpp_concept` now carries two meanings: C++ concept name for `@native`-only structural protocols, and C++ class name for `@native + @dynamic` protocols (Throwable). `get_concept_name` returns `cpp_concept` unconditionally; if Throwable were ever used as a type-param bound (`class Foo[T: Throwable]`), the emitter would put `"::tpy::Throwable"` in a concept-constraint position -- ill-formed C++. Sema doesn't guard against `@dynamic` protocols as bounds today. Cleanup: split into a separate `cpp_class` / `native_base` field on `ProtocolInfo` for the `@native + @dynamic` case so callsites are unambiguous. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the Phase 20 branch; also flagged by Codex during planning.
- **Phase 20 test coverage gap: `raise self.exc` (Box[Throwable] field narrowing) at snippet level.** The pattern is the live production code path in `lib/tpy/asyncio/_executor.py::TaskState[T].__poll__` -- narrow `self.exc` from `Box[Throwable] | None` and rethrow. Exercised transitively by `tests/cases/async/` cases via CancelledError, but no snippet test under `tests/cases/exceptions/` directly exercises the narrowed-Box-field raise shape with a user-defined exception subclass. A dedicated `tests/cases/exceptions/box_throwable_field_raise/` (or equivalent under `tests/cases/async/task_raises_user_exception/`) would lock down dynamic-type preservation through the Task boundary for user exceptions specifically. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the Phase 20 branch.
- **Phase 20 test coverage gap: concrete-subclass borrow rejection.** `tests/cases/exceptions/error_slicing_borrow_into_field/` covers the same-type case (`def store(self, e: BaseException)` storing into a `BaseException | None` field). The concrete-subclass case (`def store(self, e: AppError)` storing into a `BaseException | None` field) exercises a different source-type branch in `_check_polymorphic_slicing` and has no dedicated error test. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the Phase 20 branch.

Remaining: M7 (generic async free funcs + methods), M10 (`Task.cancel()` runnable-mark hook), and M11 (`gather` variadic-positional + `gather_list_settled`) still have no explicit SHIPPED rows though they're all in `docs/ASYNC_PROGRESS.md`. Add SHIPPED rows for M7, M10, M11. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the Phase 20 branch.

Lifting field subjects is tracked under the "isinstance / match subjects are bare-name-only" entry above; a test follows that, not this. Add a case that mutates through a wrapper local and reads back from the field. (2) No test exercises a record *method* with a *non-generic* wrapper param under Part B const-inference (free-function + generic-method are covered; `gen_params_with_protocols` / method path is not) -- include the self-mutating-method-returns-the-param shape (verified working, was BUGS.md residual). (3) A generic-type (`Tree[int32]`) parallel of `wrapper_param_const`. (4) `generic_recursive_return_readonly_error_return` is readonly-masked; a mutable GENERIC-wrapper `@error_return` borrow variant would guard the alias binding with an actual write-through (the borrow-copy bug itself is fixed; the non-generic-wrapper residual is the `_call_returns_cpp_ref` BUGS.md entry). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the wrapper-reference migration.
- **Tuple-form `isinstance` member reordering via `make_union`.** `isinstance(x, (RuntimeError, OSError))` reorders alphabetically before codegen iterates `check_members`, so the emitted dispatch tries `OSError` first then `RuntimeError`. Semantically neutral for single-inheritance hierarchies (any concrete type matches at most one alternative) but observable for multi-inherited types and changes the source-order semantics CPython preserves. Tracked here as a watch-item; not blocking. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` of the v1.5 M2 polymorphic dispatch landing.
- **Auto-readonly inference for never-mutated local-var aliases.** Local-var bindings emit non-const references by default, even when the variable is never written. For polymorphic-isinstance narrowing this propagates non-const back through the cast chain and demotes the source param from `const T*` to `T*`. Reproducer: `def classify(r: Optional[Root]) -> str: if isinstance(r, Sub): narrowed = r; return narrowed.name` -- the `narrowed = r` alias emits `Sub& narrowed = (*__r_ptr);` (non-const), forcing `__r_ptr` to `Sub*`, the `dynamic_cast` to non-const, and the param signature to `Root*` (not `const Root*`). `narrowed` itself is only read, so a mutation-propagation analysis on locals could mark it `const Sub&` and preserve the const-borrow chain. Lives in sema's local-binding analysis; sibling to the existing `@auto_readonly` machinery for methods/fields (which doesn't fire on locals today). Visible as a snapshot delta in `protocol_dynamic_marker` / `protocol_dynamic_optional_isinstance` after adding `narrowed = r  # tpyc: type(Sub)` annotations. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` of the `isinstance-subclass-narrowing` branch. **Also gates `@auto_readonly` accessor alias-read const:** `x = o.b.get(); return x.v` keeps `o` mutable today because the non-const local `x` requires a mutable source (`auto-readonly-usage-clone-selection` marks the receiver mutable when an accessor result is bound to a local, precisely to avoid an ill-formed `Foo& x = const Foo&`). Once locals can bind const, relax that mark so aliased reads also get a const receiver -- the same change unblocks the aliased-read variant of the field-path element-borrow case in BUGS.md.
- **Implicit-readonly stub dependency on `@dynamic` protocol methods.** `BaseException.__str__` satisfies `Throwable.__str__`'s `@readonly` declaration only because `__str__` is in `IMPLICIT_READONLY_METHODS`. Any future `@dynamic` protocol method declared on an `@native` class hierarchy requires either an entry in that list or an explicit `@readonly` on the stub, with no diagnostic if missing. Should be a registration-time sema check that flags mismatch between protocol-method `@readonly` and stub-method readonly status. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` of the Throwable activation.
- `__stream__` / `__write__` dunder: efficient stream-based output for records (avoids allocating a string just to print). Needed for no-alloc logging.

- Finish per-compilation-state-on-Compiler migration: address `_dynamic_attached_qnames` (`tpyc/type_def_registry.py`). The other six globals (`_namespace_map`, `_include_path_map`, `_native_cpp_names`, `_union_alias_names`, `_protocol_modules`, `_return_exception_names`, plus the dynamic slice of `_type_defs` and `_dynamic_created_qnames`) have moved onto `Compiler` and are read via `tpyc/compilation_context.py`'s `ContextVar`. `_dynamic_attached_qnames` stays module-level because it tracks mutations to the SHARED static `_type_defs` entries (e.g. `builtins.list` getting its `RecordInfo` attached at sema time) -- the rollback has to outlive the originating Compiler so the next compilation's startup can clean up. The declared-native-flag latch (`latch_declared_native_flags`, `@native(borrowing_view=..., iter_yields_ref_tuple_proxies=...)` on a builtin stub) writes the same static entries through it too. So do the element facts a native container stub declares: `owns_elements` rides the same flag latch, and `native_members` is latched later, when the stub's record is registered (`latch_native_members`: it needs resolved method signatures), a second path with its own step and reset. The proper fix is to stop writing payloads back into the static registry from sema (so static TypeDefs become genuinely read-only post-`_populate()`); requires reshaping how `attach_dynamic_type_def` handles the static-overlay case. Also unblocks parallel in-process compilation. See `docs/IR_DESIGN.md` for the architectural direction; the conftest autouse fixture (`_TestCompilerContext`) can also be retired once tests stop relying on module-level state. Side cleanup: add a dedicated `tpyc/test_compilation_context.py` covering (a) `require_current_compiler()` raises outside any active context, (b) nested `activate_compiler` restores the outer compiler on exit, (c) an exception thrown inside `with activate_compiler(...)` still restores the prior context. And add a note to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` about the static-vs-dynamic TypeDef split (the rationale is currently inline in `type_def_registry.py` only).
- Function-scope vs module-scope sema unification: `_analyze_top_level` already reuses `FunctionTrackingState` and `deduction.resolve_all()` for module init, so the two paths are mostly the same. The `_ModuleInitSentinel` (in `sema/context.py`) lets code distinguish a real `TpyFunction` from the module-init host. Legitimate uses rely on `TpyFunction`-specific attributes (`.params`, `.return_type`, `.type_params`, `.is_method`, `super()`); but several gates just ask "am I in a function body?" and reject the sentinel by accident -- empty list/dict literals at module scope were two of those (fixed; `is_body_like_scope` helper in `sema/context.py` names the predicate). Remaining suspect: `calls.py::_can_defer_generic_inference` at ~`:3375` reads *"Only in function bodies (resolve_all runs there)"* -- same mistaken rationale, needs a real repro before changing. A broader pass should: (1) audit every `isinstance(current_function, TpyFunction)` in `sema/` (~15 sites) and classify each as legitimate vs accidental; (2) migrate accidental sites to `is_body_like_scope`; (3) consider making `MODULE_INIT_CONTEXT` a real `TpyFunction` with empty params/return/type_params so the sentinel can be retired entirely. Medium effort, independent of other refactors.
- Strict-warning hardening follow-ups (the test suite already runs under the downstream-mirroring flag set; see `STRICT_WARN_FLAGS` in `tpyc/compiler.py`):
  - `-Wshadow` not in the strict set. Record/dataclass constructors emit the idiomatic `T(P p) : p(p) {}` pattern which always shadows. Either rename the ctor parameter (e.g. `T(P p_) : p(p_) {}`, snapshot churn across every record) or document `-Wno-shadow` for downstream tpy-gen TUs (current state -- documented next to STRICT_WARN_FLAGS).
  - **Low-prio:** TPy-level diagnostic for unread local variables. `-Wno-unused-variable` is in the strict set because user TPy code can legitimately write `x = compute()` with no read (Python idiom), and per the "users never see C++ errors" invariant we can't let that surface as a C++ `-Werror`. Adding a sema-level info/warning diagnostic would let the user learn about unused locals in TPy terms while the C++ side stays silent (so the suppression stays). Convention to consider: skip the diagnostic when the var name starts with `_`.
  - Sign-mixed comparison handling: codegen routes `int32 < uint32` and friends through `std::cmp_*` (`expressions.py:_gen_binop`) so the result is mathematically correct without the "promote signed to unsigned" reinterpretation; sema additionally emits a warning so the user knows they're hitting that path; a comparison over a literal-seeded local is judged at the type the local settles to, once its function has been analyzed.
  - **Consolidate async-for `_build_async_for` loop-stack lifetime.** `_build_async_for` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/resumable_cfg.py:740`) appends to `_loop_stack` before one try/finally pair (which only pops `_region_stack`) and pops in a separate try/finally pair around the body build. A `CodeGenError` thrown from the handler-body build between the two would leak the loop ctx for subsequent compilation in the same session. Currently unreachable in practice (the synthesized handler body is a single `TpyBreak` that can't fail given the just-pushed loop ctx), but fragile. Mirror the sync `_build_for`'s single-try pair around the loop stack. Surfaced by /tpy-review of M6.
  - **Elide async-return copy for lvalue sources.** Async-def returns lower uniformly as `T __tpy_async_ret = <expr>; return Poll<T>::ready(std::move(__tpy_async_ret));` (e.g. `tests/cases/async/async_for_break/expected/src/main.cpp:38`, `await_in_for_range`, `asyncio_run_returns_value`). For value types this is free, but for owning non-value return types like `BigInt`, `std::string`, `list[T]`, etc., the assignment from a named source (frame field / local / param) is a real copy at every async return. The temporary local exists so the `std::move` into `Poll::ready` is unconditional. **Fix:** when the return expression is an lvalue at last use (frame field, local, or param), `std::move` directly into `Poll::ready` instead of going through the materialized local; when it's an rvalue (literal, call result), pass it through without the intermediate. Mirrors the sync-return value-categorization that codegen already does. Pre-existing async codegen pattern -- broader than M6 -- but worth tracking since it touches every async function returning a non-value type. Surfaced while reviewing M6 snapshots.
- **Bidir-hint inference follow-ups (post `feat-bidir-hint-inference`).** Surfaced by /tpy-review and /code-review of the shipped feature; none blocking, none worth shipping alone, but worth tracking so they don't rot:
  - **`partial_inferred` Fn-hint poisoning** (`tpyc/sema/calls.py:2923`). Phase-2 of `_infer_arg_types` seeds `partial_inferred` from `seed_subst`. When a non-Fn arg's inferred type disagrees with the seed, `match_type_with_inference` returns False and the seed binding stays. The Fn-arg hint then reflects the seed, not the arg-derived type. Design question: should seed or arg evidence win in the Phase-2 partial_inferred when they disagree?
  - **Wildcard partial-explicit merge semantics** (function-call site `tpyc/sema/calls.py:4247`; record-constructor site `tpyc/sema/calls.py:4571`). Both merges do `for tp, ta in zip(...): if ta is not None: merged_seed[tp] = ta`, so a user-written wildcard at a given position doesn't opt-out of LHS-seed influence. Design question: should `_` mean "infer from args only" (clear seed) or "infer from args + LHS" (current)? Whatever answer wins, apply it at both sites together.
  - **kwargs not iterated by the methods.py seed closure** (`tpyc/sema/methods.py`). The closure iterates only `expr.args` (positional). Kwargs at seed-eligible positions silently miss the contextual hint that the seed would have produced. Pair with the two-phase-Fn alignment work; `_analyze_generic_method_call` should pre-flatten kwargs before the closure (or the closure should consult `expr.kwargs` directly). Same gap in the overload-probe siblings: `_probe_candidate_args` (calls.py, shared by method calls) iterates only the positional args, and `candidate_arg_hints` (type_ops.py) takes only positional `n_args`.
  - **Union not stripped from seed-derived hints.** `post_substitute_hint` now strips Own/Readonly/Ref/Optional, but `UnionType` (e.g. `T | A | None` constructor params with multiple non-None members) still doesn't unwrap. A param `value: T | A` with seed `T=Concrete` propagates a `Union[Concrete, A]` hint that the inner record-ctor / function-call seed match rejects. Needs design: try each Union member against the inner pattern? Pick the matching member? Skip seeding for Union params?
  - **`IntLiteralType` / `FloatLiteralType` filter affects pre-existing function/method seed paths too.** The filter additions live on the shared `_seed_subst` helper, so they apply to `seed_subst_from_return_hint` (function and method-call seeders) as well as the new record-pattern sibling. Pre-this-PR, a function/method call whose return-type match pinned T to `IntLiteralType` would propagate that binding via `seeded_arg_hint` to per-arg seeded hints. Now the filter drops it; per-arg hint falls back to None. Theoretical (no current trigger -- annotations don't carry literal markers), but the behavior shift across two previously-shipped paths is undocumented. Decide intent: keep filtered or restore unfiltered with explicit comment.
  - **Same-name cross-module records can mis-seed in `seed_subst_from_record_pattern`.** `_match_record_with_inference` compares NominalType by simple name, so a hint of `other_module.Box[Pet]` matched against a pattern built from `my_module.Box`'s record can yield a bogus seed binding before the assignment-level cross-module mismatch is reported. Fix: gate the pattern match on `qualified_name()` equality.
  - **kwargs not iterated by the record-ctor seed loop** (`_analyze_record_constructor`, tpyc/sema/calls.py). Parallel to the methods.py kwarg gap above. Pair the fix across both sites (and the overload-probe siblings `_probe_candidate_args` / `candidate_arg_hints`) so the rule is uniform.
  - **Bound check runs after `_apply_dyn_hint_at_position` uplift.** Pre-existing in both function-call and record-ctor paths: bound validation operates on the inferred dict after the @dynamic uplift overwrites T=Concrete with T=Protocol, so `T: Hashable` + non-Hashable Concrete + Hashable LHS Protocol type-checks despite the heap payload failing the bound at runtime. Restructure bound validation to run twice -- once against arg-derived T pre-uplift, once against the uplifted T -- or restrict uplift to bound-respecting positions.
  - **Defer path consumes seeded arg cache.** `_create_pending_generic_instance` re-iterates args via bare `analyze_expr`; any inner record-ctor arg that was seeded by a failed outer call returns its cached seeded type. The pending instance therefore carries arg types influenced by an LHS hint the deferred resolver may never see. Worth a focused reproducer (outer ctor with wildcards leaving a TP unresolvable from args alone but inner ctor's seed pinning a flippable T).
  - **Macro re-entry inherits outer `ctx.expr_type_hint`.** Synthetic constructor calls emitted by class macros run inside the enclosing analyze_expr_with_hint scope, so the seed fires using the outer site's hint even when the macro author intended T to come purely from explicit args. Pre-existing risk in the function-call path; the new record-ctor seed extends the surface. Fix: clear `expr_type_hint` at macro expansion boundaries, or gate the seed on a per-call opt-in.
  - **Test gap: type-mismatch diagnostic shape for nested-generic regressions.** The deleted `error_rc_box_box_pet_nested` was the only test pinning the 'Type mismatch in variable r: expected ... got ...' shape for 3-level chains. Replaced by a conformance-failure test, but a partial-degradation regression (seed silently drops one nesting level) would re-trigger the old shape with nothing catching it. Add a regression test that pins the type-mismatch shape via a setup that bypasses the seed deliberately (e.g. via an opt-out flag if one exists, or via a known limit-case).
  - **Probe / `_infer_pending_container_element` interaction** (`tpyc/sema/calls.py:_probe_candidate_args`, for a method call). `_infer_pending_container_element` pre-analyzes args into the `pre_analyzed_method_args[id(expr)]` side table; the new overload probe then re-analyzes the same args. For inner generic-ctor/call args, the cache short-circuit at `_analyze_record_constructor` / `_analyze_generic_function_call` returns the previously-cached type. `_check_and_coerce_args` pops the pre-analyzed cache but uses probe's `arg_types`, so the element-type inference work done in the pending path is duplicated and the ordering of `info.coerced_element_type` updates becomes path-dependent. Worth a focused reproducer.
  - **Direction-swap admits LHS=Optional[T] vs return=T** (`tpyc/sema/type_ops.py:candidate_arg_hints` non-generic gate). The current swap (LHS-side as param) correctly rejects `return=Optional[Foo]` vs `lhs=Foo`, but symmetrically accepts `lhs=Optional[Foo]` vs `return=Foo` -- a bare-T-returning candidate matches against an Optional-annotated LHS via the matcher's param-side Optional unwrap. Likely intentional (T flows into Optional[T] slot via narrowing), but undocumented. Either tighten (direction-symmetric structural match) or add a code comment.
  - **Routing divergence: calls.py vs methods.py probe inputs** (`_probe_candidate_args`, tpyc/sema/calls.py). The function-call path passes it UNSUBSTITUTED `func_infos`; the method-call path (tpyc/sema/methods.py) passes SUBSTITUTED `resolved_overloads`. `candidate_arg_hints` routes generic-vs-non-generic on `func.type_params`, so a class-generic-only method (e.g. `class Box[T]: def push(self, x: T)`) post-substitution goes through the non-generic branch in methods.py, while the equivalent free function in calls.py would go through the generic branch. Branches are independently correct but the asymmetry isn't documented.
  - **Audit `substitute_method_type_params`'s dropped FunctionInfo fields** (`tpyc/sema/type_ops.py:1554`). The constructor explicitly passes ~24 fields; the FunctionInfo dataclass has ~46. Dropped fields include `is_pure`, `is_inline`, `is_property_getter` / `is_property_setter` / `property_name`, `native_cpp_return_type`, `type_param_defaults`, `is_constructor`, `special_handling`, `builtin_decorator_key`, `owning_type_qname`, `addr_escapes_params`, `direct_mutated_params`, `direct_structural_mutated_params`, `call_edges`, `direct_self_mutated`, `self_mutated`, `is_auto_readonly_mutable_clone`, `inline_body`, `originating_module`, `const_borrow_params`, `deep_const_borrow_params`, `returns_self_borrow`. That last one is VERIFIED to bite, which lifts this from hygiene: a GENERIC context manager's `__enter__` reverts to the default `True`, so `class Wrapper[T]` gets a `__with_ctx_0` manager field its non-generic twin does not, and the manager's `__del__` then runs at enclosing-scope end rather than block end -- a silent CPython divergence (safe direction, no UAF). Some are presumably defaulted on purpose (mutation-tracking state that's per-original-function), but others (`is_pure`, `is_inline`, `inline_body`, `originating_module`) look call-site-relevant. `kwarg_name` was confirmed-and-fixed in `bidir-hint-quick-wins`; the same shape may bite for other fields when a future caller consults them on a substituted method. Audit each field: should it propagate, or is the default correct? Add a comment block explaining the per-field policy so future maintenance doesn't accidentally drop more without justification -- or build the copy as a `dc_replace` of the substituted fields, so a new field propagates unless reset on purpose. RESOLVED for `const_borrow_params` / `deep_const_borrow_params`: never propagate -- they are populated post-sema on the raw fi only; consumers read via `fi.root` (documented at the `typesys.py` field declaration; call sites fixed in `fix-gen-async-dcbp`).
  - **Chokepoint the `fi.root` const-verdict reads -- DONE** (`refactor-dcbp-root-property`, 2026-07-24): `const_borrow_params`/`deep_const_borrow_params` are properties forwarding through `root` over private storage, written via `set_const_borrow_verdict` -- a forgotten `.root` is structurally impossible now. The explicit `.root.`/raw-registry spellings left at existing read sites are harmless no-ops; simplify them opportunistically (e.g. at cutover).
  - **`addr_escapes_params` has no root-reading accessor, unlike its sibling `return_borrows_from`.** The provenance readers of the borrow fact all go through `recorded_return_borrow_sources` (`tpyc/typesys.py`), which reads `fi.root` so two readers of one call site cannot disagree when a synthesized specialization carries a stale copy. `addr_escapes_params` has the same hazard and no accessor: `arg_lend_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) spells `root.addr_escapes_params` by hand, while the const-ABI readers (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/param_const.py`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) read the RAW field. Not a one-liner: adopting a root-reading accessor at the const-ABI sites is an ABI-affecting widening (a substituted fi's empty set would start reading the root's non-empty one), so it needs its own byte-diff rather than riding a refactor. Raised as S13 by the property-read normalization review round 5, 2026-09-18.
  - **Per-candidate trial-and-rollback at the overload probe** (`tpyc/sema/calls.py:_probe_candidate_args`). The current single-LHS-matching gate over-rejects calls where 2+ candidates LHS-match and all of them would accept the user's args via per-candidate hint propagation. Concrete shape: overloads `f(Own[Box[Pet]], str)` and `f(Own[Box[Pet]], Own[Box[Pet]])`, called as `f(Box(Dog()), Box(Dog()))` under `r: Result = ...`. Both returns match; pre-fix B-first ordering succeeded via Adapter wrap, A-first failed -- a real declaration-order-dependent bug. Post-fix consistent rejection (see `error_overload_cross_candidate_hint`). Principled fix is regime-C-style per-candidate trial: each LHS-matching candidate gets a scratch-space analysis under its own hints; the candidate whose scratch result type-checks wins. Today's regime-C path already handles this for Fn-bearing args (2+ Fn-bearing-supplied candidates -> per-candidate trial). Extend to non-Fn LHS-matching candidates. ~100+ lines + analysis-state save/restore.

- **Thread the deep-const verdict into the two remaining mutable-into-const arg renders.** Two call-site renders still spell the MUTABLE tuple form against a now-const factory param, absorbed silently by `std::tuple`'s element converting ctor (compiles, byte-identical on both codegen paths, but inconsistent with the verdict): (1) tuple-LITERAL args (`gen_expr_deref`'s tuple-literal render and THIR's `TpyTupleLiteral` call-arg arm key only on explicit `ReadonlyType`, ignoring `target_const_borrow`/`readonly_target`); (2) OVERLOADED free-call sites read the resolved STUB's empty verdict while the factory reads the implementation's (`overloads[-1]`) -- pinned as-is by a unit that went with the THIR unit suite. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `fix-yield-escape-verdict`.

Diagnostic-text only (the reject fires regardless), so this is a low-priority guard against a future merge-policy change silently flipping which index the error names. Add a 3-element-tuple case (then fresh at idx 0, else fresh at idx 1). Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the consolidation.

Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the tuple borrow-pointer unification.
- **Skip the `tuple_to_storage` wrap for fully VALUE-captured tuple literals at storage destinations.** The wrap sites key on the destination TYPE having a pointer-repr element, so an all-VALUE-captured literal (whose fresh rvalue members already render the storage form) still routes through `tuple_to_storage` -- a runtime identity (the same-shape branch forwards), but one needless move per element plus template noise. Two known sites: `records.py`'s field-init wrap, and the container-literal element path (e.g. `[("a", Node(1))]` in `warn_dict_ctor_copy`'s generated code). Gate additionally on the source literal's elem_capture. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the tuple borrow-pointer unification.
- **[LOW] Emit `copy(lvalue)` as a bare in-place copy when it's a tuple-literal element with a matching slot type.** `(77, copy(b))` lowers `copy(b)` via `_gen_copy_expr` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py:632`) to the prvalue `Box(b)`; as a `std::tuple{...}` element that prvalue binds to the ctor's forwarding-ref `Box&&` and is MOVED into the member -- one extra move vs the bare `(77, b)` form, which copy-constructs the member in place from `const Box&`. Fix: at the tuple-literal element emit site, when the element is `copy(x)` (lvalue/field source) and the slot type equals `x`'s type, emit the bare `x` and let the normal element copy-construct path run (the warning stays suppressed -- it's a sema fact keyed on the `copy()` wrapper, independent of codegen). Saves the move, keeps explicit-copy semantics. **Low value:** the extra move is elided at -O2 for trivial-move types (the common case) and only bites non-trivial-move *copyable* tuple elements (`@nocopy` types don't use `copy()`); it's also a sub-case of the broader "prvalue element into a `std::tuple` literal incurs a move" (`(77, Box(5))` has it too), so the general fix is in-place tuple-element construction, not a `copy()`-specific unwrap. Pairs with the value-captured `tuple_to_storage`-skip item above (that targets the other move in the chain). Surfaced reviewing the per-element-Own rebind test field-store copy.
- **[LOW] Consolidate the per-element-Own walrus collapse across its sema + codegen sites.** The walrus per-element-Own collapse is applied at two sema sites (`_analyze_named_expr`: collapse `resolved`, and override the walrus expression `result_type` to the collapsed type for a pointer-repr tuple) plus one codegen site (`_gen_named_expr`: collapse `value_type` for reassigned targets). For a pointer-repr tuple sema already carries the collapsed type as the walrus result, so the codegen collapse is a no-op there; it is load-bearing only for the exotic Own-of-value-element tuple (`tuple[int32, Own[int32]]`), where sema deliberately returns the uncollapsed raw `value_type` to preserve literal-ness. A clean unification would have sema carry the collapsed form for that edge too so the codegen collapse can be dropped -- but NOT by unconditionally setting `result_type = resolved` (that drops scalar-literal preservation for `(n := 5)`); it needs a tuple-scoped path that collapses without losing the literal types of value elements. Low value (current code is correct; the duplication is a parallel-mechanism smell, not a bug). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the walrus per-element-Own fix.

The `isinstance` second-arg path (`_resolve_isinstance_type`) does its own import-table-first resolution inline with different shape (unconditional import lookup, no collision guard). Removing `__del__` is the clean end-state but NOT a mechanical edit: it drops the codegen-emitted custom move ctor + `__tpy_owned_` guard (the types fall to C++-defaulted move/dtor) and may shift their TPy value/reference classification, so it needs verification that the defaulted member-wise move stays correct (all members -- `Box`/`Rc`/`UninitStorage` -- are correctly movable) and the pass-by classification is unchanged, plus a full suite run. Surfaced by /tpy-review (convention/safety) of the liveness-flag cleanup.

Add a `panic_`/output case that cancels a task parked in `send` on a full channel with a `@nocopy`/`__del__`-tracked payload so a leak or double-drop would surface. Add a `Mutex[@nocopy]` / `unsafe_store` of a `@nocopy` value case (rvalue/last-use move admitted; a still-live-lvalue `set` a hard non-copyable-into-owned-storage error) so the consumption is proven at the type level, and consider hardening `mem_unsafe_store_object` to mutate-after-the-boundary. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `mutex-set-alias`.
- **[thir] The validator's plain-non-value BORROW exemption is unscoped -- key it on a positive marker instead.** `tpyc/thir/validate.py:133-142` exempts a same-form same-type `THIRFormConvert` from the no-op rule whenever the form is BORROW and the result type is plain non-value, because BORROW spells both `T&` and reseatable `T*` for such a type and the node cannot tell the address-of lift from a dead node. Keyed on form + type ALONE, with no per-node marker (unlike `addr_of`, a real field on the arg/ctor nodes), so it exempts ANY such convert anywhere -- the resumable address-of lift it was written for, and equally a genuinely dead one an ordinary body might grow. Harmless today only by accident of lowering: `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:3690-3699` refuses to construct the shape outside resumable-leaf mode, so nothing else reaches the exemption. Fix shape: mint the lift with an explicit flag on `THIRFormConvert` (the `materialize` precedent) and narrow the exemption to nodes carrying it, so the rule reads the DECISION rather than re-deriving it from the shape. Surfaced by the review of the resumable/simple-gen validator wiring.
- **[thir] The validator matches `coercion_name` STRINGS where a structural field belongs.** `tpyc/thir/validate.py:184-201` exempts the coerce form-passthrough check by testing `node.coercion_name in ("async_ret_addr_of", "async_ret_val_or_ptr")` -- the async return slot's borrow/trait lifts, which materialize a pointer or trait-selected prvalue out of any source form while deliberately keeping the SOURCE's type spelling, so the result-type rows structurally cannot see them. Sound today: exactly two sites mint those names and both are pinned. But it pattern-matches a symptom -- a `value_wrap: bool` alongside `wrap` (mirroring how `THIRFormConvert.materialize` carries its own decision) would let the check read the "this wrap materializes a new representation" fact directly, and would not silently miss the third such coercion the moment one is minted under a different name. Surfaced by the review of the resumable/simple-gen validator wiring.
- **[thir] Two lowering fences now reject on a rationale that no longer holds -- ablate them.** `decl.ptr_alias_borrow` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:3690-3699`) and `decl.reseat_param_source` (`:8753-8764`) both refuse the `T&` -> reseatable `T*` alias because the resulting same-form same-type `THIRFormConvert` was the no-op node the validator hard-rejected. That is no longer true: the `ref_to_ptr_lift` exemption added with the resumable/simple-gen wiring lives in the SHARED `_check_node` (`tpyc/thir/validate.py:133-142`), so it admits the shape for every body kind, not just resumable leaves. Neither fence was re-checked after the exemption landed, so both may be blocking bodies that would now validate clean. Cheap probe: delete each fence in turn, re-run the corpus, and read the routed count and any divergence -- a rotted fence is the class this repo has paid for repeatedly. Surfaced by the readiness second opinion on the validator wiring.
- **Callable contract (designed; compatibility gate before coupled implementation).** Design:
  `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md`. A callable's result FORM is read off its
  spelled return by the rule a `def` return obeys (bare reference = borrow,
  `Own[R]` = fresh, type parameter = form-neutral), in `Fn`, `Callable` and
  `def -> R` alike, and erasure into `Callable` does not change it. That half is
  decidable from types and declarations. The PROVENANCE half -- which of the
  caller's places a returned borrow roots in, and what later invalidates it --
  is a requirement on the analysis-only MIR (see the MIR track below); until it
  exists this half stands on a conservative ADMISSION LAYER (A1-A12) that admits
  a borrow-returning binding only when every root is proved an admissible
  argument and rejects everything else with a located error: capture-rooted
  results, stored or returned closures with borrowed environments (`self`
  included), global-rooted borrows, escaping temporary roots, borrow-bearing
  aggregates, unsupported helper compositions, and any call with unknown effects
  under a live loan. Hard errors, not warnings. Closes
  BUGS.md#callable-value-borrow-return-copies-unwarned, and is the prerequisite a
  TPy-source `map` waits on (TODO.md "Builtin combinators in TPy source"; builtin
  `map` stays in C++ until this lands).
  The implementation plan (steps in landing order, files and lines, the five
  independently mergeable steps first) lives in the design document only.
  Its shared-reader checkpoint extracts existing representation decisions only;
  designing permission and contained-borrow analysis remains part of the
  feasibility checkpoint, and the complete semantic result descriptor lands
  with the coupled implementation. A storage representation is not proof that
  its payload contains no borrows.
  The initial checkpoint-3 findings are in
  `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_FEASIBILITY.md`: generic forms are feasible but need a
  new channel, and the proposed admission layer needs substantial provenance /
  effect propagation while rejecting ordinary safe callbacks. Analysis-only MIR
  first was approved on 2026-09-17; `docs/MIR_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` records the scalar
  foundation and remaining increments. The coupled contract remains gated.
  Its "Compatibility gate" first measures programs newly rejected by A1-A12,
  separating actual lifetime violations from safe false positives, including
  scalar callbacks under ordinary loans. Contract-first is conditional on an
  explicit decision that this compatibility cost is acceptable. If the admission
  layer needs substantial new flow analysis or rejects common safe callback
  idioms, reconsider sequencing and bring analysis-only MIR forward.

  **Incomplete subtotal: ~49 engineer-days, not a release estimate** (the
  contract-half rows of the
  implementation dry run's table: P0.1 1, P0.2 2, P0.3 4, classifier 4, runtime
  traits 1.5, reader unification 3, `borrows=` / `element_of=` 3, conversion legality 7,
  codegen/THIR 8, rejects 6, stubs 2.5, tests+docs 7). That EXCLUDES the four
  dataflow steps of the original 79-day estimate -- places and summaries,
  environment loans, effects, and the provenance half of the lambda stamp, 30
  days between them -- which move to the MIR track; the admission layer is a
  conservative subset of them whose cost is not in that table.

  Later slices, additive on this half: **D1** the hedged owning-slot obligation
  with a FORM dimension (lifts the neutral-into-owning-slot reject AND the
  open-type-parameter over-reject, closes the callable leg of
  BUGS.md#generic-own-slot-borrow-call-unwarned); **D2** the consuming fold
  `Fn[[Own[U], T], Own[U]]` with a Python-compatible `reduce` designed
  SEPARATELY (BUGS.md#reduce-accumulator-copied stays open until then). **D3**
  (stored-`Callable` capture lifetimes) and **D4** (a neutral result at a `yield`,
  callable loans across a frame) are provenance work and live under the MIR
  track. Out of scope either way: method / constructor / staticmethod references
  at a callable slot (current errors stand); `Optional` and union callable results
  (BUGS.md#fn-contract-reference-optional-result); form-carrying `U`, rejected
  outright (it would make `list[U]` a container of borrows -- recorded in the
  design's Alternatives list, so it needs no entry of its own). NOT deferrals: a
  C++ `T&&` stub result (a stub-author obligation, which `borrows=` / `element_of=` makes
  unspellable anyway) and the three rollout preconditions above.
- **[diagnostics] A located envelope for unexpected internal errors.** The CLI catch-all (`tpyc/cli.py`, `except Exception` -> `Internal error: {e}`) prints `str(e)`, which for a `KeyError` is only the key -- `Internal error: 't'` gave a user no file, line or construct (the finally first-bind crash, fixed 2026-09-28). Print the exception type, and wrap an unexpected exception at the per-body lowering attempt (`_thir_resumable_attempt` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`, and the `_thir_callables` loop in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py` for plain functions) into a located "internal compiler error in function 'f' (line N)". Separate branch.

## Deferred to THIR/MIR & workload-gated
- **[design][POSTPONED 2026-09-16 -- its own branch, not mixed into a queue batch] Call-graph fact propagation: make the unit the import COMPONENT, then generalize the lattice.** Two points, one shape. (1) `propagate_mutation_facts` (`tpyc/sema/mutation_propagation.py`) runs per MODULE: it topologically sorts the module's call graph and resolves call-graph cycles with a monotone fixpoint, but an imported callee whose module has not yet run Phase 2 has `mutated_params is None` and takes the conservative leg (every flowing parameter marked mutated). Across an import cycle that is safe but order-dependent: two modules `a`/`b` importing each other, each forwarding a parameter to the other's read-only function, render `int32_t via_a(const Rec& r)` in the member analyzed second and `int32_t via_b(Rec& r)` in the member analyzed first (probed 2026-09-16), so a signature in a cycle depends on which member the driver analyzes first -- the external-C++-surface instability the project rules against elsewhere. Fix shape: the compiler already condenses import cycles into components (the `_cycle_peers` / forward-declaration machinery); analyze bodies for every member of a component, run ONE propagation over the union of their functions (external callees outside the component stay ground truth, so the acyclic corpus is byte-identical by construction), then `_sync_inferred_const` per member. A sequencing change in `Compiler._analyze_bodies` / `_finalize_workspace` plus a two-module cycle case; medium priority (cycle members are rare under the v1 gate), cheap. (2) The next call-graph fact is visible in the filed gaps: 'a borrow of parameter i escapes through the return' (what `ptr-readonly-dest-counts-as-write`, `readonly-borrow-of-temporary-receiver` and the dangling-return checks approximate locally from declared signatures). It has the mutation fact's shape exactly: a per-function summary on `FunctionInfo`, a monotone join, evaluation in call-graph order with cycles by fixpoint, external summaries as ground truth. Today every transitive fact has its own bespoke walk (mutation = the one call-graph lattice; owning-copy verdicts = a workspace-wide edge discharge; borrow/lifetime checks = local, deferred until mutation facts settle; global rebinding = per-module phase one; header reach = a type-graph closure). Do not build the abstraction before the second instance exists (measure before designing); do implement (1) as the evaluation order the abstraction will need, and fold the lattice abstraction in when the escape fact is built -- the natural first citizen of the MIR direction in `docs/IR_DESIGN.md`. Raised by the user reviewing batch 5 ("what if there is a cycle import"; "is the const deduction common with other fact inference, e.g. lifetimes"). ANALYSIS DONE 2026-09-16 (batch 6, measured on 9813ac2a26), design ready to implement: `Compiler._compute_compile_order` (`tpyc/compiler.py` ~1594-1696) already runs Tarjan over the import graph and then FLATTENS the components away, members in alphabetical order -- the only cycle break in sema that is an order rather than a fixpoint; 31 of 6171 cases contain an import cycle (lib/tpy none), 5 of them order-dependent (four on `const X&` vs `X&`, one on which module reports an error). Four probes: (a) the signature split above; (b) readonly inference has the same split one level out (`via_a() const` only in the second-analyzed member); (c) a SILENT use-after-move -- filed HIGH as `BUGS.md#cycle-peer-borrow-fact-read-as-stub`, because `return_borrows_from` is read during body sema where `None` means both "opaque stub" and "not analyzed yet" and `_seed_pending_borrow_fact_fis` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py` ~913-944) seeds per module; (d) ACCEPTANCE depends on order: `b.f(x: readonly[a.A])` calling an inferred-readonly method compiles when `a` runs first and errors when `b` does, because body sema reads `is_readonly` as an admission gate. (d) shapes the design: the component pass must be TWO-PHASE -- the provisional per-member `run_phase2_fixpoint` exactly as today (but not clearing `call_edges`), then a final pass over the component union; monotone (the provisional pass marks a superset of the mutated sets, so the final pass only shrinks them and only grants `is_readonly`), skipped for singleton components so the acyclic corpus is byte-identical by construction. Steps: A keep `compile_components` beside `compile_order` and derive the latter (partition components, not modules, at the implicit-stdlib step, assert none straddles); B the component loop with `_run_component_phase2` (one snapshot moves: `imports/mutual_cycle_with_dataclass` `add_pair(Pair&)` -> `const Pair&`, verified correct; new cases for both members const and for probe (d) so the provisional pass can never be dropped); C the borrow seed per component (zero churn measured over the 31 cyclic and 120 random cases; a case with the list mutated after the boundary); D replace the workspace SCAN in `_propagate_mutation_facts` (`analyzer.py` ~1055-1104; 89 calls x 15,473 FunctionInfo visits = 1.38M visits for 6.6 ms of work, 205 ms = 7.1% of the stdlib_render front end, O(modules x workspace)) with a per-analyzer index of the FIs it wrote facts onto; E (later, with the escape fact) the lattice: Tarjan over the CALL graph plus a worklist; today's `_resolve_cycle` round-robin is quadratic in the call-SCC (rings of 50/100/200 functions: 2.3/9.7/36.3 ms), the corpus's largest set is 11 FIs. Citizens of the lattice: the three mutation facts, `return_borrows_from` as a real summary, the transitive twin of `addr_escapes_params`; NOT citizens: `is_readonly`/const verdicts (decisions, anti-monotone), frame Send/Sync (a greatest fixed point over the await graph), own-copy discharge (a reachability closure), the deferred checks. A second home found on the way: signature emission (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py` ~491, ~607, and open-coded at ~582/~595) re-derives the const verdict from raw `mutated_params` while call-site lowering reads the materialized `const_borrow_params`; it also carries `reassigned_params`, which is not on `FunctionInfo` -- hoist that first, then collapse the emitter (its own unit, spelled out in "The sync function/method signature emitters"). One home for all of it: `FunctionInfo.const_borrow_params` stays the verdict and every other spelling becomes a projection of it -- see "A resumable frame answers" for the frame half. Risks recorded: copied `mutated_params` on substituted FIs keep provisional (conservative) values; frame Send/Sync across a cycle is unmeasured.
- **[design][filed 2026-10-01, not for now] `pure` is two facts under one word: a declared binding fact on stubs and a checkable contract on TPy bodies.** On a stub (423 `@pure` sites in `lib/tpy`, every one on a `@native` / `@cpp_template` binding) it declares C++ the compiler cannot see, exactly like the `transient=True` kwarg; it should become `@native(..., pure=True)` / `@cpp_template(..., pure=True)` the same way (parser reads the kwarg into the existing `FunctionInfo.is_pure`; nothing downstream changes; mechanical). On a TPy-bodied function (seven uses, all in `tests/cases`: `readonly/pure_decorator` and siblings) it is TRUSTED today -- `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` says so -- and sema acts on it: the borrow-argument conflict check (`sema/calls.py`), the loop-frame write checks (`sema/loop_frames.py`) and `receiver_calls.call_mutates_receiver` treat a `@pure` callee as mutating nothing, so `@pure def f(p: Point)` assigning `p.x` hides a real conflict; only the `self` half is enforced, through the readonly implication. The fix is to VERIFY it rather than trust it: purity is the call-graph lattice above with three more bits (writes no global, calls only pure or transient callees, no I/O through an unmarked native), inferred per function, and `@pure` on a body becomes an assertion sema checks and errors on (the ESCAPE_ANALYSIS_DESIGN section 7 "Phase 2"). Keep the two spellings apart on purpose: a kwarg says "declared about the binding", a decorator says "check my body". Order: the stub kwarg first (small, own branch), the enforced contract when the lattice lands. User decided 2026-10-01 to file rather than change now.

  loans in progress: declared storage members and user method summaries

  alongside; B6 advisory
  checker and authority transition. Lifetime/loan bugs tagged `deferred: MIR`
  in BUGS.md wait on it. The history below records the landed increments.
  **Snippet-test verdicts** (landed): every case that reaches codegen runs
  MIR (`tpyc/mir/collect.py`: one `MIRBodyVerdict` per body, the record

  `mir_summary(...)` pin a body's verdict on its `def` line. Deferred: a
  source-site selector for `conflict` (today the regex names only the
  conflict kind, not where it happens), and stable reason codes in place of

  in the ladder: `certified` is the THIR storage certificate, so the
  owned-root certificate (`certify_storage_origins`, CERTIFIED for every

  (`tpyc/mir/test_owned_leaves.py`); and `covered` passes whatever the
  storage state is (NO_PROOF_REQUIRED, NO_FACTS, NOT_COVERED alike), so a

  either a `mir_storage(state)` item or `covered` refusing the gap states.
  The verdict family pins the OUTCOME per body. The line-level fact family
  (landed with the views half) pins MIR's facts per statement line:
  `mir_owned(x)`, `mir_borrowed(x)`, `mir_borrows(x, a|b)`, `mir_copy(x)`

  Deferred: a loan-end item and a conflict site selector; a condensed

  **B2 second half, views as places** (landed): view holders, owned-leaf
  fields with member-init and call writes, str conflicts as existing kinds

  **B3 first half, containers as places** (landed): owned and borrowed

  **B3 second half, declared storage members** (landed): native types

  A user `@native` container lowers from the same two facts where THIR

  **B3 second half, user method summaries** (landed): a plain record's

  **B3 second half, retained loans** (next, needs `/tpy-add-feature`; unit
  order in `docs/MIR_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` "Breadth-first order"):
  - `scalar_leaves._ELEMENT_DISPATCH_DUNDERS` (the comparison and hash
    dunders that make a record element non-plain) stays a name list: no
    RecordInfo fact exists and one would relocate the list.
  - `SpanIter` declares no element member (its `__iter__` returns `Self`
    and is not readonly), so a `SpanIter` holder stays unmodeled.
  - A keyed container without a value member (a user stub `Index[T]` with
    `__getitem__(self, key: T) -> T`) refuses ("unsupported keyed
    container", at the subscript): MIR models a keyed subscript only
    beside a value member.
  - `mutates="structure"` is not spellable: it is what an undeclared
    mutating method means, and on a view receiver the view rule would
    override it. Add the spelling when a stub needs to say it explicitly.
  - A `borrowing_view=True` stub whose `__iter__` / `__getitem__`
    declarations disagree (two readonly `__iter__` overloads yielding

    the reason and the view arm latches no members, so MIR refuses the
    type. `elements=True` raises on the same declarations. Raising for
    views too is a new diagnostic that could reject a view stub compiling

  - A `varargs` parameter is a view holder like a `Span` parameter. Its
    body lowers when the declared element is the one sema settles on: a

    body. A body that only READS an unannotated element (`*items: Box`,
    `*xs: int32`, even `len(items)`) does not: sema infers the parameter
    `varargs[readonly[T]]` and types the name in the body `varargs[T]`, so
    MIR refuses ("container name type mismatch"); the fix is one type for
    both in sema. The pack a call site builds (`f(1, 2, 3)`) is not modeled
    either ("call needs resolved ordinary callee"); when it is, a callee
    write published as `param[elements]` must expand to each packed
