  - View FIELDS refuse as "record holds a borrow": storing a view in a
    record is a retention effect, reading one needs the field's loan.
  - Inherited records, what the model leaves out
    (`docs/MIR_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` "Inherited records" has the rules):
    - `super().m()` / `Base.m(self)` inside a subclass body refuse ("call
      needs resolved ordinary callee"): the call is a THIRCall whose
      receiver is implicit in its C++ spelling (`this->A::m()`). MIR needs
      the call to carry its receiver (`self`, bound at `A`) and the
      declaring record's callee, a THIR change of its own.
    - One field lookup: `TypeRegistry.declaring_record` (THIR's, returns the
      declaring record, no generic substitution) and sema's

      bases are in MIR's slice.

      predicates are asked from the validator and from MIR, under the
      active compiler) and the generic-base refusal reads `type_args` off
      the raw MRO entries, which the registry walk drops.
    - Layouts from a layout index, not the constructor definition index:
      MIR fetches a derived record's layout from `MIRDefinitions.records`,
      so an inherited-field read of a subclass whose `__init__` fails to
      verify (a body effect, an expression initializer) refuses with the
      constructor's reason although the layout is a type fact THIR
      publishes without any constructor (`THIRRecordLayout`). A layout
      index keyed by record type, filled from every `record_layout`,
      would decouple the two; the constructor index then answers only
      constructs.
    - Derived-to-base outside call arguments: a local alias (`b: Base = s`),
      an Optional or union payload (`cur: Base | None = s`), a container

    - Inherited constructors beyond one struct base with no own fields and
      no own special members: a multi-base `pass` class (the other bases

      refuses. Both need the definitions chain to compose a default-
      constructed base and default member inits.
    - Generic bases (`Sub(Base[int32])`): the eligibility

    - Records with an exception or a native ancestor stay refused by the

  - Inline-record getter results and nested records: `return self.inner`

    from inside a record is no return origin yet ("summary unsupported

    its layout is the subclass's, inherited fields included.
  - A `Span` over a field as a return origin (`return self.items[0:]` at

    a region under the field, which the return grammar does not spell.
  - Accessor FunctionInfos skip const inference and
    `populate_const_borrow_params` (sema pops them from the method table

    so MIR agrees with the emitted C++; the gap is in sema.
  - Record and container setter parameters: a record setter parameter
    expands to `Own[R]` and refuses as a free function's `Own[R]`

  - Receiver access from the lowered receiver: `THIRMethodCall.receiver_access`

  - Methods with no callee: consuming, generic, inherited, static and class
    methods, `@error_return` methods, and every method of an owner that

  - `--dump-mir` and the snippet harness analyse only the modules under the
    entry point's directory, so a method of a record from a library module
    has no summary there ("call needs finalized known summary"; probed with

  - "The body a callable runs" has two channels: a free function's
    `FunctionInfo.declaration`, and for a method the per-compilation table

    back to the declared write facts and no diagnostic moves. One field

  - An explicit `@readonly` callable returning its record PARAMETER

  - Callers blocked on an OPAQUE method summary (44 sampled bodies), by the
    method's reason: a nested call with no known summary, "stub protocol
    argument is not a builtin leaf", a record whose constructor refuses,
    "summary storage or value shape", "unsupported statement".
  - Recursive and mutually recursive callables have no summary (B5; timing by
    cost and return, decided 2026-10-03): the workspace marks every identity
    still pending after the leaf-first schedule OPAQUE ("recursive or
    recursion-dependent call"), and each caller refuses. The shape when it
    comes: strongly connected components over the call graph the workspace
    already builds; a component is summarized by iteration from the bottom
    (no writes, no returns, `normal_return_only`) until nothing changes --
    the lattice is monotone and bounded by the declared types -- and any
    member that cannot summarize makes the whole component OPAQUE. Low
    return today: one opaque method summary in the sample is recursive
    (`Counter.countdown`); the blockers behind the other 43 are the
    callee's own body or its record's constructor.

  - Nested container elements beyond one hop ("unsupported native

    `BUGS.md#mutating-callee-non-name-arg-unchecked` and the original
    `list[list[str]]` witness of the loop-variable element view (sema's one
    view rule now copies the inferred element; the explicit `StrView` face
    is the containers case's `last_row`).
  - `extend` takes an `Iterable[...]` protocol parameter and refuses
    ("stub declares no contract"); `xs += ys` (a `THIRInplaceContainerOp`)
    and slice assignment are statements and refuse as "unsupported
    statement"; call-duration
    loans (`xs.extend(xs)`, `BUGS.md#list-self-extend-aliases`,

  - Iterating or unpacking `d.items()` (tuple elements, with the tuple
    unit); `in` (`THIRMembership`) as an `[elements]` read.
  - Return origins of container parameters: a Span or element result
    rooted in `param[elements]` summarizes as the whole parameter (an
    empty-path `MIRReturnOrigin`, which the caller projects into the
    argument's elements); filed with the alias-basis precision item below.
    Origins into a record parameter's field keep their path.
  - Sibling-element precision: element identity is not tracked, so
    `xs[i] = v` / `d[k] = v` under a live iterator over the same container

  - Protocol `for` over user iterators and generators, comprehensions and

  - `bytearray` (a reference type) and tuple / Optional / union elements.
  - The record-element rule (plain: no custom copy / move / destructor, no

  - A container returned by reference from a RECORD parameter
    (`items_of(b)` returning `b.items`) has a known summary, but no caller

  - A record element write through a Span is a THIR reject
    (`setitem.family`), so its conflict is pinned over hand-built MIR only.
  - Sema records the resolved builtin `__setitem__` overload on the

    parse node). THIR lowering re-resolves it by exact parameter type

    refuses ("element write needs a stub contract").
  - Rows for everyday refusals: `self.items = []` in a method as an
    own-site replacement of a container field ("container field
    replacement is unsupported"); `p = Point(1); ps.append(p)` as a copy of
    owned storage into the container ("unsupported record argument"); a
    literal or a parameter at an `Own[list[T]]` argument (`take([1, 2])`,

  - One view-holder path: the Span holder (`span_local` / `span_value` /
    `span_rvalue`) beside `view_local` / `view_value` / `view_rvalue`,

  **B2 follow-ups** (sliced out or found while landing it):
  - Owned leaves inside tuple / Optional / union members; owned-leaf global
    writes (admitting them replaces the immortal-handle model of a global
    with a place that has invalidation events; module init is not
    lowered); `String` in-place methods beyond `+=` and `THIRMethodCall`s
    on an owned leaf; f-strings.
  - Stepped slices refuse ("stepped slice"): fresh owned and allocating,
    but `MIROp` takes one or two operands.
  - A reassigned explicit view parameter (`v: StrView; v = w`) refuses
    ("reassigned view parameter"): reseating a VALUE-passed loan.
  - Structured return origins (B5): a view result rooted in a global or a
    static literal lowers but its summary is opaque ("view result origin
    outside the parameters"), since `summary.returns` holds parameters only.
  - The private-write summary rule is implemented but invisible: a body
    with local record storage stays OPAQUE ("summary storage or value
    shape").
  - View-producing if-expressions refuse as "unsupported owned-leaf
    expression"; a view returned by a method stub (`v: StrView =
    s.strip()`) refuses as "unsupported view source" (a user method's view
    result rooted in a parameter lowers as a free function's does).
  - Owned-leaf fields still refuse: constructor-argument temporaries
    outside a declaration, `readonly[str]` fields, BORROW-form field reads;
    a lent holder overlapping the call's own field write
    (`rename(r, r.name)`) is not checked (the holder is dead after it).
  - A view or str bound in an `if` arm is hoisted by THIR and refuses as
    "missing or inconsistent hoisted binding facts" (plain owned-leaf
    hoists too).
  - `THIRCoerce.conversion_refusal` keys "the result is a new value" on
    the render's `wrap` template; the declared fact is
    `Coercion.builds_fresh_value`, which `fixed_int_to_bigint`,
    `int_type_param_to_bigint` and `char_to_str` do not set although their
    renders build one. Sema's value_category and prescan read that flag,
    so setting it is its own unit, expected zero-churn (a churn makes it a
    decision); then the certificate reads
    the rule, not the render.
  - `int32(a)` and the other fixed-int constructors resolve to the generic
    `__init__[T]` overload, whose parameters still hold `T`, so no
    `THIRStubCallee` is published for them; a C-linkage native call
    (rendered through `callee_cpp`) refuses as "unsupported metadata:
    stub_callee". Both need a decided stub-callee shape, not a wider gate.
  - Summaries: private record storage keeps a
    summary opaque (only private owned-leaf storage is admitted); a by-value
    copy of a global into an `Own[T]` parameter refuses because THIR
    produces it as a named argument temporary; a stub result that could
    borrow a scalar bound to a protocol parameter refuses.

    checks void separately, but the function should say STORAGE or refuse.

    changes the answer for `StrView` mid-test (`tpyc/mir/test_stub_calls.py`
    computes the verdict inside its fixture, `tpyc/mir/test_views.py` and
    `tpyc/mir/test_fields.py` re-latch in theirs); the holdout's removal
    fixes it.
  - Sema accepts every comparison it cannot resolve to a dunder and leaves
    the verdict to C++ (`sema/expressions.py`, the comparison arm); THIR's
    reject gate refuses unlike builtin pairs, so nothing is silent, but the
    acceptance should be sema's.
  - Precision: distinct external roots are assumed to alias, so every
    two-field setter (`ssl.SSLContext.load_cert_chain`) gets a
    `replacement` conflict; the body cannot tell, only a caller can. Design
    (B5/B6): the conflict record carries its alias BASIS (same root: the
    body wrote the storage it views, certain; two external roots: possible),
    an advisory checker reports only certain ones in the body, and a
    possible one becomes a summary PRECONDITION ("parameter `s` must not
    view field `name` of parameter `r`") the caller discharges from its
    argument origins -- `f(r, r.name[3:])` violates it, `f(r, "x")`
    satisfies it, an unknown origin passes the obligation up -- the mirror
    of `summary.returns`. The true positive this keeps is
    `BUGS.md#param-view-of-replaced-field`; sema today never considers the
    aliasing and compiles it silently.
  - `--dump-mir` prints no section for the return-escapes analysis.

    family path is one rule, so each is a cheap section when a bytes shape

    bytes field read and write.

  THIR has landed and is the
  sema->codegen boundary; MIR has not. The FIRST stage worth building is
  analysis-only -- no optimization passes, no MIR-backed C++ emission -- and it
  needs six provisions: stable place identities (locals, temporaries, captures,
  qualified globals, fields, derefs, summarized container elements); explicit
  operations (alias, borrow, copy, move, rebind, closure construction, call,
  return, escape into a field or container); a CFG preserving evaluation order
  including short-circuits, back edges and exceptional cleanup; liveness plus loan
  propagation that follows every holder; summary and effect application at call
  sites, named callback-forwarding calls included; and obligations discharged per
  instantiation. It subsumes the `BorrowTracker` loan table and its flow-fact
  snapshots, alias/root propagation, the AST lifetime analysis, and the element /
  iterator / view / pointer invalidation checks. Several entries in this section
  are waiting on it; the one with a written specification is:
  - **Callable provenance (requirements on the analysis-only MIR).**
    `docs/CALLABLE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMENTS.md` -- the FIRST consumer, and the only
    one stated as acceptance criteria rather than as a wish. Rules 9-23, 28-29 and
    33-36 of the callable design (environment loans, `self` as a view over the
    receiver, symbolic compositional summaries with OPAQUE recursion, argument
    loans, global and temporary roots, and place-granular mutation effects with
    their conflict matrix), each with the minimal programs it must admit and the
    ones it must reject. Lifts the admission-layer rejects of
    `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md` one at a time -- the capture accessor, the
    widget-in-constructor idiom, the observer, helper composition beyond one hop,
    global-rooted borrows -- and closes
    BUGS.md#readonly-method-global-write-under-live-borrow (a live silent
    use-after-free through two gates). Carries D3 (stored-`Callable` capture lifetimes) and D4 (a
    neutral result at a `yield`, callable loans across a frame). Two constraints on
    the checker it lands in: these verdicts are hard ERRORS even in the default
    advisory mode, and the conflict rule is invalidation, not exclusivity -- two
    shared loans on one place coexist, matching TPy's permissive aliasing.
- **[MIR] Consuming-method field moves outside `return`.** In a consuming
  method (`self: Own[Self]`) a read of `self.<field>` moves the field out only
  inside a `return` of the method itself (not of a nested def) that is not in
  a `for`, `try` or `with` body, in a method that is neither a generator nor
  `async`, when the returned expression reads that field once, does not use
  `self` whole (method call, property, `super()`), holds no lambda,
  comprehension or walrus, and every other name in it is a local or parameter
  of a number, `bool`, `char` or enum type, or a module-level function or
  class (`StatementAnalyzer._consuming_return_move_fields`, tagged as
  `TpyFieldAccess.consuming_move`). Every other read is a borrow that copies
  and warns at an owning slot, or errors for a `@nocopy` field -- so
  `x = take((self.a, self.b)); return x` copies where moving would be sound.
  A `return` is also not the last code the method runs: its locals are
  destroyed after the return value is built, and a destructor can read the
  moved field (a local generator's `finally`, a `__del__` holding a `Ptr`
  into `self`). The stopgap therefore blocks the move whenever any name the
  method binds anywhere, or any parameter it owns or rebinds, is not a
  number, `bool`, `char`, enum, `str` or `bytes`
  (`_method_teardown_cannot_read_field`) -- a list local keeps the field
  borrowed too. MIR's cleanup and exceptional-flow modelling (W3 of
  `docs/MIR_M3_COMPLETION_PLAN.md`) is what lets those destructors be
  proven not to observe the moved field.
  The precise question is whether any live holder still depends on the
  field's storage after the read: MIR M3's holder/loan propagation plus
  liveness answers it, and should replace the stopgap. A sema-only attempt
  (place-keyed liveness plus a type-based "does anything else point into this
  field" gate) leaked a new shape each round over 15 rounds; it is on the
  unmerged branch `tuple-own-followups` (tip 8830df3093) for reference. In
  case that branch is gone: it moved a field at its liveness-proven last read
  unless an observer could still reach it -- a live borrow-tracker loan or
  borrow chain placed on the field or on `self` whole, or a live holder whose
  type could reach the field's storage (a pointer's pointee, a polymorphic
  class or an open `T` counting as reaching) -- and each round found a holder
  shape the type test did not see.
  Acceptance shapes for the MIR version -- a `@nocopy` field moved outside a
  `return` and never read again must flip from today's error to a quiet move
  (a copyable one from a warned copy to a move), at every owning position:
  `r = take((self.a, self.b)); return r` (an `Own` tuple member),
  `o.t = self.a; return o.t.n` (a field store) and
  `r = take1(self.a); return r` (an `Own[T]` parameter; that spelling also
  needs `BUGS.md#consuming-field-last-use-sink-rejects`'s lowering row). The
  shape that must KEEP its error is `tests/cases/tuple/
  error_consuming_field_nocopy_outside_return`: the field is read again after
  the move, and a `@nocopy` value has no copy to fall back on.
- **Converge the method-RECEIVER model: AST slot convention -> THIR's typed local (post-cutover).** The AST models a method's receiver as a positional CONVENTION, not a parameter: `_parse_method` validates the first arg's name (`self`, or `cls` for a classmethod) and `continue`s it, so it never enters `params`; its annotation rides an out-of-band `self_annotation` channel consumed by `sema.method_expansion`. THIR already models it the way one would design it fresh -- `params_set["self"] = self_type`, `Local("self")` in the place model, and `@readonly` expressed as `const_locals.add("self")` (a property of the LOCAL, not a flag on the method). The mismatch shows up as code: `Base.method(self, ...)` has to build a synthetic `TpyMethodCall` with `obj=self_arg` and self dropped from the args, purely to translate between the two shapes. Converging the AST onto THIR's model would touch every `params` consumer (arity diagnostics, overload resolution, kwargs mapping, defaults, the C++ param-list emit -- where `self` is `this`, not an argument, so the special case MOVES rather than disappearing, `macro_api.MethodInfo`, protocol signature matching), which is why it belongs AFTER the THIR cutover: one boundary to change instead of two. Would also give a polymorphic `cls` (`type[Self]`) a uniform home as a phantom param 0. Surfaced designing `@classmethod` v1.

- **[porting gap] One THIR site still spells "already a pointer?" as bare
  `name in lc.pointers` at a RENDER decision, and must switch to
  `_already_pointer_source` if its arm is ever widened.** The walrus
  borrow-alias (`expr.walrus`), plus the residual `lc.pointers` disjunct in
  the optional-ptr `'pass'` render arm. The walrus is not a defect: it
  rejects a `Ptr[T]` source STRUCTURALLY, because `PtrType.is_value_type()`
  is True so the borrow-alias arm's `is_plain_nonvalue` gate is unreachable.
  The optional-ptr CALL-ARG half is PORTED: `_optional_ptr_arg_face` now
  carries an explicit `PtrType` arm returning `'pass'` (it no longer rejects
  by type inequality), and its old boundary pin was converted to a routing
  pin, `test_ptr_at_optional_ptr_call_arg_routes_bare`. The hazard on the
  walrus is that widening it without switching the spelling silently
  reintroduces the `T**` lift, and neither the ratchet (a fallback emits
  byte-identical AST) nor the byte-diff (nothing routes the shape) catches it.
  Two adjacent shapes that are NOT in this set:
  the ternary borrow-tuple element has no THIR spelling at all -- it is an
  unported AST arm (`_borrow_ptr_form_value`'s `TpyIfExpr` branch), so
  whoever ports it writes the predicate fresh and should reach for the
  helper; and the generic-tuple `TypeParamRef` guard's `lc.pointers` test is
  an ADMISSION guard, not a render decision, so widening it there would only
  cost routing (a byte-identical fallback), never correctness.
  Full rule in THIR_EMIT_INVENTORY.md's third hard finding.

- **`cpp_shape` redesign (THIR-aligned, post-IR-migration).** TPy types currently decide their C++ boundary form (value / borrow / pointer / storage) through three uncoordinated predicates -- `is_value_type()`, `needs_wrapper()`, `uses_pointer_repr()` -- plus 5+ consumer sites that spell `is_value_type() or needs_wrapper()` disjunctions, plus per-site specialcases (`functions.py:557-568` for wrapper unions, the `RefType.to_cpp_return` qualifier delegation, the `_gen_array_literal` ReadonlyType peel, `OptionalType.uses_pointer_repr`'s force-pointer-repr flag). Every new type-shape concept (recursive-alias wrappers, future variant-form unions, MIR places) re-discovers the decomposition and adds another consumer-site disjunction. The /tpy-review medium pass on `generic-type-aliases` flagged this as the underlying altitude issue. Right shape: a single `cpp_shape` property per `TpyType` (VALUE / BORROW / POINTER / STORAGE) that consumers ask once; lowering methods (`to_cpp_param`, `to_cpp_return`, `to_cpp_storage`) read it and emit. Qualifier types (`ReadonlyType`, `OptionalType`, `RefType`, `OwnType`) compute their shape from their inner uniformly. Codegen never spells the disjunction. Touches typesys.py + sema (the auto-Ref insertion sites must refuse VALUE-shape inners) + every codegen consumer. **Deferred to THIR/MIR migration** -- exactly the kind of refactor THIR is designed to host (per CLAUDE.md's perf section: "THIR is explicitly designed as the natural cache boundary"). Surfaced by the iterative bug-fix passes on `generic-type-aliases` (the recurring "consumer site missed wrapper-aware predicate" pattern is what this redesign eliminates).
  - **Attempted standalone 2026-06 (branch `cpp-shape-redesign`), then the classifier was REVERTED -- the premise didn't hold.** A 3-way `ReprKind {VALUE,BORROW,POINTER}` classifier (design via /tpy-add-feature + Codex review) was built and most consumer reroutes were undone in review: the global-storage sites ask a *storage* axis (where `force_pointer_repr` Optional-of-value diverges from the boundary axis), not the boundary form; and the remaining look-alike predicates (`not is_value_type() and not isinstance(x, (OwnType, TypeParamRef))` etc., ~6 sites) turned out to be **distinct context-specific decisions** (return-Own-wrapping, slot-mutability, has-ref-elements, capture-mode, vararg-is-ref), not one drifted boundary-form predicate. With only one trivial consumer left and no real unification to enable, the classifier was a half-used abstraction and was removed. **Lesson: the "~38 disjunctions" repeatedly dissolved on inspection -- mostly storage-axis, multi-axis (repr+ownership), single-predicate, or structural unwraps; there is little genuine boundary-form duplication to unify.** The full contextual `cpp_form(type, context)` end-state (Codex's sketch) remains THIR's job (`lower.py`); no near-term driver justifies building it on the AST first.
  - **Genuine wins kept from that branch (independent of the classifier):** (1) the wrapper-union return special case was dissolved by making `UnionType.to_cpp_return`/`to_cpp_return_const` wrapper-aware (the `recursive-union-ref-return` merge settled this on the Family C convention -- wrapper returns `X&`/`const X&` by reference, and functions.`_return_type_cpp` no longer special-cases wrappers; the standalone `cpp-shape-redesign` branch's by-value variant was overridden); (2) the motivating tuple-local fresh-member dangle (`t = (i, Box(i)); yield t`) is now **diagnosed** via a per-local dataflow fact `owns_fresh_tuple_member_vars` (sema/context + flow_facts UNION merge + init_tracker; set at the tuple-literal assignment, rejected at the yield/return boundary, pointing at the `Own[T]` element escape) -- NOT via the classifier. Only the *fresh*-member face is fixed; the *durable*-member face (tuple local holding a reference-type member is storage-form and silently COPIES it -- CPython divergence, plus return-build-fail and loop garbage) is a distinct pre-existing codegen bug, now one MED entry in BUGS.md, needing `/tpy-fix-bug`. **Effort 2 follow-ups (deferred, non-blocking):** the UNION branch-merge conservatively over-rejects a mixed `if/else` fresh/safe tuple assign (escape is `Own[...]`); no `tuple_local_own_member_return` happy case yet (settle the return-ctor gap first).
- **Param-const verdict: collapse the body-side re-derivation onto the materialized fact.** `decide_param_const`'s per-param const verdict is now materialized as the single `FunctionInfo.const_borrow_params` set (`populate_const_borrow_params`, post-Phase-2) and read by the call site, resumable factory field, and union signature. But `compute_body_const_sets` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`) still *re-derives* name-keyed `(const_ref, deep)` sets by re-calling `decide_param_const` -- it needs body-local, name-keyed, `reassigned_params`-aware facts the index-keyed FI verdict doesn't carry. Kept in lockstep only by both paths calling the same `decide_param_const`; will silently drift if either grows a rule the other lacks. Also `param_const._is_ptr_variant_union` hand-copies `CodeGenContext.is_ptr_variant_union` (justified -- no Compiler ctx at Phase-2 time -- but a duplicate predicate). The emit-window analysis has since settled the home: `FunctionInfo.const_borrow_params` stays the verdict, the frame-layout pass owns its projection and `compute_body_const_sets` is DELETED rather than generalized (see "A resumable frame answers"), which leaves the sync signature emitter's re-derivation as the only sibling -- it needs `reassigned_params` hoisted onto `FunctionInfo` first. THIR-aligned final form: a single per-param ABI descriptor (the `ParamABI` Codex sketched) consumed by the signature emitter, body, call site, and frame field, so there's one code path, not one fact read by N sites plus a parallel body derivation. Fits with the `cpp_shape` redesign above. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `fix-readonly-union-param-const`.
- **Tag the resolved constructor `RecordInfo` on `TpyCall` instead of re-deriving it in codegen.** The cross-module-identity fix left codegen's record-constructor path (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py`) re-resolving the record from the expr's sema-assigned type (`get_record_for_type(get_expr_type(expr))`) to override the short-name `get_record(func_name)` for same-name cross-module collisions. Sema already resolves the authoritative record in `_analyze_record_constructor` / `_set_record_constructor_info` -- it should stamp the `RecordInfo` (or its qname) on the node so codegen reads it directly, eliminating the consumer-side re-derivation (the THIR node-fact pattern CLAUDE.md flags). The qualified-call path (`_gen_method_call`, `expr.user_module_call is not None`) is a second instance of the same re-derivation: `fix-qualified-ctor-import-shadow` made it probe `find_record_by_qname` / `fi.originating_module` at emit time to recover the authoritative module; sema should stamp `defining_module` on the `TpyMethodCall` node (like `user_module_call` already is). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of `fix-cross-module-type-identity` and `fix-qualified-ctor-import-shadow`.
- **`mark_param_mutated`'s `through_field` field-path climb -> MIR place projection.** The `through_field=True` path (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) strips one dot off a storage key via `_storage_root` (`o.items` -> `o`) to attribute a genuine through-reference write back to the owning param. It's a second string-split climb alongside `effective_storage_through_borrows`, exactly the BorrowTracker string-key shape CLAUDE.md says should be expressed as a `Place::Field` projection traversal under the MIR place/loan model. Works today; fold into the place-model migration. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of `auto-readonly-usage-clone-selection`.
- **`return_borrows_from` receiver-borrow fact: make it precise (does-borrow), audit-enforced -- not a capability heuristic.** Bodyless native/`@cpp_template` stubs get no body-derived borrow facts, so registration (`tpyc/sema/registration.py`) stamps `return_borrows_from={-1}` ("result borrows the receiver") for any such stub whose return passes `signature_may_return_borrow` (`tpyc/sema/type_ops.py`). That predicate is a *capability* check ("could this type carry a borrow") -- true for `str`, views, tuples, generics, and any non-value reference -- so it OVER-stamps owned-returning stubs (`str.upper -> str`, etc.) with a *literally false* "borrows self" fact. Inert today only because all three consumers (`is_dangling_return`, `_register_call_result_borrow`, the auto-move gate) re-filter on the *binding's* storage form, so the false fact never acts. The hazard is a future consumer that treats `return_borrows_from` as authoritative -- the MIR/THIR loan generator most of all -- producing phantom loans of the receiver. **Principle (from the co-brainstorm): the stored fact should mean "does borrow," not "might, unless a later filter disproves it"; the signature heuristic should be a coverage GUARDRAIL, not the source of truth.** Design (synthesis of two brainstorm passes): (1) split the predicate -- keep `signature_may_return_borrow` as the broad capability check, add a precise `call_declares_return_borrow` that becomes `return_borrows_from`; (2) auto-stamp only the unambiguous cases (borrowing view return -> borrows receiver; `Own`/void/value/owned-`str`/owned-`bytes` -> fresh, no stamp); (3) for the ambiguous middle (non-value reference / tuple / generic returns: `dict.get`, `list[i]`, `setdefault`, ...) REQUIRE an explicit contract -- `@native(borrows=("self",))` (the landed declaration, docs/NATIVE_INTEROP.md; rejected on methods today, so admitting it there comes first) or a new `@returns_fresh` opt-out -- and an audit at registration that FAILS the `lib/tpy` stub tests if a bodyless ambiguous stub declares neither. That gives the can't-forget property without polluting the fact with false positives, and mirrors the `@readonly`/`auto_readonly` duality (inference where a body exists; declared contract at the bodyless library boundary). **Context:** branch `fix-view-lifetime-tracking` removed the redundant `@borrows_self` decorator (master's heuristic already covered every stub it was on), accepting the heuristic's inert imprecision until this lands. Best done WITH the MIR loan model (the consumer that makes precision pay off); independently buildable but not worth the churn before then. Surfaced by the /co-brainstorm on the view-lifetime fix.
- **Consolidate the three view-source provenance predicates into one classifier.** `_view_source_is_temporary` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`, new), `is_dangling_return` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`), and `is_view_compatible_source` (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`) each walk the same expression tree to answer a provenance question, and the first two re-implement view-constructor detection and `return_borrows_from` traversal independently -- when a new node kind or `fi` attribute is added, all three need lockstep updates (the method-call-arm `return_borrows_from` gap filed in BUGS.md Safety is exactly this drift). They differ only in the boundary policy: `is_dangling_return` treats a local name/field as DANGLING (function-return scope), while `_view_source_is_temporary` treats it as STABLE (same-scope binding). Right shape: one stateless `view_source_provenance(expr)` classifier parameterized by the stable-vs-dangling policy (or returning a provenance category the callers map to their policy), so the walk and the view-ctor/`return_borrows_from`/walrus/ternary recursion live once. This is the provenance classifier the IR migration's place/loan model wants; folds with the `return_borrows_from` precision item above. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, safety-model) of the view-lifetime fix.
- **Phase 20 endpoint design (Stage 4c) -- captured, not planned.** Phase 20 shipped Stages 1, 2 (ABI + sema rules + invariant tests), 3 (`raise <expr>` desugar with fresh-construction peephole keeping idiomatic `throw X(args)`), 4a-b (`what()` auto-emit + runtime `raise_X(msg)` helpers replacing the `raise<E>` template), and 5 (slicing-site sema rejection + asyncio `TaskState[T]` / `Future[T]` migration to `Box[Throwable] | None`). The headline BUGS.md slicing bug is closed: mechanism fixed, stdlib workaround removed, new occurrences rejected at compile time. **Stage 4c is design-captured-but-not-planned**: it adds no user-facing behavior (the mechanism is already shipping), and the design walls below give it a poor cost/benefit ratio against current needs. The right trigger to revisit is a concrete future feature that *needs* exception classes to be TPy-defined -- e.g. `@dataclass` on user exception classes, a macro that introspects the exception hierarchy, or some other capability the macro can't accommodate. Until that emerges, the `TPY_THROWABLE_VIRTUALS` macro is small (~20 lines), stable, and approximately zero maintenance.

  **What 4c would complete:** move the 17 exception classes (`BaseException`, `Exception`, `ValueError`, ..., `CancelledError`) from `core.hpp` / `async.hpp` to pure TPy code in `lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_exceptions.py`. Drop `TPY_THROWABLE_VIRTUALS` (auto-emit covers all Throwable subclasses now). Replace the inline `raise_X(msg)` helpers in `core.hpp` with forward declarations in `throwable.hpp` + definitions in a new `lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_raise.py`. Rewrite the ~40 format-using runtime call sites to bake `std::format(...)` inline (the linker-resolved helpers take `std::string_view` only).

  **Design walls (why this is more than a mechanical move):**

  1. **StopIteration tier-coupling.** StopIteration is a value-type `ReturnException` marker used by the iterator protocol (`std::expected<T, StopIteration>`) in 15+ runtime headers that construct `StopIteration{}` by value. Forward decl is insufficient -- needs a complete C++ type at runtime-header parse time. Forces either special-casing StopIteration as `@native` (with the awkward consequence of dropping `Exception` inheritance, breaking the "StopIteration is an Exception" relationship), or introducing a runtime stand-in marker type with a sema/codegen bridge at the user-visible boundary.
  2. **Method `...` body restriction on non-native classes.** Sema rejects `def clone(self) -> Own[Throwable]: ...` on regular classes with "only allowed on @native classes". After dropping `@native` from `_exceptions.py`, the Throwable protocol's clone/__raise__/what methods need a sema-visibility declaration on BaseException for conformance checking, but the C++ implementations come from the codegen auto-emit -- the stub body is intentionally synthetic. A name-based carve-out for `("clone", "__raise__", "what")` works but smells like the wrong layer; the right design is a "compiler-synthesized method" category with explicit AST attestation.
  3. **BaseException auto-emit symmetry.** Today `_needs_throwable_auto_emit` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/records.py` excludes `builtins.BaseException` (the historical macro handled it). After 4c that exclusion needs to flip (auto-emit fires uniformly including the root). Small change, interacts with item 2.

  **Cost:** ~2-3 days focused work + ~100 snapshot regenerations. The headline downside is that 4c's payoff is purely architectural -- if it never lands, nothing breaks.
- **State-aware destruction for `frame_slot<T>`, drop the runtime alive bool.** `tpy::frame_slot<T>` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/frame_slot.hpp`) currently carries a runtime `alive_` bool that the helper's destructor checks before running `~T()`. The bool is redundant: codegen already knows which frame fields are live at each suspension point. Replace with: (a) liveness analysis emitting an alive-set per `__state` value; (b) the generator/coro struct's destructor switches on `__state` and calls `slot.destroy()` on each live slot; (c) `frame_slot::~frame_slot()` becomes a no-op (caller-driven). Saves one byte + one branch per slot and makes "uninitialized until source-level write" a fully compile-time invariant. Care points: exception thrown mid-suspension must destroy the partial frame correctly (catch path needs the throwing state's alive-set); interaction with pointer-form (`T*`) slots and synthetic optional slots stays consistent. Defer until a workload needs the cycles.
- **Pack `__cancel_pending` into `__state`'s high bit on coro frames.** Every async-def coro struct emits parallel `int32_t __state` + `bool __cancel_pending` fields (see e.g. `tests/cases/async/asyncio_cancel_unblocks_future_wait/expected/include/main.hpp`). With alignment this is 4-8 bytes per frame the bool effectively costs. The bit-packing alternative: states never exceed a few dozen so the int32_t has 25+ free high bits; encode cancel as `__state |= CANCEL_BIT` on cancel, mask via `__state & STATE_MASK` on dispatch in the resumable switch. Codegen sites: `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py` (field emit + every state transition + every cancel-check). Cost: every dispatch needs the mask, every state write needs `& ~CANCEL_BIT` somewhere. If multi-threaded async ever lands the read/write would need atomic ordering (today both are plain single-threaded writes, ordering is implicit). Single-byte saving per frame is small in absolute terms but cumulative across long-running programs with many tasks. Touches every async-def expected snapshot in the test corpus -- defer until a workload demands the cycles, or until a broader resumable-frame refactor lands.
- **Heap-allocated slots for `Optional[Polymorphic]` locals with rvalue rebinds.** Local declarations of `Optional[Polymorphic] = ValErr(...)` work for the init-only case (codegen types the slot at the rvalue's actual class type so `&slot` upcasts), but the rebind path raises a clean `CodeGenError` because the shared rebind slot is typed at the polymorphic base and would slice. Phase 20 (above) rejects this shape at sema entirely, pointing users at `Box[Throwable]` for owned polymorphic locals. This entry is preserved as the *alternative* direction (transparent `std::unique_ptr<Base>` slot, one heap allocation per rebind, no source-level change required) -- not planned unless Phase 20's explicit-Box ergonomics turn out to be too heavy in practice. Lives in `_gen_pointer_local_init` and `_gen_pointer_local_rebind` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/statements.py`.
- **Multi-protocol-diamond const-merge in `_get_dynamic_override_info`.** Current behavior is first-wins (most-derived MRO ancestor's protocol decides const-ness for a given method name). In a diamond where two sibling `@dynamic` protocols declare the same method with conflicting `is_readonly`, the first-visited one wins and the override emitted by the concrete record may silently fail to override the sibling's virtual slot (the sibling's pure virtual stays abstract, derived class stays abstract). Latent today -- no stdlib or test exercises this shape. Fix when a real reproducer surfaces; the right resolution is probably to reject the conflicting-const declaration at registration time, not to silently pick one.
- Per-slot const inference for tuple borrow params. Today `decide_param_const` is per-param all-or-nothing: if any tuple slot is mutated, all slots stay non-const. Per-slot precision (`tuple[mut_slot, readonly_slot]` -> `const tuple<T*, const T*>&`) requires extending `mutated_params: frozenset[int]` to a slot-aware map (`frozenset[tuple[int, int]]` of (param_index, slot_index)?) plus matching propagation in `mutation_propagation.py` and tracking through `_analyze_tuple_unpack`'s borrow edges. Codegen already supports per-slot const through `TupleType._element_to_cpp_param(t, const)`. Worth doing once a real user case emerges where the per-tuple coarseness forces awkward signature splits; defer until then.
- Unify `TypeDef.cpp_formatter` and `@native` / `_native_cpp_names`. They're two implementations of "how to render this type in C++ when the Python name isn't the answer": `cpp_formatter` handles builtins (parameterized: `list[T]` -> `std::vector<T>`), `_native_cpp_names` is populated per-compilation in `codegen_cpp/generator.py::generate` with four kinds of entries: (1) `@native` records with `native_name` -- static per-qname; (2) nested types (`Outer.Inner` -> `Outer::Inner`) -- static per-qname; (3) **cross-module canonical qualification** -- `ArrayList` in one module's view resolves to `::tpystd::tplib::array_list::ArrayList`, but the resolved path depends on the compiling module's import graph (facade routing, etc.), so this is **per-compilation, not per-qname**; (4) builtin stub records (`TextIO` -> `tpy::TextFile`). Cases 1, 2, 4 could move to `TypeDef.cpp_formatter`; case 3 cannot because `TypeDef` is keyed by qname and the answer depends on compilation context. A proper unification requires first splitting `_native_cpp_names` into "static per-qname" and "dynamic per-compilation" tables, then migrating only the static part. Naturally pairs with the per-compilation-state-onto-Compiler refactor below, since both case 3 and the Compiler-instance move require the same "which module am I compiling right now" context plumbing. Also blocked on `@cpp_template` composition for parameterized native records. Defer until the Compiler-instance refactor lands.
- Explicit variant-alternative construction at recursive-union value sites. Codegen currently emits `return 42;` / `return 3.14;` / `return "hi";` and relies on the wrapper struct's forwarding constructor + `std::variant`'s overload resolution to land on the right alternative. Sema already classified the source's TpyType (after the int->float coercion fix), but that decision isn't transmitted to C++ -- it gets re-derived from the literal's C++ type. Fragile: a future variant-member addition or reordering can silently shift selection (same class as the int->float regression, one layer down). Cleanup: thread the resolved alternative through codegen and emit explicit construction at every recursive-union value site -- function returns, list/dict element initializers, field assignments. Forms to consider: `return ::tpy::BigInt(42);` (typed temp; works because the wrapper's template ctor accepts BigInt unambiguously), or `return V{std::in_place_type<::tpy::BigInt>, 42};` (most transparent, no overload-resolution dependency). Skip the wrap when the literal is already typed correctly (`3.14` is `double`; `"hi"` is `string_view`/`string`). Scope is wide: every value-into-recursive-union site, not just returns. Defer until a real bug forces it; current behavior happens to be correct for our existing tests after sema's natural-member fix.

## Frontend-plugin v1 follow-ups
Surfaced by the v1-shipped review; none block existing functionality
but each is a real architectural / hygiene gap worth fixing before a
second concrete plugin lands.
- Plugin-emitted `StarImport` is fully wired through `frontend_ir/` and `compiler._expand_star_imports_for_module`, but `docs/FRONTEND_PLUGIN_DESIGN.md` "Imports (v1)" explicitly says plugin-emitted modules may NOT use star imports. The Pascal frontend relies on it for `uses` clauses, so the doc is the side that's wrong -- either update the spec to allow star imports under the constraints actually in force, or carve out a narrower form.
- `tpyc/compiler.py:32` imports `FrontendDiagnosticCategory` and uses it nowhere; `_discover_via_plugin` strips `FrontendDiagnostic.diagnostic` immediately, so the category-aware banner path in `FrontendDiagnostic.format()` is permanently unreachable. Either route plugin diagnostics through `FrontendDiagnostic.format()` (preserving category) or remove the unused machinery.
- `get_module_name` is implemented twice with identical logic: as a standalone function in `tpyc/cli.py:179` (consumed by conftest) and as a static method on `ModuleResolver` (consumed by the compiler). The two will drift. Fix: have `cli.get_module_name` delegate to `ModuleResolver.get_module_name`.
- `_all_plugin_entry_extensions` uses `lru_cache(maxsize=1)` while the sibling `discover_cases` uses `@functools.cache`. Both are no-arg caches; pick one decorator and use it consistently.
- `_frontend_registry_for(src_file)` derives the case dir as `src_file.parent.parent` without asserting the immediate parent is `src/`. Fragile implicit contract. Fix: assert (or document) the layout.
- `lib_dirs` ordering between CLI (`_run_cli` slots plugin libs at `len(lib_dirs) - 1` so the final order is `user_libs + plugin_libs + stdlib`) and conftest (`extra_lib_dirs + DEFAULT_LIB_DIRS`, no user-libs channel) is asserted by mirroring rather than shared logic. The next CLI ordering tweak (e.g. adding env-var lib dirs) will silently drift from the test harness. Fix: extract `compose_lib_dirs(user_libs, plugin_libs, stdlib_dir, no_stdlib)` in `tpyc/cli.py` and call it from both sites.
- `Record.base` -> `TpyRecord.bases` lowering (`tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py:_lower_record`) has only unit coverage of the lowered shape (`tpyc/test_frontend_lower_records.py`); nothing exercises the full pipeline (lowering -> sema registration -> inherited field/method resolution -> codegen). No frontend plugin emits `Record(base=...)` yet, so the integration regression guard for the original "inherited members unresolved" bug can't be added until one does. Add an end-to-end case when the first plugin emits a subclass. (Note: a fixing commit message claimed an end-to-end record-inheritance case exercises this; no such case exists -- the claim is unsubstantiated.) Surfaced by `/tpy-review` test-coverage.
- `Decorator` -> native lowering (`tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py:_route_decorators`, `BUILTIN_LOWERING(tpy.native)`) has only unit coverage of the lowered shape (`tpyc/test_frontend_lower_macros.py` -- native fields on `TpyFunction`/`TpyRecord`, registry/target/conflict errors, `macro_data`); nothing exercises the full pipeline (lowering -> sema -> codegen -> C++ link/run). No in-tree frontend plugin emits a native decl yet, and a full native-interop case needs a C++ companion + include/link directives. Add an end-to-end case when the first plugin emits native -- a downstream plugin's native-binding cases are the intended integration guard. (Same deferral shape as the `Record.base` note above.) The `macro_data` channel (`FrontendModule.macro_data` -> `TpyModule.macro_data` -> `FunctionMacroContext.module_data`) likewise has only unit coverage until that plugin lands.
- `Call` kwargs -> `TpyMethodCall.kwargs` lowering for an attribute (method) callee (`tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py:_lower_expr`) has only unit coverage of the lowered shape (`tpyc/test_frontend_lower_method_kwargs.py`); nothing exercises the full pipeline (lowering -> sema kwarg binding). The original bug was sema reporting "too few arguments" because kwargs were dropped, but the unit test stops at the lowering boundary and can't reach sema. No frontend plugin emits `obj.method(key=value)` yet, so the sema-level regression guard can't be added until one does. Add an end-to-end case when the first plugin emits a method call with keyword args. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` test-coverage.
- `BUILTIN_LOWERING` dispatch in `_route_decorators` (`tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py`) hard-codes `if dec.name != "tpy.native"` in parallel to the registry that is supposed to own routing. Adding a second `BUILTIN_LOWERING` entry to `CORE_DECORATORS` requires editing both `decorators.py` and `lower.py`. Unify the dispatch (e.g. a per-entry lowering handler keyed off `DecoratorEntry`) when the second builtin decorator lands. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` architecture-fit.
- `Conditional` -> `TpyIfExpr` lowering (`tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py:_lower_expr`) has only unit coverage of the lowered shape (`tpyc/test_frontend_lower_conditional.py`); nothing exercises the full pipeline (lowering -> sema -> codegen). No in-tree frontend plugin emits a ternary yet -- a downstream plugin's branch-selection lowering is the intended integration guard. Add an end-to-end case when the first plugin emits `Conditional`. (Same deferral shape as the `Record.base` / `Decorator` / `Call`-kwargs notes above.)
- `Param.default` -> `TpyFunction.defaults` lowering (`tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py:_lower_function`) has no constant-expression gate, unlike the parser path: the parser validates every default via `_validate_const_default` (`tpyc/parse/parser.py`), which the lowering path bypasses. Sema's `_validate_param_defaults` type-checks a default it can name, but a non-constant one is exactly the shape `const_expr_type` returns None for, so it is skipped rather than rejected, and codegen `default_to_cpp` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`) falls back to a bare `return "0"`. So a plugin supplying a non-constant default (a `Call`, `BinOp`, or arbitrary `Name`) would silently miscompile to `0` instead of erroring. Latent -- no in-tree plugin emits `Param.default` yet, no test triggers it. Fix needs a design decision on where to share the constant-default predicate (reuse `expr_to_cpp_default` / `_validate_const_field_default` in `tpyc/sema/registration.py` so both producers are gated at the point sema owns, or factor the parser's `_validate_const_default` into a loc-agnostic predicate callable from lowering) -- run `/tpy-add-feature`, present the placement decision before code. Fold in the related edge case: an untyped param (bare `self`) with a default is now newly reachable and accepted silently (a defaulted `self` is nonsensical) -- decide reject-vs-accept as part of the same validation work. Also add an end-to-end case exercising lowering -> sema -> codegen when the first plugin emits a defaulted param (same deferral shape as the `Record.base` / `Conditional` notes above). Surfaced by `/tpy-review` architecture-fit / test-coverage.
- (really low prio) `AugAssign` -> `TpyAugAssign` lowering (`tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py:_lower_stmt`) has only unit coverage of the lowered shape (`tpyc/test_frontend_lower_aug_assign.py`); nothing in-tree exercises lowering -> sema -> codegen. The in-tree path to a real end-to-end guard is the Pascal frontend: its `DESIGN.md` specs `inc(x)`/`dec(x)` as `AugAssign`, but `pascal_translator/translate.py:_lower_inc_dec_stmt` actually emits `Assign(x, BinOp(x + n))` (the `x = x + n` form). Aligning the plain-`Ident` path of that emit with the spec (the var-param path routes through `unsafe_store`, which has no augmented form, so it stays as-is) both fixes the spec-vs-impl drift and provides the guard. Confirm first whether `x += n` vs `x = x + n` changes generated C++ for `int` (`__iadd__` vs `__add__`); if so it churns any Pascal snapshot using `inc`/`dec`. Same deferral shape as the `Conditional` note above.
- `docs/FRONTEND_PLUGIN_DESIGN.md` "Expressions" advertises several IR nodes that are NOT implemented in `tpyc/frontend_ir/nodes.py`: `TupleLit`, `DictLit`, `Slice`, `CharLit`, `BytesLit`, `Lambda`, `FormatString`, and the comprehension nodes (`ListComp`/`DictComp`/`SetComp`/`GeneratorExpr`). A plugin emitting any of them gets an unrecognized-node lowering failure, not the documented behavior. (`Conditional` was in this set until this branch implemented it.) Either implement them on demand (as `Conditional` was) or mark them planned in the doc so the contract matches the implementation. Spec-vs-impl drift, same kind as the `StarImport` note above.
- `module_data` is threaded to `FunctionMacroContext` but not to `ClassInfo` (`tpyc/macro_api.py`). A `MACRO`-routed decorator on a `record` (via a plugin `decorator_manifest`) would see `module_data == None` in its class macro. Currently latent -- the function-macro phase now scans methods (pass 5.5 walks `record.methods`), but the `module_data` gap is on the *class-macro* path (`ClassInfo`), which is unrelated; thread `module_data` to `ClassInfo` when class macros on plugin-emitted records become reachable. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` architecture-fit.
- `_TARGET_KINDS` (`tpyc/frontend_ir/decorators.py`) is an over-broad `build_registry` validation whitelist: it accepts `enum`, `enum_value`, `field`, and `constant`, but `_route_decorators` is only ever called with `"record"` / `"function"` (`_lower_enum` and field/constant lowering never route decorators at all). So a plugin manifest entry targeting one of those four kinds *registers* successfully yet can never fire -- a plugin-authoring trap (a decorator that registers but silently never runs), not a miscompile of user code. Remove the unroutable kinds from the whitelist until their lowering is wired (leaving only `function`/`record`), or wire the routing. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` architecture-fit.
- `_route_decorators` / `_native_spec` reject branches lack unit coverage: MACRO-route positional args, `BUILTIN_LOWERING` with an unimplemented name, unknown `target_kind` in a manifest, `@native` with more than one positional arg, and a non-bool `@native(function=...)`. The `module_data` channel is also only verified to land on `TpyModule.macro_data`, not end-to-end through `run_function_macros` -> `FunctionMacroContext.module_data`. Add these to `tpyc/test_frontend_lower_macros.py`. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` test-coverage.
- `CallMacroContext.module_data` (now exposed via `ctx.macro_data`, set in `bind_imports`) has only unit coverage (`tpyc/test_compiler.py::TestCallMacroModuleData` wires `bind_imports -> ctx -> CallMacroContext.module_data` directly, bypassing the `FrontendModule.macro_data -> lower.py -> TpyModule.macro_data` seam). Add an end-to-end snapshot case under `tests/cases/macros/` when a plugin first sets `FrontendModule.macro_data` -- ideally covering `FunctionMacroContext.module_data` parity in the same case (that sibling channel is also only unit-tested; see the `Decorator`-native note above). Surfaced by `/tpy-review` test-coverage.
- The same `module.macro_data` payload now reaches macros via two channels: `FunctionMacroContext` gets it as an explicit ctor kwarg threaded through `run_function_macros` / `run_deferred_sema_macros` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`), while `CallMacroContext` reads `ctx.macro_data` (always set in `bind_imports`). Since the ctx slot is now live before any macro expansion, the kwarg threading is redundant -- `FunctionMacroContext` could read `ctx.macro_data` directly, unifying the two paths so they can't drift. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` architecture-fit.
- The new `module_name()` plugin hook renames the entry module inside the compiler (`Compiler._module_name_for` -> `compiled.name`), but `tpyc/cli.py:501` still derives the build identity (`BuildLayout` output dir, CMake target, binary name, and the `Compiler.from_source` name) from the path-based `get_module_name()`, which never consults the hook. A plugin whose `module_name()` returns a name differing from the file stem gets `compiled.name` and the output/binary name out of sync (latent: no in-tree plugin overrides `module_name()` yet). Fix: route the CLI's entry name through the same plugin-aware path. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` architecture-fit.
- `compiler._discover_module_via_plugin` (`tpyc/compiler.py:1610-1612`) builds `(resolver.base_dir, *resolver.extra_dirs)` inline -- the same construction now provided by the new `_plugin_search_dirs()` helper, differing only by an explicit `resolver is None` guard. Fold the inline copy into the helper (giving the helper the None-guard it already has) so the search-dir set has one source of truth. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` architecture-fit.
- `Compiler._module_name_for`'s fallback branch (a plugin claims the extension but its `module_name()` returns `None`, so the path-based name is used) is untested. `tpyc/test_frontend_plugin_naming.py` only covers the plugin-provides-a-name path. Add a case with a plugin whose `module_name()` returns `None` and assert the entry is named by its path stem. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` test-coverage.
- The `module_name()`/`resolve_module()` contract documents the invariant `resolve_module(module_name(p)) == p` for every claimed file, but nothing enforces it -- no assertion in the compiler, no round-trip test. A plugin that violates it (e.g. `module_name` and `resolve_module` disagreeing on a name) fails in a confusing downstream way rather than at the boundary. Add a round-trip test (and consider a debug-time assertion) once a second plugin exercises the pair. Surfaced by `/tpy-ready` retrospective.
- IR overload groups (`Function.is_overload` -> `is_overload_stub`, `tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py`) have no IR-path regression test for the two overload error diagnostics that the lowered flag makes reachable: `_reject_same_param_overloads` (two `is_overload` members with identical param-type sequences) and `_reject_bodied_overloads_with_impl` (a bodied `is_overload` member paired with a same-named non-overload impl). Both are exercised for source-level `@overload` (`error_overload_same_params_diff_return`, `error_overload_body_with_impl`) and key purely on `is_overload_stub`, so the IR path can't diverge today -- these are regression anchors, not gap closures. Add them via a plugin emitting a bad group (the existing `_OverloadPlugin` in `tpyc/test_frontend_lower_overload.py` is the template). Surfaced by `/tpy-review` test-coverage.
- No `tests/cases/` snapshot test exists for a plugin-emitted overload group; `test_ir_overload_group_resolves_by_arg_type` exercises sema but produces no generated-C++ snapshot, so codegen drift for IR-synthesised overloads would be invisible. Codegen is unchanged by the `is_overload` work (the lowered group is identical to a source group), so this is low urgency -- add an end-to-end case when the first concrete plugin emits an overload group, alongside the other "first plugin emits X" deferrals above. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` test-coverage.
- `FunctionMacroContext.self_type` (`tpyc/macro_api.py`) resolves the enclosing record via the qname-carrying `_resolve_record_name` (falling back to a bare `NominalType`), but its docstring says it "mirrors" `CallMacroContext.self_type`, which uses the plain form and does not. The two "mirrored" properties can drift as a result. Backport the qname-aware lookup into `CallMacroContext.self_type` so they stay in lockstep (small design step -- confirm the call-macro consumers want the qname form). Surfaced by `/tpy-review` (architecture-fit) of feat-method-function-macros.

## Open feature gaps

- **[codegen] A user operator method with a type parameter of its own.** `def __lshift__[C: AnyFixedInt](self, k: C) -> Own[V]` on a user record is refused at its definition (*operator method '__lshift__' cannot have its own type parameters yet*, `OPERATOR_DUNDERS` in `tpyc/sema/operators.py`, checked in the method loop of `tpyc/sema/registration.py`; pinned by `records/error_generic_dunder_type_param`), because the C++ it would take does not build: the member renders as `template<::tpy::AnyFixedInt C> V __lshift__(::tpy::readonly_form_t<C> k) const` and its friend `operator<<` (`_gen_binary_operators`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/records.py`) has no template header, and adding one is not enough since `readonly_form_t<C>` is a non-deduced context. Sema already resolves such a use (operator resolution binds a dunder's own type parameters since the shift-count unit, for the fixed-int shift stubs). To lift the refusal: the friend shim of a member template takes the operand by a deducible parameter (`template<AnyFixedInt C> friend V operator<<(const V& lhs, C k)`) and calls the member with its template argument spelled (`lhs.template __lshift__<C>(k)`), for forward and reflected dunders alike. The direct-call renders need the same spelled argument: `v += int32(2)` over `__iadd__[C]` renders `v.__iadd__(2)` and `v // int32(2)` renders `v.__floordiv__(2)`, and both fail to deduce `C` (probed 2026-09-30); `DUNDER_CPP_TEMPLATES` has no slot for it, so the resolved binop has to carry the bound type arguments to the render. A unary dunder has no operand to bind a type parameter from and stays refused. The same shim shape serves `__getitem__` / `__call__` / `__contains__` (BUGS.md#generic-user-nonop-dunder-type-param-ill-formed).
- **[thir] Widen the remaining flag-keyed rejects over an UNPROVEN `Optional` container receiver to the checked render.** Reads through such a receiver now render the runtime check sema's warning promises (`::tpy::deref_check(d)` / `::tpy::deref_optional_check(h.d)`, one site: `_lower_optional_container_recv` in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`), but every sink with its own `needs_optional_runtime_check` gate still rejects, located: `r = d[0]` / `p = d[0]` with a record element (`decl.slot_type`), `d[0].x += 1` and `d[0] += 1` (`stmt.aug_assign`), `d[0].m()` (`method.recv.subscript`), `d[0].rows.append(4)` (`method.recv.field_chain`), `len(d[0].rows)` (`call.native_arg.container`), `print(d[0].rows)` (`print.arg.container_field_access`), `d[0].x = 1` (`assign.field_write_shape`), `d[0].rows[0] = 5` / `d[0].kids[k] = 3` (`setitem.recv.field_chain`), `for v in d[0].rows` (`foreach.iter_borrow_unplaceable`), `(q := d[0])` / `(r := xs[0])` (`expr.walrus`), `take_p(d[0])` (`call.arg_shape.record_f1`), `take_opt(xs[0])` (`call.arg_shape.optional`), the record-`__getitem__` read in a value position (`subscript.record_getitem`), and the element writes `d[0] = x` (sema's "read-only" text, BUGS.md#optional-container-setitem-says-read-only). Each is the same receiver wrap at its own sink; the write sinks also need the checked receiver in `THIRSetItem` (its emit reads `target.receiver` directly). Measured by the 292-probe sink sweep `/tmp/agents/bundle3/row2/sweep/` (`gen_sweep.py` / `run_sweep.py`).
- **[thir][design] One checked-unwrap mechanism for an unproven `Optional` receiver.** A subscript receiver is wrapped by the node `THIROptionalRecvCheck` (PTR / OPTIONAL spelling, one site: `_lower_optional_container_recv`), while member access and method calls still carry their own `deref_check` / `opt_deref_check` flags on `THIRFieldAccess` / `THIRMethodCall` (and `opt_deref_check` on `THIRName`), each re-deciding the PTR-vs-OPTIONAL choice through `_optional_ptr_borrow_name` / `reads_storage_form_optional`. Fold the flags onto `THIROptionalRecvCheck` so one node owns the check and its spelling. The fact it keys on is inverted too: `needs_optional_runtime_check` defaults to False, so a node sema never analyzed (or a trial left stale) renders UNCHECKED; replace it with a positive proven-non-None fact, so an un-analyzed receiver rejects instead. A `str` / `bytes` element bound off such a receiver owns a copy, as it does off every container under the one view rule; this fold does not change that. The three `opt_recv is not None` rejects at the slice / tuple / record-getitem arms of the subscript lowering (`subscript.optional_check`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) are a deny-list; one check after arm dispatch that the checked receiver was consumed would replace them.
- **[parse][sema] One import-name validator.** A `from tpy|typing|builtins import X` is validated by the parser (`_check_implicit_module_names`, `tpyc/parse/imports.py`) and every other module's names by sema (`_register_user_module_import`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`): two validators in two phases for one question.
- **[sema][design] One type-param binding finalizer.** Ten sites finalize a type-param binding map by calling `resolve_int_literals`, each with its own int rule: `resolve_inferred_type_arg` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`, the template arguments of every generic call, `default_int_type`) and the two Fn-slot hint maps (`_infer_arg_types` and `_build_regime_c_evidence`, `default_int_type or INT32`) use the configured width; the builtin container factory in `analyze_call`, `_create_pending_generic_instance` (`calls.py`), `infer_type_params_for_function` (`tpyc/sema/type_ops.py`), `_analyze_pending_generic_method_call` (two maps) and `try_resolve_pending_from_expected_type` (`tpyc/sema/methods.py`) and `_build_type_subst` (`tpyc/sema/operators.py`) use the range-safe `default_int_for_literal`. `infer_type_params_for_function` still resolves only a top-level marker: resolving a nested one there makes a pending literal argument fail its own substituted parameter (BUGS.md#generic-method-tuple-literal-marker-arg), so the generic call's per-argument check substitutes a callable parameter from the finalized `inferred_type_args` and every other parameter from the marker-keeping map. One finalizer means choosing one int-width rule for a literal-learned type argument, which is a user decision; once chosen, the sites call it and a literal marker can no longer leave a binding map. The callable-vs-other split at that per-argument check is a stopgap of the same one-map-two-jobs problem: one marker map serves both as the template arguments and as the coercion targets of literal arguments. A comprehension argument checked against the marker-keeping map shows it (BUGS.md#generic-float-tuple-comprehension-arg-rejects); the fix is two maps with one job each, the finalized bindings for every parameter type and the markers only where a literal argument coerces. What finalized markers leave behind downstream is "Literal markers leak past sema" above.
- **[sema][design] Analyze a lambda body under its own frame.** A lambda body is analyzed inline in the enclosing function's tracking state (`ScopeTracker.lambda_scope`, `tpyc/sema/scope_tracker.py`), so every name-keyed fact -- parameters, locals, tuple facts, loop variables, auto-move, borrow facts -- answers for the ENCLOSING function: a lambda parameter that shadows an outer name reads the outer name's sema facts (lowering strips them through `lc.shadow_scope`; sema has no counterpart), and the return-rooting oracles (`_name_is_param_or_global`, `is_dangling_return`) cannot tell the lambda's parameter from the enclosing function's local. A nested `def` gets its own saved/restored state (`nested_def_scope`); analyzing the lambda body under the same mechanism makes those facts answer for the lambda structurally, instead of by per-oracle overrides (two review rounds of those did not converge). Prerequisite for `BUGS.md#lambda-body-partial-return-checks` (running the def return's checks on a lambda body, and returning a temporary-rooted body by value). The fix removes the stopgap that rejects a lambda borrow rooted in a body temporary -- `TypeCompatibility.borrow_temp_root`, `ExpressionAnalyzer.resolve_pending_lambda_borrow_checks` and its queue, `_temp_root_spelling` -- since the def-return pipeline answers that question then. The abandoned per-oracle attempt is branch `fix-lambda-result-rooting` (a `LambdaFrame` stack, a shared def/lambda result-slot check, and the review probes that sank it); read it before designing, but do not build on it. Related: the one-construct entry under "Architectural stabilization" (a lambda is a nested `def`).
- **[sema] A candidate-scoped key-consumption fact, so `key=` lambdas may treat their parameters as durable.** `sorted(ss, key=lambda s: s[1:])` over `list[str]` is refused ("Cannot return StrView referencing a local or temporary", `BUGS.md#key-lambda-str-and-subscript-rejects` part (2)), because a lambda states no borrow contract: the same body at `map(lambda w: w[1:], words())` over a generator of owned strings would dangle (`BUGS.md#map-owned-element-borrow-result-dangles`). A `key=` callable's result is consumed while the element it was called on is alive (sort / min / max compare keys and drop them), so the key slot can make the parameter durable for the view rule. The fact must be decided for the CANDIDATE before the lambda body is analyzed (a key-consumption flag on the callable parameter, set from the stub), not read off `TpyLambda.readonly_params`, which is set after overload selection.
- **[sema] An emptiness GUARD does not prove a loop runs, so a name the body binds is still rejected after it.** A name first bound in a loop body counts as assigned after the loop only when the head provably runs (`NarrowingTracker.for_head_provably_runs`, `tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`). That predicate proves a `range` the value ranges decide, a non-empty list or `str` literal at the head, a TPy enum, and a local whose only binding is a non-empty container literal. It does NOT prove the guarded spellings, all of which CPython runs fine:

  ```python
  if not xs: return -1           # or `if len(xs) == 0: return -1`
  for x in xs:
      v = x
  return v                       # rejected: `v` may not be assigned

  if xs:
      for x in xs:
          v = x
      return v                   # same
  ```

  **Improvement: a container LENGTH fact, so the head proof stops being a list of shapes.** The `while` side asks the value-range engine one general question (`condition_provably_true`); the `for` side pattern-matches its head, so every new proof is a new arm and the literal-bound-local arm reads a flow-insensitive write history. One question serves both loop kinds: a `for` over `X` provably runs when the engine proves `len(X) >= 1`. Track length as a fact on the same footing as the integer value ranges, keyed on the container place: SEEDED by a non-empty literal (exact length), `range(a, b, s)` (computed from the bound ranges, which also retires the second `range` decoder of `BUGS.md#range-literal-bound-arm-unreached`), an enum (static member count), `if xs:` / `if len(xs) > 0` / `len(xs) != 0` / `if not xs: return`, and `append` (lower bound plus one); KILLED or adjusted by a rebinding and by any mutation that can shrink it (`clear`, `pop`, `remove`, `del`, a `@native` call taking it mutably, a pass to a mutating parameter); CARRIED through length-preserving views (`d.items()` / `keys()` / `values()`, `enumerate(xs)`, `reversed(xs)`) by a property the stub declares, never by a callee name in the compiler; MERGED at branch joins like `ValueRange`. `NarrowingTracker.for_head_provably_runs` is the one predicate all four loop arms call, so the change replaces its body and touches no caller and no rule text; expected corpus churn is cases that start compiling. The fact pays twice: `xs[0]` after `if xs:` loses its bounds check, which the engine cannot elide today. The kill set is what makes the literal-bound-local seed sound, so `BUGS.md#literal-bound-local-proof-ignores-mutation` closes with it and neither half should be built without the other. Feature-sized: `/tpy-add-feature`. Until then the remedy is the one the reject implies -- assign the name once before the loop, or narrow the bound.

- **[diagnostics] The zero-trip loop reject gives no route out.** A read of a loop-clause local after a loop that is not proven to run reports the generic `variable 'x' may not be assigned at this point`. Name the loop and the remedy (assign the name once before the loop, or narrow the bound) when the name is a pending loop-clause local; the emptiness-guard gap above makes this the first message a user of the rule meets.

- **[perf] Mandelbrot: where TPy stands against hand-optimized C++, and what would close the gap.** `tpy-examples/basics/mandelbrot.py` (100x50, MAX_ITER 1000, ~894k inner iterations, output compared byte-for-byte) on an i7-11700K with g++-13, min of 21 runs of the program's own `elapsed[ms]`, 2026-09-15:

  | variant | ms |
  |---|---|
  | TPy as written (untyped ALL_CAPS constants, int32 counter), `-O3` | 2.73 |
  | TPy with `MAX_ITER: Final[int]` (BigInt counter; see the Missed-optimizations entry) | 4.67 |
  | C++ scalar, direct translation of the Python | 2.51 |
  | C++ four pixels interleaved per loop (ILP, no SIMD) | 1.07 |
  | C++ 8-lane GCC vector extensions, `-march=native` (AVX-512) | 0.62 |
  | same, escape test every 8 iterations (escaped lanes go NaN and stop counting) | 0.44 |
  | same kernel built WITHOUT `-march` (SSE2 splits the lanes into ILP) | 1.06 |
  | same kernel over 4 threads (rows interleaved) | 0.21 |
  | C++ four-pixel ILP kernel over 4 threads, no `-march` | 0.38 |
  | **TPy today**, hand-optimized the same way (probes under `/tmp/agents/mandel_char/`): | |
  | TPy scalar + `Final[int32]` constants + gradient LUT + one print per row | 2.68 |
  | TPy four-pixel ILP kernel (`mandelbrot4` returning a 4-tuple of `int32`) | 1.14 |
  | TPy ILP kernel over 4 `tpy.thread.spawn` tasks, rows interleaved | 0.44 |

  Reading: TPy matches C++ at every tier it can express today (scalar, ILP, threads -- within 7-15%); what it cannot express is the lane-typed kernel, which is the remaining 2.5x. Writing the TPy tiers surfaced three defects, filed 2026-09-15 and fixed the same day: the two char-at-a-str-slot ones (a `char` at a `str` slot now carries its coercion at every sink) and the reference-typed spawn result (`JoinHandle.join()` returns `Own[R]`). The emitted scalar loop is already at the scalar C++ bound (the 8% gap is 5000 per-char `print` calls plus one `log` per pixel); `-march=native` buys nothing for the scalar loop; every further step is a rewrite the C++ compiler does not do either -- the kernel over N lanes with the early `return i` turned into per-lane masks and counters. ILP and SIMD are the SAME source transformation: the C++ compiler maps lanes to whatever width the target has and splits them into independent scalar chains where it has none. Ideas, in the order they should land:
  1. **A `Simd[T, N]` library type** (the spelling `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`'s naming rule already reserves) as a `@native` type over GCC vector extensions (g++ and clang, no intrinsics): lane-wise arithmetic, comparisons yielding a lane mask, `any()`/`all()`, `where(mask, a, b)`, load/store from `Span`. The user writes the masked kernel by hand. No compiler work beyond `@native`; a CPython stub is a list of N scalars. Reaches the 0.44 ms row.
  2. **A `--march` CLI option** (TPy builds with `-O3` and no `-march`), without which tier 1 lands on the 1.06 ms row. It must pair with `-ffp-contract=off`: CPython rounds every operation (its only fusion is the explicit `math.fma`, which `lib/tpy/math.py` already has), and GCC contracts `x*y + c` into FMA by default once `-march` allows it, so a contracting default would print output CPython cannot reproduce (it did not here -- luck of the input). Contraction as an opt-in per FUNCTION is feasible and verified 2026-09-15 on both toolchains: GCC honors `__attribute__((optimize("-ffp-contract=fast")))`, Clang `#pragma clang fp contract(fast)`, each turning the multiply+add into one `vfmadd` while the rest of the build stays exact. Shape: a decorator that names the relaxation (`@fp_contract`, or `contract=True` on the hot-path decorator) -- contraction ONLY, never `-ffast-math` -- with a no-op CPython stub, so the decorator is the declared parity divergence. Two seams: without a global `-march` the attribute needs a per-function `target("fma")` too, and a target-attributed function is not inlined into callers without it (measured on both compilers) -- free for a kernel called from a loop, a call per use for a small helper. The 8-lane kernel measured 0.44 ms contracted vs 0.68 ms exact, so the opt-in is worth having.
  3. **An SPMD function transform** (`@simd(lanes=N)` on the scalar `def mandelbrot(cx: float, cy: float) -> int`, ISPC-style): the compiler generates the lane version, lowering `if`/`while`/early `return` to mask updates and the result to `Simd[int, N]`. The tier that lets users keep the scalar Python. Needs restrictions (no allocation, only `@simd` callees and math builtins, fixed-width scalars). Design work; the resumable-frame CFG already gives a per-body CFG to lower from.
  4. A `parallel_for` over rows on `tpy.thread` + `tplib.channel` is independent library work for the 0.21 ms row.
  Automatic batching of pure calls across loop iterations is NOT on the list: it needs purity, a known trip count and a control-flow rewrite of the callee, and would be invisible and fragile.

- **[match] Audit the `match` error cases: which rejections are RULES and which are LIMITATIONS pinned as errors.** `tests/cases/match/error_*` holds ~55 cases, and at least two of them (found 2026-09-02 while reviewing the or-pattern flattening commit) assert a diagnostic whose header comment explained the rejection as a property of the dispatch model when it was a gap: `error_or_nested_as_binds_wide` (BUGS.md#or-pattern-as-binding-no-join) and `error_or_union_none_alt` (BUGS.md#or-pattern-none-alt-union), the second of which rejects a shape codegen already dispatches on when it stands alone. Walk every error case and bin it: (a) STRICTER than CPython by design -- dead-arm and duplicate rejections, unreachable arms; keep, and make sure `docs/MATCH_CASE_DESIGN.md`'s divergence table lists it; (b) DECLARED divergence -- `case None as x:`; keep, table entry required; (c) a GAP CPython accepts -- must have a BUGS.md entry (or a row here) and a header comment that says gap, not rule. Known (c) rows going in: the two above; the int-literal-on-`IntEnum` row directly below; the union-field literal (BUGS.md, `error_field_literal_union`); the capture-retype pair (`error_nested_capture_retype*`, filed as a common-supertype bind); sequence patterns (`error_nonunion_subject`, the row further down). A third one pinned as a mechanism with no verdict: `error_recursive_union_union_arg` (BUGS.md#recursive-alias-leaf-union-member-unnameable, nested-variant dispatch). Unfiled (c) candidates to price: the `bytes` literal against a `bytes` subject or field (two cases, both say not-yet-implemented, nothing tracks them); the named-constant field comparison `case Dog(size=Big):` on polymorphic AND union subjects (two cases, guard workaround only); and `error_or_type_mismatch`, which is the field-capture face of the no-join rule -- fold it into that entry rather than filing twice. Do the binning as a table in `docs/MATCH_CASE_DESIGN.md` so the next reader of an `error_*` case can look the verdict up instead of re-deriving it.
- **[MED] `match` on an `IntEnum` subject should accept an int literal pattern.** CPython MATCHES
  `case 1:` against an `IntEnum` member, and TPy already renders the equivalent comparison --
  `c == 1` emits `static_cast<int32_t>(c) == 1`, and `docs/ENUM_DESIGN.md` commits to `==`/`<`
  with int for `IntEnum`. So the comparison is wired up everywhere except `match`. Today the
  pattern is REJECTED with a not-yet-implemented diagnostic (it previously ICEd, via an
  affirmative `is_enum_type` allowance in sema with no codegen behind it). Implementing it means
  giving the enum switch tier an int label -- a `static_cast` case label, or routing the arm to
  the if/elif tier. Rejected deliberately rather than implemented inside a bug fix, so it goes
  through the design gate. A plain `Enum` must keep rejecting: CPython never matches there, so
  the arm is dead code and rejecting it is the documented policy.

- **[MED] A `None` alternative in a union or-pattern -- `case A() | None:` on `A | B | None` --
  should compile.** Ordinary, idiomatic Python; CPython matches it. TPy ICEs today with a bare
  assertion in the union switch grouping. The assertion is being converted to a real diagnostic,
  which stops the crash but still refuses the program. Note this shape is NOT fixed by the
  or-pattern flattening work -- it has no nesting at all and reaches the same line by an
  independent route, so it needs its own support. Likely wants the `None` alternative routed to
  the monostate arm the union switch already emits for a bare `case None:`.
- **Rebinding a non-value-type GLOBAL.** `global PROTEINS; PROTEINS = []` inside a function is rejected with `Cannot reassign global variable 'PROTEINS' of non-value type 'list[int32]'` -- a deliberate, clearly-worded restriction, not a defect, which is why this sits here rather than in `BUGS.md`. `.clear()` covers the reset case, but not rebinding to a genuinely new value (a freshly built list, a container returned from a helper), and there is no spelling for it today.
