- **[sub-item of the `Place` design row, `BUGS.md#iter-borrow-place-needs-hops` -- no priority of its own] The view-family field-WRITE gate is a SUBTRACTION from a ladder that keeps growing under it.** `_viewfam_field_write_receiver_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) names the receivers a held `str`/`bytes` view CANNOT be demoted through and removes them from `_field_write_receiver_ok`, so every rung added to the shared ladder for the scalar axis is admitted for the view families by default and has to be noticed by hand. It was one entry short in five successive rounds of batch 6 (a `Ptr`, a tuple element, a container element, a borrow-returning call, a `@property` getter), each found by a review rather than by the gate. When escape becomes a `Place` fact the gate inverts: admit a receiver iff the write RESOLVES TO A STORAGE KEY the tracker can demote under, which is one positive predicate over the place and needs no list -- and a new ladder rung then fails closed instead of open.
- **[LOW][THIR] `field_owned_str_ok` is information-free at most of its call sites and is still being opted into one site at a time.** The kwarg tells `_lower_expr_impl` that a `str`/`bytes` FIELD read may land at an owning slot -- the same question the field-read ladder now asks the SINK through `use.admits(SinkForm.FIELD_VALUE_TUPLE)` and `use.result is BORROW_BIND` -- and 16 of its 24 set sites spell it as `field_owned_str_ok=isinstance(<the same expr>, TpyFieldAccess)`, a fact the callee re-derives from the node it already has, so the flag carries nothing at those sites. Three more such opt-ins were added in batch 6 (`tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py` ~1623, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` ~7060, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` ~11906) because the chokepoint change made the field read reach a slot the caller had not granted. Each new sink that wants the read has to remember the incantation, which is the shape of a per-sink grant. The fold is NOT mechanical: the other 8 sites carry real conditions (`view_str_field or str_field_inner`, `own_str`, `str_field_init`, a forwarded flag), so pricing the rename means pricing those. Fix: one `field_read_kind` discriminator -- let the field-read row inside `_lower_expr` decide it from the node and the SINK it is lowering into, and keep the kwarg only where a caller genuinely overrides that (the handful of sites that pass a DIFFERENT expression than the one being lowered). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, W8) of batch 6; the untyped-verdict sibling is the `_optional_ptr_arg_face` entry.
- **[LOW] A resumable frame answers "is this capture const" twice, and the two answers genuinely differ.** The emit window (`GenAsyncCodegen._resumable_frame_ctx`) seeds the body's `const_ref_params` / `deep_const_borrow_params` from `FunctionCodegen.compute_body_const_sets`, while the frame's fields, the prescan's const sets and `const_frame_bindings` all come from `_frame_capture_const_names`. Both route through `decide_param_const`, but they are not one fact: measured over the whole corpus they diverge in BOTH directions on ~20 distinct bodies. The body pair names captures the frame holds by COPY and never renders const (`Pattern.finditer` -> body deep `['subject']`, frame deep `[]`; the same for a scalar `x` / `k` / `n` / `count`), and the frame pair adds the explicit `readonly[T]` / ptr-variant half the body model does not reach (`gsum` -> frame const-ref `['pair']`, body const-ref `[]`). No miscompile is known -- the extra body names are value captures whose reads do not consult the const sets -- but a name that is const to the body and mutable to the frame is exactly the split that produced the `const B*` -> `B*` frame build failure this entry was filed alongside. Fix shape: decide at the window which names the BODY may treat as const-bound, derived from the capture verdict for the names the frame captures by borrow, so a value capture is in neither set; then the second spelling goes. THE HOME for this and its three siblings ("The sync function/method signature emitters", "Param-const verdict: collapse the body-side re-derivation", and the second home named in "Call-graph fact propagation"): `FunctionInfo.const_borrow_params` remains THE verdict, the frame-layout pass (`_classify_params`) owns its per-capture projection so the const bit and the C++ capture type are decided in one arm, and `compute_body_const_sets` is DELETED rather than migrated onto -- it has exactly one caller. The sync signature emitter is the sibling half and needs `reassigned_params` hoisted onto `FunctionInfo` first. Needs its own measurement -- the divergence list is the input, not the answer. A WHY comment sits at the `compute_body_const_sets` call. Surfaced by the batch-5 fix round that folded the view-accessor const verdict into `is_const_storage_source`. **A third classifier of the same question joined the pair in batch 6:** the body's const-borrow verdict for a source NAME is now assembled once in `_const_borrow_name` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`), and `_frame_capture_const_names` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`) remains a second hand-maintained list of the SAME source families -- explicit `readonly[T]`, the deep-const verdict, a `@readonly` method's `self`, the unmutated varargs pack, and now a `Ptr[readonly[T]]` pointee. The family LIST should come from the one assembler while the frame-edge closure (which names the frame HOLDS by borrow, and which pointer-repr forms join `deep` only) stays frame-specific. The lockstep cost is measured, not hypothetical: batch 6 added the pack family to the lowering assembler and the generator twin kept emitting `Box*` into a `varargs<const Holder>` frame until the same family was added here by hand, and the `Ptr[readonly[T]]` family repeated it one fix round later -- the sync unpack was correct and the generator twin failed the C++ build. The two readonly-pointee tests now both call `typesys.is_readonly_ptr`, and their one remaining difference (only the lowering side peeled the Send/Sync marker) was never reachable: `Send[Ptr[readonly[T]]]` is refused at parse as not Send. **The complaint is narrower than it reads (measured 2026-09-17):** of the assembler's arms only `_readonly_self` RE-DERIVES a decided fact, and it answers by POSITION -- `ovs[-1].is_readonly` into an overload set `@auto_readonly` fills with a `[mutable, const]` pair (`_clone_auto_readonly`, `tpyc/sema/method_expansion.py`), so a third overload or a flipped clone order changes the verdict with nothing failing. The other arms read a fact decided elsewhere (`const_loop_vars`, set at the for-each head; `decide_param_const`'s param verdict) or are plain type queries (`is_readonly_ptr`, the pack's element flip). What the two spellings duplicate is therefore the family LIST, not the verdicts.

- Give an escaping loop-body local per-iteration storage, closing the acknowledged divergence. A local declared in a loop body and bound to a longer-lived name hoists to ONE function-scope slot, so the outer name observes later rebinds (LANGUAGE_FEATURES "Scope Escape Detection"); the warning states this and names `copy()`, and the specific wrong-value shapes are in BUGS.md. Closing it needs storage per BINDING, and every mechanism costs something the source does not show. THREE were prototyped and discarded, all fully working -- do not re-derive them: (1) a per-iteration heap arena (`std::deque`), killed because an EMPTY deque costs 2 allocations and it retains every iteration's object to function exit; (2) copy-at-escape, matching what field and container boundaries already do -- zero allocation and sibling-consistent, but it silently drops aliasing, so mutation through one name stops being visible through the other; (3) a two-slot rotation keyed on a "handed out" flag -- correct aliasing, zero allocation, one predictable branch, byte-measured in the noise for any loop constructing a non-trivial object, but a runtime state machine the source does not show, and it serves exactly ONE alias (two targets can hold two slots at once, so the generalization needs a held-bitmask over k+1 slots). A fourth option, rejecting the shape outright, was built and reverted: it is zero-cost and honest but refuses idiomatic Python, and a measured scan of ~30k functions (CPython stdlib + site-packages) found the shape only about SEVEN times, so the reject bought little at a real usability cost. If this is picked up, (3) is the cheapest revival. Effort: M.
- Unify block-local reassignment onto ONE C++ object. A local first declared inside a block and assigned after it currently emits TWO C++ declarations for one Python local (`int32_t n` in the loop body, a second `int32_t n = 9;` after it) -- correct today, because a READ after the block instead takes sema's pending-loop-var promotion (one pre-declared object), because an escaping alias has its STORAGE hoisted to function scope so the block-scoped thing is only the binding, and because the two declarations are now required to share ONE TYPE (the one-type-per-local check rejects a second type across the block boundary), so they can differ only in identity, never in shape. But Python's model is one local, and the compiler already emits that on the read path; the split exists only because the promotion path is currently the buggier of the two (it emits the promoted binding const, breaking a reference-typed loop var's later rebind, and it reuses one hoisted slot per NAME rather than per binding, which clobbers escaped aliases -- both filed in BUGS.md). Routing writes through promotion collapses it to a single object -- verified, `in_for` emits one `int32_t n;` with both sites assigning -- but ONLY once the alias-clobber entry is genuinely fixed: with the collapse on top of today's slot model, `block_local_reassign_after_record::escaped_alias` returns 909 instead of 209, because one object means one hoisted slot and the post-loop rebind overwrites what the escaped alias points at. That entry is harder than it looks (its obvious fix regresses destructor timing -- see BUGS.md), so this stays gated behind it. Surfaced answering a review question on the block-local scope-revoke fix. The alias-clobber entry closed with the alias-gated slot model (2026-09-14), so this is no longer gated; `records/rebind_slot_block_scope_drop` pins the block-exit drop timing it would also settle. Effort: M.
- **[cleanup] `_declare_rebind_slot` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py`) hardcodes the `__slot_` prefix and omits the `static` keyword.** The AST's `ctx.declare_rebind_slot` derives both from the emission scope (`slots.global_scope` -> `static `, `slot_prefix`); the THIR mirror spells `std::optional<T> __slot_{n};` literally, so a module-scope slot would come out non-static and named `__slot_` instead of `__global_slot_`. Unreachable today -- every call site is preceded by `state.assert_local_slot()`, which fails before a module-scope body gets there, and lowering rejects the top-level shapes anyway -- but `assert` vanishes under `python -O`, and the AST's own `static` branch is equally unreachable, so this is symmetry cleanup rather than a latent bug. Do it before top-level lowering is widened to admit slot-allocating shapes. Effort: XS.
- **[thir][cleanup] The match ladder still derives its own pointer / const-pointer hoist rungs.** `_route_hoists` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`) consumes `_nonvalue_hoist_flavor` for the OPT_STORAGE verdict only; its `ptr` / `ptr_const` / `ptr_slot` tiers re-derive the borrow-only / const / rvalue-reassigned conditions the classifier already answers (`HoistFlavor.POINTER` / `CONST_POINTER` / `CONST_REBOUND`), so a flavor change there (the pointer-repr Optional admission of 2026-09-14, say) has to be ported by hand. Route the tiers off the verdict; byte-diff-sensitive across the match snapshots -- own pass.

- **[cleanup] ONE mechanism for the alias-clobber hazard: fold `scope_tracker.check_escape` into the alias-rebind storage pass (`alias_rebind.decide_rebind_storage`).** Two checks now diagnose the same hazard from opposite ends and word it differently. `check_escape` (`tpyc/sema/scope_tracker.py`) fires at the alias BIND, keys on scope DEPTH, and says "'X' will not keep the object it was given -- 'Y' is rebound on each iteration"; the storage pass (`tpyc/sema/alias_rebind.py`) warns at the REBIND, keyed on a loop-carried loan still read after the site re-executes, and says "...'Y' is rebound here". A reader who hits one of them cannot tell which mechanism they are in, and the depth key is the weaker of the two: `BUGS.md`'s declared-above-a-loop entry (`saved = p` and the rebind both at function scope) states the fix shape as exactly this -- "the escape check must key on an ALIAS fact ... rather than scope depth -- the borrow tracker is the natural owner" -- and the alias fact now exists. `check_escape` also has side effects the rebind-site check does not (it populates `hoisted_vars` and strips `Own[T]`, which changes emission), so this is not a message merge: the hoist has to move to the alias fact with it, or stay behind a narrowed depth predicate. They would double-warn on a loop body's first bind aliased into an outer name, so the storage pass skips the ALIAS-kind clobber at a site `check_escape` already hoisted (`hoisted_vars`, 2026-09-14) -- the fold removes that skip along with the depth key. Point at both entries when picking it up. Effort: M. Now also a FALSE POSITIVE at module level: `V = Node(3); S: Node = V; V = Node(4)` warns that `S` will not keep its object, yet the alias-gated write gives the rebind a static slot of its own and `S` keeps it (verified 2026-09-14); the fold is the fix, not a second gate inside `check_escape`. What the fold has to absorb grew with the call-source escape walk: `check_escape` now reads a call's `return_borrows_from` through `ScopeTracker.lend_roots`, judges a multi-root source per name, and defers its diagnostic for a callee whose body is not analyzed yet (`settle_deferred_escapes`, after every body in the module) -- the alias-rebind pass runs per function, so the deferral needs a home of its own in the folded form.
- **[cleanup] ONE walk for "which named storage does this expression reference".** `ScopeTracker.lend_roots` (`tpyc/sema/scope_tracker.py`), `addr_taken_roots` and `_borrow_storage_root(s)` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) walk the same name / field / element hops and differ in the call arm (only `lend_roots` follows a call's `return_borrows_from`, which is also why `_register_call_result_borrow` takes a reference-returning receiver call for a temporary, `BUGS.md#ref-returning-receiver-call-called-temporary`) and in what they return (names with how they were reached, vs storage keys). One walk that optionally follows calls, returning the key plus the hop facts, stops the three from drifting. The hop facts are the second half: `_key_member_is_indirection` re-resolves a STRING key (`root.member`) to a field type through the scope and the registry to learn that a hop went through a `Ptr` or a view, a fact the walk had in hand when it crossed the `TpyFieldAccess` -- carry it on the key's producer (or on `LoanInfo`, where `BorrowKind.PTR` already lives) and the consumer stops re-deriving it. It is also what `BUGS.md#self-aimed-ptr-field-borrow-unrecorded` needs, and what `BUGS.md#call-source-escape-through-alias-unchecked` waits on: an alias or a for-each variable can only be judged by the storage it points into when its loan says where that storage lives, element or slice, this scope or the caller's.
- **[LOW perf] Reuse the slot under a DEAD alias when the drop is unobservable.** The alias-rebind storage pass (`tpyc/sema/alias_rebind.py`) counts a holder while it is BOUND, read again or not, because CPython keeps the object alive as long as any name refers to it and a `__del__` would show the difference: `r = Noisy("d1"); alias = r; r = Noisy("d2")` with `alias` never read again must still print `drop d1` at scope end, not at the rebind (`records/alias_gated_rebind`, the `dead_alias` section). For a type with no `__del__` anywhere in it (transitively, through its fields) the earlier drop is invisible, so liveness could be the key there and the rebind could write in place -- one stack `std::optional<T>` less and the old object (a big container's buffer, say) released at the rebind instead of scope end. Deliberately NOT done: it makes a rebind's emitted shape depend on whether some field deep in the type defines `__del__`, so adding a destructor would silently change the storage of unrelated functions, and the pass is interim (the MIR loan checker supersedes it). Worth it only if a real program keeps a large container alive under a dead alias; `del alias` is the spelling until then. Decided 2026-09-14.
- **[LOW perf] The alias-rebind storage pass's "unknown counts as aliased" fallbacks, and where they over-reserve.** Every one costs a stack `std::optional<T>` and a later drop, never a wrong value (`tpyc/sema/alias_rebind.py`). Two are worth refining: (1) a slice view or pointer passed as a CALL ARGUMENT (`total(xs[1:])`, `bump(take_ptr(p))`) pins the root for the rest of the body (the `_ESCAPED` holder), so every later rebind of `xs` / `p` takes its own slot although most callees do not retain the argument -- needs a callee-side "retains its argument" fact, which does not exist; the slice spelling is the common one; (2) a holder bound from a call that READS another holder (`w = make(q)` with `q` a `Ptr`) inherits `q`'s loans even when the callee returns a fresh object -- the tracker's own rule is narrower (it consults `return_borrows_from` and registers an opaque loan only when that is unknown), so the pass's inheritance should key on the same fact; (3) the OWN sites of one name in the mutually exclusive arms of an `if` / `elif` / `match` each draw their own slot (`records/alias_gated_rebind`, `match_arm`: `__slot_2` and `__slot_3` for the two arms) although at most one of them runs -- the pass could hand such a group one shared origin and the emitter one slot per origin, with the group id flowing through `THIRAssign.rebind_storage`'s neighbour field and the frame's per-site field prescan; safe only when no loop encloses the branch (arm A on one iteration, arm B on the next, would overwrite an object an alias still holds -- a wrong value, not a drop shift) or when the residual check is extended from `site_id in lorigins` to the group. Accepted as is: a pointer-variant UNION local always takes a slot per site (the current alternative's type may not be the new member's, so there is no in-place write); a global rebound inside a function (`global g; g = X()`) always takes its own static slot (module-level aliases are invisible there); a handler / `finally` entry sees the union of every state the `try` body passed through, so a rebind there can be OWN because of a loan the body took and killed before raising. In the other direction, documented in LANGUAGE_FEATURES: a per-site slot inside a loop destroys the previous iteration's object when the site runs again, one statement earlier than CPython for a holder rebound right after the site. Decided 2026-09-14.
- **[cleanup] The frame's TUPLE yield arm still keeps its own container-element lift leg.** `res.btuple_yield_elem_lift` (`tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py`) is a third ladder over the reference axis, beside the bare `record_like` ladder that unified the record and container halves; absorb it into that ladder next time the tuple yield family is touched.

- **[hardening] Frame ptr-slot prescan: structural agreement with the emit arms.** Two lockstep risks in the per-site frame-slot machinery, both currently safe by convention or coincidence rather than structure: (a) `ptr_slot_field_type` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/statements.py`) re-derives `_gen_pointer_local_rebind`'s routing conditions instead of the emit arms consulting one classifier for their own branching -- the dangerous direction (slot-needing write with no prescanned field) raises loud, but over-reservation drifts silently into dead fields; (b) the prescan runs before `setup_body_scope` seeds `optional_locals` / `storage_form_optional_locals` / `current_func_params`, so its `needs_optional_to_ptr_lift` / `is_storage_form_optional_source` reads see stale per-body state -- today every divergence collapses to "no slot" on both sides only because `is_rvalue_source(TpyName)` is unconditionally False. Fix shape: extend the seed-before-prescan block that `_build_resumable_cfg` already has for `var_types`/`const_ref_params` (added for exactly this risk class) to those sets, and restructure the emit arms to branch on the shared classifier's verdict. Zero observable change today -- deliberately deferred off the fix branch as untestable churn. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the frame ptr-slot placement fix.
- **[perf] Suspension-liveness-precise view promotion for frame locals.** The frame view-local owned promotion (`ViewVarInfo.frame_unsafe_source` + the `in_resumable` term in `_resolve_pending_view_types`) is deliberately coarser than liveness -- it promotes any non-static-sourced str/bytes view local in ANY generator/async body. Two refinements, both perf-only (the coarse rule is the safe direction): (a) a loop var in a loop containing NO suspension point copies per iteration where the view was already safe (`resumable_view_loopvar`'s `words_gen` now does `std::string w = *__beg_0` each pass) -- needs a per-local "crosses a suspension" fact at resolution time; (b) a local aliasing an `is_owned_in_coro_frame`-captured param (plain `str`/`bytes`) could stay a view of the frame's owned field (durable), though param REBIND then dangles it, so this needs a no-rebind fact too. Sema-side suspension liveness is the real prerequisite for (a)/(b); revisit post-THIR where the frame layout is already a queryable plan. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + architecture-fit + safety-model) of the frame view-local promotion fix.
- **[thir hardening] `lower_top_level`'s lambda-hoist protection is incidental, not stated.** The two deliberate rejection points for a rebind slot a lambda-rendered body cannot reach (`lower_function`, `lower_constructor`, both via `_rejects_lambda_hoist` / `_needs_held_back_slot` in `tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`) do NOT include `lower_top_level`. It is safe today only because `_rejects_global_slot` happens to inspect `THIRPtrLocalRebind` nodes as well -- a predicate whose docstring and maintenance contract are about GLOBAL-scope memory safety, not lambda placement. Nothing ties the two invariants together, so widening that predicate's allow-list for an unrelated reason would silently drop the coverage. Related: THIR's emit side has no analogue of the AST's `hoist_scope_id` / `rebind_slot_scopes` runtime check (a single flat `hoist_lines` list per function, no per-nested-def scoping), so the upfront predicate is the ENTIRE protection -- which is why one omission in it was directly reachable, THIR being the only author. Either apply `_rejects_lambda_hoist` at `lower_top_level` too, or give the emit side the scope check. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready targeted safety-model pass. Effort: S.
- **[thir hardening] Two hoist-write paths sit outside `_needs_held_back_slot`'s scope.** The predicate (`tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`) covers the emit sites that call `_declare_rebind_slot`, which is what its three rejection points key on. Not covered: (a) `RECORD_HOISTED`'s unconditional `std::optional<T> __slot_N;`, the `DYN_PROTOCOL` rebind and every OWN rebind slot (`_own_slot`, `tpyc/thir/emit.py`) append to `state.hoist_lines` DIRECTLY, guarded only by `assert state.hoist_drainable` -- inside a nested-def body that reproduces the ctor/lambda placement divergence, and inside a resumable body it raises rather than falling back. No constructible repro, so it is latent -- but this is the exact class that produced three build-breaking regressions and a ctor divergence, each found only after the fact. Surfaced by the /tpy-merge-master semantic hunt. Effort: S.
- **[cleanup] The rebind-slot registration chokepoint is not enforced.** `ctx.declare_rebind_slot` is the single entry point for a PRE-declared slot (one that may never be consumed), but `rebind_slots` stays a plain public dict that nine sites write directly -- legitimately, since they allocate at a rebind site or register an already-declared init slot for reuse, so nothing can go unconsumed. The distinction lives only in the helper's docstring. A future site that pre-declares without routing through the helper would silently reintroduce the dead-local class the helper exists to prevent. The companion invariant is newer and sharper: a held-back declaration must have a reachable drain site -- `nested_hoist_scope` / `_lambda_body_sink` supply one per lambda-rendered body, and nothing structurally stops a future body emitter from omitting it. Effort: S.
- Mark codegen's intentionally-unread locals `[[maybe_unused]]` and drop the name-blind `-Wno-unused-variable` / `-Wno-unused-but-set-variable` suppressions (`tpyc/toolchain.py` `_COMMON_WARN_FLAGS`). Today the suppressions are global, so a codegen-emitted dead local is as invisible as the user's legitimate `x = compute()` with no read. Emitting the attribute at the declaration site keeps the "users never see C++ warnings" invariant while letting the C++ compiler flag the artifacts we did NOT mark. Scope note from a g++ probe: `-Wunused-variable` does NOT fire on any `std::optional<T>` declaration -- GCC skips the warning for non-trivial ctor/dtor types, and `optional`'s default ctor is user-provided -- so this catches dead PLAIN-SCALAR temps (tuple-unpack, `error_return`); dead rebind slots are structurally impossible now that their declaration is held back until a rebind consumes it. Effort: S.
- The precompiled stdlib `.o` set omits package `__init__` modules. `_discover_stdlib_imports` (`tests/conftest.py`) skips every `__init__.py` on the grounds that "parent package import brings these in" -- but a package's own `__init__` is the only way to reach it, so `asyncio`, `http`, `os`, `urllib`, `tplib`, `tpy.coro`, `tplib.json` are absent from the shared `.o` cache despite the docstring's "every importable runtime module", and every case importing them recompiles them per-case. Perf-only. Widening it re-keys every case's exec marker (the cache's `output_hash` covers the whole set), so it wants its own change. Effort: S.
- Wrap the codegen block-scope snapshot/restore pair in a contextmanager. `snapshot_local_scope()` / `restore_local_scope()` are now hand-paired at ~9 sites (`_gen_if` and its elif/else arms, `_gen_while` body and else, `_gen_loop_body`, the for-else arm, `_gen_try_finally_only`, `_gen_try_return` handlers, `_gen_try_throw` body and handlers, `match.py::_emit_case_body`) -- a `with self.ctx.block_scope():` helper (mirroring the existing `nested_def_emission_scope` pattern) would make it harder to miss a site, which is exactly how the loop-`else` arms were missed until review. Not all sites can be wrapped: a few restore mid-block rather than at the block close. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the block-local scope-revoke fix. Effort: S.
- `directly_implements_dynamic` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/protocols.py`) only checks DIRECT `implemented_protocols`, so a user class that inherits a `@dynamic` protocol transitively through a concrete ancestor (`class Dog(Animal)` where `class Animal(Cloneable)`) is NOT recognized as implementing `Cloneable` directly. Codegen then wraps `Dog()` into an `Own[Cloneable]` slot via `make_unique<Adapter<Cloneable, Dog>>(...)` instead of the leaner `make_unique<Dog>(...)` -- both compile and run correctly (Dog IS-A Cloneable through C++ inheritance, so the Adapter indirection is unnecessary), but the Adapter form is a wasted allocation + indirection layer. Fix: walk `(record, *iter_ancestor_records(record)).implemented_protocols` (transitively) and drop the `is_native` exclusion (the comment claiming `@native` C++ structs don't inherit their declared protocol is stale -- `tpy::BaseException : tpy::Throwable` in core.hpp:35 does inherit). Pure optimization; changes the snapshot for `infer_const_dynamic_transitive` (Adapter -> concrete). Surfaced during the covariant-return exploration (dropped); this widening was the one independently-valuable codegen finding from it. Effort: XS + snapshot regen.
- **[cleanup] Fold the record-dunder binop fallback into OperatorResolver.** `sema/expressions.py` `_analyze_binop`'s record path (~line 1343, reached when `operators.resolve_binop` returns None) constructs a `FunctionInfo`/`ResolvedBinop` from scratch, independently of `OperatorResolver._make_resolved` -- the operator-dunder borrow-return fix had to thread `is_readonly` and `canonical_fi` into BOTH constructions, and any future fact added to the primary path risks being missed on the fallback. Fold the fallback's param-match nuances into `resolve_binop` so there is one construction site. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the operator-dunder borrow-return fix.
- Unify comparison operator codegen with arithmetic: comparisons (`==`, `!=`, `<`, etc.) now resolve through `BINOP_TO_METHOD` + `resolved_binop` like arithmetic ops, but two issues remain: (1) `DUNDER_CPP_TEMPLATES` in `operators.py` duplicates `DUNDER_TO_BINARY_OP` in `codegen_cpp/context.py` -- both map dunder names to C++ operators. Consolidate into one table or derive templates from the operator character. (2) The comparison codegen section still has its own special cases (BigInt/float cast, IntEnum coercion, Optional unwrap, literal folding) that run before `resolved_binop` dispatch. Ideally these would be handled uniformly in the binop result path.
- Extract shared arg-binding helper between `_gen_call` and `_gen_method_call` in `codegen_cpp/expressions.py`. Today each dispatcher has its own loop over `(arg, param)` pairs that applies coercion, covariant wrapping, `@dynamic` adapter insertion, `TpyTypeParamConstruct` / `TpyVarargPack` materialization, TypeParamRef substitution, etc. The loops have diverged repeatedly: `TpyVarargPack` was first handled only in `_gen_call` (broke `math.hypot(*coords)` -> mirrored into `_gen_method_call`'s first-pass loop), and then again only in that first-pass loop (broke method `*args` user-record calls -> mirrored into the user-record branch at the bottom of `_gen_method_call`). `_gen_method_call` alone has at least two arg-emission loops (first-pass + per-record-type fallback) that drift independently. Fix: pull the per-arg transformation into a helper `_bind_args(args: list[TpyExpr], params: list[(str, TpyType)], type_subst) -> list[str]` and call it from all paths. Keeps the dispatch split (the paths resolve very differently -- registry lookup vs receiver-type method resolution + TypedDict/callable-field/nested-constructor/property/dunder special cases) while eliminating the duplicated arg-list logic that has been the source of "feature X added to one path, not the other" bugs. Pairs with: consider having sema rewrite module-qualified calls (`math.hypot(x, y)` is currently `TpyMethodCall(obj=Name("math"), ...)`) into bare `TpyCall` with a qualified name, so they route through the simpler dispatcher -- `math` is a compile-time namespace, not a runtime object with methods.
- **[XS] `FieldInfo.has_in_class_init` property for the "field has an in-class initializer" fact.** Three sites now inline the same `fld.default_expr is not None` guard to mean "this field is default-constructible regardless of its type": `tpyc/typesys.py` (`_labeled_fields_and_parents_under_args`), `tpyc/sema/protocols.py` (`_is_default_constructible`), and `tpyc/sema/calls.py`. Add a `has_in_class_init` property on `FieldInfo` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) so the fact is authoritative and a future site can't silently omit a leg. First-class type fact, moves cleanly across the THIR boundary. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` (architecture-fit) of the enum-field-default branch.
- Inplace operator C++ return type: `__iadd__`/`__ior__` etc. declare returning self type (Python semantics) but the C++ helpers (`list_extend`, `dict_update`) return `void`. Add thin wrappers that return `T&` (e.g. `list_extend_inplace`, `dict_update_inplace`) so the declared return type matches the C++ signature. Affects list and dict.
- `tpy::ptr_variant<Ts...>` wrapper: replace `std::variant<Ts*...>` in param signatures with a thin wrapper that has an implicit converting constructor from `ptr_variant<T*...>` to `ptr_variant<const T*...>`. This would let deduced-const (non-mutated) params use deep const consistently with `@readonly`, without breaking callers. Currently deduced-const uses shallow const (`const variant<T*...>`) which doesn't prevent mutation through the pointer at the C++ level. Start with param signatures only; locals/fields/returns can stay `std::variant`.
- Inline `and`/`or` chains for side-effect-free operands: `a or b or c` currently emits an intermediate temp (`auto&& __tmp = (a ? a : b); result = (__tmp ? __tmp : c)`) to avoid double-evaluation. When all operands are provably side-effect-free (variables, literals), the temp is unnecessary and the chain can be emitted as a single nested ternary (`!a.empty() ? a : !b.empty() ? b : c`), which is more readable.
- `tpy::tpy_callable<F, R(Args...)>` concept: replace verbose `requires requires(__F0& __fn, ...) { { __fn(...) } -> std::convertible_to<R>; }` blocks with a compact `tpy::tpy_callable<__F0, R(Args...)>` concept in the runtime. Same `R(Args...)` notation as `std::function`. Needs a helper trait with partial specialization (`std::invocable` + `std::convertible_to` for return, void special case). Cosmetic improvement -- only worth prioritizing if it measurably speeds up C++ compilation for template-heavy Fn usage.
- Unify rvalue materialization: two overlapping mechanisms exist for extending rvalue lifetimes -- the slot system (`std::optional<T>` slots in `_gen_pointer_local_init`, tied to var decl infrastructure) and TempState (`auto&&` temps, expression-level). Both solve the same problem at different abstraction levels. Consider exposing a lower-level "materialize this rvalue" API that both var decls and expression-level temps (e.g. `and`/`or` ternaries) can share.
- Transparent coercion codegen: `TpyCoerce` in codegen has a growing list of special cases for when to forward `coerce_target` vs `actual_type` to the inner `gen_expr` (literals need the target to pick C++ representation; view coercions need it for zero-copy paths). Add a `transparent: bool` flag on coercion definitions so the decision is made at coercion definition time in `coercions.py`, not with `isinstance` checks in codegen.
- Deferred type resolution in parser: the parser currently resolves type names eagerly during parsing, but its per-module TypeRegistry lacks cross-module types. Two workarounds exist: (1) a `resolved` guard that accepts any import-resolved name as a NominalType in annotation context (sema validates later), and (2) speculative `_parse_type_annotation` at call-parsing sites with a sema fix to clear `call_type` when the name turns out to be a function. The proper fix: the parser should produce unresolved type reference nodes and let sema (which has full cross-module information) resolve them. This would also eliminate `_resolve_primitive_type` special cases for `slice`/`int`/`float`/etc. -- sema would resolve all type names uniformly through type factories.
- Push marker-protocol metadata from compiler hardcoding into library-declared `@builtin_type` annotations + add docstrings. Today `tpy.ValueType` / `tpy.Copyable` / `tpy.Default` / `tpy.NativeIterable` / `tpy.Send` / `tpy.Sync` / `tpy.ReturnException` / `tpy.Covariant` / `tpy.AnyFixedInt` / etc. are declared as bare `@native("tpy::X") class X(Protocol): ...` stubs with no docstring -- compiler dispatch on them lives in `tpyc/sema/protocols.py`'s marker arm (an `if qname == qnames.X` chain), with the qname strings centralized in `qnames.py`. Same per-type-knowledge-in-compiler-if-chains shape as the sibling "Push subscript metadata" entry below. Migration shape: (1) add `@builtin_type("tpy.X", is_marker=True, cpp_concept="tpy::X", marker_predicate="value_type" | "copyable" | "default" | None, ...)` to each marker so the metadata lands on its static TypeDef payload; (2) replace the marker arm's qname-chain with a single TypeDef-property lookup (`marker_predicate == "copyable" -> not is_type_non_copyable(actual)` etc.); (3) retire the now-dead qname constants from `qnames.py` (VALUE_TYPE / COPYABLE / DEFAULT / ...) and the per-marker fields in `qnames.py`'s "tpy protocols" block. Also add one-line docstrings to each protocol stub in `lib/tpy/tpy/_core/_types.py` (and sync `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py`) explaining what conformance grants (e.g. "passes to range-for codegen", "static `T{}` construction", "implicit `Box[Parent] <- Box[Child]` upcast") and how conformance is established (implicit predicate / explicit `extends`). The docstrings are useful even without the migration; folding them into the same pass keeps the touch local. Two known gaps in the existing predicates that the migration should also close: (a) `_is_default_constructible` returns False unconditionally for `TypeParamRef` parents in the aggregate-record walk (lines 502-504) -- doesn't consult `get_type_param_bound(name)` to check whether the bound conforms to Default, so `class Holder[T: Default](T): ...` (aggregate, extends T) is silently rejected; (b) regression-test coverage on `error_copyable_extends_contradiction` and `error_default_extends_contradiction` only exercises the `__init__ + required-params` denial branch -- the `del_suppresses_default_ctor` paths (@nocopy+__del__, __del__+no-__init__+indeterminate-init-field) and the aggregate-record-with-non-default-field path are unguarded.

Today the codegen bounds-safe path needs to know whether a type's C++ `operator[]` takes `size_t` (built-in containers: `vector`/`array`/`span`/`string`/`bytes` families) or the user's declared param type (typically `int32_t` for user records). The decision lives in `_is_concrete_user_record` (`codegen_cpp/expressions.py`) gated on `is_list/is_array/is_span/is_str_category/is_bytes_category` predicates from `type_def_registry.py` -- "STL types use size_t" is a fact about the library that's currently baked into the compiler. Pairs with the broader "Unify `TypeDef.cpp_formatter` and `@native` / `_native_cpp_names`" entry in the strict-warning hardening section -- both are about pushing per-type C++ properties from compiler-side hardcoding into library-declared metadata. Same shape applies to other ad-hoc per-type knowledge in codegen (e.g. the `iter_range` adapter dispatch, Python-int polymorphism per-type rules).

The precise rule: reject only when the subject's storage *root* is a dispatch-local copy (a non-lvalue root like `match foo():`); a narrowing alias is transparent (safe iff its source is frame-resident, unsafe iff it narrows a non-lvalue). Proper fix: track root-frame-residency through `narrowed_vars` rather than the blunt syntactic check. Small follow-up to the finally-top wiring; left as its own item because the original pair partner (`frame_slot` unification) has shipped.
  - **Resumable frame-field size: drop the engaged-bool for default-constructible field types.** The synthetic for-loop fields (`__for_i`/`__for_stop`/`__for_itr`/`__for_r`/`__for_src`/...) and hoisted locals are emitted as `std::optional<T>` / `tpy::frame_slot<T>`, both carrying an `alive_`/engaged bool, because they're constructed in the setup state (not the struct ctor) and may be non-default-constructible. For default-constructible field types (range counters `int32_t`, `std::vector` sources, most iterators) the bool is pure waste -- e.g. a range counter is `optional<int32_t>` (8 bytes) vs a bare `int32_t` (4). Bare storage is correct there (default-construct in the struct ctor, assign in setup; the struct dtor handles non-trivial destruction). The compiler can't see C++ default-constructibility, so it needs a `std::conditional`-style wrapper (`tpy::frame_field<T>` = `T` when `is_default_constructible_v<T>` else deferred storage) selected at the C++ level. Frame-size win for hot generators; pre-existing (the legacy generator path wraps these in `std::optional` too). Pairs with the "unify resumable frame fields on `frame_slot`" cleanup in `docs/GENERATOR_RESUMABLE_MIGRATION_PLAN.md`. Surfaced reviewing the `gen_resumable_for_temp` `__for_src` field.

So every frame instance pays a default-construction per such field regardless of which branch runs. Non-value locals already avoid this (deferred `tpy::frame_slot<T>`, constructed on first write, destructed only if engaged); value locals don't. Fix shape: extend the deferred-slot storage to value fields that are NOT assigned-before-use on all paths (liveness-gated), so construction is skipped on branches that don't reach the assignment, with destruction conditioned on the alive flag. Caveat: only a win when default-construction is non-trivial -- for cheap-default value types (`int`, small `BigInt`) bare storage + the no-bool form is better, so this must be gated on default-construction cost, not applied blanket. The unified answer is a per-field storage strategy driven by liveness + default-construction cost; pairs with the "drop the engaged-bool for default-constructible types" (`frame_field<T>` wrapper) entry above and the state-aware-destruction entry (which removes the alive bool). Low priority. Surfaced by user review of the `async_match_binding` frame layout.

Common when a `yield` is the last statement in a loop body (resume just loops back to the condition). Fix: a CFG simplification before emit -- when a Yield terminator's `resume_bb` is an empty BB with a single `Fall` to BB X, retarget the suspension's resume state directly to X and drop the dead BB (standard empty-block elimination / jump threading). Benefits both generators and async coroutines (per-suspension dispatch overhead, relevant for hot loops). Surfaced reviewing `gen_for_else`'s `S_RESUME_1`.

The "true type" intent of the annotation is lost. Unlocks: (a) validation that the declared `cpp_return_type` is wider than `fi.return_type` (catches accidental `cpp_return_type=int8` on a method declared `-> int64`), (b) using the source type to drive smarter codegen (e.g. choosing between `static_cast` and `tpy::checked_cast` based on the conversion direction), (c) better error messages when the name doesn't resolve (today: silently accepted at parse time, breaks at codegen lookup if anything reads it).

The current `tests/cases/union/error_union_*` snapshots cover only single-module diagnostics; the cross-module display-name code path (`setdefault` first-write-wins behavior across module-sema passes) is exercised only implicitly. Parallel-mechanism drift risk if one grows a rule the other misses. Effort: XS. Surfaced by /tpy-review of fix-finally-lowering.

Effort: XS. Surfaced by /tpy-review of fix-finally-lowering.
- Migrate `_gen_while` / `_gen_for_each` (and the explicit `narrowed_vars` snapshot blocks in `_gen_with` / `_emit_case_body` / `_gen_try_throw` / `_gen_try_finally_only`) to use `snapshot_local_scope` / `restore_local_scope` for the body-scope save/restore. Today each construct that opens a fresh C++ scope save/restores the narrowing map manually, in parallel to LocalScopeSnap which already covers it. (Re-scope before picking this up: only `_emit_case_body` survives under that name, and the persistent-alias map this item also named is gone -- the statement-level aliases now live on the lowering context.) Two-mechanism risk: when LocalScopeSnap gains another scope-bound field, every manual site has to be touched too. The blockers are (a) save_local_scope also tracks user-declared variables (`declared_vars`, `var_types`, etc.) which should NOT be restored at loop-body / try-body close (Python scoping makes them visible after), so the migration needs a narrower "narrowing-only" snapshot variant; or (b) the existing if-body pattern that does `restore_local_scope` at body close demonstrates that the broader restoration is in fact correct for narrowing-bearing scopes (worth verifying). Either way, consolidating onto one mechanism is the right shape post-fix-poly-early-return-narrowing. Effort: S. Surfaced by /tpy-review.
- Split `@nocopy`'s two meanings. The decorator currently covers two distinct intents: (a) **move-only at the C++ level** -- the C++ class actually deletes its copy ctor (explicit `@nocopy`: `Task[T]`, `Rc[T]`, `Box[T]`, user TPy classes that opt in); the TPy-level rejection mirrors the C++ ABI; pairs with `is_value_type=False` because copies are physically impossible. (b) **TPy-level ergonomics gate only** -- the C++ class is freely copyable but the TPy side rejects user-visible copies for safety (e.g. `SpanIter[T]`: a freely-copyable struct over `std::span + index`, but copying gives two iterators advancing independently and is almost always a bug); pairs with `is_value_type=True` because the C++ side is copy-friendly. Conflating (a) and (b) blocks a drift guard between explicit-stub `@nocopy` and `TypeDef.is_value_type` (the contradiction we hit on `tpy.Task` -- `is_value_type=True` despite the deleted copy ctor -- shipped silently for months). Possible shapes: (i) introduce `@no_implicit_copy` as the ergonomics-only sibling and reserve `@nocopy` strictly for C++-deleted-copy-ctor cases; (ii) add a `cpp_copyable: bool = False` knob on `@nocopy` so authors opt into the ergonomics-only meaning explicitly. Either lets the registry assert `@nocopy + not cpp_copyable + is_value_type=True` is impossible. Also re-opens the question of whether `SpanIter[T]` should be `@nocopy` at all -- the current footgun-prevention argument is real but might be better served by switching `is_value_type=False` on iterators (so `it2 = it` is a reference-binding, matching Python's mental model) and dropping the decorator. Effort: S; touches `lib/tpy/tpy/_core/_containers.py`, `lib/tpy/tplib/rc.py`, the @nocopy parser hook, and the registry. Surfaced after the `tpy.Task is_value_type=False` fix.
- **[LOW] `DUNDER_TO_REVERSE_BINARY_OP` is a static parallel table that is the filtered inverse of the adjacent `DUNDER_TO_BINARY_OP`** (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`): derivable as `{"__r" + k[2:]: v for k, v in DUNDER_TO_BINARY_OP.items() if k not in <comparison dunders>}`. Keeping it a separate literal means any future `DUNDER_TO_BINARY_OP` addition (e.g. `__matmul__`) needs a matching manual edit in the reverse table. Unify into one derived constant to drop the lockstep. Effort: XS. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, codegen-correctness) of `feat-reflected-operators`.
- **[LOW test-coverage] Reflected-operator codegen exercises only `__radd__`/`__rmul__`/`__ror__`.** The other reverse ops in `DUNDER_TO_REVERSE_BINARY_OP` (`__rsub__`, `__rtruediv__`, `__rfloordiv__`, `__rmod__`, `__rand__`, `__rxor__`, `__rlshift__`, `__rrshift__`) share the one friend-emit code path, so a single added case (e.g. `__rsub__`) proves the loop handles the rest; and `__rpow__` (deliberately excluded from friend-op emission, dispatched via `std::pow`) has no test confirming a user-defined `__rpow__` still works. Add as a completeness guard. Effort: XS. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `feat-reflected-operators`.
- **[LOW][THIR] Two `match` tiers each spell their own "this arm matches everything" rule.** `_arm_always_matches` (the scalar/switch tier, via `_dispatch_order_safe`) and `_match_record_arm_always` (the record tier, via `_record_always_arm_last`) in `tpyc/thir/lower/match.py` answer the same question with different bodies: the scalar rule counts a wildcard, a capture or an irrefutable or-group; the record rule adds a class pattern with no condition-rendering field sub-pattern, because on that tier the class test is already the label. The or-ALTERNATIVE half of the divergence is folded (`_or_alt_irrefutable`, shared with `_lower_or_field_conds`); folding the two arm-level rules needs the tier difference stated as a parameter rather than assumed, so it is a design call, not a mechanical merge. Surfaced by the batch-4 review (S1).
- **[LOW] Three traversals walk an aggregate literal's elements to reach ONE materialization owner.** Every one of them ends at `compat.materialize_fresh_value` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`); only the walk to it is duplicated. The ARRAY/list literal's annotated-mode loop (`_analyze_array_literal`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py` ~2296) runs `check_type_compatible` inline per element and materializes with the coercion that check returned; the SET and DICT literals materialize in a separate pre-pass (`_materialize_fresh_value_elements`, ~2155) that resolves its own coercion through `_materialize_narrowing_element_coercion`, and only afterwards reach their compat checks through three LATER branches (union/Optional/Any per element, covariant-generic upcast, peer unification). So the same element position is visited twice in two of the three literals and in a different order in the third. Consolidation: ONE contextual element pass per literal that checks and materializes in the same step. **Not mechanical** -- the set and dict unification currently runs after the pre-pass and reads the retyped element types, so folding the pre-pass into the checks means restructuring the unification in all three analysers, not moving a call; that is why it was declined as an in-round fix. Surfaced by the round-2 review of the fresh-value slot-conversion consolidation, re-verified in round 3.
- **[LOW] Four hand-mirrored walkers answer "where does this expression's storage come from".** All four walk the same chain -- coercion peel, walrus, name, field/subscript base, ternary arms, pointer-returning call, view constructor, `return_borrows_from` -- and each keeps its own copy of it: `TypeCompatibility.is_param_derived_expr` and `is_safe_to_return_expr` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) answer a BOOLEAN about the root, `_root_name_of_expr` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) answers ONE root name, and `_borrow_root_names` (added 2026-09-15 for the rebound-global rule, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) answers the root SET. The set-valued walk is the generalization: a boolean is `any(pred(r) for r in roots)` and a single name is the set when it has one member, so the three can read one walker. Not mechanical -- `is_param_derived_expr` short-circuits on literals (rodata is durable with no root at all) and `is_safe_to_return_expr` carries per-arm exemptions the root set does not express, so the fold has to decide what a "root" is for those before it can delete anything. The `## Type System` entry "`dict.get(key, default)` should return a BORROW like `get(key)`" is the first consumer that NEEDS the set-valued form -- it wants `_borrow_root_names`' verdict stored on `FunctionInfo.return_borrows_from` -- so that design fixes what a root is, and this fold should follow it rather than precede it. Surfaced by the round-4 review of the `global`-rebind borrow rule.

- **Match route admission from access shape.** `_route_match` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`) admits a field or subscript subject through a hand-kept tuple of tier NAMES; two review rounds in a row found a tier missing from it, and every future tier silently excludes field subjects by default. The fact the gate needs is the tier's subject-access shape (an `auto&` alias vs a by-value dispatch local), decided in the tier lowerers; derive the admission from that, after BUGS.md#match-subject-alias-under-guard-mutation makes scalar subjects snapshot by value.
- **Evaluation-order policy (language decision, open).** TPy evaluates the subexpressions of one expression in the C++ compiler's order (`BUGS.md#subexpression-right-to-left-eval`, postponed): g++ runs call arguments right-to-left, clang left-to-right, the standard guarantees neither. Three options, none chosen: (A) Python's left-to-right everywhere -- a temporary per observable operand at every multi-operand site (call/ctor/method arguments, two-operand binops, f-strings, moving container literals, dict key/value), the render being the sequenced stmt-expr build that bundle 2 built for the container literal and reverted pending this decision; the cost is priced once for the whole class and lands as one snapshot class; (B) Python's order by default with C++ order inside hot-path annotated sections (`@noalloc`-style opt-out), so annotation marks where the divergence is accepted; (C) declare the divergence permanently and document it. Whichever lands also settles the one site that rejects today (the `print` computed-`sep=` gate) and the operand-purity predicate: `_expr_evaluation_inert` (`checks.py`) is the one home of "can this operand be observed running", and `emit_prims.is_duplicable_expr` answers duplication only. Until decided, no per-site order fix; a case that observes the order may pin the RENDER, never the output (toolchain-dependent).

- **[design] Let the CPython `Box`/`Rc` stubs answer `isinstance` for the payload, so deref-view cases lose their `no_cpython.txt`.** Deref-view narrowing (`isinstance(b, Bird)` on a `Box[Pet]` sees the polymorphic payload, decided 2026-05-29 with the wrapper-composition phase 2) is declared a CPython divergence and about 19 cases under `tests/cases/` carry a `no_cpython.txt` citing it, which removes the parity phase for every other section in those cases. The divergence is simulable in `lib/cpy/tpy`: CPython's `isinstance` consults `obj.__class__` after `type(obj)`, so a wrapper stub exposing `__class__` as a property returning the payload's class makes `isinstance(b, Bird)` answer for the payload under CPython (the technique mock objects use). Design questions before doing it: whether spoofing `__class__` on the stubs is acceptable (it also changes `b.__class__` reads, `repr`, and any user `type(b) is Box` check stays `Box`), whether `Rc`/`Arc`/`Weak` follow (`Weak` has no deref view and must NOT), and whether the batch-3 lesson applies again: a `no_cpython` marker is a claim to test, and three such markers turned out false once the `Deref` stub forwarded reads. If accepted: change the stubs, drop the markers case by case with `--force-exec`, and reword the LANGUAGE_FEATURES sentence that says tests need the marker. Raised 2026-09-15 while reviewing `protocols/deref_view_alias_shadows_local`.

- **Division semantics switch: Python way vs C way for `/` and `//` (and `%`).** One compiler switch (or per-scope opt-in) selecting between parity and raw-C++ cost, covering both operators:
  - `//`/`%`: Python floors (round toward -inf; `-7 // 2` = `-4`), C++ truncates (`-3`). Codegen emits `div_floor`/`mod_floor` (a branch per op) plus the zero-divisor check (`div_check`/`mod_check`, elided when `divisor_non_zero` range tracking proves it). C mode = raw `/`/`%`, no floor adjustment, no zero check (UB on zero, like C++).
  - `/`: Python raises catchable `ZeroDivisionError` and defines int/int as the exact quotient rounded ONCE (the `truediv` overloads in `bigint.hpp`; magnitudes >= 2^53 take a BigInt slow path). C mode = plain `(double)a / (double)b` -- no zero check (yields inf/NaN), double-rounding above 2^53 accepted.
  - Implementation shape: the semantics live entirely in the stub `cpp_template`s (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_types.py`, `_core/_types.py`) and the runtime helpers, so the switch swaps templates like `--default-int` does; no sema change. Sub-options from the original entry remain live: default-to-C for fixed-width types only (int32 users already accept C++ semantics) with BigInt always Python; and range-tracking elision (already partly in place via `divisor_non_zero`) as the no-semantic-change fallback. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (mode naming, scope granularity -- global flag vs `# tpy:` directive vs decorator -- and the documented-divergence story).

## tplib (TPy standard library)
- **[stdlib][cosmetic] `itertools.cycle`'s `while len(saved) > 0:` can become `while bstack:`-style container truthiness, and a generic generator is unwitnessed.** The two `os.walk` explicit-stack loops dropped this workaround once container truthiness of a frame-resident generator local started compiling; `lib/tpy/itertools.py`'s `cycle` carries the same shape (`saved: list[T]`, a frame local in a GENERIC generator) and was left converted-not. Probed: `while saved:` compiles and matches CPython. Worth doing for consistency, and worth pairing with a test case -- no case in the truthiness set uses a generic generator, so the type-param element flavour of the container truthiness render has no witness. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready second opinion on the resumable-truthiness fix.
- Protobuf macro (tplib.protobuf) — designed in the doc, would be the next real use case for the macro system

## Standard Library

See `docs/STDLIB_ROADMAP.md` for the per-module tracker (status, priority, items, blockers). Update that doc when adding or changing stdlib coverage.

- **Downstream-blocked stdlib gaps (2026-08-03 port report) -- each already tracked in the roadmap, listed here because each one BLOCKS a specific program outright rather than costing an edit.** All five verified missing at HEAD. `struct.pack` (`Module 'struct' has no function 'pack'`; struct sits at ~60% with `unpack`/`calcsize` done and `pack` noted as "needs statement-expr or buffer builder") blocks minpng, an uncompressed PNG encoder whose entire job is packing binary headers -- the one direction not available. `sys.stdin` (`'stdin' not found in module 'sys'`; sys is a ~20% stub with argv/stdout/stderr/exit/maxsize done, stdin "needs read-side protocol") blocks brainfuck, which does `from sys import stdin` + `ord(stdin.read(1))` for the `,` instruction -- note the asymmetry, `stdout.write` works so the interpreter compiles right up to the point it needs to read. `collections.defaultdict` (`'defaultdict' not found in module 'collections'`) blocks life, sokoban and mastermind2, all of which use it as their core data structure, so its absence means rewriting the algorithm's storage rather than adjusting a line. `itertools.product` / `chain` / `groupby` (`'product' not found in module 'itertools'`; itertools is ~35%, chain/product blocked on variadic tuples, groupby/tee/batched on buffering) blocks sudoku5 and contributes to life -- `product` is what solvers reach for to enumerate grid coordinates. `hashlib.md5` (`Module 'hashlib' has no function 'md5'`; hashlib is ~20%, SHA-256 only, with MD5/SHA-1/SHA-512 noted as straight follow-ups sharing the class pattern) blocks rsync, which needs MD4/MD5-style rolling checksums. Ranking by cost-to-unblock: hashlib and defaultdict are the cheapest (a known class pattern and a factory-storing dict); `struct.pack` and `sys.stdin` are each self-contained; `itertools.product`/`chain` are gated on variadic tuples and should wait for that.
- **[perf] A file loop in a generator or `async` frame copies every line twice.** The resumable frame's loop reads `line = *it++`; the file's line iterator returns its post-increment by value (a copy that still holds the line), so each line is copied once into that temporary and once into the frame slot -- 1001 allocations for 1000 forty-character lines where the plain `for` loop makes 1 (it reads `*it`, then `++it`). `enumerate(f)` and `zip(f, g)` pay the same through `enumerate_direct_iter` / `zip_direct_iter` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/itertools.hpp`) and `native_iterator` (`dunder.hpp`). The fix is at the consumers -- read with `*it`, then `++it` -- in the frame loop emit (a render change across every generator snapshot) and those three adapters; a proxy that moves the line out of the iterator was measured and is worse (`getline` regrows the emptied buffer). Probes `/tmp/agents/bg/review/probes2/runtime/c_lines.cpp`, `c_consumers.cpp` (2026-10-02).
- **Iterating a file object: the rest.** A text file bound to a name iterates its lines since 2026-10-02 (`for line in f` in a function, generator or `async` body, comprehensions, `list(f)`, `enumerate(f)`, `zip(f, g)`, a generator expression; `tests/cases/builtins/open_iterate_lines`). Still missing: the unbound form `for line in open(p):`, refused at lowering with *not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:iter.call_shape)* -- the loop source is an rvalue of a move-only native class and the begin/end arm takes an lvalue name or an owning container call only; a `TextIO` PARAMETER as a loop source (*Cannot iterate over type TextIO*); `with open(p) as f:` inside a generator or `async` body (`BUGS.md#with-call-manager-in-frame-unlowered`), where `f = open(p)` ... `f.close()` is the spelling; and the `BinaryIO` sibling (`for chunk in fb`), which has no `__iter__`. Related and worth landing together: `TextIO` is also unusable as a class field or a parameter today (both filed in `BUGS.md`), so "open a file and stream it through a helper" fails at three separate points. Surfaced by a downstream port.
- **End-to-end `--no-signals` coverage in a real host.** The option is pinned by a runtime self-check, a mixed-link rejection and CLI runs of a standalone program (`tests/test_runtime_cpp.py`, `tests/test_cli_signals.py`); no test builds a CPython extension module or a `sources.cmake` host with it and shows that an `asyncio.run` export leaves the host's SIGINT handler alone -- only the self-check's declining `tpy_interrupt_async_begin` covers that. Needs a way to pass the option to one `tests/interop` case (the exec harness links a shared stdlib object set, so the case builds its own).
- **Effect graph for cleanup bodies.** A Ctrl-C check point inside `__del__`, `__move__`, the `std::hash` wrapper or an abandoned frame's cleanup now defers (a `::tpy::DeferSignals` scope, emitted unless the body-local `FunctionInfo.may_interrupt` allowlist walk in `sema/may_interrupt.py` finds the body inert). Next: a per-body callee inventory (separate from the mutation edges) carrying `may_interrupt` precision, so a cleanup body calling an inert TPy helper (or hashing a record whose `__hash__` is inert, e.g. `hash((self.a, self.b))` over records) emits no scope (the `std::hash` wrapper is where it matters: an inline thread-local costs two `__tls_get_addr` calls per bump in a `-fPIC` extension build, one `fs`-relative add in an executable), and a reachable-explicit-raise warning for `__del__` / `__hash__` (an exception escaping them is fatal by the fail-fast rule); the full nothrow fact stays with MIR's `exceptional_exits` once stubs carry nothrow annotations. Rejected shapes, for the record: catch-and-repost (the frame cleanup would skip its outer `finally` / `__exit__` actions, and a half-moved object or a wrong hash cannot be returned) and a per-body static omission without deferral (a helper called from the body still raises). Still documented as a limitation: a blocking wait inside such a body does not end on a Ctrl-C (an `asyncio.run` started there declines SIGINT ownership, so it completes and the Ctrl-C follows after the body).
- **One expression visitor: move the hand-rolled `children()` walks onto `parse.nodes.walk_expr_tree`.** The pruning pre-order visitor (`visit` answers whether to descend) landed with the inert-body walk (`sema/may_interrupt.py`, 2026-10-02); eighteen other walks each carry their own `children()` loop or stack and are marked with a `TODO` comment naming it: `parse/nodes.py` (`collect_name_refs`, `expr_reads_self_field`, `expr_contains_self_method_call`, the suspension scan, `read_names`, the walrus collector), `prescan.py` (two), `sema/analyzer.py`, `alias_rebind.py`, `builder_trace.py`, `expressions.py`, `flow_facts.py` (two), `loop_frames.py`, `match.py`, `narrowing.py`, `statements.py`. A mechanical sweep, one site at a time, each kept behaviour-identical (the `TpyLambda.children() == []` scope boundary and the `into_lambdas` opt-in must survive); drop the comments as the sites move.
- **A `...` method of a `native_module` class is not a bodyless binding to `is_bodyless_binding`.** The parser leaves `is_stub` False on a `...` method that carries no `@native` of its own inside a `# tpy: native_module` class (the builtin exception initializers), so `typesys.is_bodyless_binding` answers False for it; `sema/may_interrupt.py` works around it by asking the callee's module for `is_native_module`. Fix at the predicate (or set `is_stub` in the parser), then drop the workaround; MIR's `collect.py` and THIR read the same predicate, so run the suite for verdict changes.
- **One owning-FunctionInfo lookup for a `TpyFunction`.** Four sites find the registry entry of a callable by name with different overload policies: `thir/lower/predicates.py` `_owning_fi` and `codegen_cpp/gen_async.py` `_frame_deep_const_verdict` take `[-1]`, `thir/lower/callables.py` `resolved_definition` requires exactly one entry and checks `fi.root.declaration is func`, and `gen_async.py` `_frame_fi` (the `DeferSignals` fact of a frame) requires exactly one with the identity check. One identity-checked helper; the `[-1]` sites change which overload a THIR verdict picks (BUGS.md#frame-const-verdict-last-overload), so merge them with the suite. Two more readers of the `[-1]` policy: `predicates.param_passing` (every `THIRParam.passing` and every callee signature `method_callee` publishes, through `record_method_fi` / `_owning_fi`; equal to the resolved FunctionInfo's own verdict today only because `method_callee` admits single bodies and clone pairs) and `_param_is_deep_const` (the tuple layout's verdict, still read through `_param_const_verdict` beside the per-parameter verdict the THIRParam builders compute once).
- **Ctrl-C in a pure CPU loop stays pending (chunked loop polling).** A loop with no interruptible operation never consumes a Ctrl-C; the second Ctrl-C terminates the process like an unhandled SIGINT (no `finally`, no `KeyboardInterrupt`). CPython checks for signals at bytecode boundaries. A per-iteration flag check was measured at 2.5x on a vectorizable loop under clang, so any fix must poll in chunks (every N iterations, or only in loops that already contain calls) and keep vectorized loops untouched. Surfaced building synchronous SIGINT delivery.
- **Uncaught exceptions skip the destructors of frames with no handler (top-level catch in generated `main()`).** With no matching handler the Itanium ABI calls `std::terminate` without unwinding, so an uncaught exception -- including a Ctrl-C's `KeyboardInterrupt`, which now reports `KeyboardInterrupt` and dies by SIGINT -- runs no C++ destructors (`__del__`, RAII guards, unflushed buffered files) of frames between the throw and `main`; `finally` / `with` / `except` clauses still run because they are handlers. A `try`/`catch` in generated `main()` that rethrows into the terminate handler would unwind first, but it changes when and in which order every uncaught exception's side effects appear, so decide it on its own. Surfaced building synchronous SIGINT delivery.
- **Ctrl-C is not delivered inside some blocking waits.** The SIGINT handler uses `SA_RESTART`, so a wait that does not also watch the layer's wake fd sleeps through a Ctrl-C and delivers it at the next check point. Done: sockets, `JoinHandle.join()`, and (2026-10-02) `subprocess.Popen` -- `wait()` and the pipes it creates; the rule is that the owner of a blocking resource composes the wait through `lib/tpy/_interrupt.py`, and the raw `os` calls stay plain system calls (`BUGS.md#sigint-sa-restart-blocking-calls`). Open, each its own unit: (1) `tpy.sync` `Mutex` / `RwLock` locks and `Condvar.wait` (std::mutex / std::condition_variable; fix shape: timed slices like `JoinHandle.join()`, entered only once a lock attempt actually blocks so an uncontended lock stays a plain lock); (2) `socket.makefile()` readers (the bodies `http.client` / `urlopen` read): a socket-specific raw reader over the socket's own interruptible receive and its live timeout -- CPython's `SocketIO` -- in place of the `FileIO` over a dup'd fd with `SO_RCVTIMEO`; (3) `open()` file objects on a FIFO, pipe or tty (`std::fstream` has no portable fd to wait on) and a blocking `os.open` of a FIFO; (4) TLS sockets (`ssl`, whose mbedTLS bio does blocking `read`/`write`), `getaddrinfo` (DNS), `fsync`-style calls; (5) the polling fallback of `Popen.wait()` (no pidfd: macOS) notices the exit up to 50 ms late -- a kqueue `EVFILT_PROC` wait would make it exact. Dropping `SA_RESTART` runtime-wide is the global alternative and needs every native call without an EINTR loop audited first. Surfaced building synchronous SIGINT delivery.
- **`tpy.thread.scope` (structured threads) and an unused-`spawn` warning.** Dropping a `JoinHandle` without `join()`/`detach()` detaches the thread, as Rust's `JoinHandle` does (a drop-time panic was tried on the Ctrl-C branch and rejected: the runtime cannot tell a forgotten join from a handle unwound by an exception). So a forgotten join silently discards the worker's result or exception. Rust's answer is `thread::scope`: threads spawned inside the scope are joined when it ends, may borrow from the enclosing frame, and a panicked one re-raises after all are joined. Design that (`with thread.scope() as s: s.spawn(task)`, the borrow rules for a scoped task, exception aggregation) and, cheaper and independent, a compile-time warning when a `spawn(...)` result is discarded as a statement.
- **A detached thread dies when `main` returns; CPython waits for a non-daemon thread.** A worker whose handle was dropped or `detach()`ed and that still runs when the program ends is killed at process exit in TPy, while under the CPython stub the interpreter joins it at shutdown, so output the worker produces after `main` ends appears only under CPython. Decide: a process-exit join of still-running detached threads (CPython's model), or document TPy's as daemon-only.
- **Raw OS primitives in `tplib`, Python-named modules built on them (user direction, 2026-09-30).** The Python-level primitives (`print()`, `socket`, `time.sleep`, `input()`, `sys.stdout`, file objects, `JoinHandle.join`) carry the Ctrl-C check points, timeout emulation and CPython semantics; programs that want none of that should have a lower layer to reach for. Three layers: `_bindings/` (libc calls, not for user import; unchanged), `tplib` raw primitives (a thin TPy type over an fd or handle -- `RawSocket` with plain `recv`/`send`/`accept`/`connect`/`setblocking`, a raw `sleep`, a raw stdin line reader, raw fd files; OS errors only, no timeouts, no interrupt checks, no wake fd, zero overhead), and the Python-named modules composed from the raw types plus ONE shared interrupt primitive (today the private `_interrupt` module's `check` / `wait_readable` / `wait_writable` over a deadline -- the poll on the fd and the wake fd; the unit decides whether that module is promoted to a public name). The socket and join composition is already TPy code: `socket.py` builds its blocking / timeout-mode `recv`/`send`/`accept`/`connect` from libc calls plus the `_interrupt` module (`check()`, `wait_readable` / `wait_writable` over `_bindings.posix_signal.wait`, the one C++ wait primitive `tpy_interrupt_wait`), and `tpy.thread`'s `JoinHandle.join` slices its wait over `_RawJoin.wait_for`. Still C++: `time.sleep` (`sleep_op` in `signal_impl.cpp`, reached from the header `tpy::time_sleep`, since `time` is a native module and a TPy `sleep` would change every caller's generated C++) and `input()` (`read_line_op`, which needs stdio's buffered-byte count). What remains for this unit is the public `tplib` raw types and routing the Python-named modules through them. The raw types are not drop-ins for `asyncio.sock_*` or `socket.makefile()` (those take `socket.socket`). Behavior of the Python layer does not change, so the Ctrl-C tests and docs carry over. Not pressing (user, 2026-09-30) -- keep on the radar; design through /tpy-add-feature when picked up.
- **`signal.signal` (user signal handlers).** `signal` exposes only `raise_signal` + `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL`; the runtime's SIGINT layer is the only handler and always raises `KeyboardInterrupt`. CPython's `signal.signal` / `getsignal` / `default_int_handler` (and handlers for other signals, e.g. SIGTERM) would run the Python handler at the same check points the SIGINT layer already has. Surfaced building synchronous SIGINT delivery.
- **CPython extension modules do not see CPython's Ctrl-C.** An extension build (`# tpy: ext_module`) installs no SIGINT handler (the CPython host owns it); CPython's handler only sets a flag that `PyErr_CheckSignals()` reads, so TPy code blocked in `time.sleep` / `input()` / a socket inside an extension call sleeps through Ctrl-C. Fix shape: in ext builds, arm the layer without a handler (`tpy::install_interrupt_handler(false)`) and forward CPython's pending signals via `PyErr_CheckSignals()` at the check points, mapping its KeyboardInterrupt. Surfaced building synchronous SIGINT delivery.
- **argparse builder-trace limits hit by a real CLI.** (1) `choices=` must be a literal: `EFFECTS = [...]` at module level then `choices=EFFECTS` fails with `expected a tuple or list literal, got TpyName`. (2) `parser.print_help()` under an `if` fails with `builder-trace symbol 'parser' may not be used inside a control-flow block, lambda, or nested def`, so a bare run has to parse `["--help"]` instead; `parser.error(...)` under an `if` hits the same wall. (3) `default=` and friends refuse a `Final` constant although the diagnostic offers one (`expected a literal or Final constant, got TpyName`): `_resolve_final_literal` in `tpyc/macro_api.py` is a stub that never resolves a name. (1) and (2) are design limits of the trace expander (`tpyc/sema/builder_trace.py`), not bugs, while (3) is unfinished; the help-text divergence is `BUGS.md#argparse-help-omits-positional-choices`.

- **datetime -- v1 through v4 landed (`timedelta` + `date` + `time` + `datetime` with fixed-offset `timezone` AND `ZoneInfo` awareness, PEP 495 fold, strftime/strptime/fromisoformat, timestamp/astimezone, TZ-honoring Hinnant backend, `zoneinfo` module).** See `docs/DATETIME_DESIGN.md` for the full phased roadmap and divergences. Remaining deferred surface: (a) DONE -- `dt.date()`/`dt.time()` accessors landed once the member-name/type-name C++ collision was fixed (test `stdlib/datetime_accessors`); (b) `timedelta` float OPERATORS -- `timedelta / number`, `timedelta * float`, `timedelta / float` (round-half-to-even, via the new `float.as_integer_ratio()` builtin) -- DONE (test `stdlib/datetime_timedelta_float`); float CONSTRUCTOR args (`timedelta(hours=1.5)`) intentionally DECLINED (would need an `int | float`-union ctor that boxes integer construction and `@overload __init__` support fighting the THIR ctor migration -- integer equivalent `timedelta(minutes=90)` exists; a symmetric-ctor-overloads impl was built then reverted for this reason -- see DATETIME_DESIGN.md); (c) `timedelta + datetime` / `timedelta + date` reflected forms (need `__radd__`-style dispatch on the record operand); (d) `zoneinfo` residual surface (v4.1 added `available_timezones()` + `ZoneInfo.fromutc`): `from_file` + `TZPATH`/`reset_tzpath` are deferred backend work (no public TZif-stream parser in the vendored provider); `no_cache`/`clear_cache` are PERMANENTLY unsupported (identity semantics + mid-run db reload conflict with the value-typed pin-once model -- see DATETIME_DESIGN.md); (e) aware `time` incl. `time.fold` (tzinfo field on `time`, `time.fromisoformat` offset suffix -- currently a loud documented rejection); (f) `f"{dt:%Y}"` strftime delegation -- blocked on the `__format__` protocol feature below; (g) `timezone.utc` spelling -- blocked on Final/class-constants-of-record-type below (module-level `UTC` alias is the supported spelling); (h) aware-arithmetic micro-opt, only if profiling ever shows it: `.tzinfo` reconstructs the tz value via a zone_key+zone_lookup round-trip (mutex + hash lookup) and `datetime.__add__` re-ingests tzinfo per operation -- a raw tz-block copy constructor would skip both; cold today, do not build speculatively.
- **Make `time.tzset()` genuinely re-resolve TZ (currently a CPython-parity no-op).** The tz provider pins at first local-time use, so a SECOND `os.environ["TZ"]`+`tzset()` switch mid-run is silently ignored (acknowledged divergence in DATETIME_DESIGN.md; set-once-then-use is fully correct). Fix shape (meta-review-verified sound): `date_shim.cpp` swaps the pinned provider through an `std::atomic<const TzProvider*>` (readers stay lock-free -- one acquire load on the per-conversion hot path; replaced providers deliberately leak since an in-flight reader may hold one and tzset frequency is ~never), `tzset()` forwards to a shim `retzset()`. Wrinkle to solve: `time.tzset()` lives in header-only `time.hpp` while the provider lives behind the managed `date` lib -- keep the no-op fallback when the backend isn't linked. Unlocks a deterministic mid-run-TZ-switch parity test. Deferred by user decision at the datetime v3 review (option (a) now, (b) filed).
- **`__format__` protocol: record format specs in f-strings.** CPython dispatches `f"{x:spec}"` to `x.__format__(spec)`; TPy has no `__format__` dunder -- today the spec is misapplied to the `__str__` result (silent-divergence defect filed in BUGS.md; the sema-side rejection is the bug-fix half). The feature half: recognize a user-defined `__format__(self, spec: str) -> str` and route record format specs through it; datetime then adds the CPython strftime delegation (`__format__` = strftime for non-empty specs). Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. Surfaced by the datetime v3 design survey.
- **`Final[T]` (module + class constants) for value-type records.** `Final[timezone]` is rejected (constexpr model: primitives + tuple only), so a record constant is spelled as a plain annotated global (`UTC: timezone = ...`) -- exportable but not Final-frozen, and a class-level `utc: Final[timezone]` inside the class (CPython's `timezone.utc`) is inexpressible. Design (worked out at the datetime v3 review follow-up): the CONSTEXPR arm is permanently out of reach for records (ctors run BigInt validation -- not a literal type -- and named timezones call `intern_name`, a mutex'd table), so ride Final's EXISTING non-constexpr arm (`extern const T NAME;` header / `const T NAME = ...;` source -- exactly how `Final[int]`/tuple lower today, dynamic init at startup). Prereqs verified on the packed layout: value records are trivially copyable, readonly methods emit const member fns (calls on a `const timezone` compile), and dynamic-init interning is SIOF-safe (`tz_intern`'s table is a function-local magic static, constructed on demand; `UTC` itself is unnamed and never interns). Two halves: (1) module-level -- small: admit value records in `is_final_allowed_inner` (no flag-ordering trap: globals analyze after the ValueType pass), route record Finals to the extern-const codegen arm, frozen-binding sema generalizes as-is (~1d + tests); (2) class-level `utc: Final[timezone]` -- fiddlier: a new class-constant emission arm (in-class `static const timezone utc;` decl + out-of-line definition; the current class-const path only emits inline `static constexpr`), incl. the self-referential static-member-of-own-type sequencing. Half (2) is what makes CPython's `timezone.utc` spellable and shrinks the DATETIME_DESIGN divergence entry (the `error_datetime_timezone_utc_attr` case then flips to a happy case). The ALL_CAPS-without-Final warning already keys on `is_final_allowed_inner`, so widening the predicate auto-revives the suggestion for record constants. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. Surfaced by datetime v3's UTC constant.
